t_00144836d542.overview: Platform action follows the last of a tribe of changelings as he battles an army of evil mutants that has imprisoned nearly everyone. Collecting red "W" items transforms him into a werewolf with a longer-range melee attack and the ability to climb walls, while blue "W" items picked up in werewolf form turn him back into a human. Bubbles fill an anger meter, and gathering five turns him into a super werewolf that jumps higher and deals double damage for a limited time. Switching between the two forms, and building up rage for the stronger transformation, shapes how each stretch of the journey is fought.

t_0067f6836f35.overview: Never released, this Sunsoft action game began life as a Superman project before its hero was reworked into a generic caped superhero. Play resembles Sunsoft's Batman games: the hero runs, jumps, punches and ducks, but can also take to the air at any time simply by pressing up, which lets him skip large parts of some stages. Between the platforming stretches come side-scrolling flying sections in which he fires lasers from his eyes. The adventure is divided into five scenes of one to four areas, each closing with a boss; the first boss is a giant helicopter. Enemies include gunmen who fly in pairs and shoot lasers, and a fast, narrow tunnel precedes the final boss.

t_0091b4c1bfc8.overview:
Controlling the chipmunk Chip or Dale, players navigate side-scrolling levels by walking, jumping, ducking, and tossing objects. Items including boxes, bolts, and balls can be grabbed and hurled at adversaries and stage bosses. Each enemy hit costs a heart, and losing every heart costs a life, though extra hearts can be earned. The story follows the Rescue Rangers pursuing the escaped criminal Fat Cat, defusing a restaurant bomb and retrieving an ancient urn.

Levels advance in a linear order, except for a set of three late stages that can be tackled in any order. Single-player and two-player cooperative options are included. In cooperative mode, one player controls Chip while the other directs Dale, and partners can pick up and throw each other as weapons.

t_00b76f197841.overview: Jaleco's Famicom adaptation of Wonder Boy in Monster Land, developed by NMK, recasts the action role-playing game in the world of the novel Journey to the West: Sun Wukong takes on a demon king to rescue a kidnapped holy monk. The basic system follows the original. The hero fights through side-scrolling rounds and buys shoes, shields and armor in shops, while each sword beyond the starting dagger is dropped by a particular boss, and equipment changes his appearance on screen. Magic items used by pressing down include rolling orbs, fireballs, ground-hugging tornadoes and lightning that damages every enemy on screen, and power-ups grant temporary invincibility, halve damage, slow falls or double attack strength. No time limit is displayed, but damage still accrues as time passes. Two more characters from the novel appear in hidden events.

t_00d8049b87bb.overview: The mahjong manga Gambler Jiko Chuushinha by Katayama Masayuki, serialized in Young Magazine from 1982, returns in a second Famicom mahjong game from Asmik. Matches are again played against characters from the series, and three modes are included: free matches, a winning-streak tournament, and a Tako battle mode. Two guest characters from the manga Ōtoro Club also join the lineup of opponents at the mahjong table.

t_0160881cb051.overview: Released in Brazil by Milmar in 1991, Futebol is a modified version of Ultimate League Soccer, an unlicensed soccer game from C&E. The original game it is based on is built around teams made up of the top players from around the world, with a choice of eight of the world's top teams. Matches can be played against the computer, or two players can take each other on in a head-to-head contest of skill. Milmar's edition is the version of this soccer game sold in Brazil under the name Futebol, with its contents modified from the original release.

t_017111bb9194.overview: Captain Red-Hat Jack is assigned to grab the enemy's defense information center distribution plan, but first he has to overcome a series of complex locks. Sachen's game mixes action and puzzle play. Each round opens in a randomly generated building maze: Jack starts in the southeast and must reach the safe in the northwest, while guards pop up as he changes rooms and take one more shot to defeat with every round. The puzzle side is a sliding puzzle in which pressing A shifts everything in the current row or column, with the grid growing from 3x3 up to 8x8 in later levels. A timer runs throughout, and leftover minutes and seconds become bonus points.

t_017afa90c718.overview: Super-deformed characters from robot anime and tokusatsu series form teams and face off on the diamond in this entry in the Compati Hero series from Banpresto. Its teams draw on the Ultraman, Kamen Rider and Gundam franchises, along with Godzilla characters. Spending HP lets characters unleash special batting techniques and special pitches. A league mode has the first player face every team, an open match lets a second player or the computer pick any team to play, and an all-star mode has both sides alternately choose characters to build their rosters. Games can be set to three, five, seven or nine innings, and seasons run 21, 35 or 70 games. One or two players can take part, and the two sides cannot select the same team or character.

t_017f64a665ad.overview: Based on the TV anime, this action puzzle game has two players share a single playing field. Each side throws pairs of vertically joined pieces into the field, and pieces of the four patterns vanish when several matching ones line up vertically or horizontally. Clearing pieces this way helps carry blocks into the opponent's territory; the blocks shift left or right whenever either side drops pieces, but unlike pieces they never disappear, however many line up. Characters controlled by the players stand outside their territories, with the player taking the role of Shinnosuke Nohara. Two single-player modes are offered alongside a two-player versus mode.

t_01b6eda06c88.overview: Thirty-five years after a nuclear apocalypse devastates the world in 20XX, the protagonist explores the post-apocalyptic remains of Tokyo, where humanity has survived in underground bunkers. He and his friend free the demon Pazuzu, who names them messiahs, but the friend later turns against him, and the path eventually leads to a confrontation with Bael and the other demon lords. Dungeons are navigated in first-person and linked by an overhead overworld. Demons met in battle can be talked to and persuaded through negotiation to join the party, and two different demons can be fused into a new one at a special location. Morality-based dialogue options affect how people treat the protagonist and which ending he receives.

t_01bdeda387e1.overview: Four college students at a campfire see a UFO crash-land, and its alien crew warns of a coming invasion. Unable to save everyone, the aliens ask the students to gather space power before the end of 1999 so they can escape to the aliens' home planet. Up to four players take part in the board game, with the computer filling empty seats, each choosing a name, face and occupation. Players draw cards bearing a number from 1 to 6 or a trap, move around a town laid out as a sugoroku board, and handle the events on the squares where they stop. Each completed lap pays a salary, plus bonus space power for the leader, and advances the calendar half a year, bringing invasion events, such as a cult, desertification and an ice age, that turn squares into penalties. The player with the most space power escapes by rocket.

t_024990cb31a9.overview: Known here as Knight, the cyborg hero is sent from Earth in the year 2395 to the artificial planet Altile, where the alien Xantho Empire has seized the weather-control stations and forced citizens underground. His mission is to defeat the invaders' leader, Xur. Bombs clear blocks and enemies while a laser gun fires rapid shots, and in this Japanese release a single bomb blast that catches the hero kills him. Each of the eight Periods contains one to three stages whose exits open only with a key hidden under a block, and some stages also demand a chalice. Items found in blocks or bought in shops include candles and lamps for underground areas and energy batteries for a steadily draining energy meter. A Theme Song mode displays lyrics for the main theme.

t_026951bfd4ec.overview: Hunting dinosaurs with a light gun, the player in Blood of Jurassic rides through a rail shooter while avoiding fire shot by certain dinosaurs. Six stages can be picked from a level selection screen, among them a desert stage and a jungle stage, and every stage ends with a main boss. In these boss fights the targets are floating dinosaur heads rather than the dinosaur drawn in the background. Shooting red dinosaurs releases power-ups that float to either side of the screen and are collected automatically, but other dinosaurs can destroy a power-up if they touch it. Some levels include parallax scrolling.

t_028a422e9c51.overview: When the ten puppies of Punch, the Uesugi family dog, fall into another dimension, twins Tatsuya and Kazuya Uesugi and their childhood friend Minami Asakura head there to rescue them. Based on the Touch manga, the action game has the player roam a wide field, defeating large numbers of tough enemies while leading Minami, whose attack power is zero. Baseball survives mainly in the form of thrown balls, and the adventure departs heavily from the world of the original story. The difficulty is high.

t_035f5844c8ee.overview: Side-scrolling 2D action carries this 1992 Famicom release from Hect, which sends Ricky, a green-haired boy, on a quest to rescue his father from the evil necromancer Count Crimson. The rest of Ricky's family has also been kidnapped, and a blonde girl named Rosina appears in the story cut-scenes, though she does not take part in the gameplay. Ricky can grab onto ledges, and an item grants a temporary double jump. The adventure runs across seven stages with settings that include a pirate ship and a clock tower, ending with an escape stage in which the player must dodge needles to get out.

t_037ced21144c.overview: The ninth and final Super Cartridge holds three games and, like the second volume, lacks a logo on its menu. Challenge of the Dragon, developed by Joy Van, is a Double Dragon clone included in its English version. Rockball, developed by Sachen, is a puzzle game very similar to Chew Man Fu, a game for the TurboGrafx-16. Popo Team, also developed by Sachen, is a clone of Oil's Well. Each game is chosen from the menu and played separately.

t_039d0ff917cb.overview: Despite its name, the Sunsoft cartridge is a conversion of After Burner II, and its title screen reads AFTER BURNER II. The player pilots an F-14 fighter against enemy aircraft, firing a forward machine gun and missiles that lock onto targets. There is no throttle control; pressing Start during play ignites the afterburner for a fixed time to accelerate, an element inherited from the sequel. The carrier the jet launches from at the start is renamed from the arcade's SEGA ship to a SUN one. Clearing the game unlocks a much harder second loop in which the speed climbs sharply as the stages progress. The large cartridge memory holds pseudo-rotation and scaling patterns and partial digitized voice samples. The unlicensed Tengen release shares its basic character graphics but follows the first After Burner, with different stage layouts, title demo and colors.

t_03a3a50c4e6b.overview: Six inter-connected tables make up this pinball simulation, which invites players to explore them and post high scores. The tables include a sports car level, a casino level, a Breakout level complete with a movable paddle, and a robot boss battle. Beyond scoring, the overall goal is to find and collect certain Mahjong pieces to complete a winning hand. Up to four players can take part, taking turns throughout the game. Despite the title, it has no relation to the original Pinball developed by Nintendo for the Famicom; it was developed by Soft Machine and published by Coconuts Japan.

t_03cec2c84c50.overview:
Seven levels structure this beat 'em up crossover, which sends the heroes to the giant spaceship Colossus to thwart an alliance between the Dark Queen and the Shadow Boss. Players choose from five characters, consisting of martial artists Billy and Jimmy Lee alongside humanoid amphibians Zitz, Pimple, and Rash. Progression shifts across environments, beginning on the exterior of the spacecraft, moving through interior corridors and the bowels of the ship, and transitioning to a space craft shooting sequence and a race along a missile headed for Earth before concluding with boss confrontations.

Two buttons control attacks and jumping. Combat maneuvers include specialized strikes, slams, throws, attacks from hanging ropes or ledges, and moves executed while riding speeder bikes. Play options provide single-player action along with two-player setups, offering settings with or without friendly fire. Each hero has a limited number of lives, and bonus pods can hold extra lives, energy, or weapons.

t_03df9d30853f.overview: Instead of a conventional game, this Jaleco cartridge, developed by Sanritsu and Aicom, is a fortune-telling simulator that uses Eastern mysticism to forecast the player's future from his or her year of birth. Readings can be requested for distinct areas of life, including romantic prospects, the best time to marry a partner and the outcome of future business dealings.

t_0488fa5f75b4.overview: Fighting a dictator who is arming to seize neighboring countries, the player flies 37 missions. Each one has two parts: an air game, a dogfight against enemy defenders seen in 3D from the cockpit, and a ground game in which every target named in the briefing must be destroyed while dodging attacks from ground forces and enemy aircraft. Missions are offered four at a time for each level, and a cleared mission cannot be picked again. Before takeoff the player chooses an F-18 Hornet, F-14 Tomcat or Harrier and loads weapons such as Sidewinder, Sparrow and Phoenix missiles, bombs and fuel tanks; the Harrier can hover. A head-up display points to the nearest enemy and shows missile lock-on, and chaff decoys incoming missiles. Losing all three fighters ends the game, and progress continues by password.

t_0496ae7fb513.overview: Square's Famicom conversion of the Game Arts computer game puts the player in control of Thexder, an experimental robot that can transform into a jet. A weapons-development ship has been trapped by magnetic lines of force from a mysterious asteroid, and only a small craft can slip inside to destroy the device generating them. In robot form, Thexder can jump about three times its own height and fires automatically aimed shots, while the jet form flies in the direction of travel. Activating a barrier costs energy but blocks contact damage and destroys enemies touched from the side. Energy serves as life and drains on contact with enemies and damaging floors, though some enemies restore it when destroyed. On the Famicom, the laser is replaced by bursts of three round shots that still aim automatically but no longer consume energy, and a cycle of five levels repeats in new colors up to level 99.

t_04c87bb3efa2.overview: Players take the role of mayor in this unfinished NES build of SimCity, designing and managing a city as it grows. Produced through a collaboration between Maxis and Nintendo, it introduces Dr. Wright, a mentor character who teaches the basic concepts of city planning. The main menu offers a practice mode alongside scenarios, among them monster attacks. Bank loans give a struggling city a way out of an early financial death spiral, and achievements unlock rewards such as special buildings for hitting population milestones. The build is very playable but incomplete: some property values are miscalculated, and a glitch grants easy infinite money at the end of an in-game year.

t_04ec13d0f2e6.overview: Based on the fairground whac-a-mole game, this Famicom action title is played by striking a mat controller with a rubber mallet. Moles poke out from eight different spots on the ground and must be hit before they quickly duck their heads back down. The game shipped with the mallet and a smaller version of the mat known in Japan as the Family Trainer, whose grid of buttons corresponds to the holes the moles emerge from. Because the mat has twelve buttons, stages can arrange their eight holes differently: the first level uses a ring of eight buttons on the right side of the pad, while the next forms a U shape around an island from the left, right and bottom rows. Later stages replace the moles with other animals and characters that must be bopped quickly.

t_053b307b9203.overview: Anco's basketball game Tip Off was in development for the NES before that version was cancelled, and what survives is a very early prototype originally developed by Enigma Variations for Anco. The build contains playable characters but no CPU player, so two control pads are needed to play. Development never reached the stage of title screens or option menus, the prototype itself is silent, and a number of glitches remain from its early state, as work had focused purely on getting the basic game running.

t_05453b1c202a.overview: Hudson Soft's Famicom adaptation of the arcade vertical shooter puts the player at the controls of a starship called the Final Star, shooting down enemies and destroying structures for points as the screen scrolls upward. Each stage is named after a letter of the Greek alphabet. The ship is kept deliberately simple, with only two levels of weapon power and no secondary weapons such as missiles or bombs, so success depends on steady shooting and dodging. In this version, holding fire on the enemies already on screen keeps new ones from spawning, a quirk absent from the separately developed NES version.

t_0558de63c585.overview: Taito's Kyuukyoku Harikiri baseball series moves from the professional leagues to high school baseball in this 1992 Famicom entry, the high school version of the Harikiri games. Its distinguishing system is Nekketsu points, a resource the player spends to unleash special techniques in the middle of a game. On the mound, Nekketsu pitching offers a heavy ball, a forkball or a high-speed fastball, while at the plate the same points power special Nekketsu batting.

t_0595a2df5bc6.overview:
Multiple gameplay modes structure the adventure, beginning with Robin Hood escaping an Arab prison alongside Azeem and Peter Dubois. Upon returning to England, Robin discovers his father was killed and that the Sheriff of Nottingham governs unjustly. Robin seeks out outlaw allies hiding in Sherwood Forest, establishing a home base where he continually receives and completes missions, culminating in a final confrontation to remove the Sheriff.

Standard exploration occurs from an overhead perspective, directing Robin through environments while fighting hostile soldiers. Other sequences shift mechanics: side-view duels allow Robin to jump, flip, and strike single opponents; high-angle overhead views manage large clashes between rival armies; and horseback sequences have Robin leaping over obstacles during high-speed rides. An equipment system lets players place items in either of Robin's hands, with each hand tied to its own action button.

t_05c44cec9bdb.overview: Darces the Dark Overlord has returned to the land, and a young hero sets out in search of a holy sword capable of destroying him. Long ago, the legendary warrior Magi rose to challenge Darces. This real-time first-person role-playing game handles movement through towns, across the world map and inside dungeons, as well as fights with monsters, entirely in real time. During battle, weapons are selected through icons, and spells are created by combining runes from various elements. An elder explains the task at the start of the adventure.

t_05d7cf0853ae.overview: Based on the manga and anime about the thrifty schoolboy Hagemaru, this single-player action game also includes adventure elements. Long ago, the Tsuru Seko no Akashi arrived from space, and Hagemaru, as its heir, sets out on a journey to find it. Adventure stages are spent gathering hints, while action stages have him defeating enemies and earning money on the way to each goal. Jumping and then pressing the B button sends him headbutting down onto enemies below, and holding up on the direction pad with B charges a coin throw that knocks enemies out. Picking up the coins that defeated enemies drop is dubbed tsuru-seko. There are no extra lives and the three hit points can never be increased, so three hits or a fall into a pit ends the game, and continuing costs half of the money he holds.

t_06166c6f5bf7.overview: Mine Sweeper 3, the last of Sachen's three Cai Di Lei games, turns Minesweeper into a two-player versus contest. Each side gets a fixed 12x16 board with 20 mines, and this is the only variant with a time limit; clearing tiles labeled with a number adds to the timer. A player who clears the board earns a point, while triggering a mine or running out of time hands the point to the opponent. The first player to score three points wins the match.

t_061a2b9930e0.overview:
Final Fantasy is a role-playing game where players control four Light Warriors seeking to restore the light of four darkened Orbs. Play begins by assembling a four-person party from six classes: Fighter, Thief, Black Belt, Red Mage, White Mage, and Black Mage. Characters explore towns, dungeons, and an overworld map, initially traveling on foot before gaining access to a ship, canoe, and airship. Towns offer information, items, and equipment, while dungeons feature treasure chests and boss encounters.

Encountering enemies triggers turn-based, menu-driven combat where players select commands including Fight, Magic, Drink, Item, and Run. Defeating monsters yields money and experience points, allowing characters to raise their attributes and advance in level. Later in the journey, characters can undergo a class change that expands equipment and magic capabilities. Staying at an inn restores the party's hit points and magic and saves the game to the cartridge's battery.

t_06657c6d5053.overview: Board-game movement meets role-playing combat in this adventure from Technos Japan. In the kingdom of Siland, four adventurers set out to talk to the king, and the player picks one hero from four types: the well-rounded Fighter, who is weak with magic; the Elf, who relies heavily on offensive spells; the Dwarf, who excels at close combat but cannot use magic at all; and the Half-Elf, who mainly casts spells that support attacks. Dice decide nearly everything. The hero advances by the number rolled, and in battle both sides roll, with the higher roll winning and the gap setting the damage. During a fight the player can also call on Dice Man for help. The single-player quest spans six areas, each guarded by a boss monster, with a base for preparing equipment and items before setting out.

t_0678a78164e0.overview: Released outside North America with all references to Al Unser Jr. removed, this Data East racer is based on the Formula 1 World Championship. The car is steered with the D-pad, accelerating with A and braking with B, and turbo boosts can be used when needed but must be refilled once empty. Signposts and other cars have to be avoided, since accidents can harm the engine or blow tires, which are repaired by pitting. The World Championship Season runs a 16-race schedule against a field of 26 cars, with a single qualifying lap setting the grid and set-up points earned to improve the car. Two time trial modes, with and without computer opponents, offer any of the sixteen tracks, and up to four players can take turns.

t_068093499141.overview: Takahashi Meijin sets out across a side-scrolling island adventure to rescue his girlfriend Tina, who has been kidnapped. The journey spans 32 stages: eight areas of four rounds each, with every round divided by checkpoints, and a boss waits at the end of each area's fourth round. A health gauge drains steadily over time and whenever the hero trips on a rock, so fruit and milk bottles must be collected to keep it filled, while touching an enemy or falling into a pit or water costs a life. Attacking is possible only after picking up a stone axe, which can be traded for longer-range fireballs. Eggs hold weapons and bonus items, though one may contain an eggplant that drains the gauge, and the fairy Honey Girl grants brief invincibility. Some hidden spots summon a cloud that warps to a fruit-filled bonus stage.

t_06a3816cb728.overview:
Solid Snake infiltrates the fortified state of Outer Heaven, avoiding enemy detection from an overhead perspective across flip-screen areas. The rookie special forces operative must rescue captured hostages and neutralize a nuclear-armed bipedal mecha known as Metal Gear. Snake begins without armaments and collects gear across five fortified strongholds of one to three floors each. Weapons including handguns and rocket launchers, alongside items like rations, key cards, and a gas mask, help him progress through locked sectors and combat mercenary bosses.

Guards follow set routes and trigger alert states upon spotting Snake or detecting noise. Cameras and unsuppressed gunfire also raise alerts, and alerted guards summon reinforcements until Snake defeats them or flees to another screen. Rescuing hostages raises Snake's star rank, boosting his maximum health and ammunition capacity. Throughout the operation, a radio transceiver allows communication with Commander South and resistance contacts across designated frequencies.

t_06a79753b8ab.overview: Europe is the subject of this quiz game in Russian, made for the Dendy by A. Chudov. In the first section the player must correctly guess the name of a country in Europe: a wrong answer costs $10, while a right answer wins $10 and moves the player to that country. After entering a country, the player has to correctly answer questions on its capital, its flag and its neighboring countries. Running out of money prompts the player to earn more by playing Math Fight or Warehouse No. 18, or by gambling at a casino. Once every country has been visited, the game offers the player a real trip to Europe.

t_06b1a580313b.overview: Racehorse breeding drives the first Derby Stallion, a simulation created by Hiroyuki Sonobe. The player acts as breeder, owner and trainer at once, producing horses at the ranch, training them and entering them in races at the stable on weekdays, then watching the races at the track on race days, all in pursuit of GI race titles. Races follow the schedule of a fictitious body called the SRA, and while stallions carry real names, broodmares and racehorses have invented ones. In the Famicom original, horses can mostly race only in the Kanto region, with just a few Kansai GI races reproduced. All owned horses are colts, so filly-only races are absent, and inbreeding is the only breeding theory modeled. Progress is saved automatically.

t_06d351038671.overview: Life itself becomes a board game in the third entry of the series, with each character advancing from early childhood through school, a move to the big city, college or job hunting, and working life. One to four people can play, starting from two participants, and computer opponents are optional. Dice give way to a roulette for movement, and practiced players can partly time where it stops. The board is drawn as a raised, top-down map, and a player who lands on an occupied high square kicks the one already standing there down to the square below. Apart from paycheck squares, every square is hidden, so players must remember what each one does. Promotions and demotions come from three-choice job cards, and minigames include rock-paper-scissors, a quiz, horse racing, a high-low game and blackjack. Final ranking depends on money, while money, stats and events encountered lead to multiple endings, and arrests happen often.

t_0705c6bb1fc2.overview: While the Turtles vacation in Key West, Florida, Shredder hijacks April O'Neil's news broadcast, takes her hostage and reveals that he has turned the borough of Manhattan into a floating island. One or two players choose among Leonardo, Raphael, Michelangelo and Donatello, each wielding a signature weapon, and fight through eight levels running from the Florida beaches to the floating island, the Technodrome, Shredder's lair and finally Krang's spaceship. Besides attacking and jumping, each turtle can toss enemies and use a special attack that costs some energy. Bosses include Bebop and Rocksteady, Slash, Leatherhead, Tokka and Rahzar, with Super Shredder waiting at the end. In this Famicom edition, the option screen is available from the title menu, a game type setting turns friendly damage on or off, and extra cheat codes provide a stage select and more continues.

t_075ba64cb456.overview: Kamen Rider 1, Kamen Rider 2 and Kamen Rider V3 each take the lead in one area of this single-player action role-playing game, fighting through stages toward the final boss. Each rider has different power, speed, jumping and attack abilities and special moves, and the helper riders Amazon, X and Stronger can be bought in shops to join temporarily. Enemies appear as symbols on the map, and battles are an unusual shoving contest: fighters push each other, and slamming a foe into a wall deals damage. Defeating enemies earns experience that raises a rider up to level 8, and a set amount of money is needed to open the entrance to the next stage. The three opening areas, Shocker Land, Shocker Town and Shocker Mountain, can be played in any order.

t_078097b2887a.overview: Sanrio characters including Hello Kitty, Keroppi and Minna no Tabo take the court in this sports game, essentially volleyball or tennis played without nets in a way that closely resembles four-square. Matches can be played by two, three or four players, and a difficulty option raises the intelligence of the computer-controlled opponents. Do-overs are allowed during play. Before a match, players can pick one of three background music tracks or play without music, and a victorious player is awarded a large ostrich trophy.

t_078209265641.overview: A jungle warrior, Toki in the arcade original, is turned into an ape-like creature by an evil witch doctor who has kidnapped the princess of his tribe and transformed the island's people into beasts. Keeping his own mind, he crosses the island toward the witch doctor's golden palace to defeat him, rescue the princess and lift the curse. The hero attacks by spitting energy balls from his mouth, battling hordes of jungle monsters through levels that each end with a miniboss and run on a timer. Lucky rabbit feet grant bursts of agility and jumping power, and clocks add time. Taito's Famicom version is slightly altered and adds a health bar, so a single hit no longer costs a life.

t_07aac602a989.overview: Tengen planned this Nintendo Entertainment System conversion of the 1987 Atari Games arcade shooter, but the port went unreleased and survives only as a prototype. In the arcade original, Major Rock Hardy and Captain Ace Gunn travel through a three-dimensional maze and battle a series of robots known as the Xybots, whose mission is to destroy all mankind. One or two players navigate corridors with a laser gun, seek cover from enemy fire behind objects and try to reach each level's exit, with a large boss Xybot waiting in certain levels. Energy is replenished by collecting energy pods, and shops between levels accept coins dropped by defeated Xybots for energy and power-ups such as armor, speed, firepower and maze maps.

t_08600d1b9fdc.overview: Modeled on Dance Dance Revolution, Street Dance is a music game built for Famicom/NES hardware, credited on screen to "INVENT" and attributed to the developer Inventor. Its unauthorized renditions of pop songs, among them "Butterfly" and "Funkytown", play through the Sunsoft soundfont, and Jar Jar Binks from the Star Wars series appears as one of the dancers. The song menu offers 68 selections, but only a handful of real tracks exist: many entries repeat earlier songs under other names and serve as higher difficulty options, while the rest have no music at all. The circulating ROM appears to be unfinished rather than a polished commercial product.

t_086690dce91f.overview: Irem's Famicom shooter expands its Game Boy counterpart with added stages while keeping a relatively simple design aimed at younger players. Missions begin with rescue stages, each with its own objective and a time limit, flown in the rescue mechs of the Baron Team, which can be swapped at any time. Once the rescue is complete, Kenta or Katori takes over and sorties in flight form; when a transformation order comes partway through, the craft can change into a humanoid form, and combining carries play into the second half of the map, fought as Fighbird or Granbird. Scrolling is forced, so getting caught on buildings at the screen edge costs a life regardless of remaining health. Standard and extra weapons are switched rather than fired together, and the final stage pits Great Fighbird against Dryas.

t_0867d7a44600.overview: Riders compete in a 4,000-kilometer bicycle race around Japan, following the coastline and crossing countryside between major cities past scenery such as forests and cattle farms. The rider comes from Team USA, Team Japan, Team France or Team Italy, each team having five members with different strengths and weaknesses. The altitude of each section and the distance to the stage finish are always shown. Teammates hand out power-ups that raise bicycle speed, along with on-the-spot repairs and extra energy. Finishing close to first place earns points that serve as currency for buying faster, longer-lasting bicycles, some suited to mountains and others to lower, flatter ground. Running out of energy or falling behind a certain ranking loses the race, and passwords save progress for this single-player game.

t_08774e06e5de.overview: Supervised by Japanese professional golfer Jumbo Ozaki, this golf game offers 36 holes of play split between an East course and a West course. Three modes are available: Stroke Play, Match Play and Tournament. In every mode except Tournament, players can receive advice from Jumbo Ozaki as they work their way around the course, and Match Play lets two players compete head to head. HAL Laboratory later produced a Super Famicom golf game that can be considered its sequel.

t_08844b12dc69.overview: Goemon, a righteous thief armed with a kiseru pipe, lands in jail after a careless mistake and meets the ninja Ebisumaru, who tells him of treasure hidden in a mechanical castle. The pair break out and travel across Japan from Kyushu to Ezo through about ten stages, each themed on its region and some ending in a boss fight. Most stages are cleared by collecting three passes to open a checkpoint gate. Gold coins buy items in shops, Maneki-neko figures change weapons, and Okame boost speed and jumping. Maps now also scroll vertically, and a continue system is included. One or two players can play simultaneously, with the second player controlling Ebisumaru; speed and weapon levels are shared, so a hit costs both players the upgrade.

t_08b4b82492f4.overview: Unifying ancient China, divided here into 41 provinces, is the ultimate aim of this historical strategy game, the second in its series. Six scenarios begin at different points between 189 and 220, and after choosing one, players decide which warlords they will control; some rulers are reserved for the computer. For the first time, a player can also create an original character and start as a new lord in an unoccupied territory. Commands are limited to one per officer stationed in a province, which makes recruiting more important, and diplomacy is greatly expanded. Battles add duels, turncoat schemes, ambushes, and joint and reinforcement armies, with attackers limited to five units against up to ten for the defender. A reputation system affects how loyal officers stay toward their lords, and advisers can predict a plan's chance of success.

t_08d51e82e528.overview: Gamtec's vertically scrolling shooter carries the subtitle Thunderbolt Fighting Plane on the Famicom, a name that may refer to the player's own aircraft. Controls are minimal: the plane moves with the directional pad and fires with a single button, with no bomb attack. Three types of weapon are available, along with orbiting ships that act as shields and secondary missiles. Collecting power-ups of the same color raises a weapon's level, while getting hit levels it back down; a hit is only fatal once the shields are gone. Infinite continues are available for getting through the stages.

t_096875a4fbc9.overview:
Behind the wheel of a Formula One car, the player steers, accelerates, and brakes across international circuits while competing against twenty-four other drivers. Modes include single-course practice sessions and the full sixteen-round Grand Prix World Championship. Before starting, the player chooses between an automatic transmission or a three-speed manual gearbox shifted via the directional pad, using the tachometer lights to determine the best time to change gears.

In championship mode, each round opens with an uncontested qualifying lap to set the car on the starting grid. During the five-lap races, drivers must maintain an active position limit shown on the dashboard; dropping behind this cutoff results in disqualification. Excessive track excursions or collisions degrade tire grip, requiring a stop in the pit lane where rapid button presses speed up the tire-changing crew. A password system allows progress through the season to be resumed.

t_098596badd8f.overview: Falling blocks meet poker hands in this card puzzle. Cards from a standard 52-card deck drop one at a time toward a 5x5 grid, and each can be steered into one of the five columns. Lining up adjacent cards into a three-, four- or five-card poker hand earns money and removes those cards from the board; three of a kind is the lowest hand accepted. A round is cleared by reaching a money target, set by the difficulty, before the deck runs out, and every extra card beyond the deck costs $50. Stacking cards six high also ends the game. The single-player game has ten levels of rising speed, a limited 99-second freeze lets the player study the board, and a two-player VS. mode has players take turns trying to take points from each other.

t_09a0778fb8cd.overview: Set in Shelldorado, a world where humans live alongside kaiju, creatures that carry shells on their backs, this role-playing game from developer Birthday follows a quest to defeat the demon king Fat Badger. The hero Rikki, a boy who bears the fire shell, must reunite with three kaiju companions, Kupikupi, Poyon and Bub, who each begin the adventure in a different place; a command switches control between them until they join together as a party, and some combinations unlock combined magic. Battles are turn-based, with the side that acts first decided at random each turn, and guarding makes companions shut themselves inside their shells to greatly reduce damage. Chess-like encounters on an eight-by-eight grid trigger one-on-one fights when pieces collide, and each character has a special skill, such as saving anywhere.

t_09bfeef1f826.overview: Seven pinball tables and four game modes make up this pinball collection for one to four players. Regular pinball plays like a traditional machine, with points earned in the upper area, and hides a Pac-Man theme room. In nineball, money is wagered and nine balls are knocked into a Bingo pattern. Battle pinball works more like Pong, with a player and opponent chosen from six characters, specialized flippers and ball, and thunder, bomber and attack variants; in bomber, the ball explodes after a time limit. The sports mode turns the table into a soccer or ice hockey field. Guest characters include Valkyrie, Wonder Momo and Kai, and the table can be shaken left and right to move the ball.

t_0a1186f2bcff.overview: Thirty levels of vertical shooting put the player in control of the robotic aircraft FX-1, which collects weapon parts called wings to fight through each level and destroy the Gobunasu boss waiting at its end. Without a wing equipped, the second button drops the craft to a lower ground level where airborne attacks cannot reach it, though ground units and obstacles still can, and it returns to the air after a while. Wings attach to the ship's sides, each with its own firing pattern, and can be ejected or damaged until they break away. The Famicom version adds the Hammer, Dyna and Fire wings, three hidden special weapons, rapid fire, warps and hidden items such as Voltage and Comet, along with an ending screen. No story is given.

t_0a40e4bff8f2.overview: Set in Japan's Sengoku period, this historical simulation opens in 1555 with the player choosing a warlord from among the Sengoku daimyo and distributing his ability points, a choice that also sets the difficulty. Each year runs through phases of battle, domestic affairs, movement and political maneuvering. Seasons restrict marching and fighting in cold regions, and random events such as famine, bumper harvests and typhoons affect tax income. Unification is the aim, though not by force alone, as a court rank system and subordination between daimyo shape the campaign. Officers' abilities are hidden. Fights take place in the field and, if the defender loses, become castle sieges decided by troop strength and collapsing morale, with only broad orders given. At a fixed year the player's daimyo dies of natural causes, ending the game.

t_0b0c7026cc4d.overview: Based on a manga license, this fishing simulation centers on a timed contest in which Sanpei has a limited amount of time to catch the largest blue marlin of all the competitors. Each outing begins on a map of the sea, where promising areas are marked with large fish icons; time passes more quickly on this screen, so a spot has to be chosen fast. Once in position, the player picks the right kind of bait for hooking billfish and waits for a bite. Landing a fish means using the gauge above the screen to maneuver and reel in the line, and every catch is judged on its size before play resumes and the hunt for a bigger marlin continues.

t_0b640caba299.overview: Peace has returned to the Central Continent after the long war with the Zenebas Empire, until a distress signal from Valesia goes silent under unexplained jamming. A private of the Helic Republic army stationed in Darios is ordered to investigate aboard an Alozaurer, the Republic's newest medium Zoid. Rather than liberating occupied cities as in the first game, the player visits friendly towns, defeats enemies to earn money and upgrades equipment, clearing caves and enemy fortresses as the story advances. Enemies appear through random encounters. Each battle opens with a screen offering enemy data and the choice to fight, flee or use items, followed by real-time shooting from a fixed position against a pair of identical enemies. Rewards are deposited in a bank account that can only be drawn on in towns with a bank, and some Zoids can launch scout aircraft to map nearby areas.

t_0b7fb9c1b736.overview: Supervised by political scientist Masuzoe Youichi, this text adventure casts the player as a businessman racing between meetings, negotiations and dinners to make his company's major project succeed. The hero, a sales section chief at a trading company, inherits responsibility for the project when his department head suddenly falls ill, and is drawn into a power struggle between the chairman's faction and the president's faction. The story unfolds over four chapters, each followed by a quiz of 20 business questions. At the end, the number of correct answers out of 60 is announced and Masuzoe himself comments on the result, sometimes scolding a poor score. Text appears in large characters that include kanji to keep it easy to read.

t_0b8978161d6c.overview: Loosely recreating the plot of the television drama, this action game sends the three Kazama sisters, Yui, Yuka and Yuma, against Kage, a dark group plotting to rule Japan. The player switches between the sisters as each situation demands. Yui is the attacker, with weapons that progress from a yo-yo to a heavy-alloy yo-yo and finally to the only weapon able to defeat the last boss. Yuka handles defense and support with paper cranes and then marbles, and knows the most ninjutsu. Yuma is balanced, fighting with a lilian stick and later a chain ball, and alone can clear dark caves and pass electrified fences. Defeating enemies earns experience, raising levels and teaching new ninjutsu. The adventure covers five stages, and a password lets the single player resume later.

t_0bc07a8d8805.overview:
Set across castles located in different parts of the world, 8 Eyes tasks the player with clearing eight levels ruled by dukes to recover the 8 Eyes jewels. The player picks which of the first seven castles to enter, but they must be cleared in a certain order. Finishing a level awards Orin a new sword, and every castle boss has a vulnerability to a specific blade. Seven scrolls hidden in those stages hold hints for placing the jewels. Once those seven areas are beaten, the Castle of Ruth unlocks as the final stage, leading to the return of the recovered jewels to the Altar of Peace in a specific sequence.

Controlling both Orin and Cutrus simultaneously is required in single-player mode, with limited commands available for the companion. Alternatively, two participants can join in a cooperative mode where one person directs Orin and the second operates Cutrus.

t_0c0af76e36a1.overview:
Taking control of the hero Orpheus, the player travels through ancient Greece across side-scrolling environments featuring light platforming and combat. The journey requires fighting through mythological creatures such as the Minotaur, cyclops, and Cerberus to reach Tartarus, defeat Hades in a two-stage encounter, and rescue his lover Helene. A top-down overview displays eight different locations, beginning in Arcadia, where players explore city-states and dungeons in a somewhat non-linear fashion.

Progression involves meeting Greek gods in their temples to receive important items. Beginning with a simple club, Orpheus gathers swords, shields, and other equipment, while ambrosia raises his maximum stamina. Available equipment includes the Staff of Fennel, which can emit the fire of Prometheus at distant enemies, and the Divine Sword, which shoots the power of Argus in a straight line. Players also acquire special items like the Sandals of Hermes and the Harp of Apollo, which lets Orpheus fly on Pegasus when played at the Monolith of the Sun.

t_0c158e666fe0.overview: Sometime in the year 20XX, a pilot is assigned to defend the Earth from an evil nation's global revolution in this horizontally scrolling shooter. The mission is to infiltrate the enemy base, take out its defenses and army, and then kill its leader. Opposition includes battle stations, groups of aircraft, barriers, cargo planes and mechs. The player's flying craft can pick up a mech attachment item that turns it into a mech, which carries heavier firepower but presents a larger target. Instead of a conventional life bar, an energy counter rises with each hit, and the game ends if it reaches 99. The campaign runs through 25 areas on one of four difficulty levels, for a single player.

t_0c3914a64bca.overview: Set in the Hanazono area, this brawling action RPG takes place several months after Kunio, the boss of Nekketsu High School, rescued his friends from a criminal organization. Since the Double Dragon brothers transferred in, the elite Reihou Academy has been seizing control of neighboring schools, and Riki's girlfriend Mami has been taken there. Kunio and Riki head for the academy, fighting student gangs on the way. Defeated enemies drop money, which is spent in enemy-free shopping streets on items that raise stats, and books bought at the bookstore unlock special techniques. Wooden swords, stones and tires can be picked up and used as weapons. If the party is wiped out, half the money is lost. There is no save feature, but a password restores stats. One player or two players at once can take part.

t_0c539afc3348.overview: Poker against a computer-controlled girl is the core of Idea-Tek's 1990 card game, sold in Taiwan under a title meaning 'Poker Wizard'. Before a game starts, the player chooses which girl to play against; unlike later versions, this edition does not give the girls names. Hands follow standard poker: five cards are dealt, the player may give up or bet, trade selected cards for new ones, and then bet a second time. Winning earns reward pictures of the opponent, and the cartridge is classed as an adult game. The design was later modified and released in Japan as AV Poker and in the USA as Peek-A-Boo Poker, both with completely reworked reward sequences, more images and far more suggestive pictures than the original.

t_0c65ba2fcb5d.overview: Two penguins in love, Gurin and Malon, are kept apart by a wall in this top-down puzzle game from Hudson Soft. The player steers both at once, but they move as mirror images of each other, so a step that helps one may hinder the other. Each level is a 10-by-15 grid of maze walls, and the goal is to bring the pair together at the upper central cell, which holds a caged heart, while a timer adds pressure. Spiders, birds and other creatures stand in the way and can be attacked with the penguins' spray. Cobwebs can trap either penguin, leaving it helpless until the other crosses over and frees it with its spraycan. The Famicom version has 99 levels.

t_0cefde76d4ca.overview: Long ago, before humans appeared in the Ghoul Realm, the Black Light suddenly destroys the home of Firebrand, a young gargoyle warrior from the town of Etruria. Told to hurry to King Morock, Firebrand sets off on a journey to unravel the mystery of the Black Light. The adventure alternates between an overhead map view, on which Firebrand moves in the four cardinal directions along semi-linear paths, and side-scrolling action areas that take place in dungeons, across giant pits and elsewhere. His wings let him glide horizontally in mid-air, and one of his staple abilities is clinging to walls to climb vertical cliffs. New powers extend his abilities along the way; the Magic Tornado, for example, allows him to raise himself into the air.

t_0d0fe9b6dd7c.overview: Mario takes to the links in a golf game played over a series of international courses. Each shot is set up from a bird's-eye view, where the club, direction and range are chosen, before the view shifts behind the golfer and timed presses on a power meter set the strength and type of the stroke; wind and ball spin affect where it lands. Only the Japan course is open at first, and clearing it in single-player stroke play unlocks Australia, then France, Hawaii and finally the UK course, each ending the round early once the score passes a stricter limit over par. An Extra course mixes previously played holes at random. A second player controls Luigi, who also appears as a match-play opponent, and Princess Toadstool serves as the caddie.

t_0d2be9fc443d.overview: A sequel in a series of Go study cartridges, Igo Shinan '91 lets players watch celebrated professional games replayed automatically or advance through them move by move. Its library of game records grows to 110, sorted into four categories: 30 classical games, 20 early modern games, 40 modern games and 20 handicap games, with the early modern category new to this edition. A playing-strength assessment is included as in the series' first release, although the beginner-level test has been dropped, leaving intermediate and advanced tests.

t_0d33d6caf61a.overview:
Magic Darts simulates traditional dart games for up to four participants. Competitors select from a roster of characters, input three initials, and choose light, medium, or heavy dart weights. Executing a shot requires adjusting the starting position, stopping an indicator to choose the dart curve, and timing moving gauges to set the aiming angle and throwing power. Upon release, throws display through both two-dimensional and three-dimensional views.

Six game modes are available. The 301, 501, and 701 modes challenge players to reduce their starting total to zero without busting, using customizable rules that dictate whether matches require standard or double-ring hits to open and close. Count Up awards victory to the highest score across eight sets of darts, Round the Clock requires hitting numbers one through ten in consecutive sequence, and Half It penalizes failures on assigned board targets by halving point totals.

t_0d5f5973a76b.overview: A secret monk of Mount Hiei who carries the blood of Fudō Myōō sets out to rescue the shrine maiden Sayo, kidnapped by Kuro Okina, a man scheming to rule the land. This side-view action game gives one button to the sword and another to projectiles. The hero's sword, the Shichishitō, grows longer after each stage boss falls, ranged weapons are picked from a selection of items, enemies drop items that take effect automatically, and ninja scrolls grant temporary powers. There is no life gauge, so a single enemy hit costs a life, though a substitute item can absorb a miss. The quest covers four stages divided into 13 areas, with bosses such as Hannya and Yukionna before the final battle in Yomi. Progress is kept with passwords. The overseas release, Demon Sword, restructured the stages and added a life meter.

t_0d8df0a99a5c.overview: On Ripple Island, humans and animals live together in peace until a gigantic frog who calls himself the emperor of darkness appears and kidnaps the daughter of King Dotella. The king promises that whoever rescues the princess may marry her, and a young boy named Kyle sets off on a long journey to bring her home. Rather than a murder mystery, Sunsoft's adventure is a peaceful, storybook fantasy in which small humans and friendly animals such as raccoons and rabbits coexist. Progress is driven by commands: the player chooses among five actions, look, take, enter, hit and push, to examine scenes, deal with the characters met along the way and work toward the ending.

t_0d90f60d9217.overview: Instead of fixed rosters, this arcade-style softball game builds every team through a schoolyard-pick draft. With the exception of the Amazons, there are no set teams; before each game, ten players are chosen from a large pool of characters that includes animals, celebrities and other offbeat figures. Each character has different attributes, so some are very slow, some pitch in unusual ways and some can even fly. Two modes are available: two-player exhibition games and a single-player tournament. The tournament requires beating five other teams, one at each of five neighborhood-style parks, before a final game at a sixth park against the all-girls final boss team, the Amazons.

t_0df2b13e90e8.overview: In 2062, after humans have colonized the Moon and established several space stations, Tadashi, a heavy machines operator based on Earth, buys a worker mech with his girlfriend Elina and discovers it is actually a Metal Slader, a military grade mech from a war eight years earlier. Its memory holds a secret message saying Earth is in danger. Tadashi, Elina and his younger sister Azusa fly to the space stations and colonies near Earth and the Moon to investigate the machine's origins. As Tadashi, the player talks with other characters to advance the story, often choosing what to do or say, and some choices can end in a game over. Resting at certain points provides a password for returning to that point later.

t_0e113dbef9d7.overview: Two cavemen, the green-haired Joe and the blue-haired Mac, battle through prehistoric levels to rescue a group of women who were kidnapped by a rival tribe of cavemen. Along the way they use weapons such as boomerangs, bones, fire, flints, electricity, stone wheels and clubs against the enemies in their path. Health drains steadily over a period of time, except during boss battles, which keeps the side-scrolling platform action moving. This NES version, developed by Elite Systems as a conversion of the Data East arcade game, lacks the option of choosing levels or endings that the arcade release offers, and its bosses are variants of the arcade boss.

t_0e470c309ff0.overview: Lucia, a magic-wielding warrior of the Rameru clan, sets out to stop Darutos, a Rameru descendant who used the power of the Wing of Madoola to build a demonic fortress and summon demons to conquer the world. The adventure is a side-scrolling action-platform game with role-playing elements. Lucia can jump, climb ladders, crouch, attack with her sword and use magic, and there are six types of magical attacks, ranging from flame swords to flash magic. Collectibles include swords that increase attack strength, health jars and spell books. Play is for a single player. This edition is a modern re-release of the 1986 Family Computer game originally published by Sunsoft.

t_0e85bc737b05.overview: Rather than offering a single fixed adventure, the cartridge is a tool for building and playing 3D dungeon role-playing games. In edit mode, a fantasy or science fiction style is chosen first, then dungeons of up to eight floors are drawn by placing walls and doors on a grid, along with treasure chests, stairs, fixed enemies and messages. Item and spell names and effects, enemy parameters and spells, shop wares, and opening and ending text can all be defined, while graphics are picked from a preset selection. In play mode, a three-member party sets out from a home town to conquer the dungeon, fighting through a command-based system in which characters ram enemies to attack. Creations are saved automatically to battery-backed memory, and a sample scenario sends a young prince to defeat a sorcerer.

t_0e8e01741d4e.overview: Licensed by Japan's professional baseball organization, this baseball game uses the official names of the 12 Japanese teams and their players. The Tokyo Dome, which had opened shortly before release, is depicted under its actual name and makes a showy appearance on the opening screen. Pitching relies on the directional pad: fastballs are given changes of pace by rapidly tapping up and down, while the break on curveballs is set by how many times left or right is pressed. Batting works somewhat like a golf game, with the batter moving a batting point to read the course of the incoming pitch.

t_0ea5e21d87e0.overview: Waixing's 1998 adaptation of Heroes of Might & Magic, also known as M&M Heroes, carries the turn-based fantasy game over with all of its text in Chinese. Set in a medieval fantasy world filled with creatures from myth and legend, it has the player lead generals called heroes at the head of armies of troops, with exploring, attacking, defeating and acquiring as the basic principles. The ultimate goal is usually to capture all enemy castles and defeat all enemy heroes. The port retains most of the gameplay elements of the PC version but simplifies the graphics heavily: the hexagons of the battlefield cannot be seen, although the units are fully animated.

t_0efdf992be91.overview: Building on Best Play Pro Yakyuu II, the '90 edition switches to real player names, and its package carries a sticker marking the latest data officially approved by Nippon Professional Baseball. As before, the player serves as a team manager through a pennant race, sending in pinch hitters and relievers and giving signs such as steals and defensive shifts, while player names and ratings remain open to editing. Extra innings can now be set to run as long as 18 innings, and a Japan Series can be played between any chosen Central League and Pacific League teams. Passed balls by the catcher, which earlier occurred even with the bases empty, are now reproduced only when runners are on base.

t_0f03f6332787.overview: Proto Man apparently leads an army of robots in a series of destructive attacks on the world and even kidnaps his own creator, the genius scientist Dr. Light. Mega Man sets out to stop the rampage, battling eight Robot Masters: Star Man, Gravity Man, Gyro Man, Stone Man, Crystal Man, Charge Man, Napalm Man and Wave Man. The real culprit turns out to be Dr. Wily, who created Dark Man to frame Proto Man for his robots' crimes. Mega Man's charged shots have been upgraded to cover a wider area. Hidden across the stages are eight collectible letters, and finding all of them unlocks Beat, a robotic bird that serves as a weapon.

t_0f75d1e060b6.overview:
A password feature allows play to resume at a later level. The storyline involves aliens seizing control of a robot-manufacturing planet and reprogramming its robots for war. Players control Low-G-Man, whose jump grows higher as anti-gravity material capsules are collected, from about three-quarters of a screen at the start to about one and three-quarter screens with three capsules. Defeating enemies without freezing them first yields items far more often.

Standard combat relies on the Electro-Magnetic Disruptor Pistol, which freezes targets. Once adversaries are immobilized, the player attacks them from above or below using an extending spear. Additional available weapons comprise fireballs, boomerangs, waves, and bombs. Some enemy vehicles, the Walker, Spider, and Hover, can be captured by freezing them and stabbing the robot driver.

t_0f768f3b28fb.overview: Ki, a priestess, is sent by the goddess Ishtar into a tower to retrieve the Blue Crystal Rod. Ishtar gives her a golden tiara that enables the power of flight, and the dragon Quox helps her during the climb. Ki carries no weapons; her only abilities are to dash and jump, and as long as the jump button is held she keeps rising into the air. Striking a ceiling or dashing into a wall makes her drop to the ground and leaves her stunned for several seconds, and any contact with enemies such as slimes, ghosts and wizards results in death. In each level, the goal is to pick up a key and open the door leading to the next area. Treasure chests hold items whose effects last only on the floor where they were found.

t_0f7d3b166b81.overview: A giant tengu mask flies across the sea to America in this side-scrolling shooter. In 199X, an unknown planet approaching America becomes an evil life-form that turns people into mindless undead, and the prayers of the survivors reach a tengu, who creates a great mask with his spiritual power and sends it to restore freedom. The mask moves with a peculiar inertia and attacks air and ground targets at once with eyeballs and spit. Falling humans crying for help are the only power-up: every five rescued strengthens the shot, and fifteen supplies a bomb that wipes out the screen. Eight tengu faces form the life gauge, which recovers with score, while lasers and lightning bolts can drain all but one unit at a touch. Rounds one to four can be started in any order before the final round.

t_101f18e53a33.overview: Kenshiro fights through side-scrolling stages in this action game, battling crowds of thugs and the boss waiting at the end of each stage. He can punch, kick, jump and crouch, and his jump has a distinctive height and speed. Landing several punches on an ordinary enemy strikes a pressure point and makes the foe burst. Red thugs drop the word "abeshi," and collecting it raises his power through up to seven levels. Bosses include Heart, Shin, Jagi and Souther, who attack with body-slam rushes, energy waves, gunfire and three-way vacuum waves, while Raoh stands as the final and strongest opponent. A hit counter and an energy meter track the fight, and the game is for one player.

t_109a21225045.overview: Set in the Three Kingdoms era, this unlicensed Famicom release is a turn-based tactical role-playing game in which a party of generals and civil officials fights across battle maps. Each character may act once per turn, choosing to attack, move, rest or use a skill, and since there are no magic points, skills cost nothing to use. Twenty-five classes are split into infantry, cavalry, archer and civil official lines. Promotion happens automatically once a character's accumulated experience reaches a threshold, and some promotions offer a choice of branch, such as a defensive or an offensive infantry path. Cavalry units cover more ground, archer classes attack through long-range skills, and civil officials learn healing, freezing, fire and other spells, culminating in an ultimate strategist class.

t_10a03356f6b8.overview: A lone soldier must slip into an enemy POW camp, rescue an important prisoner and escape within 24 hours of game time, about five real-time minutes. Trenches and barbed wire give the battlefield a First World War flavor. The hero carries a machine gun and a knife and can also take down enemy soldiers by ramming into them, while gunfire, drowning, land mines and being run over by a tank all cost lives. Tools are essential: TNT and fuses blow up facilities, clippers cut barbed wire, mines work against tanks and troops, and a ladder scales a wall in the fourth stage. Picking up a key and exiting at the right edge of the map clears a stage, and the five stages loop endlessly. Game A is the basic game, Game B adds constant missile fire at the player, and the two-player mode lets a second player steer the missiles, which can destroy enemy soldiers but also harm the first player.

t_10aaf4bc0276.overview: Adapted from the Shounen Ashibe manga, this command-selection adventure follows young Ashibe, who remembers his friend Sugao, now living in Nepal, and becomes determined to visit him. The story unfolds over three chapters, beginning with a search for his baby seal Goma-chan, who has wandered off at the very start. Play consists of choosing commands such as talk, examine, take, items and move, visiting locations and interacting with a large cast of characters from the original work, each drawn with expressive portraits. Simple minigames, including a coin toss and a quiz, break up the conversations. The long road to Nepal has Ashibe dredging a ditch, working a part-time job, getting caught up in an airplane's emergency landing and heading into a jungle. A diary from a teacher allows saving anywhere, in a single slot.

t_10ca6b911e77.overview: A parody of the Castlevania series, the Famicom platformer stars Kid Dracula, son of Dracula, who wakes from a 10,000-year sleep and leaves his castle to defeat the demon king Galamoth, who has conquered the world. Kid Dracula fires shots at enemies and can charge them for special attacks, gaining a new one after each of the first five stages: homing shots, explosive shots, a bat form for flight, freezing shots that turn enemies into platforms, and the power to walk on the ceiling. Coins earned by defeating enemies with charged shots can be spent on bonus games at the end of a stage, and mini games such as roulette and knife throwing can award extra lives. The nine stages range from the castle to the sky, underwater, ice, a pyramid and a space elevator, and passwords allow restarts from later stages.

t_10e565465e91.overview: Australian rules football is played from a third-person perspective with the basic actions of a real player: kicking and handballing the ball, marking it, and tackling an opponent in possession. One player can face a computer team, or two players can go head to head. A goal is worth six points and a behind one. Close to the goal an accuracy bar appears, and the nearer the marker is to its center when the ball is kicked, the more accurate the shot. Bounces, ball-ups and boundary throw-ins are contested by tapping the ball to a teammate or knocking it farther away. Alongside single matches there is a kick-to-kick mode and a season mode for one, four or six players that finishes with a grand final. Teams are based on 14 of the 15 clubs of the 1991 AFL season, plus fictional sides from Darwin, Canberra and Hobart.

t_10ed490a4ceb.overview:
A terrorist organization called the Sinister Seven has abducted both a prominent scientist and IMF operative Shannon Reed. Tasked with solving this kidnapping case, the IMF team tracks their targets from the canals of Venice to the Swiss Alps, working through six areas to rescue the captives.

From a top-down view, the player directs three IMF operatives named Max, Grant, and Nicholas. Because each operative possesses different skills required to finish the mission, the player can pause and swap between them in the normal scrolling areas. Discretion remains critical throughout the mission. Harming civilians on the street gets the agent detained by a police helicopter, while being spotted by surveillance cameras inside enemy hideouts gets the agent locked up.

t_110e7a2c0b20.overview: Super-deformed heroes from tokusatsu and robot anime share the stage in this side-view action game from the crossover series that brings together Ultraman, Kamen Rider and Gundam. Three heroes are playable: Kamen Rider Black RX, Nu Gundam and Ultraman Taro. Attacks are limited to close-range moves such as punches and kicks, though power-up items grant ranged attacks for a limited time. Stages are crossed like obstacle courses, with enemies confronted one at a time, and each stage is cleared by defeating the enemy's commander. A distinguishing trait is the absence of weak foes that fall to a single hit. Play is for one player and is governed by a health meter.

t_11196d5183ab.overview:
Master Higgins ventures to an island in the South Pacific after hearing that the Evil Witch Doctor has kidnapped Princess Tina, and 32 stages of side-scrolling platform action stand between him and her rescue. Touching an enemy, an enemy's attack or a fire costs a life, as does falling into a pit or water. A health gauge starts out with 11 points, and picking up fruit or a milk bottle restores it.

Higgins has no way to attack until he grabs a stone axe. Finding a bee-like fairy known as Honey Girl grants about ten seconds of invincibility, while the eggplant drains his life meter instead of helping. Each confrontation with the Evil Witch Doctor can show him with a different head, chosen from up to eight types.

t_111d0cdebd74.overview:
Rescuing Princess Eleanor and defeating Morbius requires gathering six pieces of the Staff of Demnos. Controlling the wizard Shadax from an isometric perspective, the player traverses a non-linear network of more than 250 rooms inside the fortress of Kâstleröck. Shadax can jump, lift, and drop objects to solve puzzles, navigate hazards like floor spikes, and evade hostile creatures. Boots found along the way increase jumping height, while hovering crystal balls and movable blocks serve as platforms to cross dangerous areas.

Potions stored in beakers can freeze time, grant temporary invincibility, eliminate moving objects, or reveal invisible items. Progress through the stronghold also involves detonating bombs, passing through portals, and finding magic keys. Scattered blue hats provide extra lives, while coins allow continuing from a specific room. A map screen tracks discovered rooms and exits alongside an inventory displaying completion statistics.

t_115d2d99532a.overview:
Players control Mario as falling enemies drop into four vertical columns to piece together eggshells and free trapped Yoshis. Operating beneath the play field, Mario swaps pairs of adjacent columns to align incoming creatures with matching monsters atop existing stacks, clearing them from the board. Each column holds up to eight items before surpassing the boundary line, which causes a game over. Catching enemies between the lower and upper halves of an eggshell encases the creatures and hatches a Yoshi, yielding larger bonuses based on the amount enclosed.

Two single-player options provide distinct goals: A-Type continues indefinitely until a loss occurs, while B-Type tasks players with clearing the entire screen across rounds featuring larger starting piles. A competitive two-player mode features simultaneous play on separate fields, with a second participant controlling Luigi. Each round ends when one contestant empties their field or the opponent tops out, and the first player to win three rounds takes the match.

t_11737cd9240d.overview: Set in 2040 on the island 8-JO, where the computer Kyron-5 has come back to life after the events of the Gunhed film, this Varie tie-in is a tactical strategy game about destroying Kyron-5 and seizing the island's Texmexium. Alongside a Gunhed of the same type as the film's unit 507, the player commands new variants designed by Shoji Kawamori: the reconnaissance Search Head, the fire-support Command Head and the mass-produced Assault Head. Mecha units are built from spare and scavenged parts, and the island's defense forces must be defeated. Battles against the Aerobot bosses switch to a shooting sequence.

t_11f7530aed46.overview: Drawn from the Nansou Satomi Hakkenden tale of eight half-brother samurai descended from a dog, this traditional role-playing game is based specifically on the 1983 live-action film, itself adapted from a 1982 reworking of the novel. The brothers' adventures range across Sengoku period Japan. Play can begin as any one of the eight samurai, each starting in a different location, and the goal is for the chosen hero to meet and recruit the others until all eight form a single group. Otherwise the structure follows genre convention: time is split between exploring towns and talking to townspeople, and fighting monsters and enemy soldiers in dungeons and on the overworld map through turn-based combat. Micronics developed the game for Toei Animation.

t_11fc2d6a4adc.overview: Detective Jinguji Saburo's fourth case is a command-selection adventure. On a hot summer afternoon in Shinjuku Central Park, Jinguji comes across a dog, and the encounter brings back a case from one year earlier: a request to find a stolen painting. What seemed an easy job turns out to hide a web of complicated human relationships. As in the previous entry, the story is split between parts played as Jinguji and parts played as his assistant Yoko, with scenes set in the past shown in sepia tones and present-day scenes in full color. Because the cartridge has no battery backup, a password is needed to continue; it is only four characters long, but play resumes from the start of the current part rather than from where the password was given.

t_123075a0ef93.overview: Released to celebrate the 25th anniversary of Super Mario Bros., this edition presents the original side-scrolling platformer with several graphical changes, most visibly "?" blocks that carry the number 25. Mario explores the Mushroom Kingdom to defeat Bowser and rescue Princess Toadstool, while his brother Luigi is controlled by the second player in multiplayer mode. The adventure spans eight worlds, each with four sub-levels or stages. A Super Mushroom makes Mario grow to double his size, the Fire Flower found in certain "?" blocks adds a fireball attack, and the less common Starman briefly protects him from minor dangers. The edition first appeared preinstalled on a special red variant of the Wii.

t_1256caf793f5.overview: Jajamaru sets out to rescue Princess Sakura, kidnapped by Namazu Dayuu, in a follow-up that trades the vertically oriented levels of the first game for side-scrolling stages. The screen scrolls only to the right with no turning back, and instead of defeating every enemy, a scene is cleared by reaching the exit at the far right end. Certain blocks can be destroyed by jumping into them, hiding coins, bombs or, on rare occasions, the hero's faithful frog. One item turns Jajamaru invisible and invincible for a set time, letting him pass through enemies and their attacks. Each stage ends with a fight against a boss monster in the forest, and Namazu Dayuu himself appears in a large form every ten scenes.

t_128b7624b3d5.overview:
Stopping the crime baron Cain from spreading a deadly new chemical called Nuke is the primary mission facing Detroit's cyborg officer. The title supports one or two participants, with two players taking alternating turns upon losing a life or completing a level.

Controlling the titular law enforcement officer, the player navigates through industrial and corporate environments centered around side-scrolling platforming and shooting mechanics. Progress requires walking, jumping, and shooting or punching while managing the officer's inertia. Along with battling Cain's hostile forces, the player must destroy at least sixty percent of the Nuke on each level and make physical contact to arrest at least sixty percent of designated criminals before facing Cain and the new RoboCop 2 prototype.

t_12adc09fa780.overview: A girl living in the year 2100 takes on danger inside Ropit, a large robot suit, in this side-scrolling action game developed by Micronics. A single hit breaks the suit down and dumps her out, leaving the player in control of the little girl on foot. She cannot shoot enemies, and she dies after 30 seconds unless the robot is restored, which requires special items. One more hit while outside the suit costs a life. The game must be played through twice to see the true ending, and its on-screen text is in English.

t_137daf035995.overview: Characters from the girls' manga magazine Nakayoshi come together in this role-playing game from Yutaka, a Bandai affiliate. The adventure moves through the worlds of series running in the magazine at the time, in order: Kingyo Chuuihou!, Pocket Park, Minmin!, Taiyou ni Smash!, Kurumi to Shichinin no Kobito-tachi and Bishoujo Senshi Sailor Moon. Some characters have dedicated graphics, and each series' manga artist also appears with a face portrait. Aimed at young girls, the system is simplified compared with typical role-playing games, with no experience points or equipment, and a full playthrough takes only a few hours. Battles skip command menus altogether: rotating pictures are stopped like a slot machine, and the matching images decide the action taken.

t_13c79d833265.overview: An expanded version of the Famicom programming cartridge rather than a game, V3 runs a dialect of BASIC enhanced for game development. Program memory grows to 4,086 bytes, held in SRAM inside the cartridge that can be kept alive by battery backup. The language offers commands for sprites, animation, backgrounds, musical sequences and gamepads, and predefined characters can be combined to build sprite characters and background art with little effort; the interpreter only supports integers. Four sample games are stored in the cartridge and can be loaded into memory with a BASIC command or, by default, with the F1 to F4 function keys. Programs can be saved to and loaded from cassette tape.

t_13c9ac5b2e38.overview: Roller derby provides the setting for this Jaleco project, developed by Sculptured Software and cancelled before its planned 1991 debut. Team-based racing is paired with hand-to-hand combat: skaters battle opponents as they race around an indoor track, and the action pauses occasionally for close-up fight sequences in the style of Blades of Steel.
