Play consists of skating to the left and attacking opponents while jumping over grooved floor sections. Starting in the second period of each match, ramps, floor hazards and other traps are added. The crowd can also interfere, as a thrown bottle or bomb can hit a skater and knock them out for a few seconds. Brawling and in-game cutscenes break up the racing, and there is no background music.

t_13d6299e796c.overview: Based on the novel Suikoden, this historical simulation takes place in ancient China during the reign of Emperor Huizong of the Song Dynasty, an empire composed of 49 prefectures. Rather than conquering the whole map, the goal is to bring down Gao Qiu, the corrupt minister at court. The player picks a hero, recruits followers and takes territory, and must build up sufficient popularity to gain the attention of the emperor, who then issues an edict authorizing the campaign against Gao Qiu. Each turn represents one month, battles are fought on hex maps where the seasons alter terrain effects, and characters carry attributes such as strength, dexterity and wisdom. Time is limited: Gao Qiu must be captured before the Jurchen invasion in January 1127. Up to seven players can compete.

t_13f63bda3681.overview: Based on Masanori Morita's manga, Bandai's Famicom adaptation, developed by Tose, centers on Taison Maeda, a delinquent student of Teiken High School who wants to become the world boxing champion. Three other characters are also playable, each with a storyline of their own, and most of the action takes place at the high school. Although an overworld map is used, the player does not walk around it; a menu at the bottom of the screen selects where the character goes. Progress depends on winning fights, and each victory leads to new areas. Battles work like those of a standard role-playing game but are presented as cutscenes. A battery backup saves progress.

t_143a9648981d.overview: A slot-machine spin-off of the Pachio-kun series sends its hero to the casino islands around Manhattan with $1,000, of which $900 goes on the fare to the first island. Starting in Brooklyn and moving on through Queens, the Bronx, Manhattan and New Jersey, he must win each island's clearing sum, from $10,000 up to $100,000,000, before traveling onward, and finally find and beat Capone, the boss of the islands, whose hired gamblers and slot fiends lie in wait. Islands are explored on a map with events and items, a passport is needed to enter the casinos, and cash is exchanged for tokens at the bank. Five types of slot machine are available, including Pachi Slot, whose reels the player stops by hand. Progress is kept with a 40-character password, and a separate simulation mode allows free play at the machines.

t_1456228c80ec.overview: Cony Soft's unlicensed Famicom port of the fighting game Fatal Fury 2 was released under both the Japanese name, Garou Densetsu 2, and the Western one. Despite the name, it plays more like Street Fighter II, with no Pow bar and none of the original's AI-only characters. Depending on the version, the roster has five or six fighters, each with a named recolor: Terry Bogard, Andy Bogard, Mai Shiranui, Kim Kaphwan, Cheng Sinzan and Lawrence Blood, who is missing from some releases. Graphics and music are taken from the original game and simplified, the HUD changes color between stages, and the clone characters' stages are recolors of the regular ones. In a two-player game both players can pick the same character, and the ending is a simple credits screen.

t_147f729b59c9.overview: A hacked variant of the platformer Gardman, Wonder Rabbit is built around switching between five different characters, each with their own unique ability, in order to pass obstacles. This version is best known from the many dreamGEAR plug and play units that carry it. Gardman itself is not the original form of the game either: graphics data inside Wonder Rabbit show that the game originally starred Pokémon characters, a version that has never been found.

t_14dbc56424e7.overview: A Korean one-on-one fighting game, The General's Son borrows its name from the Korean gangster movie of the same name, which follows Kim Du-han, a street fighter in Jongno who learns that he is the son of General Kim Jwa-jin. The cartridge has little to do with the film beyond the license, however: it is a typical one-on-one fighter that takes strong inspiration from Street Fighter II, with two combatants trading blows in each match. Because the developers could not match the tight controls of that model, the moveset was deliberately simplified. Controls are very simple, and a special move is performed by holding down the A and B buttons together for about a second.

t_153df8395726.overview: Adapted from the 1987 film, this adventure was supervised by the film's director, Juzo Itami. Tax office investigator Ryōko Itakura begins by auditing a pachinko parlor and uncovers not only its owner's hidden deposits but a tax evasion manual circulating through the town, with gangsters and a larger evasion ring behind it. Without the authority to force searches, she is later promoted to the regional taxation bureau's investigation division, known as Marusa, and turns her attention to Hideki Gondō, a man whose finances had escaped her earlier inquiry because of gang interference. Play moves between three layers: a regional map traveled by train, overhead town maps, and command-driven investigations inside buildings. Many characters come from the film, though several details of the story differ.

t_1554409466d6.overview: Set in the Chinese era of the Three Kingdoms, this one-on-one fighter was developed by ASDER and published by NTDEC on the same engine as Fighting Hero III. Six warriors are selectable from the start: Guan Yu, Zhang Fei, Huang Zhong, Cao Ren, Mei Hu and Lu Bu. Fighters have a three-tiered health bar and a rage gauge that unlocks a super move once it is full. Arcade mode pits the player against all six opponents, including a clone of the chosen character, with nine continues. Conquest mode has the player pick one of two preset three-character teams and lay siege to enemy fortresses, where the extra fighters Shi Ren and Xie Seng defend before each stage's owner; capturing all three fortresses wins.

t_1555db660118.overview: The Fratelli family has escaped from prison, and Ma Fratelli has led them in capturing most of the Goonies along with a mermaid named Annie. Mikey must avoid getting caught while freeing his friends and Annie. Exploration is open and non-linear: Mikey climbs ladders and passes through doors, some of which act as warps, across a side-view platform world. Entering a door switches to a first-person mode in which rooms are searched with menu commands for items and captives. Each rescued Goonie raises Mikey's health, and all six must be found before Annie can be freed. Weapons include a yo-yo, slingshot, boomerang, bombs and molotov cocktails, while special shoes improve jumping and speed and a diving suit opens underwater areas. Passwords record progress.

t_155cc58a7838.overview: Drawn from the Venus Wars saga, this strategy game opens as the nation of Ishtar uses its powerful military to storm and occupy Io City, the capital of Aphrodia, where the combat bike unit Hound has been formed. Play takes place on a map of squares, with friendly and enemy units taking turns to move. When opposing units make contact, the battle shifts to a shooting screen, so the game combines strategic simulation with 3D shooting action. Aphrodia's side fields the Hound bikes and trailer units, while Ishtar relies on conventional weapons and tanks. The campaign is for a single player.

t_15876f13d691.overview: Set in a distant future, this role-playing adventure imagines a world where women dominate society and timid men are scorned as "otaku-chan." Society has fallen into ruin, and ferocious beasts called Shura rampage across the Earth. Unable to bear the devastation, the goddess Maya sends her personal guard, the Aurora Five Girls (Yan, Yun, Rin, Min and Run), down to the planet. Instead of helping, the five take control of the Shura and torment the otaku, who grow more servile than ever. Into this situation steps one fired-up man who sets out on a journey to show the women of the world what a real man is. The adventure is played by a single player, and its story and character designs come from well-known manga artists.

t_158bcd9a7306.overview: Loosely following the 1977 film, this single-player side-scrolling platformer follows Luke Skywalker as he travels to join the Rebellion against the Empire. Luke fights with a lightsaber and can use the Force to float, speed up or stop time, powered by diamonds called Force points that defeated enemies leave behind. At the end of each level he battles one of Darth Vader's apprentices, which changes form after the first hit, while the real Vader appears on the Death Star and Yavin IV. Rescued characters later provide hints and actions needed to progress, some through an in-game menu. Between planets Luke flies the Millennium Falcon against TIE fighters, and the finale turns the trench run into a vertically scrolling, maze-like X-wing stage with dead ends and intersections. Novice and pro difficulty settings are available.

t_15a4457b4095.overview: Shogi, the Japanese board game similar to chess, is the subject of this third installment in the instructional series presented by Tanigawa Kouji, a real-life shogi expert. Numerous tutorials are built into the cartridge to teach the game. Beyond the lessons, it offers different playing modes, including an unusual one in which a slot machine determines which piece is to be moved next rather than leaving the choice entirely to the player. Play is for a single player.

t_15dc545847a0.overview: A tongue-in-cheek parody of Gradius, this shooter plays much like that series while making its graphics and music intentionally absurd. Four playable characters are offered, Pentarou the penguin, Octopus the octopus, the Vic Viper and TwinBee, with each one carrying a different weapon configuration. Bells act as one-time power-ups, such as one that destroys every enemy on screen, and on this version a white bell grants a 1up. Compared with the arcade original, several levels are missing, among them the Japanese mountain, pachinko and cloud levels. In their place comes an entirely new level set in a carnival, with a roller coaster the character can hop into, plus a new bonus stage that leads into the interior of the Moai battleship.

t_15e159a840cd.overview: Set between the first two chapters of Ryu Hayabusa's story, this side-scrolling action game begins as CIA agent Irene Lew is chased by a man who looks like Ryu and falls to her apparent death. Framed for the killing, Ryu investigates and uncovers a scheme by Foster and a man named Clancy to create bio-noids, superhumans infused with life energy from an interdimensional rift, while the ruins of Castle Rock hide the Ancient Ship of Doom. Ryu can spring off and climb walls and can now hang from overhead pipes or ivy. Alongside the Dragon Sword and secondary weapons such as the new Vacuum Wave Art, a Dragon Spirit Sword item extends the sword's range. The first four bosses are bio-noids representing earth, wind, fire and water. Compared with the later North American release, this Japanese original has a password system and Ryu takes less damage per hit.

t_1610cd13d95e.overview: Set in 1940s Chicago, this detective adventure opens with Theodore "Ace" Harding, a retired boxer working as a private eye, waking up in a bathroom stall in Joe's Bar unable to remember who he is. A dead man is found in an upstairs office, and Ace is about to be framed for the murder. Played through a point-and-click interface rather than a text parser, the investigation involves finding addresses around the bar and taking taxi rides to other locations as Ace tries to clear his name and restore his memories. His memory and mental condition progressively deteriorate, making an antidote the first major goal; in this cartridge version the deterioration mechanic was modified to allow unlimited time. Recurring flashbacks then help in evaluating the evidence.

t_162d07604148.overview: Pairs of puyo fall into the field, where they can be rotated, moved sideways or dropped quickly. When four or more puyo join together they vanish for points, and if the puyo that drop into the gap join up again they vanish too, setting off a chain. This cartridge version is based on the earlier Famicom Disk System release by Tokuma Shoten and offers an ENDLESS mode of nonstop clearing, a MISSION mode of clearing puyo under set conditions, and a 2PLAYER mode for two human opponents. In versus play, clearing puyo sends transparent nuisance puyo onto the opponent's field in proportion to the points scored, and the two-player game adopts some elements of the later arcade and Mega Drive versions. MISSION progress is kept with passwords because the cartridge has no battery backup.

t_1681940a84b4.overview: Adapted from an animated film but given a largely original setting, this adventure follows a character from the movie who fears the nuclear war awaiting humanity in his own era and travels into the past to steer history toward peace. Progress comes from answering questions put by famous historical figures, choosing either yes or no each time. A wrong answer can send the traveler back to an earlier era or into a different history, and in the worst cases ends the game on the spot with a sudden death. Missing the time machine, called COI, or running out of its fuel also brings a game over. Several endings exist depending on how the game is played, including histories ruled by money or by force, and meeting certain conditions unlocks a true ending.

t_16b7f700cf0f.overview: Based on the Bikkuriman anime series, this traditional Japanese-style RPG opens in a world once shared by three races, the Angels, Demons and Talismans, under the protection of the Holy Goddess Nadia. After Jura, the head of the Demons, devoured one of Nadia's twin children, the other child became Super Zeus and led the Angels to victory, and Nadia split the war-torn world in two. Years later, a young hero named Yamato Ouji, raised in the world of the Angels, is sent by Super Zeus to find the other Holy Warriors, reunite the worlds and bring lasting peace to every race. Towns, dungeons and the world map are explored from a top-down view, random encounters lead to turn-based battles seen in first person, and other heroes join the party along the way.

t_16f06a46ae70.overview:
DuckTales features platforming gameplay centered on Uncle Scrooge as he searches for five lost treasures. Players guide Scrooge across five destinations located on Earth and in outer space. His cane serves as an all-purpose tool that strikes enemies, uncovers items, and propels him upward like a pogo stick to cross dangerous surfaces or reach high platforms. Scattered throughout stages are diamonds that boost Scrooge's wealth and ice cream that replenishes health. Familiar characters appear to provide clues, supply useful items, grant passage to new places, or hinder progress.

Levels can be tackled in any order, though certain locations require return visits to collect necessary items. A boss defends the treasure at the end of every destination. Once these five main valuables are acquired, players enter a final encounter, which leads to a confrontation for the ultimate prize. The concluding sequence varies based on total earnings.

t_17375e3cf5db.overview: Part adventure and part action, the story follows a schoolboy with a love of archaeology whose father was murdered when he was small. Ten years later his search for the truth reveals that the death was no ordinary killing but part of a 1,600-year feud between his family and a clan destroyed in ancient times by Yamato Takeru, a clan bent on reviving a dark god. The goal is to obtain eight holy marks and three sacred treasures while dodging traps and phantom beasts, summon a supreme being and defeat the dark god. Adventure screens use commands such as move and look, and talking to people and examining things earns knowledge points that act like experience. The game is divided into eight chapters, each closing with a side-view battle against a phantom beast, and passwords resume play by chapter.

t_173a55fe3880.overview: Trapped inside an ancient Egyptian temple, an explorer meets a goddess so low in power that she can only take the form of a large, spherical jewel, and he enters the jewel to restore her strength by clearing each level. Each level is an object-elimination puzzle on an 8x8 tiled grid. Stepping on an arrow shifts its row or column in that direction, and tiles pushed off one edge wrap around to the other side. Whenever two or more objects come into contact they are eliminated; clearing every object moves on to the next level, while a single leftover object makes the level unfinishable. On the two easier difficulty settings, optional items help: the Lightning Bolt destroys walls around the player, the Feather allows up to five free moves, and the Flash destroys every wall on the level.

t_17895dfd0b55.overview: Originally released in Japan in 1987 as Hydlide 3: The Space Memories, the action role-playing adventure returns here in a simplified cartridge adaptation. Many years after the events of Hydlide II, a giant pillar of fire rises over Fairyland, and mysterious doors, fissures in the earth and monsters appear as creatures spread throughout the world. The monks charge a lone young man with uncovering the cause and tracking down where the evil comes from. Compared with the computer original, this version streamlines the game itself and changes some of the characters who appear, and it keeps progress through battery-backed saving.

t_17d5f63a0890.overview:
Rescuing Princess Eleanor and defeating Morbius requires gathering six pieces of the Staff of Demnos. Controlling the wizard Shadax from an isometric perspective, the player traverses a non-linear network of more than 250 rooms inside the fortress of Kâstleröck. Shadax can jump, lift, and drop objects to solve puzzles, navigate hazards like floor spikes, and evade hostile creatures. Boots found along the way increase jumping height, while hovering crystal balls and movable blocks serve as platforms to cross dangerous areas.

Potions stored in beakers can freeze time, grant temporary invincibility, eliminate moving objects, or reveal invisible items. Progress through the stronghold also involves detonating bombs, passing through portals, and finding magic keys. Scattered blue hats provide extra lives, while coins allow continuing from a specific room. A map screen tracks discovered rooms and exits alongside an inventory displaying completion statistics.

t_17d8611d40f7.overview: A decadent future world is the setting for this science fiction role-playing game, centered on a giant city surrounded by a polluted sea. Minami, a boy with amnesia who was taken out of Ark City by an old man, is pursued by psychic hunts carried out with robots and bioweapons. Along the way he gathers companions: Shiba, captured in the power plant, Misa, held in the security room, and Aine, who joins in the residential district and is required to finish the game. Ark City itself is eventually revealed to be a huge spaceship. Battles offer no command to flee, so the only escape is the teleport ESP, which is unavailable early on. Progress is saved with long passwords, and the ending changes three ways depending on the hero's choices.

t_17f485a46596.overview: Two ninja storm a tyrant's stronghold in this side-scrolling platform action game for up to two simultaneous players. The evil Emperor Garuda has seized power, and the ninja Hayate and the kunoichi Kaede are sent to infiltrate his well-guarded stronghold and kill him; the two characters have no performance differences. Both can run, crouch, climb ladders, jump and hang from overhangs. The default katana can be traded for a kusarigama, and picking up the same weapon again strengthens it by up to three levels, while heavy damage weakens it. Shuriken and hand grenades serve as limited throwing weapons. With more than half of their vitality left, a held button summons a thunderstorm that damages every enemy on screen at a cost of vitality. Five levels make up the adventure.

t_18496de07ebc.overview: Commandos battle up a vertically scrolling war zone toward the village of Ikari in this run-and-gun shooter adapted from the SNK arcade game. Enemy soldiers, tanks and helicopters try to stop them. One button fires the gun and the other throws grenades, and both are in limited supply, so items left by certain defeated enemies are needed to restock ammunition as well as to power up. Empty tanks can be boarded, but their fuel runs down and they explode when it is gone. The Famicom version is divided into four stages, adds attack helicopters with a spread gun and a cannon that can fly over water, and places a final boss at the end of the last stage, after which General Kawasaki congratulates the heroes. Two players can fight together.

t_186912b9dbeb.overview: Insect-sized heroes take on a vast army of cyborg insects in this horizontally scrolling shooter, converted from the Taito arcade game, with the goal of freeing the insect world from its dark ruler queen. One button fires the main shot, which grows from a single bullet into multiple streams with upward and downward fire as power-ups are collected, while the other launches special weapons. Contact with enemies or their fire, or being crushed against walls by the scrolling, costs a life. Mid-bosses such as a cicada, stag beetle and firefly release items when defeated. The Famicom version keeps the arcade atmosphere but adds a girl as a playable character, sets boss battles against a pitch-black background, changes the final boss, and offers a difficulty setting.

t_18d125de9f53.overview: Badminton is shown here from a side view, more commonly associated with volleyball games than tennis games, and because the shuttlecock's flight is irregular, the player needs to focus more on its shadow than on the shuttlecock itself. Both male and female competitors can be chosen, although every character uses the same androgynous black-haired sprite; the only real difference is that games are shorter for female competitors, as in the real sport. The main menu also offers a choice of four courts, labeled coats on screen. Up to two people can play. The game was created by the developer and publisher team of Pax Softnica and Vap Inc., who were previously behind Super Real Baseball '88.

t_18f99bccf3e0.overview: Made for the Datach Joint ROM System, the barcode reader accessory sold separately for the Family Computer, this soccer simulation uses barcodes for the players' skills. Ten teams make up its version of the J.League, and the league mode schedules 18 games per team. Matches are split into two periods of three minutes apiece, and the team can be arranged in one of three layouts: 4-4-2, 4-3-3 or 3-5-2. Beyond league play, the modes include a tournament and penalty kick practice. In the PK Battle modes, each player must select a different team and then scan a player card rather than a team card. Up to two players can take part.

t_18ffd1f759ab.overview: Interested in flower arranging, the protagonist visits an exhibition held by a famous ikebana school together with a friend, Catherine, only for the woman hosting the exhibition to suddenly fall into agony and die. Her death is soon found to be murder, and the investigation that follows unfolds as a mystery adventure set in Kyoto. The scenario was written by mystery novelist Misa Yamamura and builds on her Catherine series, whose heroine is the amateur detective Catherine Turner.

t_19003447102c.overview: JaJaMaru and Sakura leave ancient Japan and travel to space to take on the evil Don Destroyda, ruler of the universe, and restore peace once and for all. Either JaJaMaru or Princess Sakura can be chosen as the playable character. The platform action lets the hero jump on enemies, uncover power-up blocks and use a dash that has to be revved up first. A cosmic suit, the Cosmo Suit, grants special abilities such as a double jump, and the stages lean heavily on tiny moving platforms over bottomless pits. The difficulty runs higher than many platformers of its time.

t_1927676e2912.overview: Mobile suits wage war on strategic maps in this simulation for one player against the computer or two players head to head. The side that first occupies the enemy capital wins, and cities, colonies and bases are seized along the way to build a front line. Units are produced at the capital or at captured Gacha Bases, with stronger units costing more and taking more turns to complete; factories allow production at up to seven sites, and battleships attack indirectly and carry allied units. Moving onto an enemy unit starts an action battle with ranged weapons such as beam rifles, close-combat weapons and an extra weapon used by pressing both buttons. Inertia in space and gravity in the atmosphere affect movement, and a fight still undecided after sixty seconds is a draw. Thirty maps include machines from Char's Counterattack.

t_192b28fed786.overview: A bald caveman takes on a prehistoric dinosaur kingdom in this side-scrolling platformer, an arranged Famicom version of the PC Engine game. The goal is to defeat the evil overlord King Tamagodon III, rescue Princess Dragon and bring peace back to the dinosaur kingdom. The setting is a fictional prehistoric era. The hero's main attack is a headbutt delivered with his large, invincible forehead, and pieces of meat collected along the way act as power-ups that lend him special abilities and make him stronger.

t_198922d36993.overview: Parodying Gradius, this horizontally scrolling shooter keeps that series' gauge-based power-up system, in which collected power capsules strengthen the ship's equipment, and adds roulette capsules and bell power reminiscent of the TwinBee series. Bells appear when red enemies or enemy formations are destroyed, change color when shot, and grant an effect that depends on the color collected. Four characters can be chosen, each with a different weapon set: Vic Viper, the Octopus, TwinBee and Pentarou. The Famicom version has seven stages; several arcade stages were dropped, while an original amusement park stage and hidden bonus stages were added, and the second stage's mid-boss was replaced by a character called Miss Mishitarina.

t_1997e346f312.overview: Harry Potter takes the lead in this side-scrolling action game from Hummer Technology, a reworking of the earlier Titenic built around Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone. Harry fights with a standing kick, a crouching punch and a crouching kick, and gains two special moves along the way: a broom attack in stage two and a magic attack in stage three. All five levels can be chosen right after the title screen, but every one must be cleared to see the ending. The opening part of the final stage, At School, features a volleyball contest against an old woman, and each stage ends with a two-faced boss. Cutscene text is taken from excerpts of the first book.

t_19a64a8939ed.overview: Eight games make up the third volume of the Super Cartridge series from Thin Chen Enterprise, released under the Sachen name. Four are earlier Joy Van titles: Jovial Race, which is similar to Rally-X, Little Red Hood, Twin Eagle and Silent Assault. Super Pang, an unofficial port of the arcade game Pang, joins them, along with three versions of Mine Sweeper, labeled Mine Sweeper, Mine Sweeper II and Mine Sweeper III, which were released only on this cartridge.

t_19b596e69cfa.overview:
Defeating reigning world champion Disaster Don serves as the ultimate goal for competitors navigating powerboat races. In single-player mode, played at Easy, Normal or Expert difficulty, the driver goes head-to-head against rivals such as Seasick Sidney, Aquarious Rex, Vicious Vickey, Surfer Bob, Weird Willey, Mangler Mike and Veronica Alabaster before finally facing Disaster Don. Losing two races ends the run, and a two-player mode pits two drivers against each other.

Controlling a powerboat, the player steers primarily from an overhead bird's-eye perspective featuring multidirectional scrolling, though buoy sections shift to a third-person tracking view. Winnings accumulate from legs won, beating course best times, sinking the rival boat, and gathering cash bonuses. These funds pay for repairs and boat component upgrades or cover two-thousand-dollar fines assessed for false starts. Collisions with animals, stationary obstacles, or rival watercraft inflict craft damage.

t_19b5c8d02db1.overview: Waixing, working as E.S.C. Co. Ltd, built this run'n gun on the Contra series for the NES/Famicom. Five areas lead from a city through a cave of rock platforms, a jungle, a factory or base with Red Falcon symbols and a dungeon littered with skulls, each closing with a boss such as a gargoyle or an alien ship. Standard enemies never shoot but speed up when they reach the middle of the screen. The machine gun is the default weapon, joined by the Spread Gun, Laser Gun and Flame Gun, while the R power-up now gives an extra life. Gravity is lower than usual, guns fire rapidly by default, and the player starts with four lives and six continues.

t_19ddb9f87405.overview: Three light-gun games make up this 1993 compilation, developed by Chengdu Tai Jing Da Dong Computer Co and published by Micro Genius on the Famicom. All three require a Zapper to play. Each one starts from a menu headed "Gun Fighter" that offers a choice of three difficulties, which suggests the cartridge may have been meant as a pack-in with a light gun. The included games are Clown, misspelled "Clowr" on the menu screen, Snake Charmer and Shooter. The same three games also appear on a less common 6-in-1 alongside three Idea-Tek titles, F-15 City War, Poke Block and Venice Beach Volleyball, where Clown is spelled correctly on the menu.

t_1a1895e177a6.overview: Drawn from the Belgian comic series Les Tuniques Bleues, the game has the player act out the Civil War, choosing to play as either the North or the South. Armies move across a strategic map of the United States separated into states and territories. When forces clash, the battle is normally resolved as a real-time action sequence, with a standard army of six infantry, three cavalry and one cannon; battles can also be turned off so that outcomes are left to chance, board-game style. Capturing a state with a railway station requires a short side-scrolling mission through its fort, and enemy trains can be captured in a similar sequence. Single-player and multiplayer play are supported.

t_1a51699c3746.overview: A horizontal shoot-'em-up developed by NTDEC, released in Spain by Gluk Video as a reprint of Go! Benny! The player controls a bee flying through each level against enemies in the air and on the ground. Pressing B fires a stinger forward. Bonuses, including power-ups and extra lives, are hidden under wax found in mid-air, and a boss waits at the end of each level.

t_1ac412df43ae.overview: Modern warfare drives this action strategy game, in which tanks, airplanes, military bases and non-nuclear missiles are used to stage a fictional World War III. Players take on the personas of Hollywood action film stars, and battles are fought across jungle, forest, swamp and urban terrain. After choosing a tank, the player decides either to move a unit or to destroy the enemy on sight. Money decides the war: both sides receive more than $250 million in game currency to spend on military weapons, destroyed units can be rebuilt for cash, and the first side to run out of money loses. Both single-player and multiplayer play are supported.

t_1ad2609e1105.overview: Strategy war simulation and role-playing elements come together in this release from Gakken, developed by Interlink. Rather than guiding a lone hero, the player controls a party of heroes with an entire army under their command, fighting other armies as well as random encounters with monsters. Before setting out, the army has to be purchased and equipped. Battles play out in turn-based formations: each formation acts separately and can target a different formation on the enemy side, so the makeup of the army matters. Archers, for example, can aim at any of the four rows of enemy forces, while front-line melee fighters are far more limited in what they can reach.

t_1af368ef03e8.overview: Picking up after the events of Ikari, Ralf and Clark are swallowed by a distortion of space and time while flying off on a special vacation, and they arrive on an island in another world. There a man asks them to free the island from the demon king who has conquered it. The game is an overhead, vertically scrolling run-and-gun shooter for one or two players at once, with monsters fought using guns and grenades. Weapon power-ups are often hidden under rocks that can be blasted with a bazooka or grenades, and protective armor absorbs a limited number of hits. The Famicom version adds a twist ending: after the demon king falls, the man who asked for help reveals his own ambitions and forces the heroes into a final duel armed only with swords.

t_1b15ae7e6b93.overview: Rally driving here is as much about preparation as speed. Built for a single player, the game offers a variety of courses together with changing weather and track conditions, and the driver must adapt to different terrain types while keeping the car under control. Many of the car's features can be customized, so the vehicle can be set up to suit the conditions of each course before the race begins, with the action focused on high-stakes motor racing through diverse environments.

t_1b18bafadea2.overview: Rather than a standalone game, this release is a song expansion cartridge for Family Noraebang, the Korean karaoke cartridge for the Famicom developed by Daou Infosys and published by Daewoo. The main cartridge has a special slot that accepts song packs, and inserting one expands the library beyond the 56 songs built into the base unit. The main program recognizes an expansion by a header reading "OPEN FAMILY SONG". As its title indicates, this pack supplies a collection of 16 songs, which are sung through the main cartridge's karaoke menu and microphone input.

t_1b465d124e91.overview: Konami's Famicom version of the castle-defense game keeps the alternating rhythm of time-limited combat and building phases. Each side defends a territory of castles and cannons ringed by a wall; after the cannons fire, shapes like those from Tetris appear and are moved and rotated to rebuild the defenses, and failing to have at least one surrounded castle after building means defeat. Beyond one-player games and two-player versus play, the single-player side offers four modes, each with its own story and setting: PRACTICE, with stage select and a modern-war theme against tanks and infantry; EASY, a fairy-tale world with wolves and rats as enemies; NORMAL, a fantasy based on Norse mythology; and HARD, a Sengoku-period campaign in which Oda Nobunaga fights. The three story modes use passwords.

t_1b6c63efe350.overview: Built purely around fighting with no story mode, this martial arts game has players select a character from a roster in which each fighting style is represented by two fighters, then win their way through a tournament. Points earned by completing training menus are spent to make a character grow stronger, and a password lets a trained fighter be used in the versus mode. A tag match mode allows team members to switch places by tagging in during a bout. The prototype is an English localization of the Famicom game Hiryu no Ken Special: Fighting Wars, with English text, character names and portraits altered to seem more American, and the controller graphic redesigned to look like a NES controller.

t_1b6e19022dab.overview: Adapted from the manga Maison Ikkoku, this adventure brings a PC-9801 original to the Famicom with nearly identical content. The player takes the role of Godai in an original story based on the early part of the manga. Progress depends on winning over Kyoko, fending off interference from the other residents and visiting the manager's room several times, all while searching for and obtaining something the game requires. The ultimate goal is to uncover a secret that Kyoko has been keeping hidden. Play advances through the commands of a graphical adventure, with the household's residents repeatedly getting in the way of the hero's efforts.

t_1b828f7c975d.overview: In the year 200X, robots developed to assist mankind are commonplace thanks to the renowned robot designer Dr. Light. When six of his Robot Masters, Cut Man, Guts Man, Ice Man, Bomb Man, Fire Man and Elec Man, start attacking, he realizes that his old rival Dr. Wily is responsible. His helper robot Rock, who has a strong sense of justice, offers to be converted into a fighting robot. Six side-scrolling platform stages can be chosen freely, and defeating a Robot Master lets the hero assimilate its signature attack as a Special Weapon with limited ammunition, replenished by collecting ammunition cells. Because each weapon deals heavy damage to one specific Robot Master, choosing the order of stages is part of the strategy. The last stage leads to Dr. Wily's Pacific-based robot factory.

t_1bc406c0c6ee.overview: Shenzhen Nanjing Technology made this Famicom backport of the SquareSoft SNES role-playing game; its title screen reads CHRONO TRIGGER, misspelled Cnrono Trigger. Built on the same engine as other Nanjing RPGs, it follows the original only loosely. Battles use a standard RPG layout yet still rely on the gauges of the original's active battle system, which is not implemented properly. The adventure goes only as far as the fight with Magus, a battle described as near impossible because it requires near frame-perfect inputs even with maxed stats. Sprites are custom or recycled from other Nanjing games, with Rhyhorn (recolored green), Beedrill and Zubat appearing as enemies.

t_1bcee174679c.overview: Six games share the fourth volume of the Super Cartridge series from Thin Chen Enterprise, released under the Sachen name. Master Chu and the Drunkard Hu and Metal Fighter, also known as Space Boy, are 1989 Joy Van games. The remaining titles come from Sachen: Galactic Crusader; Magic Cube; Auto-Upturn, a puzzle game whose later levels contain nudity; and Super Pang II, an unofficial port of the arcade game Super Pang.

t_1c078fda4c17.overview: Teams patterned on Central League and Pacific League clubs take the field in a baseball game whose controls resemble Pro Yakyuu Family Stadium. Holding the B button while moving lets fielders jump and make diving catches, and each player has position-specific defensive ability and throwing strength. The one-player tournament is a round-robin against the other 11 teams with password continues, alongside two-player versus games, an All-Stars mode against the computer or a friend, and a watch mode where the computer plays both sides. A hidden mode, unlocked by holding directions on both controllers while pressing Reset, swaps in 12 more teams in which every player is a woman in a softball-style uniform, including a team built from Tecmo's own game characters.

t_1c14d39d9352.overview: Set in an era before the first Dragon Buster, this Famicom sequel sends its hero to recover a sacred sword stolen by a dragon. Each round opens on a map of branching paths dotted with dungeons such as graveyards, caves, towers and mansions; finding the exit of each clears the way forward until a one-on-one battle with the dragon on its mountain ends the round. Unlike the side-view original, dungeons are viewed from above and begin dark, lighting up as the hero advances. The only weapon is a bow with a limited supply of arrows that must be picked up, and arrows bounce off walls and can hurt the shooter. Damage changes the color of the hero's clothes from blue to green, yellow and red, and lingering too long summons an invincible centipede-like monster. Map items include an axe for forests, a hammer for fences, a camel for deserts, a ladder for cliffs and a boat for lakes.

t_1c2f9b70f6f7.overview: A soldier nicknamed Big Bang is pulled away from a beach vacation to rescue a professor whose doomsday bomb, capable of destroying the world, has been stolen. The bomb is controlled by medallions distributed among a group of governors, and collecting them is the only way to defuse it. Built as an open-ended platformer, the game lets the player choose which direction to go, with over 40 possible routes and free backtracking. The hero moves, jumps and fires a handgun that can be upgraded with weapons bought in a shop, while collected Force grants powers such as shrinking, flight, healing, invincibility and teleporting to earlier areas. Along the way a demon takes control of one of his allies. Money in this original release is counted in yen.

t_1c6b76f979e9.overview: Based on the Japanese television series Takeshi's Castle, this one-player Family Trainer game is controlled by stepping on the mat. The goal is to break through three castles and defeat the castle lord, Takeshi. Each of the first three castles lines up the same timed obstacles: climbing a wall by jumping, hopping across floating stones where decoys sink, crossing a rope bridge under cannon fire, dodging obstacles on a surfboard, judging a run-up to stop on a target spot, advancing through a moving mansion, choosing one of three walls, and driving a cart to the goal, which earns an item for the finale. Clearing an obstacle adds points based on time, and the total becomes life in the final cart battle against Takeshi, whose cart fires in three directions.

t_1cf782385fde.overview: Released on the Evercade Data East Collection 1 cartridge under the Japanese arcade name, this is the NES version of Data East's car-combat racer Bump 'n' Jump, which reached the Famicom as Buggy Popper. The chase covers city, country, mountain and seaside districts across 16 courses. Enemy cars, including the Jackal buggies, can be hit and pushed off the road or crushed by jumping onto them with the A button, but a jump is possible only once the car reaches 150 km/hour. Trucks deposit sand, cement mixers dump concrete and fuel trucks spill oil; running over sand or concrete destroys the car, while oil sends it sliding. Slow bulldozers try to block the way, and a speeding ambulance has to be let past. Power barrels add fuel and energy, and once power drops to zero the car can no longer jump.

t_1d44f904155d.overview: Franky, a Frankenstein's monster, is on a mission to collect the scattered body parts of his girlfriend, Bitsy, and bring her back to life. Her parts lie hidden throughout a mansion along with various items, and recovering every piece is the goal of the adventure. Progress depends on exploration: keys and special items are needed to access additional areas, where further body parts and the equipment required for the resurrection wait to be found.

t_1d4f4234fb13.overview: Planned as an English localization of Higemaru Makaijima - Nanatsu no Shima Daibōken, a 1987 Japanese action-adventure from Capcom, this canceled release survives as a prototype. The hero must sail the ocean around seven islands, collecting keys from different pirate ships, which appear in black with a pink flag bearing a skull and crossbones. Aboard each ship, a certain number of enemies must be defeated to unlock the door to the boss. Rocks scattered around can be thrown at enemies as well as barrels, and a lamp is required to unseal an island before it can actually be unlocked. Monoliths carry messages in an old language, deciphered with the help of a chart. The ultimate prize is the greatest treasure, once owned by a long-dead legendary pirate.

t_1d9bc35c9249.overview:
Elite centers on space trading and combat. Players begin at a space station controlling Commander Jameson aboard a lightly armed Cobra Mk III trading vessel with one hundred credits. Advancing through the open-ended setting involves undertaking activities such as asteroid mining, piracy, commerce, bounty hunting, and missions to earn funds. One objective involves increasing the pilot combat rating until reaching the title rank.

Accumulated money funds vessel upgrades including improved weaponry, expanded cargo space, an extra energy unit, automated docking computers, and fuel scoops. Pilots navigate planetary systems via sublight propulsion and execute hyperdrive jumps across interstellar space, with jump range limited by the fuel aboard. Star systems feature orbiting stations requiring precise manual alignment to enter docking bays unless assisted by computer systems. During hyperdrive travel, hostile Thargoid alien forces can intercept ships in transit, forcing confrontations in witch-space.

t_1dc573e91fbd.overview: Exidy's arcade shooter Crossbow, controlled with a positional gun shaped like a full-sized crossbow, is the basis for this unreleased NES port, preserved as an early prototype that AGCI solicited for sale but never released. In the arcade original, the player protects a band of adventurers from afar by shooting the objects that threaten them as they try to cross the screen from the left, while the adventurers themselves are also vulnerable to stray shots. The goal there is to reach the final scenario beyond the castle and confront the Master of Darkness. This early NES build is incomplete: it has neither a scoring system nor a loss state, and its graphics do not match screenshots of the port seen elsewhere, so a later version may have been made.

t_1dd2fd515a4a.overview: Gaou, a former criminal who turned to Buddhist sculpting, carves a phoenix statue, only to see it stolen, smashed into 16 fragments and scattered across past and future eras. The action-platforming quest sends him through time and space to recover the pieces, one in each of 16 levels. Most stages end with a boss whose defeat yields a fragment, while others instead demand dodging traps such as falling rocks or breaking through a wall. Gaou has three lives, each with a set number of hit points drained by enemies and their projectiles; losing all hit points, falling into a pit or running out of time costs a life. Pressing Select makes him self-destruct to restart a level if he becomes stuck, and after a game over play can resume from the start of the current stage.

t_1e33fa7d82a9.overview: A vertically scrolling shooter, Xevious puts the player in the Solvalou, a flying attack craft sent to destroy the Xevious forces plotting to take over Earth. A zapper fires at flying enemies, while a blaster bombs ground installations and vehicles, with a reticle in front of the ship showing where bombs will land. Sixteen connected areas, featuring forests, roads, rivers and mechanical structures, loop back to the first once all are completed. Enemies grow more advanced as the player becomes more skilled at destroying them. At certain points the Andor Genesis mothership attacks, and it is beaten by destroying its four blaster receptacles or the core in its center. Bombing specific spots uncovers hidden Sol Citadels, and yellow Special Flags award an extra life.

t_1e3d3e0e4f47.overview: Loosely following the film, this platform game sends an unnamed hero, called simply "Player" in the manual, through stages that resemble a restaurant, underground caverns and a pirate ship. In each level the hero must find three keys and rescue one captive Goonie, all hidden behind doors that are opened with bombs. Freeing every Goonie is required to reach the final stage, The Pirate Ship; otherwise play restarts from the first level. Defense comes from a kick, bombs whose blasts are fatal to the hero as well, and a slingshot found behind doors. Collecting eight diamonds refills the life meter, while a firesuit and earmuffs guard against flames and music notes. Rats patrol the stages, and the Fratellis can only be stunned, never killed.

t_1eb67433e67a.overview: Built for a 1991 competition, the cartridge strings three minigames together against one shared clock of 6 minutes and 21 seconds. Play opens in Super Mario Bros. 3, where the task is to collect 25 coins. Next comes a version of Pin Bot in which the target is 100,000 points. The final event is Dr. Mario, which lasts until the time expires. When the clock runs out, the scores from the three games are combined by a weighting formula into a single total: the Super Mario Bros. 3 score is multiplied by 10, the Pin Bot score is added as is, and the Dr. Mario score is multiplied by 100.

t_1f055aedc250.overview: Designed by entertainer Takeshi Kitano, this action-adventure follows a poor salaryman in a decadent urban Japan who receives a treasure map and sets out after a treasure on a remote island in the South Seas. Side-scrolling action, with yakuza frequently attacking, combines with a story that advances through the player's choices, and some sections add shooting. Before leaving, the salaryman has to beat up the old man who gave him the map, divorce his wife, resign from his job and learn skills at the culture center; otherwise his wife or company president drags him home, or the old man intercepts the treasure. Health returns by drinking tequila at a bar in Japan or sleeping at a hotel on Hintabo Island. The second controller's microphone is used in places such as the karaoke bar, and one stage involves hang gliding while firing at birds and UFOs.

t_1f084da621b7.overview: Despite its name, this unlicensed cartridge has nothing to do with the film or with the licensed Lethal Weapon game: credited to Aoji Go Go, it is actually a port of Konami's arcade light gun shooter Lethal Enforcers. It is played with the Zapper, and a level selection screen with rows of icons lets the player choose which stage to take on. The game was also included on Photo-Gun 13-in-1, one of J.Y. Company's compilations of mainly light-gun games such as Duck Hunt.

t_1f0faa387998.overview: Racing modeled on the Formula 1 World Championship is the focus of this Data East cartridge, the Japanese original later adapted in North America as Al Unser Jr.'s Turbo Racing. The game offers a season mode along with two time trial modes. The car is steered with the D-pad, with A to accelerate and B to brake, while gauges, speed and other readouts sit at the bottom of the screen. Turbo boosts can be used when needed but must be refueled once empty, and hazards such as signposts and other cars must be avoided on track. Qualifying is held before each race and gives only a single lap to set a time, which makes a good starting position difficult to earn.

t_1f1a92ef41d4.overview: Instead of competing against rivals, a single player lives out an entire human life on a game board, with no human or computer opponents. The story begins in heaven, where an angel's number is drawn at random, marking it as the next angel to be delivered to Earth to become a human being. Starting as a child and living until death at 100, the player works to improve six categories: knowledge, health, friendship, love, popularity and wealth. Progress is measured by a ranking against the population of Japan, starting at number 130,000,000 and aiming to climb all the way to number one. The course of a life is very long, and reaching the top of the ranking is not easy.

t_1f267f702ce4.overview: Long ago the hero Iason sealed a hidden passage to another dimension, but the seal has been broken, letting evil creatures pour into the world, and the Demon Queen Terarin holds the Golden Seal needed to close it again. In this Famicom version of a Kogado computer role-playing game, published by ASCII, the young hero is named Argus and can gather three companions, Guy, Media and Treymos. Battles are fought one-on-one, and only the character who attacks gains experience. Weapons and armor wear down with use and must be repaired by smiths. Defeating monsters yields fangs that can be traded for money or special items, and a fame rating rises or falls depending on which creatures are slain, affecting whether townspeople will talk, sell or help.

t_1f2cac06a262.overview: Back from training, Kitaro finds that youkai have taken over Japan and that his weapons, his father Medama-oyaji and his girlfriend Yumeko have all disappeared. To rescue Yumeko and save the country, he takes on the youkai army led by Chi, the Nine-Tailed Fox. The role-playing adventure divides the Japanese archipelago into six areas, each ending with a boss, and barrier clouds force Kitaro to find underground caves to pass between them; some bosses can be reached only with key items. Allies including Neko-musume, Sunakake-baba, Ittan-momen, Nezumi Otoko and Nurikabe can fight for one turn in place of Kitaro. Youkai arts consume spiritual power, while weapons can be used any number of times, and items work only outside battle. One player.

t_1faba91b7047.overview: Designed as an English tutor, this educational cartridge is a Korean adaptation of Dong Dong Nao II, a Sachen program that taught English to Chinese-speaking children. Kuk Je Academy adapted it for Korean school children, translating its text into Hangul. Learning takes the form of exercises, and after completing some of them the player is rewarded with a mini-game that was later expanded into the separate puzzle game Pyramid. The Korean release presents the program as an entry in the Pyramid series.

t_20576715b5f9.overview: Jaleco's first Moero!! sports game, known outside Japan as Bases Loaded, fills the diamond with a fictitious league of twelve teams. The player controls one of the 12 teams in either a single game or a full season, and single games also offer a two-player option. Each pitch is shown through a television-style depiction of the pitcher-batter matchup. One distinctive touch lets the pitcher provoke a batter into charging the mound, although each team has only one batter, usually its best hitter, who can be provoked in this manner.

t_2107be1d38da.overview: Mappy's son Happy wants to marry Picky, but she will not accept him until he has a house of his own, so he travels through Mappyland gathering money and valuables to build one. The side-scrolling platform action uses two buttons: a jump that can be stretched into a brief hover by tapping in midair, and a short kick that defeats enemies, opens treasure chests and breaks blocks. Taking a hit costs health and drops a bag of money that can be recovered. Each level closes with a slot machine and a mini-game that decide rewards such as extra lives, items or cash, followed by a shop selling furniture for the new home. In the competitive two-player mode, Happy and his twin brother Rappy race to build the better house and win the heart of Picky.

t_21a99e2540e3.overview: Digging tunnels through the earth, Dig Dug (Taizo Hori) must eliminate each stage's enemies to advance. Two kinds of foes roam underground: Pookas, red and spherical beings that wear comically large goggles, and the draconic Fygars, which breathe fire. Dig Dug can use an air pump to inflate them until they explode, or crush them under falling rocks; rocks cannot be dug through but fall a short time after the dirt beneath them is removed. Squashing several enemies with one rock earns extra points, and dropping two rocks in a stage makes an edible bonus item appear. Enemies can pass through dirt as harmless ghostly eyes, and once only one enemy remains it attempts to escape at the top of the stage.

t_21f91caa36ca.overview: Played in the style of Pengo, this arcade action game from Thin Chen Enterprise sends a penguin to the Arctic on a treasure hunt. The penguin must collect the gems scattered around each round and stash them safely in an igloo while avoiding becoming the lunch of seals with tusks as sharp as blades. Seals can be crushed with a pushed block of ice, or the penguin can dive out of their way. Rounds continue up to round No. 50. Besides the standard game, there is a two-player mode and a level building mode for constructing custom rounds. Outside Taiwan the same game was sold as Penguin & Seal.

t_21fdfa6547ba.overview: Mahjong is played one-on-one against a single computer opponent in this direct sequel to Family Mahjong, a two-player format common in computer adaptations. Alongside a standard mahjong mode, a tournament mode adds a slight role-playing element: after winning games, the player can enhance certain stats to improve the odds in later rounds of the tournament. Calls keep the scheme of the first game, with pon, chi, kan and riichi each assigned to a direction on the control pad and carried out by pressing it, instead of being chosen with the pad and confirmed with a button. Development was handled by Nihon Bussan, a maker then known for arcade mahjong games.

t_2229a0f6b1c4.overview:
Solar Jetman - Hunt for the Golden Warpship places the player in control of a Jetpod exploring alien environments in a multidirectional shooter. The quest requires Solar Jetman to navigate hostile planets to retrieve the scattered parts of the stolen Golden Warpship. The pod can rotate clockwise or counterclockwise and is affected by varying gravitational pulls and inertia across different planets. Maintaining sufficient fuel is necessary to travel between destinations.

Players launch from a stationary mothership across twelve planets and one hidden world. A tractor beam allows the craft to tow items back to the mothership, though towing reduces its thrusting power. Collected valuables and defeated enemies grant points, which are traded at a trading post for weapons and equipment. Destructive damage ejects the pilot into a fragile spacesuit, giving the opportunity to return to the mothership for a replacement vessel before losing a life.

t_222b628db8db.overview: Touring the country by rail while building a business fortune forms the core of this 1988 digital board game for one to four players. A year consists of four turns, one per season. Each turn a player rolls a die to move, then rolls two dice to trigger an event that usually brings a gain or loss of money. Property stations offer hotels, department stores, leisure facilities, food shops, farms and more, and railway lines can be bought between neighboring property stations. Each player heads for a separate destination, with more aid money for reaching one farther away, while a pickpocket can make off with half or all of a player's cash. Victory goes to the first to reach a set revenue amount or to the top earner after a chosen number of years.

t_222eeb4ba452.overview: Konami characters from several series share the stage in an action-adventure led by Konami Man, who can switch to Konami Lady. Six selectable levels each take place in a different Konami game, among them a Castle level and a Medieval Japan level, and in each one a key frees that game's star character, who then becomes playable. The rescued heroes include Goemon, Getsu Fūma, Mikey Walsh, a Moai and King Kong. Dr. Cinnamon's lab offers character profiles and energy refills, and his brother can revive fallen characters for a price in bullets. After the six levels come a scrolling space shooter stage, flown with the Vic Viper or TwinBee, and a final linear stage. With two players, one controls Konami Man and the other Konami Lady.

t_2255bd1478a7.overview: Drawing on Shinji Mizushima's baseball manga, this baseball simulation faithfully retells the story from Dokaben through Daikoushien, with the player guiding Meikun High School toward victory. The story begins with Taro Yamada and his teammates in their first year. On each pitch, the pitcher picks a pitch type and one of 25 locations on a five-by-five grid, while the batter chooses a meet zone and predicts the pitch speed from four levels; meet zone size and favorite locations differ from player to player. Every strikeout adds a POW gauge point that can be assigned to players to unlock special batting or pitching techniques, and stealing and bunting are supported. Special matches against the Nanba OB team and the Tokyo Mets close the game, and two players can face each other in versus play.

t_226526aa42f8.overview: Touring Japan by train, players buy properties and compete to finish with the largest total assets in this board game for one to four competitors. Every player heads for the same destination, and the player farthest from it is possessed by the God of Poverty, who causes trouble at the end of every turn. Each in-game year lasts eleven turns, followed by a settlement month. Compared with the earlier entry in the series, this installment introduces cards and the concept of debt, while railways themselves can no longer be purchased. The mechanics are often compared to the board games sugoroku and Monopoly, with wealth acquired through business transactions.

t_22900e85f8ce.overview: First-grade arithmetic is practiced through four short action games, two for addition and two for subtraction. In a racing game the player dodges other cars and touches the car showing the correct answer; in another, a numbered panel is selected by jumping over it while snakes patrol nearby, opening the wall in front of a female rabbit. A dental game has the player drill the tooth bearing the right number while avoiding devil-shaped cavity germs, and a balloon game means riding the balloon with the answer and dodging birds on the way up to the goal. Two courses are offered, one at a normal level and one at an advanced level. Each correct answer earns 10 points, while a wrong answer or contact with an enemy costs a life.

t_22a4ebe3a61e.overview: Set during the Cold War, this beat 'em up follows a military prisoner who breaks free from his cell and fights through enemy territory to reach the main base, defeat the enemy general and escape. The four stages run from a POW camp through a warehouse and a jungle to the enemy base. The hero punches, kicks and jumps, and can pick up a throwing knife or a machine gun dropped by defeated soldiers; hand grenades become usable in the boss fights against a helicopter and a tank. Unlike the two-player arcade original, this version is single player only. It also adds new enemy types such as frogmen, shotgun soldiers and a strongman, a new final boss, and power-ups found in huts and rooms, including full health, brass knuckles and protective armor.

t_23627eec0fb8.overview: Released in Japan in December 1986 by Showa Tsusho, Super Maruo is an adult-oriented unlicensed Famicom game with no relation to Nintendo's Mario series beyond a player sprite that vaguely resembles Mario. The gameplay is very simple: the player controls a man who has to catch up to a woman running around the screen while avoiding a dog that chases him. Grabbing the woman awards a scene of her stripping or posing, and both characters later begin to lose their clothes during play. Grabbing her a second time triggers an erotic animation, after which the whole process repeats. There are four such animations in all.

t_236e4edda6c3.overview: Dance and Karaoke combines a basic arrow game in the vein of Dance Dance Revolution with sing-along karaoke. After a song is chosen, a background appears with the lyrics shown at the bottom of the screen for the player to sing along to, while arrows appear that must be hit with the matching direction. The lyrics switch between English and Chinese as the song loops, and after six loops, three in each language, the player is sent to a high score screen. The song list consists entirely of nursery rhymes and children's songs aimed at very young players, including Two Tigers, Do Re Mi, Mary Had A Little Lamb, Edelweiss, Jingle Bells, London Bridge and Old MacDonald Had a Farm.

t_240c035eac54.overview: Cony Soft's 1993 pirate port of Fatal Fury 2 plays more like Street Fighter II than the original, with no Pow bar and none of the original's computer-only characters. Depending on the release, five or six fighters are selectable, each joined by a named recolor: Terry Bogard, Andy Bogard, Mai Shiranui, Kim Kaphwan, Cheng Sinzan and Lawrence Blood, who appears under the name Yeain and is missing from some releases. A punches and B kicks, holding forward can produce a stronger punch or kick, and special moves are performed by pressing a direction together with A and B. Two-player battles are a separate menu option, and both players may pick the same character. Graphics and music are simplified from the original, the HUD changes color between stages, and the recolored fighters fight on recolored versions of the regular stages. The ending is a simple credits screen.

t_241ad61402ec.overview: A time machine mishap has flung Nobita and three friends into outer space, a demon realm and the ocean floor, and Doraemon's broken four-dimensional pocket has scattered his secret gadgets across those worlds. Each of the three worlds plays differently. The first mixes overhead exploration with side-view jumping sections reached through manholes, where hidden manholes, doors and items are revealed by attacking, and the starting gun can be upgraded to stronger weapons. The second is a forced-scrolling shooter whose route turns and branches into hidden rooms, where rescued friends join in to provide supporting fire. The third is a side-view underwater stage with flip-screen scrolling: armed with a water cannon, Doraemon frees his recaptured companions and uses them to open the gate of an undersea fortress and rescue the last friend from its master. Dorayaki restore his life.

t_243855ec82c7.overview:
Set in the Forgotten Realms port city of Phlan, the story begins as the city council recruits adventurers to reclaim the surrounding ruins from invading monsters and an evil force. A single player assembles a party of up to five characters, selecting each member's race, class, gender, alignment, and attributes, or uses ready-made characters, and can hire one non-player character.

Gameplay involves moving from area to area to clear out hostile creatures and earn experience points. In town, characters trade gear, hire non-player characters, visit temples for healing, and accept commissions. Battles feature round-based tactical encounters in which more agile characters tend to act first, with commands including casting spells and bandaging dying comrades, culminating in an encounter with the evil leader.

t_2477ae92903f.overview: Adapted from the 1989 animated film, this side-scrolling action game sends the young mermaid Ariel through six undersea stages in search of Ursula. Ariel attacks by shooting bubbles that trap her foes, which she can then pick up and throw. She can also dig through sand to uncover treasure and collect sea shells used to break open treasure chests, which hold power-ups that increase the power and range of her bubbles. Icons scattered through the levels restore health, grant extra lives or boost her bubbles further. The journey runs through The Coral Sea, a Sunken Ship, the Sea of Ice and an Undersea Volcano, and it ends with two battles at Ursula's Castle.

t_249d502160a8.overview: Based on the manga and anime series of the same name, this side-scrolling action game opens after demons from another world have invaded the Earth and merged it with the fairy tale world that Henbee comes from. With humans struggling to adapt to their new tyrants and to the weirdness of the fairy tale world, Henbee sets out with his trusty parasol to save the world and rescue the human family he has chosen, reuniting along the way with Megaru and friends. Before play begins, a screen asks for the player's age, and the difficulty of the main game is adjusted to match.

t_24aa9dff127e.overview:
Final Fantasy is a role-playing game where players control four Light Warriors seeking to restore the light of four darkened Orbs. Play begins by assembling a four-person party from six classes: Fighter, Thief, Black Belt, Red Mage, White Mage, and Black Mage. Characters explore towns, dungeons, and an overworld map, initially traveling on foot before gaining access to a ship, canoe, and airship. Towns offer information, items, and equipment, while dungeons feature treasure chests and boss encounters.

Encountering enemies triggers turn-based, menu-driven combat where players select commands including Fight, Magic, Drink, Item, and Run. Defeating monsters yields money and experience points, allowing characters to raise their attributes and advance in level. Later in the journey, characters can undergo a class change that expands equipment and magic capabilities. Staying at an inn restores the party's hit points and magic and saves the game to the cartridge's battery.

t_24ac6001704e.overview: A hostile nation is secretly preparing to launch a new weapon, and a member of a special armed force must stop it, beginning by rescuing a captured covert agent codenamed Spider. The Konami first-person action game spans four missions in three styles. Each mission opens in an attack helicopter flown from the cockpit view, armed with a chosen missile load and extra equipment such as fuel, chaff grenades or ground missiles, and landing on an enemy heliport means hovering and lining up the pad against the wind. On foot, an auto-scrolling gun-shooting segment leads to the base entrance, followed by first-person maze exploration of corridors for ammunition and rations, where Spider sometimes offers hints. Mission 3 takes place entirely in the air. The Japanese release includes a password feature for starting at later missions.

t_24dbd042874a.overview: Part of a series of active simulation war games, this story follows Matari-Shuban, who as a child was told in a dream that he would become emperor and now searches for Ashvin, the promised planet. The Famicom version omits star system development and narrows play to four actions: interstellar movement, fleet production, fleet battles and planetary battles. Conquering planets raises the home world's production level, which is spent to build warships. Each player commands a single fleet, and in two-player simultaneous play each side has one fleet. Losing a fleet battle sends the player back to the home world to restart with one cruiser. Planetary battles scroll automatically to the right with no time limit, and a failed attack halves the number of ships held.

t_24faff8b122b.overview:
Stopping a destructive alien invasion of the planet Pan serves as the ultimate goal for the protagonist, army captain Max Maverick. Confronting the threat alone after the military and populace evacuate, Maverick battles hostile extraterrestrial forces that consume living creatures, machinery, and structures. The action unfolds from an overhead oblique viewpoint as the player steers Maverick through the campaign, occasionally piloting a motorcycle or hovercraft for transit.

Progressing through each level requires gathering weapon upgrades, fighting alien enemies, and avoiding hazards including pitfalls, damage zones and crushing walls. Large bosses must be defeated along the way. Story sequences appear between stages. Six stages make up the campaign, with a special seventh stage for players who finish all six before the game ends. A password feature is provided to record and restore game progress.

t_2520052cacba.overview: Exploration drives this action-adventure from Sunsoft, set in an interconnected free-roaming world in the vein of Metroid. In the western version, Bop-Louie's friends Freeon-Leon, Shades and Gil fall into a crater and lose their memories. Bop-Louie must find all three, and then the group must collect three keys by defeating guardians to open a gate and face Unyohn. Each lost friend is met as a boss and becomes playable once beaten: Freeon-Leon swims and walks on slippery ice, Shades jumps high, and Gil dives underwater, while Bop-Louie can find an item for climbing walls. Characters switch at any time from a sub-menu. Enemies are attacked by jumping on them while holding down, and defeated foes turn into balloons called Popoons that can be thrown. Health starts at 10 HP and grows with life containers, and passwords let play continue with items and characters intact.
t_2520052cacba.official: Bop-Louie's friends have fallen into a crater on the world of Ufouria and they need his help! Control Bop-Louie as he searches for his amnesiac friends. Unable to swim or walk on ice, Bop-Louie must find his friends to help him overcome these problems and complete his adventure – but with each friend having their own strengths and weaknesses, it won't be easy!

t_254e65b711fe.overview: Puzzle solving joins vertical-scrolling shooting in this Famicom follow-up to Xevious. The Earth forces have been worn down by a long war with the Xevious army, led by GAMP, a computer built to govern humanity. The Solvalou, armed with a zapper for flying enemies and a blaster for ground targets, is drawn into a space-time trap set by GAMP and must fight its way out. Many of the 21 areas cannot be cleared simply by surviving: a specific condition, such as rescuing an allied craft or destroying every designated target, must be met, or the same area repeats. Capsules grant power-ups including a barrier, a back zapper and a wide blaster, and hidden special flags award extra lives.

t_257bb95707d8.overview: Loosely based on the Chinese novel Journey to the West, this side-scrolling action game follows SonSon on a journey across a screen that scrolls automatically, stopping only for fights against major enemies. The playfield is made of six continuous platforms that occasionally feature small gaps, and the characters walk along them on their own. Holding back makes them move more slowly than the scrolling, while they can also push ahead faster than the screen moves. The goal is to fight from one side to the other, eventually reaching the statue of Buddha. A partner can join for cooperative play as TonTon.

t_2585543fa1cf.overview: Kawauso, the otter character from a popular 1980s manga, sets out on a trip to Hawaii but keeps getting sidetracked, ending up in places that are anything but Hawaii, including the South Pole, the Amazon jungle and Pluto. Though it looks like a traditional platform game, it deliberately breaks away from the video game conventions of its time, starting with a series of fake title screens, one of them off-frame as if the cartridge were faulty. Kawauso is slow and attacks by slapping with barely any reach; holding the attack button cycles through special moves, with the more powerful ones highlighted only briefly. Spike pits that seem impossible to cross can be bypassed by walking on the mountains in the background. Enemies include nude streakers felled by arrows from off screen, and the final boss is a gigantic salaryman filling nearly two-thirds of the screen.

t_25c9e6fc8993.overview: Part computer role-playing game and part board game, The Tales on a Watery Wilderness frames its adventure as a story an older sister tells to a child who cannot sleep. Inside that tale, players become medieval knights in a fantastical world, battling monsters and a demon lord with swords and magic. Everyone races to be first to grant the king's wish, and whoever defeats the boss wins. Each day, players move freely across sugoroku-style board spaces within a step count tied to their level, while random events appear in towns and on roads. Landing on another player's space allows a duel, and battles against enemies can take several days to finish. The length of a session is chosen at the start, from 1 to 99 days. Up to four players can take part, with the computer filling any empty seats.

t_264ac06e1021.overview: The kingdom of Guldred is in chaos after General Guemon assassinates King Guldred. Before he passes, Gazem tells his tale to a knight named Kein, who takes up the quest to restore the kingdom. The adventure is a side-scrolling action role-playing game in the vein of Zelda II, split between a large persistent overworld and several smaller dungeons that contain valuables. Its eight stages each hold residential areas with shops and people who share information, along with a labyrinth. Every vanquished enemy yields experience and sometimes health or money, though Kein can only level up twice per stage, and nothing in the game announces level ups. He moves at a speedy clip, can stab upward, and can buy magic spells and gain new powers during the quest.

t_266cc4b41d01.overview: Climbing skyscrapers by hand, the hero tries to reach the top while windows open and close and falling objects threaten to knock him off. The Famicom version is controlled with two controllers held upright side by side, using both D-pads in place of the arcade's two joysticks that move the climber's limbs, and a Climber Stick attachment for the D-pads came in the box. Beyond porting the arcade game, it fully redraws the graphics and adds more stages, more enemy characters and many original items. Finding a hidden key leads to an original action stage inside a building, and collecting every medal from the building rooms across all stages opens an extra stage. Failing to catch onto a window sends the climber falling to his death.

t_26d48236902a.overview: Four light gun shooting games are collected on this 1995 multicart: Space Fight of Gun, Fantasy of Gun, Abyss of Gloom and City Adventure. All four are pirate originals rather than copies of licensed games, and they are attributed to a group of unidentified developers affiliated with NTDEC. The selection menu plays a simple rendition of Unchained Melody and resembles the menu interface of the Unchained Melody multicarts, though with a different font. The same four games appeared earlier on a more obscure 5-in-1 multicart that also included Elfland.

t_26ded5950c46.overview:
Campaign matches unfold across medieval England in 1149 as factions contest territorial dominion following the monarch's demise. A single player assumes command of one of four Saxon leaders to battle Norman forces and ultimately crush the three Norman castles to claim the crown. Victory requires managing a prolonged war of attrition by building larger forces than rival factions and launching assaults at favorable moments.

Gameplay involves building armies to conquer hostile territories, clash directly with opposing military forces, and lay siege to or plunder rival fortresses. Players also compete in periodic jousting tournaments to win territory, undertake a mission to rescue a damsel in distress, and seek assistance from Robin Hood.

t_2752b8eda784.overview: Namco's baseball series returns in this 1988 edition, which for the first time on a home console fields teams corresponding to all twelve real professional clubs of the era, still grouped into a single JAPAN LEAGUE. Fielding errors, where a fielder deflects or drops the ball, are newly introduced. Before a game the batting order of the starting lineup can be rearranged, and each pitching staff grows to four starters and two relievers. Two starters are randomly marked as players in good form, and in the seventh inning every player gets that boost as a "Lucky 7." Four stadiums can now be chosen instead of a single park, a team edit feature appears for the first time, and results are reported on the NAMCOT SPORTS NEWS. Two-player matches continue until one side wins four games.

t_2766c9901201.overview: Kunio's dodgeball club takes the court in this arranged home version of the arcade game, the original of the game released abroad as Super Dodge Ball.
