Players navigate five adventure levels from an overhead perspective, entering sewers and buildings that transition to side-scrolling navigation. Guiding Leonardo, Michaelangelo, Donatello, or Raphael, the player can swap members through an information screen. Each character utilizes a signature primary weapon with distinct reach, speed, and attack power to combat the Foot Clan. A turtle whose life runs out is captured until rescued, and the game ends if all four are captured.

Throughout the journey, players collect pizza to recover life and acquire secondary armaments such as shurikens, boomerangs, and Kiai scrolls. Side-scrolling areas involve jumping, ducking, and fighting adversaries, alongside completing goals such as disarming underwater bombs. Later rooftops require ropes to cross gaps. Boss confrontations conclude most levels, culminating in an assault on the Technodrome and a final battle against Shredder.

t_3a405f665868.overview: Up to four players compete in this table game adapted from the Obocchama-kun manga. Unlike board games built around earning money, the final goal here is to grant the heroine's wishes and win a kiss from her. The board is modeled on a world map and includes an underworld region. Players hunt for the treasure the heroine asks for and earn affection points by delivering it to the city where she is staying, which is chosen at random; reaching the point total set before the game begins wins the kiss. Treasure already found by one player can be taken away by rivals through physical assault or by using items.

t_3a7786f30813.overview: Donald Duck and his friends head to Italy for a sports competition built around six offbeat events. In the Sack Race, competitors hop down a street in a sack while avoiding open potholes, and in Boot Throwing a boot is swung by its strings to build momentum before release. Pogo Stick requires timing leaps over four bars, Overboard is a shoving match on a swinging boat on the Grand Canal, Tower of Pizza means walking a stack of pizzas carefully to the finish line, and River Jump is a pole vault across a river. Players can pick a single event, play all of them in sequence, or go head to head against a friend. The main mode awards points for each event and then starts another round; a strong enough showing earns a medal and an ending sequence.

t_3b1c7206a9a2.overview: The swordsman Adol Christin is transported to the floating island of Ys, a civilization in the heavens, where he begins a quest to unravel the secrets of Ys and finally rid both the island and Esteria of evil. Exploration and combat are viewed from above, and ordinary enemies fall to the series' bump attack, in which Adol strikes automatically by walking into foes. Magic takes on a much larger role: Adol obtains spells such as a fire spell for attack and a time spell that can stop enemies, each consuming his magic points. Most bosses cannot be damaged by bump attacks and must instead be defeated with the fire spell, so managing magic becomes central to progress through the island's towns and dungeons.

t_3ba4f653a124.overview: Developed by Soft Machine and published by Varie, Grand Master is a top-down action role-playing game with a Western fantasy setting. Rody, commander of the royal bodyguards, sets out after Dante the Demon King is resurrected and Princess Serene is kidnapped. Instead of an overworld, a world map offers five stages, each built around finding the key that opens the door to its boss, with chests holding weapons, accessories and healing items. The order in which the stages are cleared decides which branching story scenes appear in anime-style cutscenes, and missing the right scene leads to a bad ending. A long final stage follows. Experience levels cap at 10, and the arsenal includes a sword, a throwing axe, a rod that blasts the area around the hero, and a morning star that can also pull him across small gaps.

t_3babc8e51aa5.overview: Hummer Team put the eight drivers of Super Mario Kart into a one-on-one fighting game built on a slightly altered Street Fighter II engine, published by Ge De Industry. The roster is Mario (named Mari), Luigi, Peach, Yoshi (Yossy), Toad (Kinopio), Donkey Kong Jr. (Donkey), a Koopa Troopa (Nokonoko) and Bowser (Koopa). Controls follow the Street Fighter pattern of punches, kicks and special moves, and every character except Nokonoko can throw a projectile; other specials include charge attacks, Peach's hair whip, Yossy's tongue attack and Koopa's tail flop. Solo play offers five difficulty levels, and a versus mode for two players begins when the D-pad on a second controller is pressed. Some backgrounds are taken from Little Nemo: The Dream Master, and several tunes are remixed from Super Mario Kart.

t_3bc106bce841.overview: This FamicomBox dump carries the Famicom version of 1943, the vertically scrolling shooter from Capcom, which was arranged for the console rather than ported directly from the arcade game. Play runs through 24 stages of air and sea combat, and a large fuel meter serves as the plane's single life. The Famicom version adds permanent upgrades: statistic points go into offensive and defensive power, maximum fuel, and special weapons and how long they last, so only a few weapons are available at the start. A charged shot fires a laser, password entry lets a session begin partway through, and the arcade's two-player cooperative play was dropped. Enemy warships and battlefields carry fictional names in place of the historical ones, and the aircraft were redesigned so their nationality is hard to tell.

t_3bfd2bc63f65.overview: Bowling is simulated here with a choice of 30 lanes and room for up to five players, recreating the feel of a bowling league. Each bowler can be either male or female and throws a ball weighing anywhere from 7 to 15 pounds. Before every throw, players change their lane positioning, determine how strong the throw is and set how much the ball curves. Single-player and multiplayer play are both supported.

t_3c5ff2017b2b.overview:
Galactic Crusader is a space shooter in which the player captains a living, metamorphic Star Ship that can transform from a huge flying insect into a metallic destroyer. The ship fights through squadron after squadron of alien fortifications on the way to a final confrontation with an all-powerful enemy. Each time the ship takes damage it transforms into a different ship, and it explodes when its metamorphic capabilities run out. A Life Force Generator restores full metamorphic power, and passing through a Star Gate earns an extra ship.

Firing devices are gained by connecting with a Device Carrier and can be attached to the front or rear of the ship or launched as detached firing stations that break up enemy formations. Weapon capsules add pulsar waves, plasma blasts or a corkscrew firing pattern. At the end of each world, a large boss waits, including Cubicus, Gorous, Spirous and the Dragon King.

t_3c66abdb0e52.overview:
Stopping the crime baron Cain from spreading a deadly new chemical called Nuke is the primary mission facing Detroit's cyborg officer. The title supports one or two participants, with two players taking alternating turns upon losing a life or completing a level.

Controlling the titular law enforcement officer, the player navigates through industrial and corporate environments centered around side-scrolling platforming and shooting mechanics. Progress requires walking, jumping, and shooting or punching while managing the officer's inertia. Along with battling Cain's hostile forces, the player must destroy at least sixty percent of the Nuke on each level and make physical contact to arrest at least sixty percent of designated criminals before facing Cain and the new RoboCop 2 prototype.

t_3c9c1740cec7.overview: Built around Japanese professional baseball, the game has the player choose one of 12 teams and chase the pennant. Team funds rise with wins and fall with losses, and the money goes toward raising player salaries or arranging trades, which succeed only on favorable terms. A batter hit by a pitch can start a brawl settled with a fighting-game style health meter, and the loser may be removed from the game. Other options include pinch runners, defensive shifts, four levels of base-runner leads, and day or night games. An All-Star mode lets players pick their own squads, including teams of former players. Venues are the Eastern Dome, the Western Stadium with its lucky zone, and the asymmetric American Stadium. One or two players can compete.

t_3d0401f67084.overview: Murobo, a burly animal-man nicknamed "The Goddess Hero," sets out with companions met along the way to save the world from an evil demon in an action RPG. A quintet of other heroes, among them Lucia and Sylvie, join the party, occasionally swapping in and out until about the middle of the adventure. Random battles appear on a screen divided like a five-piece pie, with each slice tied to one party member; a character whose slice holds foes fights a duel resembling the battles of Zelda II: The Adventure of Link, while an empty slice skips that turn. If a character dies, an ally must finish off the monster responsible. Terrain matters as well: caves have slippery floors, and in deserts the hero must keep jumping to avoid sinking into the sand.

t_3d119bdb16e8.overview: The adventure begins in the Kingdom of Faria, where a soldier from a foreign land wakes up at an inn. A wizard has abducted the princess, and the king has offered her hand in marriage to anyone who rescues her. The quest grows from there: a celebration is spoiled by poisoned food, a cure must be fetched from a distant town, and the king is turned to stone. The world is divided into towns, where people provide information and items; an overworld, where encounters shift to a separate combat screen; and dungeons that mix fighting with increasingly complex mazes. Combat is action-based, with the hero moving around the screen swinging a sword, supported by items such as bombs and a bow and arrows.

t_3d22c01b85be.overview: Simba's early adventures from the animated film play out in a side-scrolling platformer in which the player guides the young lion cub through a series of stages. Simba must leap, climb, run and descend from platform to platform, and he defeats enemies mainly by jumping on them. His roar draws on a meter that must be fully charged to be effective, and a full-strength roar can stun enemies. On other systems the story continues with Simba as an adult using combat moves, but on the NES only the cub levels are present, and those levels are considerably shortened compared with other versions. The short death jingle is also absent, with the level music simply continuing.

t_3d29deb56e77.overview: Searching for the lost treasure of Captain Silver, a young former first mate fights through a side-scrolling platform adventure loosely based on Treasure Island. Adapted from a sword-slashing arcade game, the Famicom version changes a lot: the hero now has a health gauge, refilled by picking up hearts, and can take more than one hit before losing a life, while some ordinary enemies also need several blows. Every weapon power-up can be bought in item shops and switched through a sub-menu. The stages are different from the arcade original, with new bosses such as Frankenstein's monster and a giant octopus. Houses and rooms can be entered, where old ladies offer advice such as an enemy's weak point, though some of them are hostile and lay a curse, for example cutting the hero's health in half.

t_3d2b1cdd2b3d.overview: A sequel to the arcade game Balubalouk no Densetsu, the Famicom action game follows Jason, a young archaeologist, when a dark comet that once threatened the earth returns. After discovering a book of prophecy, Jason sets out to collect the five pieces of the Aura Star, which are hidden in five ruins and must be reunited in a sixth, final temple. Jason carries no weapon, so he relies on traps that shoot at enemies and on limited items such as paralysis medicine. Touching an enemy or falling into lava costs a life, and some stages hide secrets and alternate routes. An oracle supplies passwords for continuing, and a trap near the end can take away every item and send the player back to the first dungeon.

t_3d39e321dbb3.overview: Stages in Life Force - Salamander alternate between horizontal and vertical scrolling as a lone starfighter blasts its way through waves of enemies and bosses. The first player flies the Vic Viper, while a second player can join in simultaneously at the controls of the Lord British. Certain enemies leave capsules behind when destroyed, and collecting them advances a Gradius-style power bar, so the player chooses which upgrade to activate rather than receiving it instantly. Many of the power-ups can be combined, and option power-ups are limited to two. The levels and bosses differ in part from the arcade original, with some removed to make way for new content.

t_3d492d0e3b4e.overview: Based on a manga and anime about an underdog high school baseball team and the drama that surrounds it, this baseball game pairs ordinary matches with an optional story mode. Choosing Dramatic Mode from the title screen menu opens a story mode that depicts scenes from the manga, and it also adds character portraits to the main game. On the field, pitching and batting are viewed from directly behind the batter, and whenever the ball is hit the player moves the entire group of fielders at once. The athletes are drawn in a super-deformed style. The original story follows the third-string squad of a powerhouse high school's baseball club, a group of players written off by the team.

t_3d57328da92f.overview:
The Miracle Piano Teaching System functions as an educational program designed to instruct users in playing the piano. Using a dedicated electronic keyboard connected to the console along with a standard controller, the software presents a curriculum divided into thirty-six instructional sections. Users begin on a setup screen where they select their age category, which adjusts reading text between child and adult formats, and choose a section to start their study. Chalkboard screens introduce tasks, provide performance commentary, and explain musical concepts.

Instruction encompasses note reading, rhythm, finger positions, and two-handed technique. The program analyzes input to detect errors and supplies targeted exercises. Training tools include visual pointers that advance only upon receiving correct pitches, a rhythm practice option that sounds accurate tones regardless of keys struck, and a metronome. Learners also utilize minigames such as Roboman and a duck-themed Shooting Gallery, alongside a dedicated Practice Room that supports separate hand drills and orchestral accompaniment.

t_3d6c5f6ea731.overview: Turn-based strategy battles in the vein of Fire Emblem and Shining Force drive this role-playing game. The story opens in the town of Astholm, protected by a sapphire held by the priestess Firis, one of six such priestesses. When Firis is kidnapped by the henchmen of Ezelkiel, a man bent on collecting the priestesses to revive an ancient evil, the hero sworn to protect the town sets out to rescue her, and the quest grows into a struggle over the world's other priestesses and their stones. Six main characters each lead an army of six soldiers, mixing Heroes, Wizards, Fighters and Archers. Between battles the party explores towns to buy items and talk with residents, and monster dens on the overworld keep spawning enemies until a unit neutralizes them.

t_3d7d61820ee6.overview:
Players engage in the sport of golf, taking into account environmental and physical factors such as the wind and the angle at which the ball is struck. Progress throughout the experience is maintained through the use of a password system.

Three distinct modes are available to select from. Participants can compete in a standard tournament mode, or they can practice their skills across two training modes. The game supports participation for up to four people.

t_3da677044f2c.overview: Three complete NES games share this cartridge, released in Europe and chosen from a selection screen at power-on. In Super Mario Bros., Mario crosses the Mushroom Kingdom to rescue Princess Toadstool from King Koopa, working through eight worlds of four stages each. Tetris drops randomly chosen tetrominoes into a well, with the next piece shown in a preview window; A-Type play chases the highest score while B-Type play asks for 25 cleared lines. Nintendo World Cup is a soccer game with six-player teams, up to five super shots per half, and fields of sand, ice or dirt that affect how players and the ball move. Its tournament mode offers 13 teams, and with the Four Score up to four players can compete.

t_3db247222207.overview: Tengen's planned NES conversion of Atari's 3D racer survives only as a very early demo in which many features had not yet been implemented. The ordinary stretches of road are drawn line by line with the scanline technique used in earlier NES driving games, while the track's special features, its corners and its loop, play back as pre-animated sequences. Those sequences are not purely passive: the car can still be steered left and right while they run, and the track has left and right edges that the game checks against, so it is possible to fall off the loop. Emulators show tearing in the road and other graphical errors, but the demo runs smoothly on real hardware.

t_3de0858949d7.overview: In the 666th year of the world of magic, the Crimson Kingdom faces destruction at the hands of the Black Slayer, a demon king who rules an underground empire. Randy, an infant son of the Crimson Emperor, escaped to another dimension and has grown up training as a wizard king; now he must gather the Five Crimson Family Seals and defeat the Black Slayer. The journey spans six stages made up mainly of forests, castles and caverns. Randy attacks with an unlimited supply of fireballs, and beating each stage's boss teaches new magic, from Twin Fire and Blizzard to Rock Breaker, Overdrive and Thunder, including a spell that freezes lava. Items such as the Jump Boots and Cape of Protection raise his strength and endurance.

t_3e0387b91f84.overview: Sucked into an alternate universe, a boy and his girlfriend must find their way back home, but a magnificent castle made up of many game worlds blocks their progress. Each stage is an overhead action puzzle in which the pictures on tiles are connected to build a route to the exit, while enemies on every stage can be destroyed for extra loot. A strict time limit of 100 seconds applies to each puzzle, rewarding quick solutions. Play starts with three lives, and a life is lost when time runs out or when a monster touches the character. The first player controls the boy, and a second player can control the girl. Enemies include springs, rollers, witches and zombies.

t_3e3f629d399d.overview: Two fairies, Tam and Rit, set out to rescue their mother after the once calm and quiet Fairy Village is attacked. Armed with magic rods, the pair clear single-screen levels built from platforms, ladders, monsters and, later, tunnels. A rod does not kill outright: it leaves an enemy immobilized and crying, and the fairy can then grasp it in a magic force field and smash it down repeatedly until it disappears and leaves a power-up behind. Instead of jumping, the fairies rely on ladders, and each can conjure one custom ladder above or below to reach another platform. Up to two players can work through the 40 scenes of this home conversion of the arcade game.

t_3ea3bf7a9871.overview: Adapted from the Japanese Captain Tsubasa game for the Famicom, this Westernized version replaces the manga's hero with Robin Field, a blonde young adult, and gives the players a more Western look. Robin must fight his way from the junior league all the way to the finals of the World Cup. Matches are not controlled directly in real time; instead, the player chooses actions from a timed list of commands and the results play out as animated scenes on screen. Role-playing elements give the players skill levels, and some goalkeepers are strong enough to stop the special shot of Robin. Progress is kept with a password system that uses Latin letters in place of the original's Japanese characters.

t_3ec175e99bd3.overview:
Extinguishing every flame let loose by the wizard Druidle serves as the primary goal across the frozen territory of Coolmint Island. The Queen of the Fairies summons the apprentice wizard Dana to protect the land. Players guide Dana across a grid-based landscape, walking horizontally, scaling single-height blocks, and pushing ice cubes into fires or dropping them from overhead to put out the flames. Dana can also create or remove an ice block beside his feet in the direction he faces; new ice attaches sideways to neighboring objects.

Pipes permit travel between areas, while jars catch fire when a flame sits on top of them. A burning jar cannot be put out and melts any ice placed on it. The campaign contains ten worlds of ten stages each, using passwords to record progress. Completing all one hundred levels provides a code for fifty bonus stages and a sound test. An included stage editor also lets players construct custom puzzles.

t_3ece14544d11.overview: Based on a story by mystery novelist Misa Yamamura, this murder-mystery adventure follows a game designer who comes to Ryoanji temple in Kyoto for an event promoting his new game. A series of killings soon begins, and astonishingly the murders unfold exactly like the plot of the next game he is planning. Inspector Kariya of the Kyoto Prefectural Police Headquarters marks the designer as a suspect, so with the help of Katherine, a partner with outstanding powers of deduction, he begins investigating the case on his own. The investigation is played through a command-selection system, gathering testimony and clues to uncover the real culprit.

t_3ee4a2d428c0.overview: Framed for robbing a bank by Black Bomber, Bomberman has been locked away in prison and must bomb his way out. The game follows the familiar Bomberman formula: each prison room is filled with blocks and enemies, and placing bombs clears away the blocks and destroys the enemies in the way. Some blocks hide power-ups. Alongside the single-player escape, Vs Mode lets two players compete against each other, while Battle Mode is a three-player contest that requires the NES Four Score accessory.

t_3f026e83eabb.overview: Leaving action behind, the third Famicom installment becomes a role-playing game whose storyline stays close to the original manga. Kenshiro recruits companions such as Rin and Bat, forming a party of up to four, and defeats ordinary enemies to gain levels before taking on the bosses. Regular encounters are fought by the whole party, but boss battles must be fought one-on-one. Travel between distant areas relies on maps that are bought and used to warp, and the battle music shifts among four tiers to match the importance of each fight. The quest is for a single player.

t_3f4328098229.overview: Johnson and Berry, two veteran soldiers who have come through numerous small and large battles, face their hardest assignment yet in this shooter. Their commander has called for reinforcements in a wartime emergency, but an enemy frontier military post sits along the shortcut the reinforcing army must take. With time running out, the commander sends a guerrilla strike to destroy the post so the reinforcements can pass through, and the storm-trooper pair is the only team with a chance of success and survival. The mission is to reach that frontier post and wipe it out.

t_3f667ac15502.overview: Ei-How Yang developed this 1996 Famicom platformer for J.Y. Company as a bootleg port of the SNES version of Mickey Mania. The port follows the original game but is incomplete: it contains five stages, each taken from the original and divided into ten sequences, and many sequences are missing, including the entire Lonesome Ghosts level. The levels are based on Mickey Mouse cartoons from 1928 to 1990. The player guides Mickey through them, jumping on enemies and throwing marbles. The loading screen, animation and music between screens appear to come from the SNES version, and a level select can be opened from the title screen.

t_3fc50fad189e.overview: Stock trading meets life simulation in this 1988 Famicom release from Sofel. The goal is to raise money through the wise purchasing and selling of various types of stock, with news reports and crude oil prices helping to determine how shares move. Trading involves a virtual newspaper, a telephone and even a personal computer, and the game provides tutorials on how the market works. Raising enough money at certain checkpoints allows the player to gain and keep a girlfriend, who later becomes a wife and provides children, while home life can be upgraded from a studio apartment to a terraced house and finally a mansion with its own Olympic-sized swimming pool.

t_4009838563c2.overview: Planned as the English release of Radia Senki: Reimeihen, a Japanese action role-playing game from Tecmo, this prototype follows an amnesiac hero who joins a cast of characters trying to stop a political leader's domination of their world. Exploration uses overhead environments, and battles start when the hero walks over an invisible trigger tile; fights play out in real time without a change of screen. The player directly controls one of the five party characters and can issue commands such as fight or regroup to the others, or even tell the party to act dead to avoid enemies. Spells that damage, heal or affect enemy stats are learned from scrolls, and the number of casts grows as characters gain levels. Town stores buy and sell items, weapons and armor, and the heroes can rest and save at any bed.

t_40368c46c255.overview: Milk, a pink blob, sets out to find his fiancée Yogurt while his teal rival Nuts competes for her affection. Every screen is scattered with fruit, and gathering all of it opens a previously locked house door where Yogurt waits. Milk can jump a short distance vertically or horizontally to cross pits and can climb the rope bridges hanging in mid-air on most levels. Touching Nuts or other hazards costs a life and restarts the level, and the game ends when all three lives are gone. The 50 levels can each be skipped freely with the select button, and a level editor mode allows the first stage to be redesigned. Single-player and two-player play are supported.

t_4037a00fac65.overview: A heavily armed car sits at the center of this vertically scrolling shooter, which plays out as a desperate getaway. The hero makes a living as an unbeatable street racer and courier, and is hired to obtain the Battle Formula, a secret weapon newly developed by a terrorist group. The moment the engine starts, alarms ring out, and the escape crosses the desert and the highway, with the Battle Formula at times transforming into a boat or a fighter plane. Driving toward the top of the screen speeds the car up, while dropping back slows it down. A forward-fixed shot works together with a roof-mounted turret whose firing angle is changed with a button that doubles as the special-weapon button. Red trailers carry power items, and blue trailers carry single-use special items.

t_4037a5f09918.overview: The PAL counterpart of Super C, Probotector II: Return of the Evil Forces replaces the main characters and some of the enemies with robots. Its gameplay and graphics follow the NES port of the first game, with the same power-ups, including the Rapid Bullets, Barrier and Special items. The premise has alien forces taking over an allied military base and possessing most of its troops. Up to two players can fight simultaneously through a mix of stages, three of which are unique to the NES version: a high-tech base, a mountain and an alien nest, all vertically scrolling. New bosses appear along the way, including a new final boss that differs from the arcade original.
t_4037a5f09918.official: THE ALIENS ARE BACK! In the year 2634, Earth has finally escaped from the hand of Black Magic, one year after the end of the war with the mysterious alien army... Or has it? One day, a strange radio message comes in from General Hal of the Federation troops as he heads for the South American base ruins in preparation for the seventh GX Army maneuvers.

t_405e424e37e0.overview: Gunjin Shogi, the Japanese military board game, receives a sumo makeover in this Famicom release. The board becomes a sumo ring, and pieces take on sumo names: the flag becomes the gunbai, the referee's fan; the mine becomes the oyakata, the stable master; and the spy becomes the mono-ii, the judges' objection. In the underlying game, each side places its pieces face down so the opponent cannot see them, and when two pieces meet, a referee compares their ranks to decide the outcome. That need for an impartial referee makes the game well suited to a computer adaptation.

t_408945853f1c.overview: Released only in Japan, this side-scrolling platform action game casts the player as a scientist named Jackson, whose plane comes down on Monster Island. The creatures of the island have taken the special drug Macho Max from his plane, and Jackson must cross the island with a rifle while recovering it. The journey runs through six zones divided into twelve areas, each zone ending with a boss. In his normal form, Jackson dies from a single hit. After obtaining the drug and scoring at least 5,000 points, he can transform into Macho Man, converting every 5,000 points into one hit point. In that form he trades the gun for a punch that deals eight times the damage, plus waves of energy fired from his chest that cost one hit point each. The same game was also released under the title Amagon.

t_40d4f112e3c9.overview: Third in the Deep Dungeon role-playing series from HummingBirdSoft, this entry follows a young man who leaves his village to become a hero and is drawn into a crisis when the country's king and princess are taken. Unlike its predecessors, the adventure spans a world of multiple dungeons and many towns, explored in first-person. The swordsman hero can form a party with up to three companions, each created as a ranger, magician or priest; dismissed companions can only be replaced by pre-made characters found in dungeons. Stat gains on leveling up can be adjusted, random encounters stop when the party far outlevels an area, and defeated enemies award gold. Characters sometimes fumble their equipped weapon, wasting a turn, and the game ends if the hero is defeated.

t_415d4dfcec26.overview: An amusement park called Crazyland is the stage for this side-scrolling action game, with some vertically scrolling sections, in which the hero sets out to rescue a captured girlfriend and defeat the mastermind behind it all. The hero attacks by kicking a ball: it flies straight ahead from the ground, angles upward when Up is held, and goes straight up when kicked with Up during a jump. Unusually, each hit taken makes the ball stronger, progressing through a two-way ball, a soccer ball and a two-way soccer ball; a hit in the final state, or a fall into a pit or water, costs a life. Some stages are ridden in a mine cart that speeds up while B is held. Coins, hearts, clocks that freeze enemies, and a bird helper can be collected, and a password system is included.

t_4162c84100f8.overview: Despite its title, no fighting takes place in this golf game; the challenge lies in steering shots around sand traps, water hazards, rough ground and trees. Four golfers with different advantages and disadvantages are available: Birdie Tommy, Pretty Eri, Miracle Chosuke and Big Jumbo. Pretty Eri has limited range but the easiest control, with control referring to the length of the aiming guide, while Big Jumbo has the best range but the worst control and Miracle Chosuke has average attributes. Two courses are available, the United States and Japan, ranging from relatively straightforward fairways to elaborate arrangements of sand traps; the United States course is modeled after the PGA West Stadium Course. Single-player and multiplayer play are supported.

t_4180e291ab78.overview:
Players control the hero Kickle, using his special freezing breath to overcome environmental hazards and enemies across frozen islands. After the Wicked Wizard King covers the Fantasy Kingdom in ice and imprisons its residents, Kickle ventures forth to rescue them. The single-player objective in each stage centers on navigating the layout to collect all the red Dream Bags while avoiding harmful adversaries.

Kickle can breathe cold air to transform certain foes into blocks of ice. These frozen enemies serve multiple functions, allowing players to build walkways across water or push them to defeat opposing hostiles. Kickle can also manifest an ice pillar directly ahead of himself to block paths.

t_4190cfc8a3ac.overview: Set on the planet Landorin, this NES installment in the Turrican series takes its premise from a world where The Machine still rules the surface even after its evil satellite was destroyed. The surviving Landorins have retreated into secret caves underground while machines and mutants search the ruins for the way in. A final radio distress call reaches Turrican, a man with the courage to face the hordes, who sets out to free the last survivors. The conversion makes many changes compared with the earlier games: it offers four difficulty settings, lets the hero run faster, and drops both the time limit and checkpoints, so a death means restarting the level.
t_4190cfc8a3ac.official: You are Bren McGuire, on a United Planets Freedom Forces mission to save the peaceful planet Katakis from the Machine, source of all that is cruel and evil in the universe. The only weapon on your side is the state-of-the-art Turrican Assault Suit. Equipped with multiple weapons, including the incredible Freeze-beam, that temporarily immobilizes almost any enemy, the Turrican Assault Suit gives one man the power of an entire army.

t_419645d632dd.overview: A pet chimpanzee whose human family has been kidnapped drinks a chemical concoction and hulks out into a muscle-bound brawler in this action platformer from SETA, preserved as a prototype after its cancellation. The title screen shows the family carried off by a green-clad mafioso type who kicks the ape to the curb. Across three levels the hero dashes to top speed along slopes, then grabs enemies and finishes them with suplexes, giant swings and piledrivers, each move animated uniquely for each foe. Platforming and movement challenges fill most sections, the second level hurtles him between arenas by rail, and the final level is built around a series of transporters leading to the kidnapper.

t_41bf1f954195.overview: After General Guemon and his dark forces invade the Kingdom of Guldred and kill its king, the knight Gazem flees to Chesterfield Island with the deposed queen and her daughter Karen. Guemon's forces sink their ship, kill the queen and abduct Karen, and the dying Gazem passes word of the kingdom's plight to a brave knight named Kein. In this action RPG, Kein must endure eight stages of mazes, knights, dark forces and battles on land, on sea and in the sky to restore peace to Guldred. Health is restored by picking up jars left by defeated enemies, and collected Metal buys magic spells and other important equipment from the island's few inhabitants.

t_41d1b0419074.overview: A pirated Famicom conversion of the SNES game Donkey Kong Country 2: Diddy's Kong Quest, Super Donkey Kong 2 keeps controls, graphics and audio similar to the original but downgraded to suit the NES hardware. The platforming centers on Diddy Kong alone. With Dixie Kong absent there is no partner to fall back on, so a single hit from an enemy is fatal. Several elements of the SNES game carry over, including banana coins, crates and the K-O-N-G letters to collect along the way. The adventure is very short, however, with only three levels in total.

t_42231aaac459.overview: Rather than a standalone game, Top Hit 20 Vol. 1 is an expansion cartridge for Karaoke Studio, a Famicom karaoke system packaged with a microphone peripheral capable of detecting a human voice. The smaller cartridge plugs directly into the slot on the back of the Karaoke Studio subsystem and adds twenty songs that are not contained on the original unit. Play works the same way as with the built-in songs: the singer follows along in karaoke fashion while the screen displays each song's lyrics over a graphical depiction of its theme, and the performance is scored on accuracy of singing. The cassette is meant to be used together with the Karaoke Studio subsystem rather than on its own.

t_4252d04aa297.overview: Set on a futuristic battlefield, this vertically scrolling shooter casts the player as a commanding officer leading the blue forces against the red forces. The objective is to make it all the way to the end of the battlefield using the Genesis, a warship that fires missiles, while avoiding or shooting enemy helicopters, infantrymen and tanks. Pressing the A and B buttons together calls in reinforcements from the player's own army, and a special weapon can absorb enemy units and add them to that army. An enemy spaceship shaped like a UFO sometimes appears and tries to grab a friendly unit and escape with it, and it will also engage a friendly helicopter in air-to-air battle.

t_42b1df2601d3.overview: Under this name, Hummer Team's 1992 Famicom port of Street Fighter II: The World Warrior, published by Cony Soft as Yoko Soft, avoids the trademarked title on its title screen and cartridge label. The one-on-one fighter is a simplified version of the original with four selectable characters: Ryu, Chun-Li, Guile and Zangief. Each keeps nearly all of their special moves, and the player fights through the other selectable characters in a preset order before the final battle with Dictator, whose name is misspelled as Viga. Only one continue is allowed, no difficulty selection is offered, and the computer opponents are tough. One version adds an invincibility cheat.

t_42d154a8789c.overview: Rather than an action game, this 1989 Sachen cartridge is an English tutor aimed at children who speak and read Chinese. Lessons are presented as a series of exercises for young learners studying the basics of English. After completing some exercises, the student is treated to a mini-game, which Sachen would eventually flesh out into the standalone release Pyramid. Apart from sharing most of its name and a cameo by the penguin from Dong Dong Nao 1, it has no relation to that earlier penguin action game. On multicarts the program appears under the title Middle School English.

t_42dd21e34c6d.overview:
Players control the title character, navigating hostile environments while engaging adversaries through direct combat and shooting. Based on the 1987 motion picture, the single-player experience combines elements of side-scrolling brawling with run-and-gun mechanics.

Throughout the adventure, the protagonist advances across stages by confronting opposing threats using hand-to-hand attacks alongside projectile weapons. The overall objective centers on battling through waves of enemies while surviving the hazards found across each area.

t_4321a0bc403a.overview:
Piloting the starship Caesar, the player shoots down waves of hostile forces threatening the galactic empire. This vertically scrolling journey spans sixteen stages set across a massive space station. The craft moves across the screen and fires upward to strike both grounded targets and airborne enemies arriving from above. At certain points, the ship can enter a trap zone, slipping beneath the station structure to evade incoming fire. Each stage ends with a confrontation against a supercomputer boss called Starbrain, while a Big Starbrain variant appears at the end of stages 4, 8, 12, and 16.

Destroying special markers releases power capsules that bolster the starship's capabilities. Collecting capsules enhances speed, strengthens weapon output, and alters firing patterns. Gathering multiple items enables the craft to transform, fire behind itself, and eventually shoot in five directions. A third capsule grants a shield absorbing up to five hits, while a fourth upgrade eliminates flying enemies.

t_432b7af2fddd.overview: In this side-scrolling action game, Demon Kogure roams the Famicom world to rescue fellow members captured by the god Zeus, his sworn enemy. The goal is to defeat Zeus, recover the stolen demon scripture, and hold a Black Mass concert at the Akuma Temple. Each of the five stages holds one captive member, freed by defeating a gatekeeper and obtaining a key. A timer steadily runs down and is restored by collecting a blood item, while money bags gathered along the way buy weapon upgrades and other items. Every stage also has an instrument item that must be purchased. The game ends after a single loop through the five stages.

t_433612a39701.overview:
Master Higgins' girlfriend Tina has just been kidnapped by the Evil Witch Doctor's persistent followers, and rescuing her means crossing eight perilous islands controlled by monster minions. The side-scrolling platform action adds an inventory system: each extra hammer collected is stored as a reserve in the inventory rather than upgrading the current weapon. The checkpoint system has been eliminated.

Suit cards hidden in eggs summon dinosaurs for Higgins to ride, four in all. A blue camptosaurus attacks with its tail and can walk on ice without sliding, a pteranodon flies over obstacles and drops stones, and an elasmosaurus is the only dinosaur that can survive in underwater stages.

t_4369a072d108.overview: Tecmo's action role-playing game begins as its hero regains consciousness in a forest, suffering from amnesia. Rescued by Darus, a wandering mage, he and his ally witness the crash of a plane and find the unconscious Lefis, whose stepbrother Gadiss seeks world domination and is looking for the keys to the sacred Radia Tower, whose power could reshape the world called Lemuria. The player controls one of five characters through overhead environments, and battles begin on an invisible trigger tile and are fought in real time. Party members not under direct control can be issued commands, including an order to act dead to avoid enemies. Spells are learned from scrolls, enemies drop items that can be sold, and the heroes can rest and save in any bed.

t_438ec9a591f9.overview: French-language edition of Saint Seiya: Ōgon Densetsu, with the game's menus and character dialogue translated. Adapting the anime, the story follows Seiya from the opening of the saga through the battles against the gold knights in the twelve houses. Because that arc had not yet finished when the game was made, the producers invented an original ending: some gold knights are absent, and the Grand Pope does not have the same identity as in the series. Play alternates between horizontally scrolling exploration phases and command-based battles against bosses. In those fights, cosmos is allotted each turn among attack, spirit, defense and movement, and the combat balance makes even minor enemies hard to beat. The versus mode of the Japanese original was removed from this version.

t_43f24e49f8bd.overview: Built on Takara's Transformers toys and animated series, this action shooter casts Ultra Magnus, the Cybertron city commander, against the Destron forces. The story begins in the era of the 1986 animated film, when the dying Convoy entrusts the Matrix to Ultra Magnus, and time tunnels carry him back to the period of the original series and forward to the later 2010 series. Ten stages mix horizontal scrolling with vertically scrolling time-tunnel stages. Ultra Magnus can switch between robot form and a trailer form that sits lower but cannot jump and fires only straight up or diagonally forward and down. A single touch from an enemy or its shot is fatal. Power-ups give a two-way shot, a barrier and free flight, and clearing the game after collecting the letter marks that spell out RODIMUS lets the next loop be played as Rodimus Convoy.

t_43f2fe3f92dd.overview:
Sky Kid provides horizontally scrolling shooter gameplay featuring up to two players. Participants operate biplanes piloted by Baron, in red, and Max, in blue, flying through levels filled with hostile air and ground units. Missions challenge pilots to locate and bomb specific targets, which include battleships, aircraft carriers, factories, and headquarters. Because the aircraft do not begin with explosives, players must collect a bomb along the flight path before reaching the objective, then land back at base.

Pilots use a machine gun to fire upon enemy forces and can execute a loop maneuver to evade hazards or reveal secrets. Reaching mission objectives requires flying through enemy defenses. Points are awarded for destroying opposing units and successfully bombing targets, with bonus points granted at the end of a mission for completely demolishing targets.

t_44317f95c5fa.overview: Five-card draw poker is the core of this adult card game. Before a game begins, the player picks which of three girls to play against: Ruka, Ayami or Mari. Hands follow standard poker rules: five cards are dealt, the player may give up or bet, exchange selected cards for new ones, and then bet a second time. Winning unlocks reward images, with the later ones far more suggestive than the first. The game is a revamp of Poker Jingling, a 1990 game by Idea-Tek, with completely reworked reward sequences and added images. A code entered on the title screen loads a slideshow of the reward pictures.

t_443fcb33514f.overview: Adapted from the arcade game Mahjong Block Jongbou, this Famicom title combines the tile game Mahjong with a block-breaking game in the style of Breakout. The player bounces a ball around a Mahjong table filled with concealed tiles. Tiles that are knocked loose fall, and the player collects the ones wanted for the hand by passing underneath them as they drop. A stage is over either when all of the tiles have fallen or when the player completes a winning hand.

t_445a011289aa.overview: Piloting the transforming VF-1S Valkyrie, the player battles through space and then infiltrates the Britai ship to destroy its core, which clears the round. The Valkyrie switches among Fighter, GERWALK and Battroid forms, each with different performance: the Fighter scrolls quickly but moves slowly, the GERWALK sits in between, and the Battroid scrolls slowly, moves quickly and can turn to fire backward. A power gauge drains over time and from enemy shots and ramming attacks, and an empty gauge costs a life. Four kinds of special targets serve as items, collected by flying over them, granting bonus points, restored power, homing missiles or an extra life. Inside the enemy ship a timer runs, with a bonus for reaching the core in time.

t_4461775a81c3.overview: A Famicom reprogramming of the Game Boy title Balloon Kid, this version swaps the original cast and plot for Hello Kitty and changes parts of the visuals. The balloon-flight play carries over: the heroine floats on a pair of balloons and flaps upward, can detach them to walk or jump and reinflate them after landing safely, and collects balloons through each stage while avoiding enemies. The Game Boy release's Balloon Trip and battle modes were removed; in their place two players take alternating turns, with the other player taking over from the same spot when one misses. Other changes include new stage-clear animations, a conversation scene before the ending, altered enemy and background art, music rearranged for the Famicom, and a lower score threshold for extra continues.

t_44a9b9214a69.overview: Billed as its predecessor turned upside down, this dice puzzle sequel again has the player arranging dice into rows for elimination. This time the character stands on top of the dice, and the growing pile will crush him unless the correct combinations are made to clear it. Only series such as five of the same number or a run from 1 to 5 can be eliminated, and the kind of series decides how many rows disappear. Mode 1 can be played alone for a high score, against a second player, or in a quest against the computer. In Mode 2 the pile is already stocked and cannot be rearranged, so dice in the top layer must match the die shown above the playfield; the first player to reach the bottom wins, and this mode is played only as a match or quest.

t_44d2348b3c9a.overview: Armed with a light gun, the player takes the role of a police officer who has to shoot bandits across three stages: the street outside a bank, a warehouse, and the inside of the bank. Criminals pop out of windows and the front door, while in the warehouse ninjas hide behind objects, dash from side to side or drop from the ceiling, and some of them hold hostages who must not be shot. The final stage brings back bank robbers lurking behind obstacles, again mixed with hostages. Shooting 20 enemies clears the first stage, and each later stage demands five more. The player starts with five lives, losing one after taking three enemy shots or after hitting hostages three times.

t_451662f49442.overview: Often summed up as a four-way take on Tetris, this puzzle game puts the player in control of a block at the center of the screen that can move and rotate freely. Larger blocks move inward from each side of the screen and attach to the central block, then change color depending on their distance from the center. Completing a colored ring clears that layer along with every block inside it, while the blocks outside move inward. Play ends when a newly appearing block overlaps the player's structure.

t_454af1685991.overview: Players again race through life from kindergarten to old age on a board, with one to four people taking part and computer opponents now optional. The main aim is to hold the most money at the finish, and players are ranked by their savings, while final money, stats and occupation decide which ending follows. Three parameters, intelligence, stamina and luck, shape each life; after high school, university entrance is decided purely by these values, and careers rise or fall with hidden promotion points, a fired player being forced into part-time work. Mini-games include a ball-toss contest timed to a power gauge, a diving event to collect coins or land on a target, a singer audition and casino horse-race betting. Stocks and diamonds add to a player's fortune.

t_457eaf260840.overview: Released in North America as Whomp 'Em, the Japanese original of this Jaleco platformer is a sequel to Saiyūki World and, like it, draws on the novel Journey to the West, with Sun Wukong as the hero. Its subtitle translates roughly as "Evil Spirit of Heaven." After the first stage, the remaining six can be played in any order, and each revolves around an element such as fire or water. Clearing a stage awards a new weapon, much as in the original Mega Man series. The North American release edited the sprites and graphics to remove the Journey to the West references, turning the hero into a Native American and moving the setting to the Old West. Play is single-player.

t_459609623cc1.overview: A revision of Cony Soft's crossover fighter World Heroes 2, the Pro edition shows its name on the title screen and adds an option mode not found in the regular version, where the player can listen to the music, set the timer and make player 1 invincible. The fighting is otherwise that of the original: 12 playable characters drawn from other franchises, including Ryu and Chun-Li from Street Fighter, Mario and Bowser, Sonic, Leonardo of the Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles, Haggar from Final Fight, Andy and Mai from Fatal Fury, and Goku from Dragon Ball. The Street Fighter II and Fatal Fury characters and their stages are reused from Cony's other pirate fighting games, and after a fight won by a human player, the victor appears in a victory pose with a single quote shared by every character.

t_45d177d8924e.overview:
Spanning 50 stages, this action-puzzle platformer presents multi-story brick environments filled with ladders, suspended hand-to-hand bars, and trapdoors. Players control a Galactic Commando tasked with collecting every piece of gold in each level and reaching the top of the screen to advance. While running through the stage, the commando must avoid enemy robots or guards that pursue the character and can also pick up gold bars. The character can drop from any height unharmed.

Defense relies on digging holes into brick surfaces to the character's sides, temporarily trapping pursuing guards and causing them to drop carried gold. Holes eventually refill, consuming trapped enemies and bringing new guards in at the top of the screen, but solid surfaces cannot be dug. A life is lost when an enemy catches the commando or the commando is trapped in a pit. Alongside the primary mode, an included edit mode allows players to create customized stages.

t_4687d4df82a3.overview: A side-scrolling shooter developed in Taiwan by Joy Van, released in Japan by Kinema Music under the Metal Fighter μ name, with a Sachen edition sold in Asia. The player controls a robot named MCS-920 in an attempt to free planet H17 from alien invaders. Defeating certain enemies makes them drop power-ups, and collecting these enhances the robot's weapons and speed. A special power-up grants MCS-920 the ability to fly. The same game appears under the Metal Fighter title elsewhere, and it is a single-player release.

t_468886dfbb28.overview: Released in South Korea under the Haitai Supercom brand, this edition of the Color Dreams action game Challenge of the Dragon keeps the original game and updates its title screen. Sir Burkelot, a master of Dragon style Kung-Fu, makes his way through ten levels fighting numerous foes to save his kidnapped lover, Lady Ninita, from the evil necromancer Demiwind. The hero advances by beating enemies, using a small sword, kicks and a jumping kick. The setting has a medieval European fantasy theme, and while every level offers the same basic brawling action, the enemies grow stranger from one level to the next.

t_46b0ba6866d2.overview: Named after the Night Parade of the 100 Demons of Japanese folklore, this role-playing game begins when a huge fireball falls one night and breaks the barrier that held evil creatures sealed away. Freed monsters overrun the town and its people submit to them, so the castle lord, back from his duties, hides in a mountain temple and orders a single ninja to seal the monsters away and bring back peace. Exploration alternates between a 2D map mode and a 3D dungeon mode, enemies can be seen while walking around, and battles are turn-based. Towns connect directly to the monster-infested wilderness with no separate overworld map. Companions include a samurai, a ronin, a merchant, a mountain ascetic, a monk and a thief, and three schools of arts, ninja, ascetic and priestly, take the place of magic.

t_46ba51aa0e6c.overview: Hummer Team's 1995 conversion squeezes the SNES launch title Super Mario World onto far weaker hardware, reworking it to fit the technical constraints of the NES. The result is a platformer that keeps much of the original's makeup; one description notes that it comparatively manages to retain most of the original SNES game's elements. Substantial compromises remain, though. Levels from the original game are missing, the physics behave differently, and gameplay mechanics such as warps were not implemented. What is left is a rather linear progression through a reduced selection of stages, one that does not play very much like the 16-bit game it reproduces.

t_46bc4c195f0d.overview: Air and ground targets call for separate weapons in this vertically scrolling shooter: lasers bring down aerial opponents, while missiles destroy enemies on the ground. Flying the fighter SYD, the player fights waves of enemies that threaten several space stations, with a boss to defeat at the end of each level. Power-ups found along the way upgrade the craft's weapons, and losing a life strips them all. The defining feature is the armor system: collected armor such as the Octo, Shield and Cannon types can boost the laser or missiles or raise a protective barrier, and it consumes energy while in use, over time and when hit. In the Famicom version a single armor pickup is enough to use it, and armor is equipped from a separate pause screen rather than in real time.

t_47dfcd2a727d.overview: A special edition of Namco's tag-team wrestling game, this cartridge keeps the same contest between the Ricky Fighters and the Strong Bads but differs from the regular release in its packaging, in-game music and the way moves are performed. Matches follow wrestling rules: a team wins with a three-count pinfall or by forcing a submission with a hold, and a wrestler caught in a hold must wait for a partner to break it. When a wrestler falls out of the ring, the action switches to a side view, a gong can be grabbed as a weapon, and failing to return within 20 counts means a ring-out loss. Victories raise the team through a ladder of national, continental, world and super championships, with title defenses and ever larger trophies. A second player can control the opposing team.

t_487b5a3d89e6.overview: Based on the third anime series, this right-scrolling side-view action game follows the ghost Q-Tarou through 12 stages, for one player or two players taking turns. With no means of attack at the start, Q-Tarou has to steer clear of dogs and their barks. A hunger gauge drains slowly even while walking or standing still and sharply while flying; eating food refills it, flight becomes impossible when it runs low, and a life is lost when it runs out. Special candy supplies four shots that can be fired back at the dogs. Most stages end when Q-Tarou delivers an item collected along the way to the character waiting at the end, while every third stage is a rescue of a fellow ghost kidnapped by a robber. Each day runs on a clock from 8:00 in the morning, and reaching 20:00 costs a life.

t_4891d4b85d9b.overview: Many features of earlier Famista entries are stripped out in favor of a simpler design in this Namco baseball game for the Famicom. Players return to the rounder body shape used before the '92 edition, and the batting side of a switch-hitter can now be chosen by pressing Select during a timeout. The All-American team of foreign players returns, with an outfielder pressed into service as catcher because no foreign catcher was available. A park modeled on Meiji Jingu Stadium carries over from the previous game, and two new stadiums are added: one based on Fukuoka Dome and an aquarium-themed park with glass outfield walls and a dirt field. One or two players can compete head to head.

t_490cc5d733bb.overview: Reworked for the Famicom rather than directly ported, this version of Valis keeps the story of Yuko Asou, a Japanese schoolgirl fated to protect the Earth, the land of spirits and the dream world Vecanti. The demon lord Rogles extinguishes a light that powers the inhabitants of Vecanti, and its queen, Valia, reaches out for help; Yuko answers and is magically summoned to become the Valis warrior, wielding the sword of the same name. Her classmate Reiko Kirishima has been brainwashed by Rogles into trying to destroy her. Because the console could not reproduce the multi-directional scrolling of the computer originals, the team added an exploration component and more complex maps, making the game closer to a side-scrolling action role-playing game, with large maze-style levels, multiple paths and no password or save feature.

t_49158ed98013.overview: A boxing game built around a career, Family Boxing follows a fighter's climb from rookie bouts toward the world championship. Boxers throw several kinds of punches, defend, counter-punch and unleash special attacks triggered at the right timing and distance: a hook thrown while spinning like a top, a straight that propels the opponent into the ropes, and an uppercut that can blast a rival straight out of the ring. Missing with too many punches drains stamina, which recovers between rounds by pressing the button rapidly. After each match, power points are distributed among three stats, punch, stamina and speed, to build a stronger boxer. Progress is saved by password, and two players can face off, including with boxers each has trained.

t_497bfa746a76.overview: Adapted from the Honoo no Toukyuuji Dodge Danpei dodgeball manga, this sports game plays out through a card battle system. Matches advance through four kinds of battle cards: shot (catch) cards, super cards, pass (pass-cut) cards and line-cross cards. The story follows the hunt for a mysterious team that defeated the St. Arrows Academy dodgeball club led by Taiga Nikaido. Opposing squads include St. Arrows and its second team, the Street Tigers, the Black Armors, the Tosa Attackers, the Arasaki Elementary club, the Tamagawa Elementary alumni and the Fire Emperor, while the Tamagawa Elementary dodgeball club and its Super club also take part.

t_49a8d9a5e690.overview: Bullet-Proof Software adapted its Japanese home computer versions of the falling-block puzzle for this Famicom release, built around clearing stages. Play spans six rounds of ten stages, and each stage ends after 25 lines are cleared, wiping the screen before the next one begins. Pieces fall faster with every stage, and every new round starts the well with taller garbage. Three lives allow two top-outs before the game is over. The 10 by 20 playfield shows one next piece and offers no hold. Controls follow the computer keyboard layout, so pressing down rotates a piece while the A button hard-drops it, the opposite of most later versions. Finishing the last stage of the final round brings up an ending screen before play loops.

t_49c4d69d118a.overview: Programmed in Taiwan by Hwang Shinwei, Magic Jewelry follows the formula of Columns. Blocks of three jewels fall from the top of the well, and the player arranges them into combinations of three or more of the same color to remove them and earn points, with play continuing until the well fills up. At the end of each level a column of X blocks appears, and whatever color of jewel it touches disappears. The backdrop is New York, with the Statue of Liberty taking up a considerable part of the scenery while stars and a moon drift up the screen.

t_49fc2c8381fb.overview: In the year 2089, Earth makes contact with the Baal Empire and sets up a warp gate between the two home planets, until the Empire suddenly attacks New York City. Piloting the experimental Tetra Star fighter, the player leads a small squadron through the gate to strike back. Developed by Home Data and published by Taito, the shooter plays much like the earlier Cosmic Epsilon at a faster pace. Supplementary weapons with limited ammo unlock over the course of the game, including Wide Blaster bombs, homing missiles, napalm bombs and a chargeable Bio cannon. Missions go beyond shooting and dodging: in the New York stage a nuclear reactor in Manhattan must not be destroyed, and in the second stage the captured Omega navigator, a robot dog, must be rescued or the ship cannot survive the warp gate. Cinemas expand the story, and branching points decide whether Omega lives to see the finale.

t_4a12d8146e61.overview: Built on the NES version of Donkey Kong, this edition reinstates the cement factory stage and adds some animations absent from that original port. Mario climbs a construction site to rescue Pauline from Donkey Kong. One stage has him scale crooked girders and ladders while jumping over or hammering the barrels and oil drums Donkey Kong tosses down; the cement factory has him climb a structure of conveyor belts carrying cement pans; another involves riding elevators while avoiding bouncing springs; and the last requires removing eight rivets so Donkey Kong falls. Points come from leaping over obstacles, smashing objects with the hammer, collecting items such as hats, parasols and purses, and removing rivets. A life is lost when Mario touches Donkey Kong or any enemy object, falls too far, or lets the bonus counter run out.

t_4a67a7193a6e.overview: Long ago the people of Marvelland had endless lives, but demons dwelled in their hearts. One night a man afraid of death pulled the Key of Time from the great clock, reviving the sealed evil incarnate Zouna. Hearing the suffering of the people whose souls were taken, Valkyrie, a child of the gods, descends to find the key and seal Zouna away again. The top-down action game has role-playing elements: defeating enemies earns experience, and staying at an inn brings level-ups. The chosen zodiac sign sets starting statistics, while blood type governs how health and intelligence grow. A day-night cycle makes enemies stronger after dark and triggers certain events. Only eight items can be carried, weapons and armor included. Each inn stay displays a keyword that resumes the adventure from that point.

t_4abbe0d43ed1.overview: This revision of the original Family BASIC cartridge is a programming environment rather than a game, letting the Family Computer run a dialect of BASIC enhanced for game development. It is used with a keyboard that connects to the console's expansion connector, and the set also includes a programming textbook. The language supports sprites, animation, backgrounds, musical sequences and gamepads, and ready-made character sets make it easy to assemble sprite characters and background art; calculations are limited to integers. From the GAME BASIC menu, the user can enter BASIC or open the BG GRAPHIC background editor. Programs are saved to and loaded from cassette tape, for example with the Famicom Data Recorder.

t_4ad099c4b516.overview: A young Iga ninja named Kage sets out to rescue Princess Kiri, the Shogun's daughter, from a villainous warlord and his evil samurai ally. Armed with a kodachi short sword and an unlimited supply of shuriken, Kage fights his way through a forest, along a secret passageway, up a fortress wall and through a castle. Grabbing a crystal ball changes the color of his clothes and grants new powers; if hit while wearing green or orange, he survives and reverts to red. Each rescue advances the seasons from summer to fall to winter and back to summer, and this Famicom version requires the princess to be saved three times to win, one more than in the arcade original.

t_4b00b1607c8e.overview: An elf called the Archer defends his mushroom forest from gigantic insect monsters with magic arrows in this conversion of Atari's arcade shooter by HAL Laboratory. A millipede winds down from the top of the screen, dropping a row and reversing direction whenever it hits an obstacle or the edge, and shooting a body segment splits it in two. Bees, spiders, inchworms, ladybugs, dragonflies, mosquitoes and earwigs each bring their own effects, such as slowing enemies, turning mushrooms into flowers or scrolling the field; unlike in the arcade original, earwigs here do not poison the mushrooms. Shooting a DDT bomb releases a cloud that destroys all enemies and mushrooms inside it, and bonus levels with swarms of enemies appear at regular intervals.

t_4b23614b21af.overview: Alien forces fly into formation from the top and sides of the screen in this fixed shooter, and the player's ship at the bottom must defeat them all to clear each stage. The aliens dive at the ship while firing, and contact with an alien or its shot costs a life. Some enemies take double shots to destroy and can use a tractor beam to capture the player's ship; rescuing the captured ship transforms it into a dual-fighter with additional firepower, while destroying its captor in formation turns it against the player as an enemy. Some enemies morph into new types with different attack patterns, the attacks become more aggressive as the game progresses, and bonus stages send aliens flying in a preset formation without firing.

t_4bab134340ce.overview: Squadrons of Galaga aliens swoop in from the top and sides of the screen to form ranks above the fighter, and every one must be destroyed before the next stage begins. Members of the formation break off to dive at the ship while shooting, and touching either an alien or its shot costs a life, with later stages adding more fire and faster dives. Each Boss Galaga needs two hits and can seize the fighter with a tractor beam; shooting that captor during a dive frees the ship, which docks alongside the active one as a dual fighter that shoots more but is easier to hit. If the captor is destroyed back in formation, the captured ship turns hostile. Starting with the third stage, every fourth stage is a bonus round of aliens flying set patterns without shooting. This edition carries the NES version of the game.

t_4bc7e4bea913.overview: Chinese martial arts provide the theme for this Namco fighting game with role-playing elements, designed by Masanobu Endo of Game Studio. A versus mode pits preset characters against each other, while a training mode sends the hero across a large map to visit towns, dojos and temples, training, fighting matches and running errands for hermits and other characters, all of which add new techniques. Defeating the opponent in each castle earns the title of fighter along with words that, entered on the password screen, lead to the ending; a separate goal is beating a legendary fighter, the strongest enemy of all. Passwords store the hero's stats and progress, so a character raised in training can be used in versus play. Battles switch to a large side view in which every character shares one face and body, differing only in clothing color, offset by a large number of techniques and smooth animation.

t_4beffd4146ce.overview: Rather than a racing game, Gate In is software for analyzing horse races before betting. It covers 10 central and 27 local public racecourses and handles flat races, steeplechases and races for newcomer horses on turf or dirt. The user first sets the race conditions: distance class, track condition in four grades, number of runners and any single-bracket designation. The program then asks a series of questions, answered with horse numbers, about each runner's running style, career record, recent finishes, results at the course, best time at the distance, pedigree in newcomer races, expected race development, distance aptitude, weight carried, training, jockey form, jumping skill in steeplechases, ability on heavy going, time since the last race, body weight change and popularity. A final item records the user's own personal pick, which carries a small weight in the analysis.

t_4bf67b8d6e3e.overview: In the year 2199 AD, after global nuclear war, a robotic revolt led by a robot named De Gaulle threatens what remains of humanity. The female cyborg Altiana, who does not support the rebellion, sets out to prove her loyalty to the humans. The enemy hides among seven maze-like asteroids outside Earth's orbit, each laid out on a 9×9 grid of rooms and doors. Defeating all enemies in a door's room yields either a hint or an item, mostly weapons and other enhancements. Altiana's main weapon is a time bomb, while stronger arms such as the crystal beam use up power units and require a minimum power level. Once the first six asteroids are beaten, the final area opens.

t_4bfc791a609f.overview: Years after King Amul defeated the demon Zawel, the sorcerer Galda uses black magic to bring Zawel back and kidnaps Princess Iris. Her brother, Prince Lace, takes up his father's sword to rescue her, transforming into a dragon as his father once did. Play takes the form of a vertical shooter in which the dragon fires fireballs at airborne foes and drops bombs on ground targets. Two versions of the quest are available: a golden dragon game on easy difficulty, where the dragon is faster and more powerful but several difficult levels are removed, and a blue dragon game on normal difficulty. The journey spans nine worlds, ranging from the Paleozoic Era to the Evil Palace, a parallel universe where the final boss waits.

t_4c14e22dc3f1.overview: Racing on the Famicom takes a different route from the arcade game of the same name: this version is mostly unrelated to the original, with more tracks and somewhat simpler gameplay. Rather than offering a choice of different cars, it uses an upgrade system that requires the player to continuously improve the car in order to keep up with the field. Upgrades consist of engine improvements, brake improvements, tire improvements and extra boost. Both a single-player mode and a two-player split-screen mode are included.

t_4c3d1c754721.overview:
Campaign matches unfold across medieval England in 1149 as factions contest territorial dominion following the monarch's demise. A single player assumes command of one of four Saxon leaders to battle Norman forces and ultimately crush the three Norman castles to claim the crown. Victory requires managing a prolonged war of attrition by building larger forces than rival factions and launching assaults at favorable moments.

Gameplay involves building armies to conquer hostile territories, clash directly with opposing military forces, and lay siege to or plunder rival fortresses. Players also compete in periodic jousting tournaments to win territory, undertake a mission to rescue a damsel in distress, and seek assistance from Robin Hood.

t_4c7383eb0419.overview: Released in Japan by Kinema Music, Papillon Gals is the local version of the vertically scrolling shooter known in the US as Galactic Crusader, and unlike that release it contains nudity. The action is viewed from a top-down perspective, in a style often compared to Galaga, as the player progresses through numerous stages using missiles and lasers to shoot oncoming enemies. The main departure from Galaga lies in the many bosses: one is confronted at the end of each level, and they often take many hits to defeat.

t_4ca463924126.overview: A young swordsman named Adol Christin arrives in the town of Minea in the land of Esteria, whose history centers on the vanished civilization of Ys. His quest is to collect six books that hold the lost civilization's history and use them to vanquish the darkness that has fallen over the land. Exploration of towns, fields and dungeons is shown from a top-down view, and combat relies on the series' bump attack system: rather than pressing an attack button, Adol attacks automatically by walking into enemies, and striking them off-center is the key to winning fights. The system was created with accessibility in mind. This Famicom edition, published by Victor Musical Industries, was a substantial departure from the original computer version of the game.

t_4cdeec1a0aec.overview: When the secret society Madoodan, bent on world conquest, kidnaps the space biologist Dr. Shikishima along with a crystal whose enormous power could become a weapon, Birdman asks the Perman team for help. In this side-scrolling action game the player picks Perman, Booby, Perko or Peryan, who all perform the same. Each area alternates between three-dimensional sections, where the hero can fly freely, and flat sections, and every boss is fought as a regular action battle. Six stages run from the new Tokyo Metropolitan Government Building in Shinjuku through an Arctic iceberg fortress, a secret laboratory on the Tibetan Plateau, a maze beneath a mosque and a desert pyramid fortress to the Madoodan space fortress. Attack items include punches and guns that inflate, freeze or transform enemies, and raising all four to level 2 yields the Power Ball. Bonus doors lead to block breaking, a panel puzzle whose letters form a password, and a memory card game.

t_4d0ef982e315.overview: In the year 2000, superpower S has joined forces with aliens to build a secret weapon at the giant base Goldos, and the armed super-helicopter Gyrodine sets out to destroy it. A vertically scrolling shooter developed by Crux and released by Taito, it uses one button for anti-air fire and another for ground attacks, and both shots angle left or right as the helicopter moves sideways, with the screen scrolling sideways as well. Pressing both buttons together launches a single homing missile at ground targets with unlimited range. Shooting houses or people costs points and temporarily raises the difficulty, while firing at certain ground spots reveals hidden mermaids or eyes worth bonus points. After a set distance the game loops back to the start with more bullets and enemies.

t_4d20bac9fdd5.overview: Loosely modeled on Dance Dance Revolution, Hot Dance 2000 was sold for plug-and-play dance mats running on Famicom hardware. Arrows scroll to the top of the screen, and the player hits them in time with 8-bit renditions of pop songs; the charts include left/right and up/down combinations, and the up and down arrow positions are switched compared with DDR. There is no health bar. The main menu offers three choices. Single lists the individual songs, Mix strings two or three songs together back to back, and Game holds bonus games: Hit Mouse, an original whack-a-mole game, plus versions of Pac-Man, Arkanoid and Pinball. Numerous variants of the dance game were produced by several companies under different names.

t_4d213939aef5.overview: Slot machines supply the theme for this falling-block puzzle game from Sammy. Much like Columns and Puyo Puyo, it has a rotatable piece made of two blocks guided down the playfield, and three or more matching symbols lined up in a row, a column or a diagonal are cleared away. The twist is that each block behaves like the reel of a slot machine: its symbol spins as the piece falls, and the reel can be stopped manually or set spinning again. Making matches therefore depends on timing the spinning reels as well as on moving and rotating each piece into the right position.

t_4d3453ea3e97.overview: The fourth and final installment in the Deep Dungeon role-playing series from HummingBirdSoft sends the son of a murdered man on a quest to avenge his father after a demon sorcerer appears. Instead of creating a custom party as in the previous game, the hero meets up to two additional playable characters, each with a predetermined class. The hero can learn to summon two monsters that act as a temporary extra party member for a single battle. Stat growth on leveling up returns to randomized values, and the maps are smaller, with each dungeon fitting within a 32x32 tile grid. Non-player characters offer optional requests that reward items, experience or money when completed.

t_4d7c5bf35ec5.overview: Wishing to spread the joy of pachinko, the Pachinko King of the pachinko planet sends chosen soldiers to other worlds, and Pachichi, father of Pachio-kun, is sent to Earth, where the crooked nail-setter Boruzo lies in wait. The game runs in three acts: Act 1 revives the peak pachinko boom of the Showa 50s with Pachichi as the hero; Act 2 brings new regulated machines, with Pachio-kun and his wife Ginko as heroes; and in Act 3 the couple and their child Maru fight Boruzo across three pachinko planets linked by one-way rockets. When an emergency news bulletin appears, Boruzo has seized a parlor and tightened its nails, and he is caught by emptying one machine there. Ladies' machines are open only to Ginko, a mode teaches nail reading, an optional pachinko controller is supported, and three battery-saved history books hold progress.
