t_4dce2d62d097.overview: Yumetaro, a small green creature, was mistakenly given as a toy to a young girl. One night her other toys come alive and take the girl to another dimension, and Yumetaro gives chase to save her. Platforming revolves around the star that Yumetaro creates above the horn on his head: it serves both to defeat enemies and as a platform, and riding it reaches areas that are otherwise inaccessible. The journey spans six stages and six bosses. Each stage hides an area containing a magic item, and gathering all of them without using a continue opens a secret stage in which an extra boss must be beaten. Play is single-player.

t_4df0abc34783.overview: Pack-In-Video brought this side-scrolling action game, first released overseas, to Japan on the Famicom. Based on the 1991 film, it casts the player as a T-800 Terminator across five levels. At a truck stop, the Terminator must beat up truckers to acquire a motorcycle and a gun. A diagonal overhead chase follows in a flood channel, where the T-800 flees on the motorcycle from a semi-truck driven by the T-1000, avoiding debris while shooting to keep the truck at a safe distance. In a mental hospital, the search for Sarah Connor brings encounters with staff members and the T-1000; killing hospital employees costs energy, so they must instead be disabled with a crouching shot to the leg. The mission continues at Cyberdyne Systems, where explosives must be planted to destroy the facility, and ends with a final battle between the two Terminators in a steel mill.

t_4df8e8a87194.overview: A top-down action game built around puzzle solving, Elnark no Zaihou sends its hero after his best friend, a treasure hunter who vanished while searching for the treasure of Elnark after sending a letter asking for help. The hero moves only up, down, left and right, throws knives and other weapons to attack, and examines objects with a second button to find hints that open the way forward. Enemies appear from the screen edges and fire shots that veer slightly off a direct line, making them hard to dodge. Alongside the life gauge sits a personality gauge that shifts toward light or dark as items are collected, and near the end certain passages can only be crossed in a particular personality state. A sacred stone revives words sealed by holy light.

t_4e28330a6861.overview: Designed by Uwe Mèffert in collaboration with TXC Corporation, this Famicom puzzle cartridge consists of two mini-games of pattern matching and memorization. Before playing, the player selects a difficulty level ranging from 81 to 270. In the pattern-matching game the player has to guess a pattern based on in-game hints. In the memorization variant the player must remember a pattern and re-create it on the playfield as many times as possible within the time limit. Without proper instruction the puzzles can be hard to grasp.

t_4e2da71066a3.overview: Fifteen unlicensed NES games share this cartridge, the edition for Australia of the Maxivision 15-in-1 multicart, published by HES in 1992 with games from companies including Color Dreams, Sachen and Idea-Tek. The line-up spans many genres. F-15 City War puts the player in a fully armed F-15 Strike Eagle against an invading enemy army, Puzzle asks for eight picture puzzles to be unscrambled, and Tiles of Fate requires matching enchanted tiles to reach seven ancient castles. Menace Beach is a skateboarding rescue mission, Rad Racket Tennis and Venice Beach Volleyball cover sports, and Solitaire offers the card game. Two versions exist: the later one uses a different title screen and replaces Pyramid and Double Strike, both by Sachen, with Blackjack and Deathrace.

t_4e48bddceb94.overview: The second entry in the Super Robot Wars crossover series brings together robots drawn in super-deformed style from series including Mobile Suit Gundam, Mazinger Z and Getter Robo. Dr. Bian Zoldark, a genius scientist, learns through years of research that a threat from outer space is approaching Earth, and his organization, the DC, sets out to unify the world by force. Only the White Base unit can resist, moving from place to place to gather allies as it rebels against the DC. Where the first game gave the robots personalities of their own, this entry introduces pilots, and units power up as their pilots gain levels. Persuasion lets players recruit characters who could not be saved in the original works, and the campaign runs through 26 episodes without route branches.

t_4f0237fffb72.overview: Built on the engine and level layouts of Titenic, a beat 'em up that Hummer Team never released on its own, this Hummer Technology game recasts the action around Harry Potter and the Philosopher's Stone. Harry Potter is the only playable character, attacking with a kick and crouching strikes, and he cannot attack in the air. A broom special becomes available in stage two and a magic attack in stage three. Five stages can be selected after the title screen, though all must be completed to reach the ending. Enemies include returning humans and animals plus a giant chess piece and an indestructible floating flame, and a two-faced boss closes each stage. Cutscenes quote passages from the first book.

t_4f1c263a1fb0.overview: Cast as the warlord Masamune, the player works to unite the eleven provinces of northern Japan. The campaign ends if he dies of old age at 81 before finishing the task, or if he loses a war with no territory left to retreat to. Each year passes in four seasons, and turns are spent on icon-selected commands: land reclamation to raise rice yield, troop training, ninja raids on rival lords, trading rice, guns, cavalry and bannermen with merchants, consulting a prayer shaman for unpredictable results, and scouting enemy domains. Battles play out directly on a field with foot soldiers, cavalry that can act twice, long-range gunners, and a commander unit whose loss means defeat. Typhoons, heavy rain and snow disrupt plans, action mini-games such as horseback archery appear, two difficulty settings are offered, and progress can be saved each spring.

t_4f301e51128f.overview: Set in 20th century Japan, this adventure follows two siblings, Erika and her brother Satoru, who live together in an ordinary house until a cat-like being gives them a mission to search for a powerful crown able to alter time and space. Both siblings are controlled at once, and many quests require them to cooperate, since some tasks cannot be completed without the other present. Erika can swim through the water levels while Satoru can drown, so she must keep him safe there. Talking with characters and completing their quests moves the story forward across five chapters, with the difficulty rising sharply after the third. Visiting a landmark on the map switches the view from overhead to first person, and a second player can take control of one of the siblings.

t_4f6a80d2c196.overview: Koei's mahjong tournament game reached the Famicom in 1989, using a thinking routine developed by Shanoir. The opponents are mostly historical figures from around the world and across the ages, among them Masamune Date and Napoleon, each with a distinct playing style. Play alternates between two modes. The tournament mode, mainly for earning prize money, splits 16 players, including the player, into tables of four; finishing in the top two at a table advances to the next round, and the four who reach the final contest the championship. The mahjong parlor mode, mainly for earning wagered money, lets the player choose three opponents for a match. Whenever the player's funds exceed one million yen, a title is awarded, out of 17 ranks in all.

t_4fe9088e0fbf.overview: Pachinko parlor play is recreated on the home screen here. Balls launched onto a board studded with nails bounce between the pins, and any that land in special compartments pay out like credits on a slot machine, while balls that fall past the bottom of the board are lost; play begins with one hundred balls. Two machine types are included: a hanemono-style machine and a digital machine with a probability-driven display. The GAME option is a practice mode that goes straight to a machine, while the SELECT option recreates a parlor in which any one of 120 machines can be chosen, each with nails bent differently, and played until it reaches its payout limit. On-screen text in the Famicom version is in English.

t_503d3949e8b3.overview: Dr. Wily returns a year after his first defeat with a new fortress and eight new Robot Masters of his own: Metal Man, Air Man, Bubble Man, Quick Man, Crash Man, Flash Man, Heat Man and Wood Man. Dr. Light sends Mega Man to stop him. The player traverses eight stages in a freely chosen order, gaining each boss's unique weapon after its defeat; because every Robot Master is weak to particular weapons, the sequence matters. Three support items create platforms for reaching awkward spots. Energy Tanks refill Mega Man's health at any time, and a password system records the defeated Robot Masters and the Energy Tanks in stock. The campaign concludes inside Wily's fortress, where all eight bosses must be fought again.

t_50a36189d48e.overview: A minor revision of the previous year's Family Stadium, the '87 edition keeps the basic play of its predecessor but narrows how far batters can move inside the batter's box, shifting the balance away from hitters and toward pitchers. On-screen labels for batting average, home runs and earned run average are changed, and the number of teams rises from ten to twelve, though not every professional club of the time is represented. A club that had been part of a combined team now stands on its own, an all-star team of major league players appears for the first time, and an all-star team of the publisher's characters is included. Games are still played in a single ballpark, whose listed capacity rises from 30,000 to 40,000, and a hidden team appears only in the demo screen.

t_51127a651038.overview:
Piloting the Tiger-Heli attack helicopter, the player navigates vertically scrolling battlefields to destroy enemy forces. Opposing targets include ground and air units such as tanks, aircraft, gunboats, and artillery, alongside installations like fuel depots and buildings. The craft defends itself with short-range missiles capable of striking air and ground targets, as well as bombs that damage everything across a wide area.

Shooting color-changing crosses produces items that replenish bomb stocks or recruit up to two support helicopters that provide supplemental forward or sideways firepower. A hidden continue option allows players to resume play after a game over.

t_5146f8a1514e.overview:
Set across eight cylindrical sea towers, the game tasks the player with guiding a character named Julius to the summit of each structure. Julius begins at the bottom of a tower and works upward along exterior ledges, climbing stairs and riding elevators. As the protagonist walks left or right, the cylindrical tower rotates, creating a sense of depth.

Various geometric adversaries obstruct the ascent. Julius can shoot and stun or destroy certain hazards, while others resist all attacks. Contact with an enemy knocks the character off his feet, and tumbling into the water below causes the loss of a life. Reaching a door at the peak triggers a bomb to demolish the tower, after which Julius visits a diamond-studded bonus level to collect gems.

t_5159584ca301.overview: Built by Dragon Co. and unrelated to the Hudson Soft release of the same name, this unlicensed platformer stars Felix in a story drawn from the 1936 cartoon "The Goose That Laid the Golden Egg". A pirate dog called Captain Kidd has captured Felix's golden goose, renamed Felie Goose here, and Felix sets out to get it back. The D-pad moves, A jumps and B punches or shoots. Collecting hearts lets Felix transform into a knight or take control of a car or a tank. Several levels include horizontally moving logs to jump over, and the first and last levels normally require beating a boss to finish.

t_5162630e459f.overview: Terrorists have seized an embassy in Paris, and a counterterrorist team is sent in to end the hostage crisis. The mission unfolds in phases. First, three snipers must reach buildings across the street, timing their moves and using cover to stay out of the searchlights the terrorists sweep over the street. Once in position, the snipers cover an entry team that lands by helicopter on the embassy roof; its operatives descend the sides of the building and enter through the windows, and the player can switch between snipers or take control of a descending assaulter. Inside, the assaulter searches the building for hostages while defeating the terrorists. A closing report styled as a newspaper excerpt rates speed, accuracy, hostages rescued and operative survival.

t_517f57a5e407.overview: Two ghosts open the story by praying to three deity-like figures and wishing to become human kids; they are told to find six hearts in order to transform into human beings. The game is an elimination platformer built from one-screen levels, each cleared by defeating every enemy on it. The player can only attack enemies of the same color, so jumping into the paint pots spread across a level changes color and refills paint, which runs out after three attacks. A struck enemy turns into an angel, and hitting it again yields a bonus food item or a power-up, such as a clock that freezes enemies, a shield that changes color, or clouds that skip to the next stage once three are collected. Thirty-six stages follow, with a cutscene of one of the six hearts every six stages.

t_51c10ec8fe59.overview:
Set across side-scrolling stages in Neverland, the journey follows Peter Pan on an adventure to recover his kidnapped children from Captain Hook.

The player controls Peter Pan as he traverses the land to rescue his family. Progress through the adventure ultimately culminates in a final sword confrontation against Captain Hook.

t_51c614711e46.overview: Waixing's 1997 turn-based strategy game is based on the Chu–Han Contention and shares its engine with Napoleon's War, reworked with a Chinese style of design and new audiovisuals. On the map, the player surveys territory and manages the army, while battles play out in turns as divisions move to seize enemy territories. Three main scenarios are offered: two story chapters, one of them centered on Xiang Yu, each split into four sub-scenarios, and a free mode with starting years from 208 B.C. to 204 B.C. in which the player can be male or female. Difficulty can be set to Easy, Medium or Hard, and the game can be saved at any time in one of two save slots.

t_51ee40191eeb.overview: Natsume's science fiction side-view shoot-'em-up sends its soldiers flying through five stages, each with a boss encounter, as the screen scrolls automatically horizontally or vertically. The soldiers can fly in eight directions but fire their guns only left or right. Up to two players can fight simultaneously, controlling palette-swapped male soldiers, one of whom is Russian. Each soldier is accompanied by two satellites that shoot whenever the main gun fires; rather than orbiting automatically, they are aligned by the player while moving the character left or right. Destroying certain containers releases power-up items: new weapons that replace the default gun, a speed boost and life recovery. The opening story sequence shows the obliteration of various cities before the alien invasion begins. The player starts with three lives, and any upgrade is lost whenever the character is hit.

t_520f8f6c0861.overview: Baseball supervised by the former professional pitcher known as Emoyan takes its title from his book on enjoying pro baseball. Six league teams appear under invented names because real names were not approved, each modeled on an actual club and given its own character, from deep pitching paired with a weak lineup to home-run power undercut by shaky pitching. Play revolves around pitch courses: the pitcher first picks a target course and then a pitch type with the directional pad, while the batter must predict the course and time the swing, and a wrong guess usually means a miss. Detailed data for individual players and cheer songs for each team and player are included. Unusually for a baseball game, it is single-player only, with no versus play.

t_5227340f137f.overview: The demon lord Ryūkotsuki escapes from hell, and the Getsu brothers fight him, each wielding one of the three spiritual Pulse Blades passed down within their clan. Only the youngest, Fūma, survives. Vowing to avenge his slain brothers, he ventures into Kyōki-tō, the Mad Demon Island, after recovering the blades hidden away in the three neighboring islands. Play begins on an overhead view where Fūma is guided to his next destination; entering an area switches to a side-scrolling action scene that must be crossed from one end to the other, and labyrinths switch to a pseudo-3D perspective that follows him from behind. Defeating enemies fills his sword gauge and increases the strength of his attacks, while money from fallen foes buys new items and weapons in shops. A password allows play to resume later.

t_524991235e9c.overview: Honey Bunny has been kidnapped by Wile E. Coyote, Yosemite Sam, Daffy Duck and Sylvester the Cat, and Bugs Bunny must make his way through level after level to save her, clearing each one by collecting all 8 carrots. Although presented side-on, the action differs from standard side-scrollers because Bugs cannot jump, so avoiding enemies depends on taking different routes via doors, staircases and tubes. Boxing gloves, invincibility potions, safes, crates, flower pots and ten thousand-pound weights can be used against the pursuers, which gives the game a puzzle-solving atmosphere, and passwords allow starting at a later level. Bugs Bunny Fun House is the working title shown in an early prototype of The Bugs Bunny Crazy Castle.

t_524ee9667e07.overview: Although its publisher labeled it a scrolling role-playing game, Zunou Senkan Galg plays as a vertically scrolling shooter. The player pilots a lone fighter that warps through stages cycling from an underground zone to a core zone and then into outer space, after which the sequence starts over from the underground in an endless loop. The goal is to gather 100 parts and then destroy a space control device called Dragg. Thirty areas, each belonging to one of the three stage types, hold one part apiece. The fighter powers up after shooting down a set number of airborne enemies; ground targets do not count toward it. Many items are hidden behind strict appearance conditions, and the player has three lives and no continues. One or two players can take part, alternating turns.

t_52512273c729.overview: Built as a study aid rather than a retail game, this cartridge drills sixth-grade elementary school mathematics. Konami produced the Space School series together with the textbook publisher Tokyo Shoseki and NHK, and the sixth-grade course is split across two cartridges, an upper and a lower volume. Content is divided into sections whose questions mirror classroom textbook material, and the student answers math problems through multiple-choice or calculation prompts, often framed in space-themed scenarios. Play is for a single student, with a study book supplied to use alongside the game. The special 40-pin cartridges do not fit the Famicom directly and run through Konami's QTa adapter.

t_526385635050.overview: Based on the live-action superhero series about a specially trained squad of police in power armor who fight evil and protect Tokyo, this side-scrolling action game centers on hand-to-hand combat. The hero moves through each stage punching enemies until they explode, and continued punching chains into a three-hit combo, while touching an enemy causes damage. Power-up blocks bearing alpha or beta symbols can be switched by punching them; collecting three summons a small support robot, and different combinations of blocks call different robots, which attack alongside the hero and add much-needed range. P chips can be gathered from enemies and breakable boxes. After an opening factory stage, the player chooses among five areas, which can be tackled in any order, one of them a carnival stage.

t_52658456f159.overview: Horse racing simulation from ASCII in which the player acts as breeder, owner and trainer at once, repeating breeding, training and racing with the goal of winning every JRA GI race title. Play advances in one-week units: on weekdays horses are bred at the ranch, while training and race entries are handled at the stable, and on race days the races are watched at the racecourse. Breeding theory covers only the concept of inbreeding. This nationwide edition expands the earlier cartridge, which mostly limited horses to races in the Kanto region, by opening Kansai races as well and letting the player choose between the Miho and Ritto stables. Progress is saved automatically, and resetting during a race forcibly skips ahead to the next week.

t_52679c67c540.overview:
Rescuing the kidnapped Dr. Light and freeing the city from Protoman's robots serves as the primary objective. The player controls Mega Man across stages where running, jumping, and shooting are needed to overcome enemy machines. Mega Man attacks using an arm cannon with unlimited ammunition, which can also be charged to unleash wider blasts that cancel if damage is taken during charging. Defeated foes and stage pickups restore lost health, while Energy Tanks, Mega Tanks, and extra lives provide additional support.

Advancement involves conquering eight initial stages and defeating their Robot Masters. Overcoming each boss yields a special weapon powered by finite ammunition. Specific levels include distinct features such as reversed gravity or operating a water craft. Completing certain areas unlocks traversal abilities via Rush, while collecting eight hidden letters that spell MEGAMANV grants access to Beat, a robotic bird that attacks enemies.

t_526bf79661c0.overview: Waixing ported the strategy game Europe Sensen, known overseas as Operation Europe: Path to Victory, to the Famicom with Chinese text. The port stays fairly close to the original, though some elements were removed: generals' statistics, decided by a roulette system in the original, are fixed here, and weapon and tank names were dropped. The campaign mode is gone, but all six scenarios remain: The French Blitz, Desert Storm, Battle of Kursk, Invasion of Normandy, Battle of the Bulge and Battle of Berlin. The game has four endings in total, two bad and two good, and its text mixes Simplified and Traditional Chinese.

t_526f2f2cfdeb.overview: Sachen's second Cai Di Lei release, known in English as Mine Sweeper 2, uses the same rules as the first: every blank tile must be cleared and every mine identified, and triggering a mine makes it explode and ends the game. Instead of fixed difficulty settings, this variant lets the player set a custom board size and number of mines. Choosing a board larger than 512 tiles causes the game to softlock or freeze. As in the other variants, a mine can be hit on the very first click.

t_528762b534c8.overview:
Players control a bowler aiming to knock down pins across a regulation ten-frame match. Before rolling, the bowler is positioned horizontally at the base of the lane. A swinging indicator establishes the hook angle of the throw, after which a rising meter sets the throwing power. Deliveries can be aligned using the lane pins, arrows, or floor boards to direct the ball toward the strike zone for strikes and spares.

Matches support up to four participants, with players one and three sharing the first controller and players two and four sharing the second. Each participant chooses from four distinct characters featuring specific traits such as left- or right-handed deliveries, enters two-letter initials, and selects a ball weight. Action takes place on one of five differently colored lanes that vary in how much they cause a rolled ball to hook.

t_533decc24be9.overview:
Set across side-scrolling stages in Neverland, the journey follows Peter Pan on an adventure to recover his kidnapped children from Captain Hook.

The player controls Peter Pan as he traverses the land to rescue his family. Progress through the adventure ultimately culminates in a final sword confrontation against Captain Hook.

t_5392d80fedea.overview: A side-scrolling action-platformer, the game follows four heroes summoned to stop a demon king who has been released to wreak havoc on their kingdom. The party consists of a climber, a dragon, a golem and a mouse, and the player can switch among them at any time. The climber throws bells and scales walls and ceilings; the dragon flies for brief periods and breathes fire that can be charged up; the slow but strong golem walks on spikes and strikes with short, powerful blows in any direction; and the fast mouse has the least health but fits through narrow passages. The first four stages act as a tutorial for each character and can be played in any order. Each hero has a separate life bar, while all four share a pool of lives.

t_53dbac10ad56.overview: Five Data East games share a single cartridge in this compilation. Ring King is a boxing game in which the player can choose from several types of punches and defensive maneuvers, along with special attacks. Bad Dudes is a beat 'em up built around the rescue of President Ronnie, who has been kidnapped by ninjas. Side Pocket is a billiards game. In BurgerTime, chef Peter Pepper walks across oversized ingredients in a maze of platforms and ladders, dropping them to the level below, while Mr. Hot Dog, Mr. Pickle and Mr. Egg give chase and a limited supply of pepper briefly stuns them. Buggy Popper is a racing game in which cars can be bumped into obstacles or jumped upon and destroyed, and cans of gasoline must be picked up along each course because the car steadily uses up fuel.

t_54559d50993c.overview:
Reaching an exit door to complete each town serves as the primary objective across six worlds. Guiding a character named Rockford, the player digs through mud to gather a required quota of diamonds before an allotted time limit expires.

Various hazards complicate each area, including falling rocks that drop whenever the underlying mud gets cleared away. Creatures such as Pingping, Flapflap, Puffpuff, Piropiro, Tackytacky, and multiplying amoebas also inhabit the stages. Players solve puzzles by managing interactions among these elements, such as dropping rocks onto certain enemies to produce extra diamonds while preventing Rockford from being crushed.

t_54b35cb24a85.overview: Made by NTDEC, this single-screen platform game plays similarly to Balloon Fight: the player kills snakes by bursting the balloons attached to their heads. Two players can play simultaneously, one as Adam and the other as Eve. Unlike Balloon Fight, the game has no auto-scrolling stage and no wrapping from the left or right side of the screen, since every stage is bounded by solid blocks. Beyond its title and characters, the game has very little connection to the biblical story it is named after.

t_54b970792da1.overview: On the Famicom, the shooting game casts the player as Mama Pig, whose babies have been kidnapped by a pack of wolves. She rides an elevator up and down the right edge of the screen, rescuing them with a bow and arrow and slabs of meat. In the first round, wolves descend slowly from a high ledge using balloons, and shooting a balloon sends its wolf falling; wolves also rise from below on balloons. Mama Pig loses a life if she is hit by a rock. Only two arrows can be in flight at once, and a thrown slab of meat lures a wolf into letting go of its balloon. Bonus stages involve dropping wolves with meat or shooting fruit thrown by a boss wolf. Hidden characters can speed up the arrows or the gondola or make meat unlimited.

t_54bc76101f7c.overview: A mahjong solitaire sequel ported from the arcade game, this release structures play as a progression through six puzzles rather than a single board. Five of the layouts are new and named after animals, Tiger, Scorpion, Monkey, Snake and Panther, while the sixth, Dragon, is based on the original Shanghai layout. As in mahjong solitaire, the aim of each puzzle is to remove all the tiles from the board by matching pairs.

t_54fc67420374.overview: Made for the FamicomBox, a pay-for-play system used in hotels, the cartridge carries the wrestling game first released on the Famicom Disk System, complete with that version's unique title screen. The player picks one of six wrestlers, each with a unique set of moves: Fighter Hayabusa, Giant Panther, Kin Corn Karn, King Slender, Starman and The Amazon. Matches are one-on-one, with no tag team bouts; wrestlers can lock up for body slams and piledrivers or climb the top two turnbuckles for aerial attacks, and an in-ring referee runs over to count pins. In single-player play, the wrestler beats a series of computer opponents to win a championship, defends the title and finally faces the Great Puma. Two players can also meet in best-of-three-falls matches with no time limit.

t_55076df222d4.overview: A party board game for one to four players, it follows would-be baseball players from kindergarten toward a professional contract. Each school stage moves pieces with its own minigame: rock-paper-scissors stair climbing against the sun in kindergarten and elementary school, bunny hops in junior high, and batting in high school, plus a pitching game. Entrance tests such as base running and tire pulling, cleared by rapid button presses within a time limit, admit players to elite schools that award balls. Spaces trigger lucky and unlucky events that change height, weight, stamina and popularity. After high school comes the draft; players left unpicked go to a study stage in Hawaii and, if still undrafted, take a throwing tryout where distance sets the contract money. In the final negotiation stage, hitting a prize bag with a throw doubles the money, and the player who signs for the highest amount wins.

t_55a2d00e2612.overview: Professional wrestling for one or two players, built around a roster of eight wrestlers, each modeled on a real-life star of the ring. In the single-player game, the player picks one of the eight and must defeat the other seven to reach the ending. Winning matches along the way earns points that can be spread across three statistics, attack, stamina and speed, to raise the wrestler's abilities; in head-to-head play between two players, the points are assigned before the bout. Matches begin outside the ring, where the wrestlers can brawl or climb straight in. Attempting a hold rotates the view by 90 degrees, and trading moves fills a gauge at the bottom of the screen that, once full, allows a special finishing move.

t_5639b5e538f9.overview: Boxing is shown from a first-person angle, with the screen split into upper and lower halves so that both fighters face forward, one half showing the player's boxer and the other the opponent. Each opponent follows set habits, such as evading every punch to counter or saving up power for a heavy blow, and these patterns change as the bout goes on, so success comes from reading them and striking at openings. The directional pad throws straights, uppercuts and hooks; combined with one button it guards the face or body or sways aside, and with the other it throws body blows. Winning three titles earns a bout with the champion, and the game tells a story in the style of a boys' comic, with a bad ending for losing to the champion. Two players can also box against each other.

t_566008cb92f2.overview: Penta the penguin has grown fat, and his girlfriend Penko dumps him, saying she will only return if he slims down and comes for her. Her new interest, the sunglasses-wearing Ginji, has underlings who feed Penta to keep him heavy. There is no life bar; a body gauge tracks Penta's weight, and his sprite changes as he gains or loses. Food thrown by enemies is eaten on contact, falling into water adds weight quickly, and growing too heavy turns him into a balloon that cannot move for a while. Defeating certain enemies drops slimming medicine. His attack changes with his shape: a mouth missile when slim, a kick at normal weight and a flying body attack when heavy. Each stage sets a time limit and a target weight, and the boss fights of stages 2, 4 and 6 become shooting sections.

t_56e6896bd57d.overview: A sequel to Shenron no Nazo, this card-driven RPG mixes role-playing with command-select adventure scenes as Goku sets out to defeat the revived Piccolo Daimaou. The player normally holds five cards: the stars on a card set how many squares Goku moves across a board-game-style map and decide who attacks in battle, while a kanji numeral sets defense. An event follows every move, from fights against Piccolo's forces to training with Master Roshi, food, Senzu beans and new allies. Companions such as Tien, Yamcha and Bulma are recruited through a memory-matching card game. Every battle is one-on-one, and special moves such as the Kamehameha unlock as Goku levels up. The journey passes Kame House, West City and Penguin Village before ending at Piccolo's castle. Single player.

t_575c21d31606.overview: After Clarisse is kidnapped, Lupin and his companions set out to rescue her, a trail that passes through a villa, Chinatown, a dock warehouse and a pyramid where the legacy of Pandora is sought. Play rotates among three characters, Lupin, Jigen and Goemon, choosing one at the start of every stage and relying on each one's strengths in side-scrolling action. Jigen's gun reaches the edge of the screen with up to three shots at once, while Goemon's Zantetsuken only hits at close range but can chop anything. A character who touches an enemy or falls from a cliff is captured and cannot be used in that stage until rescued, and anyone caught by Zenigata can no longer be saved. Items include bombs that wipe out every enemy on screen, a jet device for flying for a limited time and bulletproof vests that absorb a hit.

t_576a8a99cfb3.overview: Waixing's 2003 Famicom adventure adapts Resident Evil for the PlayStation, following the original game scripts but making Jill the only playable character, with all text in Chinese. The opening recreates the introduction of Resident Evil 1, originally a video, as sprite animation. From the title screen, a new game can be started or progress loaded from four available save slots. Pressing Start opens a fully functional menu, and once the map is obtained, a map option appears there. Saving requires grabbing an ink ribbon and going to a typewriter. The battle system and sprites appear to be derived from Resident Evil Gaiden for the Game Boy Color, while the music includes no tracks from the series. Play is for a single player.

t_57a061ef95ff.overview: Bagdad City has been invaded by the Space Devil Tribe, which carries off the princess and turns the citizens to stone with an evil curse. Prince Aladdin receives a magic arrow and a blanket from the Lamp God and rides a magic carpet straight into the heart of the tribe. The shoot-'em-up runs four levels, mostly in an Arabian setting, with the fourth taking place in space. Enemy groups follow set patterns that grow more complex with each level, and every level ends with a different boss: a witch, a snake in a flying jar, a giant skull and a pair of giant lips. Wiping out certain enemy groups before they disappear yields power-ups that upgrade the weapon, raise speed, add lives or restore hit points. No scoring system is used.

t_57b90028308e.overview: Four card games are gathered on this unlicensed Taiwanese NES cartridge from Sachen, released in 1990. From the menu, players choose among Omnibus Hearts, Fan Tan, Chinese Rummy and The Clock. The same program also appears on some multicarts as Poker 1, marking it as the opening entry of the company's Poker series, which continued with the four-game Poker II compilation and ended with Poker III, a casino board game built around a separate set of card games.

t_57e6c8a638f2.overview: Known in English as Wacky Races, this side-scrolling action game, developed and published by Atlus and based on the cartoon, features Muttley and Dick Dastardly as the main characters, with the player controlling Muttley. The adventure crosses three different areas, Hip Hop, Splish Splash and Go Go America, all of which must be completed to reach the ending. Each of the ten stages ends in a boss battle against one of the other racers. Muttley can jump and initially relies on a short-ranged bite attack, but bones collected along the way can be swapped for other abilities, among them the power to glide with Muttley's tail and extra health.

t_580054415676.overview:
Controlling the protagonist across side-scrolling action environments, the player navigates the setting based on the film Predator. Initial stages leave the player completely unarmed.

Progressing further requires finding and gathering weapons that appear throughout the journey. The player relies on these acquired armaments to advance through the side-scrolling areas.

t_582022ac27e4.overview: Playing as a bird, the player gathers butterflies to feed the chicks waiting in the nest in this single-player action game. The aim on each level is to feed the baby birds enough so they can grow and eventually leave the nest; if too few butterflies are delivered, the young starve. A life is lost when a chick goes unfed or when the bird is caught by predators or other obstacles. Each level represents a season, running from early spring through summer and autumn before returning to spring. Play has no ending sequence: beyond level 999 the levels simply repeat until all lives are gone. A single-level practice game is available alongside the normal game.

t_58401a18cdc2.overview:
Dirk the Daring journeys through a castle to defeat Singe the Dragon and rescue Princess Daphne. Guiding the protagonist through two-dimensional, side-scrolling stages, the player can make Dirk walk, crawl, or jump forward while finding and utilizing diverse weapons to eliminate hostile creatures. Dirk maintains two resource meters, one permitting him to generate light and another tracking the damage he can sustain.

After the Drawbridge and the Entrance Hall, an Elevator Shaft hub leads to stages such as the Gold Mines, the Hall of the Grim Reaper, and Singe's Cavern, alongside the Treasury, where gold can be reclaimed from the Lizard King. Multiplayer allows participants to alternate turns controlling Dirk in a competitive pursuit of high scores, which are recorded on a top-scores screen.

t_5855ad3e0718.overview: Mysterious earthquakes in the year 1999 set the story in motion. Moby, the 18-year-old leader of one VZR's crew, learns of a subterranean empire of monsters called the Nonmalta, which is at war with a race of peaceful humanoids called the Dinamur, and the VZR crew soon find themselves embroiled in the conflict. Released outside Japan as Wurm: Journey to the Center of the Earth, the game mixes side-scrolling travel stages in the VZR vehicles, overhead shooting levels, first-person shooting levels with boss monsters, and levels where Moby leaves the vehicle to explore underground ruins. Each boss has a probability meter that must be raised to 100% before it can be eliminated, and the game is lost if either fuel or energy runs out.

t_58595157c808.overview:
Recovering the Lost Treasure of Babylon from the evil dragon Ryu serves as the goal for Karnov. The player directs the fire-breathing protagonist across nine stages filled with obstacles and bizarre enemies, such as the knife-throwing Lion Keeper, the swooping Chicken Bone, and the boulder-hurling Rock Man. Each environment demands careful navigation to overcome end-stage bosses and reach the final confrontation atop a mountain in the deep forest.

A solo player can run, jump, swim, and project fire against hostile creatures. Gathering special items enhances offensive abilities, allowing Karnov to release double or triple fireballs. Players can also collect and store utility items, including jumping boots, bombs, climbing ladders, and wings, to surmount terrain challenges and survive perilous encounters.

t_58692c0a60b4.overview: Set in a prehistoric age when giant dinosaurs roamed, this Hudson Soft action shooter, released under the Rix Soft label, follows a young man regarded as an ancestor of humankind. Four vertically scrolling stages must be survived, the last made up of four connected areas, and each ends with a boss in a cave. The hero throws weapons and can jump; punch panels upgrade his weapon from stones to axes, boomerangs and finally torches, while taking damage drops it one level. Panels uncovered by hitting obstacles restore or extend health, raise speed, let him float over pits, or clear the screen of enemies, and a hidden panel turns him into Riki, a figure modeled on wrestler Riki Choshu who fires piercing copies of himself. Bosses include a pteranodon, a tyrannosaurus and a giant cobra, and clearing the fourth stage restarts the loop with tougher enemies.

t_58e9f3fe02a5.overview:
Players control the title character, navigating hostile environments while engaging adversaries through direct combat and shooting. Based on the 1987 motion picture, the single-player experience combines elements of side-scrolling brawling with run-and-gun mechanics.

Throughout the adventure, the protagonist advances across stages by confronting opposing threats using hand-to-hand attacks alongside projectile weapons. The overall objective centers on battling through waves of enemies while surviving the hazards found across each area.

t_591549c2736d.overview: Third-grade multiplication and division drive four action games. A submarine marked Z-80 evades depth charges from surface ships and touches the number matching the answer, while a hat-wearing character dodges UFO craft to reach the right number in the sky. In another game, the player climbs a building floor by floor by picking the correct numbers of a division problem, choosing from five options on most floors and three on the roof, with frog-like enemies about; finishing the equation earns a bonus. A car game sends the player searching four locations for numbers while two enemy cars give chase. Two courses set the size of the numbers. The player has four lives, losing one for a wrong answer or contact with an enemy, and the pace quickens as correct answers continue.

t_5924c497e0d2.overview: Developed by Tose and published by Nintendo, this Famicom puzzle game keeps the piece shapes, controls, playfield and game-over condition of Tetris but changes how blocks are cleared. Blocks come in red, blue and yellow, and each falling piece is made of four of them, though no square piece appears and some pieces connect only diagonally at the corners, splitting apart when one part lands. Three or more blocks of the same color lined up vertically or horizontally disappear; simply filling a row does nothing. Each stage begins with fixed blocks plus one glowing flash block in each color. Clearing a flash block removes every fixed block of that color, and clearing all three completes the stage. Matching six or more erases all moving blocks of that color, and falling blocks can trigger chains. In the versus mode, clearing flash blocks lowers a shutter over the rival's field, while chains speed up the rival's falling pieces.

t_592853c02f2f.overview: Seven rounds each present a scrambled picture broken into thirty squares in a five-by-six layout, and the goal is to set the image right. The player's avatar, which changes from round to round, picks up the tiles one at a time and moves them into place. Every puzzle must be finished in under ten minutes or the game is over. Enemies roam the play area while the puzzle is being solved, and running into them costs health; losing all health costs a life, and losing all three lives ends the game. Pausing lets the player view the unscrambled picture. When a puzzle is solved, the remaining time plus the leftover health is added to the score. Later levels contain nudity.

t_593ca49282b8.overview: Taito's side-scrolling action game follows Steve Treiber, an expert in military systems and weaponry, on a mission to stop an artificial brain that has run amok and thrown the world into chaos. His weapon is a boomerang; although it is thrown, its attack range is quite limited. At first the boomerang rebounds when it hits an enemy, so sending it around behind a tough foe can deal heavy damage. Power-up items extend its range or let it pierce enemies, while another item returns a piercing boomerang to normal. There are seven stages in all: the first six can be tackled in any order, and clearing every one of them opens the final stage. Clearing a stage does not award a new weapon, so the starting choice makes little difference. The hero appears as a cartoon-like robot, and the game was later reworked, with overhauled levels and a new look for the hero, into Power Blade.

t_5948c645c780.overview: Set in the Bakumatsu period, this historical simulation from Koei puts the player in the role of Sakamoto Ryōma or another dignitary of the era, with the aim of unifying Japan and starting the Meiji Restoration. Each of 13 powerful domains holds one of three national ideologies, shaped by the views of its lord, chief retainer and senior vassals, and the goal is to bring every domain around to the player's own position through persuasion or force. Dignitaries are won over through discussions, choosing an effective approach for each target from bribery, intimidation, logic, coercion and candor, and allies hand over control of their resources. Rivals may answer with sword fights played out as 2D sword-fighting action, and domains that refuse to come around can be attacked by the player's soldiers in planned assaults.

t_59510b1c6e63.overview: Two teams of five play on a full-length court in this basketball game, which displays the court vertically from a top-down perspective and reveals only half of it at a time. When the ball crosses the half-court line, the screen briefly goes black before showing the other half. A slam dunk attempt pauses play and cuts to a detailed animation of the maneuver. Eight fictional teams take part. Four modes are available: a one-player match against a computer opponent, a two-player cooperative match against the computer, a versus mode that pits two players against each other, and a watch mode for viewing a computer-controlled match.

t_5951fdb5a2f2.overview: Despite the name, this Hummer Team fighting game has nothing to do with the later Capcom release; it is a largely original one-on-one fighter. Many of its attacks and special moves are copied from Street Fighter II, and the first character, Cliff, is based on Ryu, with sprites modified from Ryu's sprites in Hummer Team's own Street Fighter II port. The roster has six different characters, five of them playable. Each character also has a recolored version, and in the single-player mode these recolors act as more difficult versions of the same fighter. The game is one of the few Famicom fighting games to include voice samples.

t_59723f3d4e03.overview: Unlike the arcade original, the Famicom version is a side-view action RPG with an automatic save feature, though it reuses the arcade music. The Space Federation Police have lost many warriors to Madius, leader of the dark organization Mado, and as a last resort the final cyborg warrior, Galivan, is sent into the enemy base. Players guide Galivan through six areas of the base, defeating enemies to make him stronger while solving puzzles such as finding a way to open the path to an area boss or locating a weapon capable of defeating it. Transforming halves the damage Galivan takes from enemies, though his attacks stay the same. The final goal is to defeat Madius.

t_59975f6ec9a0.overview: Billed as a color-based shooter, the game sends its hero through a space represented by multicolored tiles, vaguely resembling a disco floor, to destroy the 7 Masters of Space, with the seven lucky Gods appearing as their opposites. The ship is armed with a blaster and a large mallet. Destroying other spaceships earns money, and mallet kills pay a bonus at greater risk. Gas serves as life: it ticks down constantly and drops further with enemy damage, so the hero must periodically stop to buy more, creating a cycle of destroying enemies to afford fuel. The floor colors matter: green tiles burn gas at the normal rate, yellow slightly faster, and red tiles drain it rapidly while violently shifting the ship. Blue tiles, revealed by picking up a smiley face, restore gas very slowly.

t_59a20842674f.overview: Horse racing seen from the saddle: the player takes the role of a jockey who rides and develops a horse to lead it to victory. Grabbing ability-boost marks that appear during a race raises the horse's abilities, while obstacle races add jumps, and failing to clear one sharply cuts the horse's remaining stamina. Every race has six runners, and finishing fourth or better earns a place in the next race. Two ways to play are offered: a mode devoted purely to racing, and a family game that adds race predictions and betting. Up to two players can take part.

t_59e0752f310b.overview:
Ten levels of action span locations such as Times Square, the SoHo Sewer System, and Snowy Central Park, each concluding with an encounter against a lethal boss. Players select either Leonardo, Raphael, Michaelangelo, or Donatello, each outfitted with their signature weapons such as katana blades, sai daggers, nunchakus, or a bo staff. The mission involves fighting through hordes of Foot Soldiers and assorted enemy machines to rescue April and confront Shredder in the Technodrome.

Turtles can walk in eight directions, jump, attack with their weapons, or combine movements to deliver jumping kicks. Wounds deplete a turtle's life meter, though consuming pizzas restores energy. Each turtle begins with three lives, with a bonus life earned for every two hundred opponents knocked out. The game supports single-player action or two-player cooperative play. If a player exhausts their supply of lives during two-player mode, an extra life can be borrowed from their partner. Up to three continues are available.

t_5a6c72044b89.overview: Mickey Mouse is working part-time selling balloons to buy a present for Minnie, whose birthday is a few days away, when Pluto brings news that she cannot wake up. Finding her trapped in a nightmare, Mickey must journey into Minnie's mind to free her. The balloons he carries are the heart of this platformer: he can use them to attack, to jump higher, or to float. Including the introduction level, there are seven levels, each with its own theme, and at the very end of each level a bonus stage lets the player collect extra lives and extra energy.

t_5a776995d176.overview: A conventional baseball game built around an unusual double cassette system. Sixteen teams are included: twelve modeled on the real professional clubs of the time and four original teams. In versus mode one or two players can pick any of the sixteen, while the pennant race uses one of the twelve league teams over a season of 30, 60, 90 or 130 games; winning the pennant leads to the Japan Series, and becoming champion brings out a hidden SS team that must be beaten to reach the ending. A team edit mode builds a custom squad, and an events menu offers a winning-streak tournament, a home run contest and a watch mode. The back of the main cartridge has a slot for small, separately sold child cassettes carrying updated player data; inserting or removing one clears the save data.

t_5a815beb2b80.overview:
High school students Alex and Ryan journey across River City to confront the villain Slick, who has seized River City High and holds its students captive, including Ryan's girlfriend Cyndi. Reaching River City High requires battling through nine student gangs and a series of bosses. Characters move freely around an open sandbox environment, attacking rivals with punches, kicks, jumps, or improvised weapons like trash cans, lead pipes, and brass knuckles that can be swung or thrown.

Defeating opponents yields money that players spend at local shops on food and sauna visits to replenish health and permanently boost combat attributes. Players also purchase instructional books to learn advanced techniques like Grand Slam, Stone Hands, and Dragon Feet. Progress, including acquired skills, currency, statistics, and beaten bosses, is preserved through a password system. The adventure supports both solo play and a simultaneous two-player cooperative mode.

t_5add3f54a0d9.overview: Despite its title, this 1998 Famicom bootleg draws its gameplay from the SNES Jurassic Park game, while the opening cutscene follows the plot of the sequel, The Lost World. Believed to have been developed by Cony Soft and published by Hosenkan Electronics, it uses a top-down perspective in the overworld and switches to a first-person view inside buildings. The objective is to stun all of the dinosaurs and collect the eggs. Failing at that task brings up a gruesome Game Over screen not found in the SNES game, showing Grant's body with a dinosaur still visible in the background. A glitch that allows jumping through walls makes it possible to beat the game in about a minute.

t_5add7ebb35c2.overview: Whack-a-mole becomes a light-gun game here: NTDEC built the cartridge around the Zapper, and the player shoots the creatures that pop out of holes on the game board. Before play begins, a game mode is chosen from four options that combine two difficulty settings, Normal and Difficult, with the number of moles exposing themselves at the same time, either one or two. Play advances through a series of levels, and the full cartridge release frames the shooting with story and ending sequences.

t_5b0ca6da4b0c.overview: Set in a futuristic post-apocalyptic world where surviving humans cluster in underground villages and ruins, this role-playing game follows a young man who dreams of becoming a monster hunter. There is no predetermined story path: the player chooses which missions to follow and in what order, can visit any place in the world, can complete the game at almost any time and keep playing afterward. The object is to become a respected hunter by defeating monsters with bounties on their heads. Characters fight in turn-based battles on foot or from vehicles, eight of which can be collected, and tanks and their parts can be bought, found and extensively modified, with weapons divided into cannons, machine guns and special weapons.

t_5b1c0143493c.overview: Rather than a conventional game, Ikinari Musician is music software built around a piano-like keyboard, with a treble clef on a staff showing where each note lies. A five-channel backing track accompanies the player, who can pick one of four timbres and adjust common synthesizer parameters such as attack, release and LFO. Backing styles range from Rock, Techno and Jazz to ethnic flavors such as Bossa, Rio, Japan, India and Arabia, and most loop around one or two chords to leave room for open improvisation. Once a style is chosen, the keyboard is limited to a scale that fits it, such as a blues or pentatonic scale. Notes are played with the controller's directional pad, and performances can be recorded and played back.

t_5b7b477cb443.overview: Returning home to Hagure Town after a long journey, Goemon discovers that the family heirloom, the Golden Kiseru, has been stolen. Joined by Ebisumaru, a self-proclaimed righteous ninja, he sets out to recover it, a quest that crosses Shikoku, Chugoku, Sado, Kyushu, Tohoku and Ezo before heading abroad to China and a tropical island. The series turns to role-playing here: the party explores a world map, towns and dungeons, fighting random encounters with turn-based commands. Goemon is a sturdy fighter who cannot use ninjutsu, Ebisumaru balances attack and support ninjutsu, the talking cat Kobanneko is fast with many support skills, and the kunoichi Yae-chan specializes in healing. Towns hold shops, inns, bathhouses, gambling houses and a part-time job office.

t_5c30652beaf2.overview: Dodgeball matches here are fought through cards, following official super dodge rules: seven-player teams with four in the infield and three outside, ten-minute games, and overtime after a tie. Each exchange opens with a jump ball settled by cards; the attackers then pick a shot, a pass or a special shot and a target, the defenders choose a response such as a catch, and both sides play numbered cards from one to five, singly or as doubles and triples, alongside special cards that restore life or swap the hand. The scenario mode combines card battles with adventure as Danpei and his teammates chase the secret of a legendary dodgeball cup found at a temple, gathering coins to buy match items. A card battle mode offers matches against the computer or a second player, and an action mode stages one-on-one dodgeball over three rounds.

t_5c33890daaf0.overview: Based on Tensai Bakabon, this action game from Namco follows Bakabon's Papa as he sets out to rescue his son Hajime and Mama, who have been kidnapped by a junior from Bakada University. Papa infiltrates the university through very long stages, relying on his umbrella for a variety of actions; falling from a height without opening it causes damage and leaves him stunned for several seconds. Ordinary enemies cannot be attacked and must be avoided, with only mid-bosses open to attack, and his dash builds speed slowly and is hard to stop. The stages are a circus, a ninja mansion, a gymnasium and a science area, each closing with a challenge such as catching balls thrown by a clown or a hurdle race against a track athlete. A single mistake restarts the stage, and continues and passwords are available.

t_5c37691c7989.overview: An ordinary programmer who unwinds at the pachinko parlor after work is secretly Super Salary 008, an agent who solves any problem with pachinko. His boss orders him to destroy an enemy nation's hideouts, supplying only 100 balls. Each of the three hideouts has three or four floors linked by warp zones, and winning at the machines raises a score spent at counters. The item counter sells a fixed shooting technique, reach patterns that raise the jackpot odds on seven machines, and steadier spring control. The weapon counter sells grenades, rocket launchers and missiles, none of which can destroy a hideout alone, so they must be combined. Wrecking a whole hideout clears the stage and earns a 10-character password. An optional time set makes a machine explode unless it is emptied within 10 minutes of reaching the halfway mark, and a dedicated pachinko controller can be used.

t_5c555a39f000.overview: Built around the arithmetic of the fifth and sixth school years, this educational cartridge in the Tokyo Shoseki calculation series poses semi-complex problems involving fractions, decimals and long division. Two minigames carry the lessons, and in each one the player simply has to locate the number or numbers that complete the sum or equation on the screen in order to proceed. One minigame is a side-scrolling science fiction shoot 'em up with top-down sections on foot. The other is an action game in which a young girl tries to keep her garden free of bugs.

t_5c7ad2548226.overview: In the year 373 of a new space calendar, overpopulation has pushed humanity toward space colonies, and Jay McCray's father, a scientist on the colony project in the Silius Solar System, dies when the station is destroyed in an explosion. Jay finds a disk holding the complete colony plans and a message asking him to finish the work, and sets out to fight the terrorists responsible. The side-scrolling run-and-gun spans five stages, including colony ruins, an underground concourse, the enemy hideout, a flying spaceship and a factory, each ending with a boss. Jay can lie down but aims only left or right. Besides his handgun he can obtain a shotgun, machine gun, homing gun, laser rifle and grenade launcher, all drawing on a Gun Energy gauge. Known abroad as Journey to Silius, the Japanese release shows Jay covered in full-body armor.

t_5c89e979374c.overview: Beginning in the year 200, this historical simulation sets the player the task of unifying the divided land. Instead of picking a ruler directly, the player answers a personality quiz, and one of six rulers is assigned automatically from the answers. Every command costs one order sheet, and the number of sheets depends on the provinces held and the level chosen at the start. Commands are issued from four icons covering the castle, storehouse, army and town, including gathering information on generals, conscription and marching to war. Attacking an enemy unit switches to a battle phase in which infantry, cavalry, archers and general units line up in one of four preset formations; the player gives broad orders such as advance or retreat, and the fight plays out automatically. Each war has a ten-day limit.

t_5cdcf2b46ad3.overview: Long ago a race of beast-men ruled the earth until the gods, angered by their arrogance, sealed them away in stone tablets. A thousand years later a demon rises from underground, conquers the land and captures the goddess Athena, daughter of Zeus, who frees the beast warriors to defeat the demon and rescue her. In this side-scrolling action game, defeated enemies drop Spirit Balls that power up the warrior in stages; after three, he transforms into a beast-man with a special attack of its own, and the beast available is fixed for each stage. This Famicom adaptation of the arcade game expands the journey to eight stages, adds original beast forms and bosses, and does not support simultaneous two-player play.

t_5d083ee84c7e.overview: Aliens have captured a woman, and Takahashi Meijin gives chase across eight islands to rescue her in this side-scrolling platformer. He can run, jump, swim and throw weapons, while a timer counting down doubles as an energy bar that fruit, milk and meat keep replenished. Hidden eggs, opened with weapons or by jumping on them, hold weapon upgrades, restoring items, keys to secret areas and the hero's five dinosaur friends; each color-coded dinosaur has its own power, such as the flying Pteranodon or the fast-swimming Elasmosaurus, and a mount quickly abandons its rider when he is hit. An eggplant makes the energy meter drain faster. Before each level, one item of each kind can be selected, including boomerangs or axes, the invincibility of Honey Girl, a Time-Stop that freezes the timer, or a dinosaur partner.

t_5d13d46428af.overview: Drawn from the television period drama Hissatsu Shigoto Nin, this command-selection adventure casts the player as Nakamura Mondo, one of a band of hitmen operating in Edo. The goal is to unravel the mystery behind a sudden attack carried out by a child. Investigation proceeds by choosing commands from menus, and at times the story shifts into a battle mode in which enemies must be fought off. The tale unfolds over four chapters and involves the Minami-machi magistrate's office, a yakuza boss accused of spiriting away young women to sell overseas, a merchant suspected of illegal smuggling, and the leader of a group of shadow ninja. Every character is drawn in a super-deformed style, and the game is for one player.

t_5d20bd3ac605.overview: Teaching mahjong is as much the aim here as playing it, in a two-player mahjong title that opens with lesson modes. The first lesson names the tools and tiles, explains sets such as sequences and triplets, seating and choosing the dealer, and how a game proceeds; the second covers dora, scoring and point exchange, winning hands and ten multiple-choice practice questions. A third lesson is a beginner match in which a sub-menu can retry the hand, reveal the opponent's tiles or ask the computer which tile to discard. The main match mode offers a choice of six opponents, the strongest of whom, the master, adds a time limit. Calls such as pon, chi, kan and riichi are each assigned to a direction on the control pad and made by pressing it.

t_5d260e5fc812.overview:
Guiding a roller skater through side-scrolling stages, the player battles hostile goons to rescue the kidnapped commissioner. Before each stage begins, the player selects one of three star skaters: Ice Box from the Thunderbirds, Rolling Thunder from Hot Flash, or California Kid from the Rockers. Odd-numbered stages require navigating across courses and fighting off opposing team members before facing an enemy leader in a boss encounter under a time limit.

The first two even-numbered stages feature transitional auto-scrolling obstacle courses without time limits, requiring skaters to dodge barrels and bombs dropped from overhead helicopters while jumping gaps in the road. The sixth stage returns to a time limit, concluding with a final boss fight. Lives are lost whenever a skater runs out of energy, falls into a pit, or fails to complete a timed stage before the countdown expires.

t_5d8e762eb558.overview:
Controlling the mouse Mappy, the player gathers gifts scattered across themed environments while evading antagonistic cats. Progression requires navigating through eight areas, such as Railroad Town and Ghost Town, using ladders and trampolines to move between floors. Each stage requires finding the required target items—such as cheese, wedding rings, Christmas trees, or baseballs—before reaching the right-hand exit. If an exit is closed, a hidden entrance must be found to explore a sub-area for a necessary item to proceed.

Defense relies on portable protection weapons like toys, gold coins, pots, and fish to divert or incapacitate pursuers. Stages also contain fighting weapons such as bowling balls and flashlights to defeat enemies temporarily. The game spans four stories, culminating in Muky Town before delivering the collected presents to the castle.

t_5dbe1cc38f54.overview: Professor Moriarty, the nemesis of Sherlock Holmes, issues the challenge in this first-person adventure based on the stories by Arthur Conan Doyle. Taking the role of the detective, the player has to go through places like France, Austria and Germany to solve the mystery, and ten other characters can be met and questioned along the way. Progress is kept with passwords: at the start, players choose between beginning a new adventure or continuing an old one by entering a password of Japanese characters. It follows two earlier detective adventures starring Holmes from the same publisher.

t_5dbf3f690b69.overview: Told through menu-driven command selection, the story follows Erika, a granddaughter of the bedridden tycoon Tomiko, who will leave her fortune to whichever heir accomplishes the most in the next three months. While her sisters Shizuka and Reika rely on business and science, Erika's only talent is singing, so she sets out to break through as a super idol with the help of a band of allies. Standing in her way is Dark Lord Iromono, who wants to recruit her into his army. Friends and sometimes rivals offer advice on what to do next, and the commands on offer narrow to suit each scene, so little repetition is needed. Six J-pop songs feature along the way, with lyrics shown on screen instead of being sung.

t_5dcca2efce2b.overview: Played from a behind-the-bike perspective, this motorcycle racer was built around an unusual peripheral: an inflatable motorcycle with a special handlebar controller built in. Once the bike is fully inflated, the player sits on it and uses the handlebars to steer the motorcycle on screen. Two modes are offered. Grand Prix strings several consecutive races together, while Touring lets the player pick one of four courses for a single race. In both its viewpoint and its racing style, the game closely resembles Sega's Hang-On series of motorcycle racers.

t_5dd1e8b68da2.overview:
Solid Snake infiltrates the fortified state of Outer Heaven, avoiding enemy detection from an overhead perspective across flip-screen areas. The rookie special forces operative must rescue captured hostages and neutralize a nuclear-armed bipedal mecha known as Metal Gear. Snake begins without armaments and collects gear across five fortified strongholds of one to three floors each. Weapons including handguns and rocket launchers, alongside items like rations, key cards, and a gas mask, help him progress through locked sectors and combat mercenary bosses.

Guards follow set routes and trigger alert states upon spotting Snake or detecting noise. Cameras and unsuppressed gunfire also raise alerts, and alerted guards summon reinforcements until Snake defeats them or flees to another screen. Rescuing hostages raises Snake's star rank, boosting his maximum health and ammunition capacity. Throughout the operation, a radio transceiver allows communication with Commander South and resistance contacts across designated frequencies.

t_5ddc0d66698a.overview: An improved follow-up to Sachen's falling-block puzzler Pyramid, released the same year, Pyramid II drops stones of various shapes and sizes from the top of the screen. The player moves and rotates them to fill complete lines at the bottom, and the game ends if the stones reach the top. Unlike the square and rectangular pieces of Tetris, each shape has one or more angles, which makes complete lines harder to form. The sequel adds different playing modes, a better menu and a two-player mode. Its story holds that an evil living in the pyramids is released in 20xx, so God sends a "Marvelous Soldier" to stop the revival.

t_5e0035c17554.overview: Built on Hudson Soft's Adventure Island, this Taiwanese rework rebrands the game around Kiddy Sun, a character from a Taiwanese children's television show by CTS. The title screen shows Kiddy Sun climbing into a hot air balloon. The changes are mainly to graphics and music: the fruits that keep the hero going have become fast food items, Kiddy Sun rides a bike instead of a skateboard, most enemies have been redesigned, and the soundtrack has been altered. Described as an officially licensed hack, the cartridge appears to have been commissioned as a pack-in title for the Era Entertainment System, a Famiclone sold by EraTech, which had formed a joint venture with Hudson Soft.

t_5e0e426b6622.overview: Hummer Team ported Fatal Fury Special to the Famicom in this unlicensed fighting game. The roster holds eight characters with four repeats of each: Kim Kaphwan, Tung Fu Rue, Wolfgang Krauser, Ryo Sakazaki, Terry Bogard, Andy Bogard, Joe Higashi and Mai Shiranui, and all of them are playable. The difficulty can be changed on the title screen. Unlike the original, the fighters do not get their own stages; the stages instead run in a preset loop throughout the game, and some of the characters' original stages are absent. Graphics are taken from the original game and downgraded, most of the music comes from it as well, and the ending is a shortened version of the original's.

t_5e9788d04c9d.overview: Developing psychic powers through a home console is the premise of this unusual adventure, supervised by a psychic who also appears in it as a guide. In the first half, the player completes basic training and a graduation exam at a psychic school by following his instructions; in the second half, events around a psychic city are tackled to hone those abilities. Every training session, exam and event is one of three minigames: clairvoyance, such as naming the picture on a face-down card or an object hidden in a box; telekinesis, pressing the A button ten or twenty times while concentrating; and precognition, predicting which lamp will light or the color of the next passing car. Successes earn points that raise a psychic level, and reaching the maximum starts the final event.

t_5ea11bede10f.overview: Rather than a solitaire puzzle played with mahjong tiles, Sachen's 1989 Taiwan 16 Mahjong is a full game of mahjong played under Taiwanese rules, including the unique number of tiles dealt to each player that gives the title its 16. As with Nintendo's Mahjong for the Famicom, play is limited to two participants: one human player against one computer opponent. Two difficulty modes are available, Beginner and Expert. The title screen credits L.C. Tchacvosky, as on most of Sachen's SA-series releases.

t_5ec992f2b039.overview: An original sequel, this single-player side-scrolling action game brings back Yanchamaru with a new look and a staff as his weapon. Unlike the first game, touching an enemy or being hit by an attack no longer means instant failure; instead the hero has a life gauge of three, and striking foes with the staff no longer knocks it out of his hands. Princess Kurumi of Edo Castle returns from the previous adventure, as does that game's final boss Zoringen, while a mysterious figure named Arakutsuna Genyusai leads a squad of foxes. The route covers eight areas: a land of sweets, a miniature town, a forest railway, a haunted forest, an underground world, a sheer cliff mountain, a labyrinth and a final castle.

t_5ef6ca833f47.overview: Stripping away the story, transformations and magic of the main series, this Culture Brain spin-off concentrates purely on one-on-one martial arts fighting. Players choose from two fighters per fighting style, a roster that includes Ryuhi and the other Dragon Warriors except Minmin. Training menus earn points that are spent to improve a fighter, and a developed fighter can be saved as a password for later use in versus play. Wrestlers have slimmer builds and new moves, and some characters gained grappling techniques. Beyond head-to-head matches, a tournament mode has players fight their way through a bracket, and a tag-team mode lets partners be swapped mid-match by tagging in.

t_5f0e688f78b3.overview: Based on the 1991 Formula One season, this sequel to Nakajima Satoru F-1 Hero offers sixteen rounds and a choice of only four cars. Warming Up mode lets the player practice five laps on any of the sixteen tracks to master specific turns, while Battle mode splits the screen for a race of up to ten laps against a computer-controlled driver or a second player. The career is played in Grand Prix mode, a series of races to work through in order, and a spectator mode lets the player sit back and watch computer-controlled drivers compete against each other.

t_5f38c62ab36c.overview: Two fairies, Tam and Rit, set out to rescue their mother, who is trapped in a tower. Armed with magic rods, they work through single-screen levels built from monsters, platforms, ladders and, later, tunnels. A rod does not kill an enemy outright; it leaves the monster immobilized, after which the rod can grasp it in a magic force-field and smash it repeatedly against the ground until it disappears and leaves a power-up behind. Each fairy can also conjure one custom ladder above or below her to reach another platform, and summoning it again moves it next to her. The NES version adds new platform stages and, unlike the other versions, lets the player jump. One or two players can take part.

t_5f6e8c798d7c.overview: Two lumberjacks, Bob and Jim, set out to save the princess and king of Marry Land in this Famicom port of a Taito arcade platformer. Each single-screen stage is cleared by eliminating every enemy: a swing of the mallet stuns a foe, which can then be picked up and hurled at a wall or into other enemies for bonus points. Defeated enemies leave fruit, and power-ups can speed the heroes up or change the way they attack, though some items have negative effects. Lingering too long on a stage summons a flying devil. Finishing the regular stages rescues only the princess, while a hidden shortcut on the first stage opens a secret set of levels leading to the ending in which the king is saved as well.

t_5f76c5290d1f.overview: Linus, an alien from the planet Linoleum, once crashed on the legendary planet Earth, but back home his fellow Linomen doubt that it exists. He decides to return there with a camera, yet he has no money and must adventure around his home world to acquire a vehicle and a camera. Much of the game plays as a point-and-click adventure: Linus is directed with a cursor and written commands, and items must be collected and later used in specific locations. Teleporting devices in each major location often leave him with a side-effect needed to solve a puzzle. Between adventure areas, platforming sections require crossing the level while avoiding falls and enemies and collecting Cosmic candy, with ten pieces earning an extra life. Passwords are scattered at key locations.

t_5f895b71db78.overview: Built around the professional J-League, this soccer game for the Family Computer centers on club competition, with the objective of winning the championship so that the player's chosen team can be called the greatest in all of Japan. Four ways to play are offered: a one-off exhibition, a season mode, a playoff mode, and a practice mode. Matches can be played alone or by two players.

t_6055472a57de.overview: Based on Harold Sakuishi's Gorillaman manga, this board game puts up to six players in the role of students at the hero's high school, racing for the top spot across three scenarios. Dice move everyone through a school day: the race from the station to school, a dress check at the gate, a dash through the halls, a desk-grabbing game in the classroom, and the trip home with stops at the game center or a part-time job. Event points decide the winner at the finish, while hit points matter in sports events and in fights with students from rival schools. Action events include arm wrestling, baseball, a 50-meter dash, slot machines, roulette, horse racing and a high-low card game. A party mode plays only the gambling or sports events, and the Partytap peripheral lets six people play at once.

t_607ce04f21fe.overview: Teaching the basics of Go is the purpose of Jang Doo Jin's Baduk Clinic: First Lesson, the Golden Bell release commonly known as Korean Igo. Rather than a conventional game, it works as Baduk training software, and it presents its instruction through a large amount of Korean text that the program generates on the fly instead of storing every character combination. The player can either follow its lessons step by step or play a versus game against another person.

t_6092e41c2cda.overview: Pachislot competition forms the core of this adventure, whose hero takes on five rivals in a bid to become the number one slot player. Each round is played against a time limit, with everyone competing for the most coins, each coin worth 20 points. Points are awarded by finishing position in each round, and the overall winner is decided by the point total after six rounds. Several machine types are available, each with its own payouts and reach patterns, which can be checked with the select button while seated at a machine, and the effects of lining up a big bonus or a regular bonus differ from machine to machine. A difficulty level is chosen before play, and the game is for one player.

t_609d79b3d5e1.overview: Released in Japan as the counterpart of Track & Field II, the Olympic-themed sports collection has the player choose a country to represent before competing in events such as fencing, triple jump, freestyle swimming, high dive, clay pigeon shooting, hammer throw, taekwondo, pole vault, canoeing, archery, hurdles and the horizontal bar.
