Training mode tests the player's abilities in each event, while Olympic mode is a story mode in which the chosen country competes against the world's best, with hang gliding appearing as a bonus event between rounds. Versus mode lets two players compete head-to-head, and arm wrestling is offered as an exhibition against the computer.

t_60afbae94f03.overview: Found on multicarts under the English title, this edition of Waixing's Happy Biqi III: World Fighter is a clone of the SNES version of Earthworm Jim 2 in which a regular kid named Biqi takes the place of Jim. Its stages are Wood Hills, Water Monster Tunnel, Flight, Farm, Mine, Electric City and Puppy Love, each drawn from a level of the original. Maximum ammo is limited to 255 bullets, presumably because of memory limits, and movement through Water Monster Tunnel is slower than in other versions. Apart from the Puppy Love tune, all music is Waixing's own. A scene of Biqi and the princess follows each completed level. The battery save of the single-cart release was removed here, so pressing Start does nothing.

t_60c94486a7df.overview: Joy Van's horizontal shooter, released by Color Dreams as Metal Fighter, stars the MCS-920, a robot nicknamed Joyvan Kid outside the U.S. release. After three centuries of intergalactic missions it returns to Earth to find the planet overtaken by bionic alien lifeforms; the few survivors have been driven into hiding or turned into bionic allies of the invaders. Play mixes scrolling shooting with slight platforming elements: the MCS-920 starts with no flight ability and can only jump, and the first power-up is always flight. Apart from flight and speed, power-ups must be won by beating a miniboss that is a doppelganger of the player's ship, and each win also adds a point of health. Every round ends with a boss, and touching a boss causes instant death regardless of remaining health.

t_60d1794a0f05.overview: A year after his defeat, Dr. Wily builds a new fortress and a fresh set of Robot Masters to counter Mega Man, and Dr. Light sends his robot hero to stop him. Eight stages, ruled by Metal Man, Air Man, Bubble Man, Quick Man, Crash Man, Flash Man, Heat Man and Wood Man, can be tackled in any order. Every defeated Robot Master yields a unique weapon tied to its stage, and each boss is vulnerable to certain others' weapons. Some stages also award support items that create platforms. With all eight beaten, the hero storms Dr. Wily's fortress, a run of five linear levels that includes rematches against every Robot Master in a single room. The Energy Tank refills health on demand, and a password appears after each Robot Master falls.

t_60e1ead5b027.overview: Flappy, the hero of this puzzle-action game, must carry the Blue Stone to a designated spot called the Blue Area within the time limit to clear each stage, and every stage holds exactly one of each. Several Brown Stones sit in each stage and serve as tools for moving the Blue Stone, filling holes and building bridges. Enemies get in the way, including Ebira, a red crab-like creature that heads toward Flappy with some random movement, and Unicorn, a green horned foe that wanders left and right. Picking up a sleeping mushroom and throwing it at an enemy puts that enemy to sleep for a while. The Famicom version contains 200 regular stages plus 40 bonus stages, 240 in all.

t_60e4221a9401.overview: Shooting action meets role-playing elements in this horizontally scrolling Sigma Enterprises release. The Dimensional Stone, which keeps the world in balance, has been stolen, and a king selects a hero to recover it. The Fuzzical Fighter, a mechanical craft resembling a spaceship with a mechanical tail, carries the hero into enemy territory. Between stages, towns can be visited to buy weapons and artifacts with gold. Staying at the inn allows a return to an earlier stage, or the hero can press on to an unexplored one. The craft has magic points that are refilled in towns, and three healing spells are available: Riken for minor healing, Rikento for normal healing and Rikentaru for major healing. A large purple dragon waits as the final boss. Play is for a single player.

t_610ef7675adc.overview: Panic! Dizzy gathers five separate skill games on one cartridge: Four Suits, Match More, Dizzy Dice, Puzzle Path and Picture Perfect. The design keeps the idea of matching shapes in columns from the earlier computer game and reintroduces the original concept of Dizzy running back and forth, this time along the bottom of the screen. Every member of the Yolkfolk can be played, and for the first time the Evil Wizard Zaks joins them as a playable character. Each game can be tackled alone or as a head-to-head battle against a friend in two-player action.

t_611331e30633.overview: Pachio-kun, the mascot of a long series of pachinko games, debuts in this virtual pachinko hall containing 72 different machines. The overall goal is to keep playing each machine, whether through a determined strategy or simple perseverance, until every one has been emptied of its contents, which wins the game. Several machines have quirks that reward attentive pachinko veterans, such as the frequency of payouts or certain pins being bent to favor a ball's route to the bottom. To work out how to make a machine pay out, Pachio-kun can lean in and examine it more closely.

t_616325543265.overview: Taito's 1991 entry in the Kyuukyoku Harikiri Stadium baseball series introduces a pennant race of up to 130 games and adds player data editing. Beyond the regular clubs, the lineup of teams includes the all-female Idol team, a Meikyukai team of baseball greats, a team of historical foreign players, and an edit-only team for building a custom roster. For the first time in the series, games can be played in a choice of three ballparks.

t_6180ed85f15e.overview: King Suren's forces have been captured by King Ogreth and turned into trees and rocks, so this Famicom version of the action-strategy game opens with King Suren alone at 597m. Bumping into trees, cacti, rocks and walls restores his warriors, building an army that moves with him across the battlefield toward the enemy castle. When units collide, the battle is decided automatically based on the difference in their offensive strength, and units can gain experience and level up. Obstacles call for specific units: only Knights break the gates holding captive Soldiers, Soldiers clear death tiles by stepping on them, and only King Suren can break the walls at 500m, 400m, 300m and 200m. The game ends if King Suren dies and is won by defeating King Ogreth.

t_61b78500ef48.overview: Armed with a lance, the knight Arthur sets out to rescue a kidnapped princess by breaking through six gates guarded by demon generals and defeating the great demon king. Seven stages, many split into two halves, are crossed by walking, crouching, climbing ladders and jumping; every jump has a fixed distance and arc, so the landing point cannot be finely adjusted. One hit knocks off Arthur's armor and a second turns him into a skeleton, costing a life; new armor can be picked up and is restored when a stage is cleared. Pots release weapons and point items, among them a dagger, torch, axe and cross, each attacking differently, and the cross, which cancels enemy shots, is needed for the final battle. Clearing the first loop reveals it as Satan's illusion, and the Famicom version ends once a harder second loop is cleared.

t_6252947b2e85.overview: Piloting the starship Galaxip, the player faces rows of aliens massed in formation near the top of the screen, and each round ends only when every alien has been shot down. Only a single shot can be in the air at a time, so a miss means waiting until it hits something or leaves the screen. Aliens peel away from the formation to dive-bomb the ship while firing, and touching an enemy or its projectile costs a life. Flagships dive with two red escorts, and shooting all three earns bonus points, with extra for the flagship. Enemy movement and fire intensify as play continues. On the Famicom, mass wave attacks start once six or fewer aliens remain in formation, and alien movement differs slightly from the arcade original.

t_6272f6fb05fe.overview: In this maze game styled after Pac-Man, the green dragon Tamagon works through a series of mazes patrolled by monsters. Touching a Cross powers him up so he can breathe fire and eat the dots; without one he is completely helpless and cannot clear the maze. The Devil dances at the top of the screen and points in a direction, and four of his minions shift the maze with pulleys and ropes, so Tamagon can be squished between a maze wall and the moving outer boundary. After the first maze, the objective becomes gathering four Bibles and placing them into a seal, with the Bibles granting the same powers as the Crosses. Between mazes, a bonus round has Tamagon collect six Bonus Boxes under a time limit. A second player controls a red version of Tamagon.
t_6272f6fb05fe.official: In this hidden gem of an action game from Mario creator Shigeru Miyamoto, you play heroic dragon Tamagon, who must defeat evil by collecting boa-boa dots inside a maze and destroying enemies with his fire breath. However, keep an eye on the devil at the top of the screen, who instructs his minions to move the maze in random directions, trying to squash Tamagon within its walls!

t_6273248622fb.overview: Konami's block-shooting puzzle game mixes falling-block play with a fixed shooter. Blocks in various incomplete shapes descend toward a spaceship at the bottom of the screen, which fires blocks upward to turn the falling patterns into squares or rectangles. Each completed shape is destroyed and scores points based on its size, and as each level progresses the blocks drop at greater speed and frequency. A ship caught by the descending blocks is "quarthed," crushed flat. The Famicom version has nine levels with an option to choose the starting level, and two players can compete in a split-screen mode, with Player 1 on the left and Player 2 on the right, or cooperate on a shared screen.

t_627a63439e1d.overview: Set in 1931 America against a backdrop of organized crime, this shooting game adapts an arcade original in which a crosshair is aimed at enemies appearing from the scenery. When a gunman turns to fire, a countdown appears in the lower right of the screen, and he must be shot before it reaches zero. Mistakenly hitting a woman costs points, and small boxes can be broken to release items such as extra ammunition. A round is cleared by defeating every enemy in it. The Famicom version drops the vertical scrolling and replaces the endless loop with a stage structure, ending each stage with a boss whose behavior and weak points differ. Shooting certain parts of the background yields a bulletproof jacket, a password appears after every stage, and clearing all stages leads to the ending.

t_627eb6cc3acc.overview: Loosely following the early Dragon Ball manga, this action-adventure takes Goku through 14 stages in three parts: a journey with his friends, a kung fu tournament at Tarin Temple, and a final campaign against the mysterious MB Army in space. Exploration is viewed from above, with side-view screens for enemies and bosses. Goku begins with punches, but the Nyoibo staff gives him a stronger, longer-reaching attack, and the Kamehameha is a powerful ranged blast with limited uses. His Power falls over time and from enemy attacks, so food must be collected constantly. Enemies sometimes drop Hoipoi Capsules holding items, and the Nimbus instantly carries him to a specific point in the stage. Clearing stages 6 and 14 gathers all seven Dragon Balls, and Shenron appears to grant one of four wishes. Single player.

t_62b0d751c7d7.overview: One-on-one martial arts duels drive this home version, in which the hero Lee infiltrates the Menma Tower to defeat the villainous Chop Suey Gang. Where the arcade original has eleven opponents, Lee faces only five: Wang, armed with a pole; Tao, who breathes fireballs; Chen; Lang, with quick shots and moves; and the gang's leader Mu, who attacks with a leaping motion. Each fighter has a health meter that depletes with every hit, and an empty meter means a knockout. After Chen is beaten, a bonus round has the hero hit thrown objects to score points. Defeating Mu sends Lee to kick the gong, and the game loops with higher difficulty and different background colors.

t_62bafdd36537.overview: Set more than a decade after the events of the original manga, this role-playing game tells an entirely original story. The hero is no longer Kenshiro but a young boy, named by the player, who aims to become the successor of Hokuto Shinken. As in the previous installment, allies join along the way to form a party of up to four. Ordinary enemies can be fought as a group, while boss battles remain one-on-one encounters. Weapons and armor must be replaced frequently, because older equipment soon becomes useless against higher-level enemies, and the dungeons are long and demanding. Kenshiro himself appears in the later part of the adventure.

t_62bbba2bff69.overview: Murder in Kyoto sets this mystery adventure in motion: one summer afternoon in 1990, the player character and a friend, a budding actress, wait at a temple for an old high-school classmate, now a researcher at a pharmaceutical company, only to find her dead. The two set out to learn why she was killed, uncovering an affair with her superior, a lavish lifestyle, suspected industrial espionage, rivalry between venture companies and insider trading, while further murders follow. Investigation uses simple command selection, with the available commands narrowed to what each scene requires. Stock investing runs through the story: at a securities office the player can view price charts and buy and sell shares from two million yen in starting funds, although gains or losses do not affect the outcome. Up to three players' progress can be saved.

t_62d3939d8e48.overview: Hummer Team's unlicensed version of Final Fight 3 is a direct port of the SNES game of the same name. All four playable characters from the original are present, along with most of its enemies, bosses and rounds, although the weaker enemies appear throughout the whole game. Fewer enemies appear on screen at any given time to prevent sprite flicker, which makes the port easier than the SNES release, and there is only one route through the game instead of the original's branching paths. A black bar at the top of the screen holds the players' score and data, while a bar at the bottom shows the current round. Cutscenes taken from the original's stories appear between rounds, and the ending copies Dean's ending from the SNES game.

t_630d59e8fc53.overview: Battery backup arrives in the Famista baseball series from Namco with this entry, which also adds switch-hitters and sidearm pitchers alongside overhand and underhand throwers. A pennant mode replaces the earlier winning-streak format: two to six teams play a league of one to nine games per matchup, up to 45 games in all, and a game can last one, three, five or nine innings. In place of player editing, a helper registration mode creates players whose ratings depend on their name and type, and they can join any team in pennant play. The roster includes the Namco Stars, the Major Leaguers and two formerly hidden squads, the Pro Stars and Anime Stars. Six stadiums are available, four of them new, including an asymmetrical park modeled on Fenway Park. One or two players can play.

t_6321f5e037b2.overview:
Star Wars features side-scrolling platforming on Tatooine and aboard the Death Star alongside landspeeder, asteroid field and cockpit flight segments.

The player begins as Luke Skywalker, crossing the Tatooine Desert by landspeeder and exploring its caves and Mos Eisley in search of the runaway droid R2-D2, Obi-Wan Kenobi and Han Solo, before rescuing Princess Leia from the Death Star cell block. Luke, Han and Leia can each be controlled, and only Luke can swing a lightsaber. Han and Leia have a single life each, though Obi-Wan can use the Force to revive them, while C-3PO and R2-D2 offer advice and R2-D2 can display Death Star maps. After escaping through the trash compactor and hangar, the player fights waves of TIE fighters as the Millennium Falcon's gunner, then pilots an X-wing against the Death Star, ending with a trench run to hit the exhaust port. The score reflects the percentage of tasks completed.

t_634842ee2e54.overview:
Play progresses through a continuously looping sequence of three zones: a bike chase through an obstacle zone, a bike chase across a slippery zone, and a final battle with the Dinosaur Tank across the battery zone. The player steers the rescue bike Gilgitt Petras, throwing enemy Basrah bikes into walls and obstacles or destroying enemies with a laser beam.

While maneuvering through each area, the bike rescues stranded Petras for bonus points and collects Energy Packs that refill its energy; carrying too many Petras drains energy faster, and the bike stops working when its energy reaches zero. In the slippery zone, excessive movement can send the bike sliding into obstacles. Up to two players are supported.

t_635711a9238b.overview: A golf simulation for one or two players, The Golf '92 is set on an 18-hole course whose holes include greens surrounded by ponds or bunkers and a stretch of sweeping cliffs. Each shot is set up on a three-dimensional screen: the player fixes the aiming mark, picks one of 14 clubs, chooses where to strike the ball for topspin, backspin, a hook or a slice, and then stops a power gauge and a timing gauge. Stroke play competes on total strokes over 18 holes against computer-controlled golfers. Match play is a knockout bracket decided hole by hole, and winning four matches in a row takes the title. A practice round plays the course without results. Three difficulty ranks change the wind direction and strength and the slope of the greens.

t_63626305c972.overview: Sixteen players, drawn as three-heads-tall characters, take the court in this tennis game, which gives distinct handling to ball spin such as topspin and slice, serve speed and footwork. Four of the sixteen are women, who use larger rackets than the men. Matches can be played on four surfaces: an all-round hard court, low-bouncing lawn, slowing clay, and a high-bouncing cosmo court. Three modes are offered. Exhibition is singles only, with two players facing off head to head; the tournament mode lets players take turns through a bracket of up to eight; and the world tour has a chosen player working through six tournaments.

t_6394633b3880.overview: A slot machine simulation with adult rewards, the game offers three machines, Cutie Bunny, Juicy Fruits and Las Vegas, each with its own visual design and music. Players buy medallions, wager up to five of them on each pull, stop each reel by pressing a direction on the D-pad, and may move to another machine between spins. A scantily clad hostess accompanies every machine and appears whenever net winnings pass set thresholds, wearing less clothing at each higher level of profit until she appears nude.

t_64139acc5f44.overview: A one-on-one martial arts action game, Karateka follows an unnamed protagonist attempting to rescue Princess Mariko from Akuma's castle fortress. The hero advances through the fortress and enters a fighting stance to punch, kick and dodge each enemy in the way. Health bars for both the hero and the current enemy are displayed at the bottom of the screen, and the game ends when the hero's bar is empty. Akuma also sends a trained hawk that can be deflected with well-timed punches or kicks, and environmental hazards such as an open cliffside or a falling portcullis are fatal. Cutscenes show Akuma ordering his men to attack and Mariko nervously awaiting her fate. Approaching Mariko while still in a fighting stance earns an instantly fatal kick.

t_642d2b599495.overview: Built on the third Puss in Boots film from Toei Animation, this platformer stars Pero, the cat in boots, who is called Perrault in the game. Loosely following Around the World in Eighty Days by Jules Verne, the journey must be completed within 80 days, shown as a time limit in which roughly one day passes every minute; certain items take days away, and if the 80 days run out the game ends no matter how many lives remain. The trip leads through England, the Atlantic Ocean, Arabia, Hong Kong, the Pacific Ocean, Alaska, the North Pole and Big Ben, and alongside the usual walking stages Pero also drives boats, cars and balloons. Contact with water means instant death.

t_645bb04320ab.overview: Built around Gachapin and Mukku from the children's television program, this educational game sends the pair on outings to five islands: a mountain hike, a swim in the sea, a zoo, an amusement park and a trip to space. Each island holds the same five games, which grow harder from stage to stage: hide-and-seek in which a character hides inside one of eight shuffling UFO craft, rock-paper-scissors against a fixed sequence of throws, a shape game that fits biscuits into matching spaces, a maze with pests to avoid, and a jumping action game for collecting fruit. Results are counted in fruit to encourage number practice. One player picks either character, while two players each control one, cooperating or competing depending on the game. A password of four fruits resumes progress.

t_647a8f575334.overview: Based on the Legend of the Galactic Heroes saga, the Family Computer strategy release puts the player in the role of Reinhard, leading the fleets of the Galactic Empire with the goal of capturing Heinessen, the capital of the Free Planets Alliance. Success depends on planning the movements of fleets that travel at different speeds, establishing invasion routes, and seizing planets to serve as bridgeheads. Admirals normally differ only in fleet movement speed, with one exception: every Alliance fleet in the same star region as Yang fights at one and a half times its strength, so his fleet is very hard to defeat with comparable forces. Several commanders hold posts that depart from the original story, and an original admiral appears who was created for the game.

t_6486e90a17d1.overview: Built in the mold of Contra, this 1996 Waixing cartridge puts the player in control of a man who must shoot his way past enemies and bosses. Four stages are each divided into two sections: a moving train against a mountainous background, a bridge at sunset where alien spacecraft and small flying aliens emerge from pits, a desolate industrial city, and an alien lair filled with skulls and acid drops. Some stretches call for grabbing onto ledges and climbing chains, and the last stage includes a section of jumping from chain to chain or controlling a turtle-like creature that moves through lava. Four powerups appear: Machine Gun, Laser Gun, Barrier and the default Spread Gun. An options menu sets the difficulty and the number of starting lives, and a new game resumes on the last stage reached.

t_64c8f4fade05.overview: Songs, not gameplay, make up the content of this expansion cartridge for Family Noraebang, the Korean karaoke cartridge for the Famicom developed by Daou Infosys and published by Daewoo. It slots into a special port on the main cartridge, extending the base library of 56 songs; song packs of this kind held 40 songs each, matching this pack's title. The main program detects an inserted expansion through a header reading "OPEN FAMILY SONG", after which the added songs can be chosen and sung through the base unit's karaoke menu and microphone input.

t_650698826b36.overview: Taito released this 1989 edition of the Kyuukyoku Harikiri Stadium baseball series, which adds player editing, so team rosters can be customized. Passwords distributed at the time made it possible to sign characters from baseball manga, as well as Taito characters, onto teams. Player development also works differently from the earlier games: rather than being directed by the player, growth is left to the computer-controlled manager.

t_6572200a4827.overview:
Rising psychokinetic energy threatens New York City, prompting the player to establish and operate a paranormal extermination franchise. Starting with a loaned cash balance, the player visits a shop to purchase ghost-catching gear, including beams and capture traps, before monitoring an overhead street map for signs of supernatural disturbance. The player drives toward active locations along city streets, collecting fuel and vacuuming stray roaming spirits along the way.

Upon arriving at an infested building, two operatives must maneuver into position to lure ghosts into an active trap for cash rewards. When prompted, the player enters the Temple of Zuul, where the team climbs twenty-two floors of stairs while avoiding lethal ghosts. On the top floor, operatives launch a beam to destroy Gozer before the Marshmallow Man finishes scaling the building.

t_659c46ba81ec.overview: Konami's take on a Zelda-style action role-playing game opens with a legend: aeons ago, two divine dragons of opposing colors fought each other to the death, and now three foolish men are about to resurrect one of them. The hero is dropped into the middle of a hostile fantasy world with little explanation and must track down a pair of magic books, following often cryptic hints. Combat is fairly straightforward, while most puzzles are solved by casting spells on landmarks. Exploration covers detailed outdoor areas and dungeons; boots increase walking speed, a crystal ball provides an automap, and rods serve as weapons. Leveling up partly restores the character, and a defeated hero restarts at a central point of the current area with items and experience intact.

t_65c223c81efa.overview: Simple play takes priority over hard simulation in Golfkko Open, yet the player still has to pick the right club and judge the power needed to close the distance to the hole. Each shot involves choosing a club and direction, setting the strike point on a close-up of the ball, and stopping a power gauge; with a trackball, power comes instead from rolling the ball upward. The player also decides which clubs to carry. A new game, a password mode that lets a golfer keep improving, and a practice mode for studying any hole are offered. Rounds can be played alone, by two players, or against one of four computer opponents, and caddies give advice of varying reliability. Two further rivals can be challenged once certain conditions are met.

t_65f6920c6772.overview: Ten years after the first invasion, Opa-Opa must again defend the Fantasy Zone from a new attack, while his father's disappearance becomes one of the story's mysteries. Each round is split into several zones linked by blue warp gates that open when certain enemy bases are destroyed; once every base in every zone is gone, a red warp gate leads to the boss. A power meter replaces instant death, and cloud-shaped shops sell parts that extend or restore it, paid for with coins and bills dropped by enemies and bases. Hidden items appear when specific spots are shot. The Famicom version by Sunsoft gives the bases and bosses names, sets shots to rapid fire from the start, gives bombs unlimited ammunition and lets the Smart Bomb defeat the final boss in one hit.

t_6658fbaa6032.overview: Rows of alien invaders march across the screen and steadily descend, while the player moves a laser cannon horizontally along the bottom and fires upward to shoot them down. The invaders begin as five rows of eleven, and stationary defense bunkers provide cover until they are gradually destroyed from above by the invaders. As more invaders are defeated, their movement and the accompanying music speed up, raising the pressure as the formation thins. A special mystery ship occasionally moves across the top of the screen and awards bonus points if destroyed.

t_666a55a10449.overview: An 11-year-old boy who loves books makes a habit of stopping at the library after school to read new titles, until a fairy asks him to save the book worlds that have fallen into crisis. Five bookshelves in the real-world library each lead into a different book world, and the goal is to enter each one and resolve the incidents taking place inside. Psychic powers consume esper points, and the game ends when hit points run out. The fairy stays out of battles but offers hints and encouragement through a consult command. Where defeat in the previous game halved experience, here half of the money is lost and the boy is sent back to the library.

t_6684275aaea8.overview:
Set in the Forgotten Realms port city of Phlan, the story begins as the city council recruits adventurers to reclaim the surrounding ruins from invading monsters and an evil force. A single player assembles a party of up to five characters, selecting each member's race, class, gender, alignment, and attributes, or uses ready-made characters, and can hire one non-player character.

Gameplay involves moving from area to area to clear out hostile creatures and earn experience points. In town, characters trade gear, hire non-player characters, visit temples for healing, and accept commissions. Battles feature round-based tactical encounters in which more agile characters tend to act first, with commands including casting spells and bandaging dying comrades, culminating in an encounter with the evil leader.

t_66d63fc0d33d.overview: Despite its name, this sequel trades the original's cave platforming for open-ended action role-playing. Geyla took over Fairy Land in a massive demon invasion a thousand years earlier and still rules it, and the player controls an anonymous treasure hunter who seeks treasure within its borders, with choices along the way affecting the ending. Before setting out, the player picks the explorer, the clergyman or the esper, classes with different stats and equipment. Every character carries a close-combat weapon and a projectile weapon, and a health bar replaces the one-hit deaths of the first game. Exploration spans caves and an overworld, where found items unlock doors. A Toku, or virtue, meter tracks morality: falling into a pit with a low rating sends the treasure hunter to Hell and ends the game, while undead enemies can be defeated only with a Rosary item or by the clergyman.

t_66f77b9cdfc7.overview: Boxing on the Famicom could be played here with a large inflatable boxer that plugs into the front of the console, and the cartridge was sold either on its own or packaged with that figure. The punching bag, made for this one release only, contains eight sensors that register left and right hooks, left and right jabs, a straight, a body blow, and left and right movement.

t_6713653a5f27.overview: The original second Wizardry scenario, The Knight of Diamonds, arrives here as the third entry of the Japanese console series, reworked so that newly created characters can take it on. The city of Llylgamyn is under siege after its rulers have been killed, and its only hope is the recovery of the staff of Gnilda, obtainable only by trading the mystic armor of the legendary Knight of Diamonds. A party of up to six adventurers enters a six-level dungeon, and every level must be explored, since each hides a piece of the Knight's armor and all of the pieces are needed to finish. For this release the balance was heavily changed, the dungeon was restructured, and monsters and spells from later scenarios were added.

t_67349c7ef189.overview: Written in Family BASIC, this puzzle program has the player stack bombs, fuses and starters into columns. For a few seconds the player highlights the next block: a bomb shown as an apple, a fuse made of lines, or a circular starter. Luigi then moves left or right, his finger pointing to where the block will go, and placing it on an occupied spot pushes the existing block upward. A starter lights a fuse that burns along its line until the line ends or reaches a bomb, so several bombs can be chained. Each explosion spins through numbers that can clear rows of bombs and fuses, drop new bombs at random or award bonus points. The level rises and decision time shrinks as play continues, and a column reaching the top of the screen ends the game.

t_6756cf4d6f62.overview: Butch Cavendish and his gang have kidnapped the President of the U.S., and the Lone Ranger, a former Texas Ranger whose comrades were murdered by the outlaw, rides out to rescue him across eight areas. Each area opens on a large overhead map where Tonto advises on where to go next, and the Ranger travels between towns, caverns, mountains and bridges while wandering gangs of outlaws attack. Locations switch between top-down, side-scrolling and first-person maze sections, the last also playable with the NES Zapper. The main weapon is a six-round revolver, backed by stronger silver bullets, TNT and fists. In towns the Ranger talks with townsfolk, buys ammunition, heals at the doctor's office with cash taken from enemies and plays minigames for extra money, and passwords let progress resume.

t_676bf4f3d12b.overview: Fishing and role-playing come together in this Famicom game from Pack-In-Video. The goal is to catch the nushi, the master fish of the river, in order to cure the protagonist's younger sister of her illness. Fishing is not the only activity on the way to that goal: while moving between places, the protagonist can be drawn into battles with wild animals, in the manner of a role-playing game.

t_679406b3badd.overview: Hello Kitty tends a garden in this children's platform game developed by Shimada Kikaku and published by Character Soft. In each stage she must water all of the flowers while steering clear of the animals and insects that roam the area, although she carries a large mallet with which she can defend herself. Money found along the way adds to the score. Touching an enemy or letting the time limit run out costs a life, and losing every life ends the game and resets the score, though continues are unlimited. There are 18 stages in all, and the second half is harder than the first nine.

t_67c9354aca05.overview: Adapted from the title story of Akagawa Jirou's first mystery collection, the Famicom release is a command-selection adventure for one player. In a quiet hot-spring town, eight passengers vanish from a train that should have run from the local station to the neighboring one. The local police call in a 37-year-old inspector, described as the best detective on the metropolitan force, and he is joined by a 22-year-old university student whose strong curiosity sometimes produces sharp deductions. The game changes the cause of an incident that the novel mentions only briefly, and that change becomes a key to solving the case.

t_67cc2241bb9b.overview: A sequel to the 1983 puzzle-platform game Lode Runner, Championship Lode Runner keeps the original goal of picking up all the gold pieces on each level while presenting layouts that are much more difficult. Its 50 levels must be completed in sequential order, although on the Famicom any of the first ten can be chosen at the start, and every cleared stage displays a password for the next one. Enemies can only be overcome through non-violent methods, and bumping into one costs a life along with all the gold collected. Many of the levels were designed with the original game's built-in level editor, and half of the 50 stages came from Japanese contributors. Some stages are nearly impossible to solve without hints. Play is single-player.

t_67d4f069fba8.overview: Built by Super Game as a Famicom port of the PC Engine game Bomberman '94, it keeps the original's two modes: a story mode and a battle mode. The story mode spans 24 levels divided into 6 worlds, and Bomberman has to defeat every enemy on a stage to move on. Items are uncovered by blowing up specific tiles, and the last stage, 6-4, holds the only boss of the story mode. In battle mode, two players face off in a death match in one of seven arenas, each starting with two bombs of average blast length; a player loses when hit by a blast. The game was left unfinished, and two story levels cannot be beaten normally.

t_67fe99af0ac9.overview:
Set in the world of Fern, this role-playing adventure begins after the knight Emmerich sealed the soul of the evil Glory inside a candle. King Millem of Elmia orders the soldier Farreth to protect the Magic Candle at Teth Sanctuary, because its previous guardian, General Guilles, has rebelled. Farreth's son, sent to deliver a letter to the priest in Moelin Village, witnesses a henchman of Guilles steal the Time Bracelet and receives a Time Shard from the dying priest; with his ship destroyed, he must journey back to Elmia.

The son is the only playable character, and no companions join him. He travels an overworld between villages and hostile locations, fighting first-person, turn-based random battles with Attack, Magic, Items and Escape commands. Defeated monsters yield gold and experience, and villages offer chests, shops, inns and churches where progress is saved.

t_68174554ad6a.overview:
Bugs Bunny faces envious friends who try to stall his journey toward his 50th birthday party. Taking control of Bugs in this side-scrolling platformer, players advance through levels to reach the celebration. Bugs wields a hammer that can break blocks and eliminate the contraptions the other Looney Tune characters have unleashed, and striking one end of a seesaw launches him higher than a normal jump. Boulder wells lead to secret passageways. While traversing stages, he can pick up carrots and collect hearts left behind by Fireball contraptions to restore health.

Many levels culminate in encounters against familiar cartoon adversaries. Completing a level grants access to a Bonus Bingo round, where more collected carrots mean more chances to win additional lives.

t_6837c8cd8330.overview: After a ghostly White Lion attacks her village, the heroine Maria awakens in a strange new world and must find her lost parents and a way home. This role-playing game offers an exploratory open-world environment and turn-based command battles. Maria can fight enemies directly, but she can also use items to summon spirits that battle alongside her. Battles yield money but no conventional experience points; instead, Maria's Hope (level), Courage (HP) and Dream (MP) statistics improve by discovering 'Miracles' hidden in treasure chests scattered throughout the world. Play is for a single player. The game was later released in North America as Ghost Lion.

t_68489c090f0c.overview: Kunio and the captains from the earlier soccer game form a national team and challenge soccer sides from around the world, aiming to win the cup that decides the best in the Nekketsu Soccer League. Twelve national teams, split into four regional groups, stand in the way. In league mode, opponents are chosen in sequence, and winning enough matches earns entry into a knockout cup. Each player has ratings for stamina, shot power and defense plus a running type, and every team has signature special shots, which are disabled on the easy setting. Meeting events let the player talk with teammates or give them items to change their mood. League mode supports two players, with the second as goalkeeper, a versus mode allows up to four, and a penalty-kick mode is also included.

t_68610d919d5e.overview: Track and field competition is the focus of this sports game developed and published by C&E in 1992. Two modes are offered. Single Game lets a player compete in one chosen event, while Full Game runs through all ten decathlon events in a preset sequence: 100 meters, long jump, shot put, high jump, 400 meters, 110 meters hurdles, discus throw, pole vault, javelin throw and 1500 meters. Points are awarded based on performance, and in a full game the player with the high score is the winner. After choosing a mode, the player picks a competitor from representatives of eight countries: Britain, France, Germany, Australia, USA, Canada, Japan and Taiwan. Up to two players can take part.

t_6874edceb6a8.overview:
Set in the year 2029, the story follows two Iga clan ninja, Hayate and Lady Kaede, on a mission to infiltrate a futuristic metropolis stronghold and defeat the tyrannical Emperor Garuda. Players guide either warrior alone or cooperatively with a second player in simultaneous action. Both ninjas share identical abilities, navigating side-scrolling environments by running, crouching, jumping, climbing onto overhangs, and hanging beneath them. Across five levels, characters battle hostile soldiers, opposing ninjas, robots, and bosses.

Combat relies on a standard katana or a long-range kusarigama, with additional temporary armaments such as shurikens and bombs found inside item boxes. Collecting power-up items strengthens the current weapon in stages, though sustaining heavy damage lowers weapon strength. Players can also trigger a screen-clearing thunderstorm attack at the expense of vitality.

t_68a60c73f32b.overview: Pac-Man runs and jumps through side-scrolling stages in this home version of Namco's arcade platformer. Stages are grouped into trips: in the opening sections Pac-Man returns a lost fairy to Fairyland, and in the final section he heads back home to his family, wearing special boots that let him jump again and again in midair. Ghosts get in the way, often riding vehicles such as airplanes, buses and cars, alongside hazards like fire hydrants, springboards and falling logs. Eating a Power Pellet turns the ghosts blue so Pac-Man can eat them for bonus points. When a round's time limit runs out, the ghost Sue gives chase at high speed. The Famicom version has 16 rounds, and with the first controller the A and B buttons move Pac-Man right and left while the directional pad makes him jump.

t_6906ff1291f9.overview: Sumo wrestling comes to the Famicom with the same basic aim as the real sport: force the opponent out of the ring. The single-player career mode follows a wrestler of the player's own naming, starting in the lower maegashira ranks and climbing through successive tournaments. Winning two consecutive tournaments as a candidate for the top rank of yokozuna clears the game, and losing records bring no demotion. A password records the wrestler's progress, and his strength rises as he wins. Bouts are settled with standard winning techniques such as pushing out and overarm throws, alongside special moves entered as button commands, including a suplex and a brainbuster counter. A separate versus mode lets two players compete as rival stablemasters.

t_6915159b33d4.overview:
A small paddle controlled by the player moves back and forth between five positions to intercept colored tiles sliding down a conveyor. These tiles can be gathered up to five at a time and then flipped into a bin situated underneath the paddle. The main objective involves lining up three or more tiles of the same color horizontally, vertically, or diagonally, forming a KLAX that scores points.

Throwing a tile back up the conveyor or speeding up the slide gives additional control over incoming items. Uncaught tiles raise the drop meter, and the session ends once the limit of missed drops is reached. Each wave challenges the player to meet a specific requirement, such as making a certain number of KLAXes, diagonals, or horizontals, reaching a score threshold, or catching a set number of tiles. A flashing wild tile substitutes for any color, and two players can play simultaneously.

t_699c9dd8a27e.overview: Supervised by professional mahjong player Tamura, this instructional mahjong game centers on improving the player's skill under his guidance. Its four exercises are watching Tamura play, playing a full four-player game against him, a set of ten problems asking which tile to discard, and outside matches against celebrities from other fields such as professional wrestling and F1 racing. In the hand-reading lesson the player studies an arranged set of tiles, answers with the next move and receives advice from Tamura. A high score on the ten problems opens a title-match mode, a series of tournaments that keeps growing in scale, from a district event through national, world, solar-system and galaxy championships.

t_69a334f45717.overview: Buzzer quizzes form the core of this quiz game for one to four players. Once a question appears, the answer choices are revealed a little at a time, and a contestant who thinks the answer is known presses a button to claim the right to answer; correct answers, wrong answers and running out of time each move the score up or down. Special questions occasionally appear: answering a double quiz correctly earns twice the points, while a correct devil quiz lets the answerer hinder an opponent. Four different rule sets are available, although only one of them can be played by a single player.

t_69ea5e8dcff1.overview: A young duke sets out to rescue a kidnapped princess and defeat a revived king dragon in this action game. The dragon was awakened by the ruler of an evil empire that destroyed a neighboring kingdom, and none of the warriors sent to save the princess ever returned. Stages center on boss encounters, with minor enemies appearing between them, and defeating enemies earns experience that raises the hero's maximum health. The hero starts with a sword and can switch at any time to two additional weapons obtained along the way. There are no extra lives: running out of health or falling into a pit ends the game. The final stage must be tackled last, since the last boss requires items found in the other stages.

t_69ee2b045ef2.overview:
Piloting an F-14 Tomcat, the player is deployed on a three-stage military operation against a hostile armada. The opening mission tasks the pilot with destroying enemy nuclear attack submarines and then a cruise-missile-carrying Black Jack bomber. Subsequent assignments involve fighting through a tank-infested forest to destroy a Hind-Alpha helicopter, as well as maneuvering through lightning and satellite-based laser beams to take down an opposing space shuttle.

Offensive capabilities include an auto-cannon equipped with infinite ammunition, alongside a selectable missile payload consisting of Sidewinder, Sparrow, or Phoenix missiles. These missiles lock onto and eliminate aerial and ground targets, with higher-tier options granting broader target lock-on zones. In addition to the main campaign, a separate one-on-one dogfight mode allows competitive duels against seven computer-controlled aces or a second human participant.

t_69f4faab7896.overview: High school baseball supplies the theme: the player picks one of the participating schools and aims to win the summer national championship. The tournament covered is the 70th national high school baseball championship, and all 49 schools that took part in it are included, with every player on those teams registered under his real name. Only the main tournament itself is featured, without the regional qualifying rounds. Besides solo play, games with multiple participants are also supported.

t_6a2ca96daf4c.overview: Magic is part of everyday life in the world of this role-playing game, where the god of darkness is about to be revived and a party of adventurers must prevent the end of the world that would follow. One player controls a party of up to three characters, formed at places such as taverns or joined by new members during scenario events. Towns contain inns, temples, the royal palace, a guild, item shops and taverns, and choosing a destination when leaving town moves the party straight into a scenario. Twelve scenarios exist, though not all will occur, and some vanish as time passes. Characters can work jobs in town to gain job-specific skills over time, and combat, which happens only within scenarios, is turn-based in a tactical style. Both good and bad endings are possible.

t_6a7344a6db1e.overview: A cartoonish, super-deformed take on a gory horror series, this side-scrolling platformer opens as lightning strikes a grave and revives Rick, then strikes again to revive the Pumpkin King, who kidnaps Jennifer. Rick sets out to rescue her across seven stages that include a graveyard, a sewer, a church, a haunted campsite, a mountain and a mansion. Instead of punches and kicks he swings an axe, and a shotgun with limited ammunition can be picked up in certain levels. Defeating enemies raises his level and lengthens his health bar, and four-digit passwords allow stages to be entered directly. Many encounters parody 1980s horror films, such as a vampire modeled on Thriller and a fly-man based on The Fly. Two hidden entrances lead to secret areas that award crystal balls, and collecting both unlocks an extended epilogue.

t_6a948a545a97.overview: After the Hindu god Shiva curses the village where Master Chu lives, Chu sets out to stop Shiva and his minions; his friend Master Hu has already failed and has resorted to drinking. The platformer runs over ten rounds. In each of the first seven, eight symbols of harmony resembling yin-yang symbols are scattered through the area, some hidden until certain objects are shot. Finding all eight leads to the round's boss, after which the Flaming Key of Freedom must be found in the boss's room. Rounds eight and nine are boss fights, and round ten ends with a battle against Shiva. The A button fires energy shots, while the B button raises Chu's fan or Hu's knife to block certain projectiles. Two players can play simultaneously as Chu and Hu.

t_6af791794008.overview: A mother cat has to search the city for her kitten and get it home safely in this action game. On the way, the cat can jump over obstacles and open and close manhole covers to elude or trap enemies, which include cars, dogs, angry fishmongers and, in later levels, sewer snakes. The more dogs trapped in a sewer before it is closed, the larger the score bonus. Bonus items can be collected, among them a fish that grants invincibility to dogs but permanently summons the wrath of the fishmonger. The second half of each round involves escorting the kitten home, and while doing so the cat can no longer jump over barriers.

t_6afe296a94c3.overview: Ported to the Famicom by Seta, the first case in the J.B. Harold series is a murder mystery adventure set in Liberty, a sleepy little town in rural America. Bill Robbins, the wealthy president of a trading company and a man known for his womanizing ways, is found stabbed to death in a parking lot near a college gate, and the list of possible suspects keeps growing. As detective J.B. Harold, the player starts with only scant clues and must work out the who, what, where and why of the case, traveling to various locations, interviewing people and searching for clues until the truth behind the Robbins murder comes to light.

t_6afe9031a058.overview: Kung-fu masters Jacky and Lee set out to rescue Princess Min-Min, captured by the monsters that attacked the peaceful Chinese Land, and to recover the ten treasures stolen from the nameless land. Progress is stage by stage: defeating the required number of enemies opens the door at the top of the room and leads on to the next stage. The A button throws a punch, while the B button performs a jump kick with invincibility. Four stages make up each area, clearing all eight areas completes the game, and a second loop then begins. Many bonus levels can also be entered. Two players can play at the same time, with the second player controlling Lee.

t_6b41f4905103.overview: Comedy drives this Namco role-playing game, which casts the player as a rookie manager put in charge of Childs, an idol group that debuted but has been going nowhere. To turn the trio of Rin, Kiriko and Yuko into top stars, the manager tours Japan on promotional campaigns gathering fans, aiming for a successful concert at Tokio Hall. Battles are recast as sales work: the Fight command becomes Yoisho, in which the manager flatters opponents with compliments, and Defend becomes Endure, and simply enduring enemy attacks can also win enemies over as fans. A member whose discontent reaches 100% is sent back to the office, and members often suddenly need a restroom while traveling. At concerts, success comes when points earned from well-received routines reach a set target.

t_6b5ca33262b2.overview: Packaged with Bandai's Hyper Shot, a sub-machine-gun-shaped light gun for the Famicom, this on-rails science fiction shooter sends the player walking down the octagonal hallways of a spaceship. Hostile extraterrestrial life bursts forth from the side passages or the ceiling and must be gunned down before it can strike. Grenades are thrown with the gun's B button. During play, music is pumped through the Hyper Shot's own speaker, and squeezing the trigger makes the gun vibrate, giving a convincing recoil effect when batteries are installed.

t_6ba4e055be39.overview: Four-player mahjong is the focus of the second entry in Nintendo's Yakuman series, a follow-up to the earlier Famicom four-player mahjong release. Battery backup keeps up to three save files, and the cartridge uses the MMC5 expansion chip. Two modes are offered, World Mode and Free Mode, with 21 computer opponents in all. World Mode is a tour of seven cities around the globe, each with its own fixed opponents and its own clearing condition; every match costs a $200 entry fee, and falling below that amount ends the game and sends the player back to the first city. Progress is saved automatically, so quitting partway through a half-game counts as a forfeit. Winning with a yakuman hand leads to a bonus minigame worth up to $1,500. Free Mode lets the player pick three opponents, with no entry fee and no need to finish a match.

t_6bf6964af911.overview: An unlicensed Russian port of the IBM match-five puzzle Color Lines, made for the Dendy. Play takes place on a 9x9 grid that starts with three randomly placed balls of different colors. Each turn the player selects a single ball and moves it to a blank space; lining up five balls of the same color in a vertical or horizontal row makes them vanish and awards ten points. After each turn three new balls appear, and when the board becomes too full the game ends with a Game Over message. The player is represented by an anthropomorphic ball holding a sword, facing a crowned red ball with a scepter that stands for the computer. The title screen shows a jester juggling red, blue and yellow balls.

t_6c67c7a53c29.overview:
A party of assembled adventurers explores the fictional city of Skara Brae to defeat the evil sorcerer Mangar. The antagonist has turned the town into a world of winter and filled its streets, sewers, and dungeons with hostile monsters. Players guide up to six party members through maze-like environments, solving puzzles and locating key quest items.

Turn-based combat yields experience points, which raise character levels, and gold, which buys better armor and weaponry. The roster can include varied character classes like bards, who perform songs that grant group benefits, and spellcasters capable of acquiring advanced magical arts. Progression relies on building character power to survive increasingly dangerous foes and conquer multi-level dungeon mazes.

t_6c6cd4e812a5.overview: Known in Poland as Złota Piątka, Pegasus Golden Five is a multicart for Famiclone consoles that gathers five Codemasters games on one cartridge: Big Nose Freaks Out, Micro Machines, the blue version of Fantastic Adventures of Dizzy, Ultimate Stuntman and Big Nose The Caveman. At power-on a cartridge menu, stored inside the Dizzy game's data, appears and lets the player choose one of the five titles, after which the cartridge switches to that game. Ultimate Stuntman was slightly modified for the collection: its title screen was cut off and the game was adapted so that it runs on Dendy clones, where the original version hangs because of a bug in its video system detection.

t_6c81600a9359.overview:
David Crane's A Boy and His Blob - Trouble on Blobolonia offers puzzle-platform gameplay. Players guide a young protagonist partnering with an alien companion named Blobert to rescue Blobolonia from an evil emperor. The boy explores underground caverns beneath his city on Earth before journeying to Blobolonia. Progression requires avoiding falling rocks, stalagmites, stalactites, and indestructible Subway Serpents across interconnected screens. The boy can only walk left or right without jumping, and long falls or drowning cost a life.

Blobert follows the boy, altering forms when fed flavored jellybeans; shapes include a ladder, a bridge, and a trampoline, and each flavor's name hints at its shape. Whistling calls Blobert and turns him back into a blob. Subterranean regions contain diamonds and treasures that raise money to buy vitamins at a health food store. These vitamins fuel a VitaBlaster used on Blobolonia. Extra jellybeans and peppermints also rest across the terrain.

t_6cb20465e4c1.overview: Built around the popular sumo wrestler Terao, Jaleco's sumo game uses real wrestlers' names and offers three modes. In the promotion mode, the player picks Terao or an original wrestler with a chosen ring name, starts at the rank of maegashira 13 and works toward yokozuna, with promotion depending on wins in each tournament. The Japan tour mode is a role-playing adventure in which Terao travels the country, starting from Kyushu, to recover a stolen championship trophy by conquering five rings of evil. A versus mode lets two players each choose a stable and send its four wrestlers into elimination bouts. During a bout, a stamina meter rises when a technique succeeds and falls when one fails, and techniques combine the directional pad with the B button. Experience points buy up to four registered techniques, and passwords preserve progress.

t_6cb2dda4394a.overview: Murder aboard the bullet train drives this detective adventure, a sequel to the earlier Nishimura Kyoutarou Mystery game Blue Train Satsujin Jiken in a series built on the author's mystery novels. The investigation is carried out through a list of command words used to examine scenes and talk to witnesses and suspects, and the story moves forward only once the right hotspots have been examined in the correct way. Questioning people for information is the heart of the case. Near the end, the player must assemble a montage portrait of the culprit and get it right before the story can continue.

t_6cb48247ceb4.overview: Based on the anime, the Famicom role-playing game puts the player in control of Shingo Umoregi, the boy known as Akuma-kun, on a journey that spans the whole world to defeat a demon lord bent on world domination. Travel takes place on an overhead world map linking towns and dungeons, and battles are viewed in first person. Akuma-kun is backed by his twelve apostles, demons who each know a few spells; up to three follow him while walking, and others can be summoned in battle by spending control power. Each apostle has a mood shown by three faces, and an unhappy one may ignore commands or even leave. Akuma-kun casts magic-circle spells built from six demon letters and finds new ones by paying for experiments at a research lab. Progress is saved with passwords.

t_6cc6ca3945cc.overview: Set inside a maze, Colorful Dragon puts the player in control of a dragon that hunts down rival dragons and tries to bite off their tails. A rival is not beaten with a single bite: the longer a dragon's tail, the more bites are required to defeat it, so larger opponents demand a sustained chase. Two players can take part at the same time, either competing against each other or cooperating. Sachen developed and published the cartridge in Asia in 1989 under a title meaning "Chameleon"; the same game was later sold in North America as Tagin' Dragon.

t_6cf213eab414.overview: Based on the Jarinko Chie manga and anime, this graphical text adventure follows a dependable girl who struggles to help her troublesome father run a small tavern in Osaka. She secretly visits her mother, who left not long ago, and hopes to reunite her parents once her father finds a job. The story follows the plotline of several episodes of the anime and unfolds over three chapters, with Chie as the lead of the first, her cat Kotetsu of the second, and her father Tetsu of the third. Progress is mostly driven by reading, but at certain points a mini-game must be played to advance to the next chapter of the story. Much of the on-screen text is written vertically, top to bottom and right to left.

t_6d0e2ffc518a.overview: Exodus is terrorizing the land of Sosaria from his stronghold on the Isle of Fire, and Lord British summons a band of adventurers to defeat him. At the start, the player assembles a party of four, choosing each member's race from Human, Elf, Dwarf, Bobbit and Fuzzy along with a profession. The journey covers towns, the open land and multi-level dungeons, traveling on foot, on horseback or by ship. Exodus cannot simply be beaten in combat: victory requires gathering all four marks and all four prayer cards, then inserting the cards in a particular order at his altar. This console adaptation of the computer role-playing game features modified graphics, a new soundtrack, a new menu interface and expanded dialogue, and it adds an ending sequence after Exodus is defeated.

t_6d31c7ac2eab.overview: Loosely based on the sixteenth-century Chinese novel Journey to the West, Xitian Qujing is a Famicom action game developed by Chengdu Tai Jing Da Dong Computer Co and published in mainland China under TXC's Micro Genius brand in 1994, with a separate international release. Play follows a basic run-and-gun platforming structure: each level crosses a different environment and ends in a fight against a boss. Before starting, the player chooses one of three main characters from the novel: Pigsy, Sun Wukong or Sandy. A sequel, Xi Tian Qu Jing 2, was later developed by Waixing.

t_6d395168683c.overview: Playing as JaJaMaru, the player sets out to rescue Princess Sakura from the pirate lord Namazu Dayuu. Every level holds eight enemies, who give chase whenever JaJaMaru occupies the same floor as them. He can run, jump and throw shurikens, and once all the enemies are defeated he moves on to the next level. A defeated enemy's spirit appears and ascends to the top of the screen. Bricks scattered through the levels can be destroyed, and some of them yield power-ups; collecting three different power-ups summons a giant frog named Gamapa-kun. Gathering three petals transports JaJaMaru to a bonus level. Both single-player and multiplayer play are supported.
t_6d395168683c.official: Ninja JaJaMaru-kun (meaning 'determined little ninja') was originally released for the Japanese Famicom (NES) in Japan in 1985. This action game features a ninja called JaJaMaru, who uses his shuriken (ninja throwing stars) to defeat monsters and save Princess Sakura from the evil Lord Namazu.

t_6d91f6aefeac.overview: Shogi against a computer opponent is the focus of Seta's 1987 cartridge, developed by Random House, the development company of Kazuo Morita. The artificial opponent offers 10 levels of difficulty, with level one the easiest. Beyond regular games, the player can place all the pieces on the board manually, which makes it possible to continue an existing game or replay a famous match from its turning point. The software can also solve tsume shogi checkmate problems. A battery backup keeps a game in progress stored on the cartridge, and meeting set conditions in play qualifies the player for an amateur 2-kyu rank from the national shogi association.

t_6d9cad49d259.overview: Played on a scrolling view of the pitch with two-dimensional player sprites, Konami Hyper Soccer offers 24 international teams, among them Germany, Italy, Argentina, France, Spain, England and Brazil. Before a match, the team formation can be set along with attributes such as offense, defense and luck. With only two buttons the controls stay simple: one handles passing and slide tackles, the other lobs the ball or, off the ball, performs headers. Even so, more advanced moves such as bicycle kicks, flying headers and volleys are possible. Two players can face each other or team up against the computer, in a single match or a tournament, and one of two background music tracks can be chosen for each match. Neither the score nor the time remaining is shown on screen during play.

t_6dc0b1220699.overview: Developed by Idea-Tek and released for the Famicom under the Super Mega brand, with a later TXC print, this horse racing simulator offers two modes. In Gamble mode, up to six players start with 500 credits and bet on five horses; the race is then simulated without player interaction while a commentator gives live commentary and current results appear intermittently, and prize money is paid at the end of each race. Race mode pits the player against one opponent: a gauge at the bottom of the screen moves back and forth, and each correctly timed press while the cursor is in the middle increments a bar. Once the bar is full, the horse accelerates slightly for a while. The game is mainly in Chinese, but most important elements also carry an English translation.

t_6dc2a31fe67f.overview: Sharing its name with an arcade title but differing substantially in stage layout and story, this side-scrolling action game follows a first-year high school student who hears a princess's voice in his dreams. A fairy summons him to a parallel world where a demon king has enslaved the land and imprisoned the princess, and he takes up a magical golden axe to fight the monsters. Magic is chosen from a selection of spells that draw on a gauge, with each spell consuming a different amount, and the hero can also change weapons. The adventure spans 11 stages; apart from the first, each round is split into a first and second half, with a mid-boss and a major boss. The final goal is to defeat the demon king, and unlimited continues are available.

t_6defbe56dd97.overview: A gang of musicians has stolen the band and their musical notes, and a California Raisin sets out across five stages to rescue them in this single-player side-scrolling action game, which was cancelled before release. The hero can walk, jump, climb on vines and shoot an unlimited supply of grape jelly beans. Along the way, lettered icons grant temporary invincibility, black musical notes add bonus points, 'Sunshine' icons restore health and 'Raisinette' icons give an extra life, while shooting at thin air or at columns can reveal hidden items. Any of the first four levels, The Grape Vine, The Factory, The Maize Maze and The Juicery, can be chosen, and The Clouds opens only after the notes from all four have been collected.

t_6e2c83b9d79a.overview: Championship races and drivers from the 1992 Formula One season form the basis of this racing game. Circuits can be raced individually in the "Free Run" mode or one by one across the season in the "Grand Prix" mode, where a one-lap qualification drive before each race determines the starting position on the grid. Player and rival drivers are freely selected, and each driver is rated A, B or C based on real-life skill, so these choices directly affect the difficulty. Weather forecasts precede every session, though conditions can occasionally change mid-race and force an unscheduled tire change. A team-radio imitation signals when to pit, collisions heavily damage opponents, and the car's body type and color are chosen at the start.

t_6e4a3c3276e6.overview: Two 17-year-olds, Moeta Hatano from Hakata and Goro Toyota from Hiroshima, team up and head to Tokyo hoping to become stars. Their road begins with collecting items to pitch themselves to a record company and moves on to concert halls and finally overseas. Both performers are controlled at once and make the same moves, while up and down on the pad change the distance between them. Their song-powered Charisma Wave freezes an enemy for a while, and squeezing a frozen enemy between the pair defeats it and makes it drop an item. Five regular stages, set in districts such as Harajuku, Shinjuku and Roppongi, are split into areas, each with a maze-like building that clears the stage once its conditions are met. A hidden sixth stage takes the duo to New York.

t_6e5ad81afd4c.overview: Mahjong tiles serve as both the cargo and the walls in this warehouse-style block-pushing puzzle game. The player controls a pig character taken from the developer's earlier arcade game, and one button pushes a tile a single square while another punches it all the way to the wall. A stage is cleared once every target tile has dropped into a hole within the allowed number of moves. Dropping a fish tile counts as a failure and costs a life, and a surrender option is available at the price of a life. There are 99 stages, plus 40 extra stages that open after clearing the game, and an eight-tile mahjong password records the stage, score and remaining lives. Play is single-player.

t_6e64d25835b0.overview: A computer shogi program billed as supervised by the professional player Kunio Naito, the cartridge pits one player against the computer, with the human seated on the left of the screen and a robot opponent on the right. The cursor moves with the control pad, and pieces are picked up and placed with the A button. The B button calls "matta" to take back a move: a single press only shouts the word, and the move is restored only after the player bows to the robot nine times. Handicap setups and the choice of moving first or second can be selected, giving twelve ways to play, but the computer's strength cannot be adjusted, no tsume-shogi puzzles are included, and two-player games are not supported.

t_6e71934c3da9.overview: Adapted from the Tatakae!! Ramenman manga, this adventure sends Ramenman after three villains, Kinryu, Hakuryu and Kokuryu, who have broken out of their prison to take revenge on the Seven Masters. To defeat them he must learn the seven secret arts held by the masters along with a supreme fist technique, each art gained by obtaining a master's martial-arts book. Exploration uses an arrow icon: clicking a spot on the screen sends Ramenman there to investigate. Action role-playing elements are mixed in, as defeating enemies earns experience and raises his level, and battles play out like a fighting game, won by draining the opponent's stamina gauge to zero. Continuing requires a password entered in hiragana.

t_6eb742a9d69d.overview: Barcode cards drive this competitive SD Gundam game for the Datach reader. The cards come in two kinds, character cards and command cards. At the start, character cards are entered to register a team of three mobile suits; in story mode six are registered and chosen stage by stage for each sortie, and those six cannot be changed until the end. Battles are three-on-three and turn-based, with both sides entering command cards at the beginning of each turn to decide their actions. Commands spend a value called command points and can deal heavy damage, restore hit points or boost various stats. The side that wipes out the opposing mobile suit team wins.

t_6ed78a452c20.overview: Built as a hardware expansion that plugs into the Famicom cartridge slot, this karaoke package comes bundled with a microphone capable of detecting a human voice. Japanese pop songs, converted to the console's synthesized audio, play while the screen shows the lyrics over a picture depicting each song's themes, and the player is scored on singing accuracy. The modes include a lesson mode for practice, a singing contest in which a created character with a chosen name, age and gender performs on a televised show and is judged pass or fail, a star-making route from audition to debut, and an intro quiz in which up to three players race to name songs from their opening bars. Fifteen songs are built in, and separately sold expansion cassettes plug into the back of the unit to add new songs.

t_6ee1fb458d28.overview: Modeled closely on Street Fighter, this unlicensed one-on-one fighting game puts the player in control of Leon in the single-player mode, with no choice of fighter. Opponents include Masa, and Joe serves as the final boss. A punches and B kicks, but an attack only comes out once the button is let go rather than when it is pressed, an unusual scheme for the genre. Leon's special moves, a fireball, a dragon punch and a spinning kick, exist in the program but stay locked unless a cheat code is entered, and a game over disables them again. A 2-player mode pits two unnamed fighters against each other, the second being a recolored Leon. Three versions exist, and a later one changes the controls so attacks trigger as soon as the button is pressed.

t_6f1ad45e6a11.overview: Flags are scattered across a giant maze, and the player's car must collect every one of them while avoiding rival cars. Based on Namco's arcade games Rally-X and New Rally-X, the car can drop trails behind it; an enemy that crashes into a trail spins out until the trail disappears or it leaves the other side and resumes the chase. Fuel is limited and runs down faster while trails are being dropped, and the type of trail changes from stage to stage. The computer-controlled cars are faster and more aggressive than in the arcade original and constantly target the player's exact location, though the player's car can also move diagonally. BB Car is a 1991 update of the earlier Mi Hun Che, with five lives, no continues, a level select and more elaborate music.

t_6f2cfaf19ef6.overview: Originally an arcade puzzle game from Irem, Lot Lot gives the player two arrow-shaped sticks on screen: one moves under direct control while the other trails behind it. Pressing the button swaps the balls in the two rooms the sticks point at, and the aim is to work pellets resembling pachinko balls down from the upper cells to the lower ones, where receptacles award different point values or none at all. Whenever balls sit in a room, a crab gradually emerges from below; he grabs the player's pellets and tries to keep them from scoring by cutting the elastic, and a cut string costs a miss. The crab is forced to leave the board when no pellets remain for him to find. Reaching the required score clears the stage and starts a bonus stage.

t_6fd2b3857f64.overview: Based on the manga about a boy and his uneasy friendship with a demon, this role-playing game casts the player in the main role of Ushio. Tokyo is explored by moving the character around from a top-down perspective, while houses and dungeons are viewed from a perspective borrowed from traditional interactive fiction. Talking to other characters matters, since certain quests or puzzles must be solved before particular buildings and dungeons can be entered. In battle, traditional Japanese magic spells are used alongside the demonic skills of Ushio's ally. A statistics screen summarizes the hero's offensive and defensive skills.

t_6ffcc4a09a36.overview: Based on the SD Gundam Gaiden Round Table Knights card series, the third Knight Gundam role-playing game follows Crown Knight, a prince seeking to restore his kingdom, who late in the story inherits the throne and takes the name King Gundam II. Twelve knights of the Round Table are split into two parties that carry the adventure forward, opposed by forces of the Zabironia Empire. The distinctive battle system builds on the idea of a knight order: allies can be switched between automatic and manual control, and characters can spend MP to unleash guaranteed critical attacks. Encounter rates in fields and dungeons are extremely high. A separate Carddass battle game that does not affect the story also allows two players to compete.

t_7011cc6ce8c9.overview: Taito's home conversion of its arcade pursuit racer puts the player behind the wheel of a police car chasing down fleeing criminals. Each level opens with a radio dispatch, delivered here in synthesized speech, naming the target, who starts a great distance ahead; the criminal must be caught before the time limit runs out, and taking the wrong turn where the road splits makes the chase longer. Once the getaway car is reached, the time limit is extended and the car has to be rammed repeatedly until it is forced to stop and the criminal is arrested. The Famicom version runs seven stages per round over three loops, lets the player choose missions and steering sensitivity, trades accumulated points for items, and can be played with the Arkanoid Controller.

t_701f61a7945e.overview: Played with Chinese Chess pieces on half of a board, this Joy Van cartridge adapts Dark Chess, also known as Banqi. The pieces start face down inside the squares rather than on the line intersections, and the color of the first piece a player turns over decides which side that player commands. Players keep uncovering pieces while revealed pieces step one square in any of the four cardinal directions to move or capture. Cannons follow their own rule, moving any distance but capturing only when exactly one piece stands between them and the target. The General can take anything except a Soldier, and soldiers are the only pieces able to capture a General. Victory comes from eliminating every opposing piece or capturing the last one, with the computer available as an opponent.

t_70209ce203d8.overview: Sachen's version of the Little Red Riding Hood story is an action game viewed from overhead, in the manner of The Legend of Zelda. The heroine kicks her way through a forest overrun by goblins, snakes, scorpions, bears and the Wolf as she heads for Grandma, gathering fruit, candy and magic potions to keep fighting. In every level she must locate staircases, which may contain power-ups or a key, though not every staircase holds one. Finding the key makes a white exit staircase appear somewhere at random. A dog that sometimes emerges from under rocks runs around the stage and eats enemies.

t_7042348699e1.overview: Five in a row on a grid board is the whole aim: two sides take turns placing black and white stones on the intersections, and the first to line up five wins the game. Although sold under the gomoku name, play follows renju rules, which forbid certain moves for black, the side that moves first, while white is not even barred from double threes. A match consists of six games, with the players switching between black and white to compare results, and the opening formation of each game is set at random. Against the computer there are three levels: beginner, where threatening stones flash as hints; intermediate, without hints; and advanced, which adds a move time limit starting from 90 seconds. Two players can also compete head-to-head.

t_7052768a3917.overview: Water-pipe tiles fall down a vertical shaft in this falling-block puzzle game, and the player rotates and places them so that water flows from an inflow pipe across to one of the outflow pipes on the other side. The goal is to assemble a pipeline from Moscow to Tokyo in order to strengthen Japan–Soviet Union relations. A small girl wearing a Russian national costume appears alongside a second girl who waves semaphore flags, giving the impression that she guides the placement of the tiles. Each level has nine stages, and pipe segments fall faster at higher levels. Sending water into a dead end abandons that inflow pipe, and the game ends when no inflow pipes remain open or the stack reaches the ledge at the top of the shaft. This edition is the Famicom version with references to Gorbachev removed or censored.
