t_70570914cafe.overview: Spanning the late Namek saga through the beginning of the Android saga, this card-driven RPG also brings in Cooler and his Armored Squad of Neiz, Dore and Sauzer. Goku, Gohan, Piccolo, Krillin, Yamcha, Tien, Chiaotzu, Vegeta and Trunks fight in the party, with Vegeta and Trunks mostly acting automatically. The stars on a card, from 1 to Z, set both distance moved and attack power. Fights against strong foes show three party members in a 3D view, while battles with weaker enemies resolve automatically. Special attacks require matching a card's school to the character's and spending Ki. Training comes through mini-games with King Kai, Chi-Chi and Mr. Popo, and Saiyans level up when fully restored after dropping to single-digit HP. Bosses include Frieza, Mecha Frieza, Cooler and Cell, and save points split the story into six acts. Single player.

t_7057cf0999c2.overview: Set in the Old West, this action game casts the player as a sheriff who takes on vicious bounty criminals. Play resembles the Ganbare Goemon series, with a life-based health system and weapons such as guns and boomerangs that have unlimited ammunition. The first six bosses can be tackled in any order, and clearing all six stages opens the final stage, where Scorpion Murder waits. Wanted outlaws along the way include White Wolf Chief, Slash Joe, Billy Morgan, the Mad Brothers, Crusher Kong and Hawkmaster Keith. Items to collect include a vest, a western hat, meat, bread, potatoes, a map, keys and a badge. One or two players can play simultaneously, the second as an Indian partner. The game was also released overseas as Cowboy Kid.

t_707275c5784b.overview: Part simulation and part role-playing game, this Famicom conversion of a 1986 home computer title starts in the year 1550 with the player choosing one of 40 characters. Victory requires gathering 20 retainers, won over through duels or bribery, and obtaining the scrolls held in three castles. Characters fall into types such as daimyo, who may enter castles from the outset, samurai, wives, peasants, foreigners, monks, villains, fishermen and merchants; fishermen have the lowest ratings and suit experienced players, and some monks become retainers when handed a sutra. Each character tracks age, ambition, strength, belligerence, money, knowledge, retainers, loyalty and possessions. Characters age once a year, at the start of each year, and grow more knowledgeable, low-ambition characters can be bribed, those reluctant to fight must have their belligerence raised by being given weapons, and retainers with loyalty below 50 quit when the month changes.

t_70b15b1006ab.overview:
Directing an on-screen hand, the player selects and moves chess pieces across the board to play chess. The game supports special rules including castling, en passant pawn captures, and pawn promotions to other pieces when reaching the far row. Standard chess matches can be played against the computer opponent, viewed with the computer playing itself, or played between two human participants who alternate turns using either controller when Black moves.

A dedicated menu offers sixteen difficulty settings ranging from newcomer tiers to time-regulated levels and an infinite thought option. Additional gameplay features include a setup mode to custom-position pieces, a replay mode to take back or review prior moves, and an option to solve for checkmates within five turns. Matches can be viewed as a full board or in a War Room display that tracks captured units, recent moves, and computer calculations.

t_70c32dd7d6f5.overview: Sachen's take on Chinese checkers, the game also known as Sternhalma, sets three players on a hexagram-shaped board in a race to move their pieces into the home corner opposite their starting position. Pieces travel either by single-step shifts or by jumping over other pieces, and working through the star-shaped layout efficiently is the key to winning. Victory goes to the first player to relocate all pieces into the designated target area. Sachen released the cartridge for the NES in 1991 under catalog number TC-019.

t_70cc10167002.overview: Tom has mouse-napped Jerry's nephew Tuffy and locked him in a trunk in the attic, so Jerry sets out across the house on a rescue mission in this platform game. The mouse has to make his way past the cat and the dangers of the household before the little captive can be freed. Along the route, an assortment of improvised weapons can be put to use, including bubble gum, a meat cleaver, cups of water, moth balls, a hammer, invisible ink and a drill, and each one gives Jerry a different way of dealing with the obstacles in his path.

t_70fc753fddf8.overview: Built entirely around sliding puzzles, the cartridge presents ten different four-by-four puzzles for the player to solve. Each puzzle has to be completed within a limited amount of time, so the scrambled tiles must be slid back into order before the clock runs out. Players who get stuck can receive limited help at any point during a puzzle. The game was developed by Idea-Tek and published by AVE, and it was later included on the Maxivision 15-in-1 multicart alongside other unlicensed titles.

t_7176bc81ebd4.overview: Built around a roster of late-1980s wrestling stars such as the Road Warriors, the Midnight Express, Ric Flair and Sting, UWC takes its initials from Universal Wrestling Corporation, a name used very briefly before the promotion switched to World Championship Wrestling. Thinking Rabbit developed it in 1988 or 1989 with SETA set to publish, but it was never officially announced or released. Three modes are offered, Single Match, Tag Match and Elimination Series, along with three difficulty levels; starting from the lowest, the difficulty steps up every four rounds. Matches are won by lowering an opponent's HP as close to zero as possible and pinning them down. A two-player mode is included, and the game can be completed through to a staff credits screen.

t_717d86725a91.overview: Four Codemasters sports games share this cartridge, the edition for Europe of the compilation sold in North America as Quattro Sports. Baseball Pros features base stealing, an overhead view during plays, time outs, and fast balls, curve balls and bean balls, with every player carrying unique stats so the best hitters and pitchers can be picked at crucial moments. Soccer Simulator covers passing, shooting, throw-ins, penalties and fouls. The tennis game offers grass, clay and gravel courts, three skill levels and shots such as smashes, lobs, volleys and passing shots. BMX Simulator is against-the-clock bike racing over 15 circuits across three terrains: dirt biking, desert racing and quarry racing.

t_7193beb489ea.overview: Kazamaru, a young ninja who learns only as his journey begins that he is the son of Rahoi, sets out to defeat Shogun Dokuro, head of the Dokuro clan that has occupied the ninja villages. Traveling the land with the ninja dog Takamaru and his sister Akane, he searches for five scrolls that reveal where the Rahoi Scroll is hidden. This Japanese-style comedy role-playing game is full of puns and parody. Ninja arts are taught by tengu, who set various tasks, or by training ninjas who must be fought. Battle arts grow stronger the more they are used, rising through five ranks from Normal to Miracle, while field arts can return the party to a town, let it swim across shallows, prevent random encounters or even earn money with each step.

t_71dd4a000836.overview: Rival gangs of delinquents fight over territory in this mix of strategy and brawling, where the object is to acquire all of the enemies' territory and defeat the evil gang leaders. Eight maps, laid out in a manner similar to the board game Risk, divide the land into territories, including islands joined by land bridges. On each turn, gang members can be moved between territories or sent to invade; ordinary members clash on a battle screen where special effects such as a motorcycle, a thunderstorm or a call to the police riot squad can be used, while fights between leaders switch to a fighting game engine. When a leader falls, his remaining members become a leaderless gray gang. A separate Taiman mode offers one-on-one street fighting for one or two players, each side picking five fighters from a cast of 20.

t_71f998f01cc9.overview: Commanding a fast and powerful helicopter, the player battles through waves of enemy aircraft in this vertically scrolling shooter, with the goal of destroying the enemy commander. One player can fly alone, or two can play cooperatively. Instead of a conventional life bar, the helicopter relies on an "Exx" counter that starts at 66 and serves as both health and fuel: it drains steadily during flight and drops sharply when the helicopter is hit. Destroyed enemy vehicles leave power-ups, some of which refill the counter. Once the counter runs out, the helicopter keeps flying but is lost to any hit. There are three stages, each ending in a boss fight, after which play loops back to the first stage. Developed by Joy Van, the game was also released as Mission Cobra.

t_72c5686f2f57.overview: Drawing on Journey to the West, this action role-playing adventure follows the monk Sanzang on his way to India to obtain Buddhist scriptures, accompanied by Sun Wukong, freed from 500 years in a stone prison on condition that he travel with the monk. The party crosses a map modeled on ancient China, curiously starting in Taiwan, as day and night alternate and water and food steadily run down; villagers' houses allow restocking. Unmarked warp zones must be found by trial and error. In combat Wukong attacks with his staff and jumps, and if he falls, control passes to weaker companions such as Zhu Bajie and Sha Wujing. Characters never level up, and large bosses such as Golden Horn and Silver Horn must be struck on their weak points. Single player only.

t_730a0c75eff3.overview:
Reaching an exit door to complete each town serves as the primary objective across six worlds. Guiding a character named Rockford, the player digs through mud to gather a required quota of diamonds before an allotted time limit expires.

Various hazards complicate each area, including falling rocks that drop whenever the underlying mud gets cleared away. Creatures such as Pingping, Flapflap, Puffpuff, Piropiro, Tackytacky, and multiplying amoebas also inhabit the stages. Players solve puzzles by managing interactions among these elements, such as dropping rocks onto certain enemies to produce extra diamonds while preventing Rockford from being crushed.

t_731676ffea99.overview: Based on the Captain Tsubasa manga, this soccer game replaces direct control with a system Tecmo called "Cinematic Soccer." The action pauses when a button is pressed or an opposing player is met, actions are chosen from a timed list of commands, and the results are animated on screen, with special shots from the manga recreated. Each action spends guts, an energy level that falls as players dribble or shoot, and players have skill levels in the manner of a role-playing game. The story spans two tournaments: first the national tournament with Tsubasa's Nankatsu team, culminating in a final against arch-rivals Toho and their captain Hyuga Kojiro, and then the Junior World Cup with a team built around Tsubasa. Misaki Taro joins only after a short sidequest is completed, and progress is saved with passwords.

t_731d594ad3fa.overview: Sachen's first Cai Di Lei game, Mine Sweeper 1, follows the rules of the original Minesweeper: the goal is to clear every blank tile and identify every mine, and triggering a mine makes it explode and ends the game. Three difficulty settings are offered. Easy uses an 8x8 board with 10 mines, Medium a 16x16 board with 40 mines, and Hard a 28x16 board with 90 mines. Unlike standard versions of the puzzle, a loss is possible on the very first click.

t_7329b562fdeb.overview: Developed and published by Hudson Soft, this action adventure casts the player as Challenger, an archaeologist who sets out to rescue Princess Maria from the evil Don Waldorado. The adventure spans four levels. It opens aboard a special express train on which the villain is escaping with the princess, then moves to Waldorado island, where Challenger searches for her. The third level takes place inside a cave, where three keyword items, a key, a ring and a crown, must be gathered, and the fourth and final level is the rescue itself. Challenger attacks by throwing knives, and certain special enemies have to be defeated to gain items required to complete some levels. A timer runs during play, and a life is lost when it reaches zero; the game is over when no lives remain.

t_732c2c9ff62f.overview: Based on Kyotaro Nishimura's 1978 novel of the same name, the first of his railway mysteries, this murder-mystery adventure opens with a killing aboard a Blue Train, one of Japan's long-distance sleeper trains. Control switches between three different detectives as the case unfolds, and the investigation proceeds by talking to witnesses and suspects and interacting with the surroundings to discover who is behind the murder. No wrong choice can get the player killed or end the game, so clues and suspects can be examined at a steady pace until the mystery behind the murder is fully cleared up.

t_733e8b3d9d2d.overview: Taito released this edition of Kyuukyoku Harikiri Stadium as a minor revision of the first game, changing only the player data. The baseball itself matches the original: thirteen teams, twelve modeled on real Japanese professional clubs plus the all-female Idol team, and a pennant mode in which players can be strengthened between games. Batters' builds change as they develop, and pitchers who grow gain magic pitches. A zoom mode shows fine plays and close plays up close, a hit-by-pitch can be turned into a brawl, and drunk fans sometimes run onto the field.

t_7342f6b4e8b5.overview: Fantasy warfare plays out turn by turn, and victory comes only from defeating the opposing king or kings. Placing a King unit inside a castle lets it summon other units for a cost in funds, while occupying towns and castles raises the income collected each turn. The roster covers 22 unit types grouped into people, fairies, dragons and other kinds, from goblins and elves to dragons; units gain levels by killing enemies, and some can cast magic. Terrain shapes movement, with high mountains and forests costing more than plains and roads, and every unit consumes food to keep moving, so supply lines matter. A campaign sets the player against a computer team led by Lucifer across four maps, and a multiplayer mode lets up to four teams battle on eight additional maps.

t_73650a4b6a63.overview: Commissioned by Count Apple, Sherlock Holmes travels across Great Britain to rescue the count's daughter Margaret, who has been kidnapped by a criminal organization called the Papaya Gang. Exploration is combined with action: Holmes fights mainly with kicks, and innocent citizens can be kicked around just like criminals, so telling enemies from civilians is a challenge. Knives and guns can be added to his attacks, and fallen thugs yield money. Parks, sewers, private houses and famous landmarks provide clues, which are used to find items and the entrances to boss locations; a magnifying glass is among the tools to collect. Watson, at the house in London, restores Holmes's health. If Holmes is killed, the mystery becomes a perfect crime and the game ends.

t_73b3a4eaaf4a.overview: Released in German, this platform game follows an island native, the Banana Prince, on a quest to retrieve the stolen weapons of his island and rescue a princess in a world of dangerous fruit and vegetables. He starts with a short, weak sword, but rings scattered through each stage buy projectile-firing weapons, and extra rings can be won by gambling at casinos. A bag of seeds grows plants that fling him upward for longer jumps, and collecting flower tokens grows a bigger flower that reaches hidden platforms and doors. Some treasure chests grant the protection of a sage. Between levels, a board game frames a quiz show that awards health bonuses and can warp him to another level. Compared with the original release, the hero was redesigned from a super-deformed knight into something resembling a caveboy, with slightly different graphics and the quiz questions translated into German.

t_73c9f97ae2aa.overview: Konami's racing game challenges the player to reach the finish line of each stage before time runs out while dodging heavy traffic. Fuel is limited to the equivalent of about 100 seconds of driving and is refilled only by hitting a special type of multi-colored car. Six types of cars share the road: yellow cars travel in straight lines and appear in large numbers, red cars switch lanes once to block the player, and blue cars are the main threat with their varied lane changes and attempts to ram. Colliding with another car or slipping on an occasional patch of oil can send the car spinning, while trucks destroy it instantly on contact. Courses range from grassy plains and an over-water bridge to a seashore, and Konami Man appears at the roadside if the player reaches a certain point without crashing.

t_73ccfd8cbbe4.overview: Developed by Chunsoft and published by Bullet-Proof Software, this Famicom cartridge pairs standard Tetris with a new style called BomBliss. In BomBliss, each falling piece may contain no bombs, a single bomb, or consist entirely of bombs. Filled rows do not disappear; instead, the bombs within them explode, with the blast depending on how many rows are filled at one time. Rows filled with no bombs increase the size of the next explosion, and a blast that reaches another bomb sets it off in turn. Whenever a piece enters the playfield, four bombs arranged in a square become a larger bomb. After an explosion, blocks left unsupported fall under sticky gravity, which allows chain reactions.

t_73f4a0cd4349.overview: Set in the year 2114 in Vegapolis, Titan revolves around a new sport created by Professor Hybrys, in which a ball must be guided through a series of 80 labyrinths. The design builds on the block-breaking formula but lets the player's piece move vertically as well as horizontally, turning each maze into a top-down puzzle with a view that follows the player around the map. The player steers a small rectangle to knock a slightly smaller ball into blocks and destroy them, while keeping the ball away from hazardous objects that destroy it on contact. A labyrinth is cleared either by steering the ball to its exit or by destroying every breakable block, and a prize awaits anyone who completes the full set.

t_7404195e377d.overview: Released by Sachen in 1990 under the Chinese title 宾果75, this slot machine simulator was developed by Hummer Cheng after Sachen had incorporated Joy Van. Play centers on a bet screen, and the aim is to build up credits: gaining enough of them rewards the player with adult content, four pictures in total, in each of which a girl gradually loses more clothes. An international edition with a title screen reading "75 Bingo" in the Latin alphabet also exists.

t_7418c06b29bc.overview: Viewed from a first-person cockpit, this space combat game puts the player at the controls of the Gaia starship with orders to wipe out the invading Batsura fleet. A map display plots planets, bases, asteroids and enemy formations across the whole sector, and the player can choose a location on the map and warp to it, with the current date advancing based on the warp distance. Energy is consumed by everything the Gaia does, including warping, thrust, firing beams and restoring shields, and the ship can be refueled at bases. A radar shows the locations of enemies and bases, and battles are fought by engaging enemy ships from the cockpit. Destroying the Dark Planet itself and wiping out the enemy ships in its sector leads to the true ending of Adventure Mode.

t_748734fa0f6f.overview: On Io, a moon of Jupiter, a human scientific research base is under attack by aliens. Strapped into a jetpack armed with a laser, a cloaking device and three smart bombs, the hero patrols a horizontally scrolling field to rescue the scientists walking along the ground and return them to the base's dropzone. Aliens, some slow and others faster, capture the scientists and carry them off; shooting a captor sends its prisoner falling, and the falling scientist has to be caught before being carried to safety. Sometimes the aliens carry lethal androids instead, which must be avoided. Enemies can be eluded or engaged, and each level is more difficult than the one before.

t_749327e494e0.overview:
Defeating Count Dracula and his army of monsters is the primary objective of this platforming adventure. Controlling the vampire hunter Trevor Belmont, the player fights through Terror Levels, each with a time limit and a boss; there are seventeen in all, though the route chosen determines which are played. Trevor combats threats using the Mystic Whip alongside various items. At several points the road forks, and the player chooses which path to take toward the castle. Different endings can be reached depending on the companion who travels with Trevor.

Trevor can also team up with a single spirit companion encountered along the way. Available allies include Sypha, the Mystic Warlord, who attacks with flames, frozen crystals, and lightning bolts; Grant DaNasty, a ghost pirate able to cling to walls and ceilings and jump high; and Alucard, Dracula's son, who fires a Ball of Destruction and transforms into a bat. Partnering with a new companion requires leaving the previous ally behind.

t_749e11fe3795.overview: Konami's racing game asks the driver to reach the finish line of each stage without running out of time, hitting other cars or running out of fuel. Fuel lasts for about 100 seconds of driving and is topped up by touching special multi-colored cars. Traffic behaves in distinct ways: yellow cars travel in a straight line and appear in large numbers, red cars change lanes once to get in the way, blue cars vary their lane changes and attempt to ram the player, and trucks, which also travel straight, destroy the player's car instantly on contact. Colliding with a car or slipping on a patch of oil causes a spin-out that, if not corrected, can end in a crash into the side barriers and a loss of fuel. Konami Man appears at the side of the road when a certain point is reached without crashing.

t_74e6ecc4fa0a.overview: Knight Gundam's saga continues in this role-playing sequel based on a later installment of the SD Gundam Gaiden Carddass story. The adventure is divided into chapters, and when characters from an earlier chapter rejoin the party, they keep their levels and equipment. Enemy types follow a three-way cycle in which power beats magic, magic beats technique and technique beats power, and some enemy attacks can knock a weapon or shield out of a character's hands. Camping for a night fully restores HP only. Knight Gundam takes on new forms through trials, the story eventually leads to the Titan's Demon Tower hidden behind a barrier, and the controls move toward a style close to Final Fantasy. Party sprites are larger than in other role-playing games of the time. A single player takes part.

t_74fa43178545.overview: A cartridge version of the paper-and-pencil naval guessing game, Morskoy Boy (Sea Battle) has each side hide a fleet of ten ships on a grid: one ship four squares long, two of three squares, three of two squares and four single-square vessels, filling twenty squares in all. Players then take turns choosing a square in the opposing grid to fire at, judging where and how the enemy fleet has been placed rather than guessing at random. Landing a hit earns another shot, while a miss passes the turn to the opponent. Matches can be played against a friend or against the computer, which offers three difficulty levels.

t_752909a4946b.overview: The brave knight Kuros ventures through the forests of Elrond toward Castle IronSpire, where the evil wizard Malkil holds the princess prisoner. Armed with the legendary Brightsword, Kuros works through a series of mazes in which keys open doors and treasure chests; chests and doors are color-coded and require a key of the matching color. Gems gathered along the way are used to bribe the creature that guards the entrance to the next level, and items such as a shield protect against enemy attacks. Other damsels can also be rescued along the route. Published in Japan by Jaleco, this release is the Japanese edition of Wizards & Warriors.

t_75386a209309.overview: Pitching, batting, running and fielding are all handled with the controller, and on defense the player directs the fielders as well. Ten teams whose names parody real clubs make up the fictional JAPAN LEAGUE, including an all-star side of the publisher's own characters, and every game is played in a single ballpark, with results reported afterward in a mock sports newspaper. Three modes are offered: a single-player mode against the computer in a run of elimination games, with a password to resume; a two-player mode in which the same pair of teams plays three straight games; and a watch mode in which the computer plays both sides, though the player can still step in. Because of memory limits, there are no switch hitters, and players who bat from both sides all bat left-handed.

t_753b5534cd68.overview: Having come to Earth from far beyond the galaxy and become a pachinko master, Pachio-kun has married and settled down when the great king of his home star appears in a dream, urging him to train harder, become a super pachinko pro and return. To go home with his wife, he begins a new round of training in a series of pachinko parlors. Inside each parlor he walks the floor, chats with customers for bonuses such as extra lives and a fixed shooting technique, and sits at a free machine. There the spring strength is set with the control pad, the A button fires balls, B stops digital reels, and a magnifier shows the nails up close. A parlor is cleared by emptying its required number of machines and speaking to the counter clerk; some parlors span several floors, and a 20-character password saves progress.

t_7542cae0cd20.overview: Set in what appears to be the future, this bowling game pits the player against computer opponents, each with a name, appearance and style of play of its own. Lanes restock their pins with lasers, and some characters wear strange, futuristic outfits. Bowling well depends on precise inputs: the ball can be rotated to put spin on it, and power is selected by stopping a power gauge at just the right moment. During character creation, the player chooses which hand to bowl with and the weight of the ball.

t_75514a6b88b4.overview:
Ending the match with the majority of the board displaying their chosen color is the primary goal for players. Based on the strategy board game, matches take place on an eight-by-eight grid using double-sided chips that feature black on one face and white on the other. Participants select which color they wish to control, taking turns placing pieces onto the board. By trapping an opponent's discs between two pieces of their own color, players flip those sandwiched counters to match their own side.

Matches can be contested by a single participant competing against an artificial opponent, or by two human players facing each other. When challenging the computer, four skill levels are available. In addition, matches can incorporate time limits, giving each player a total of twenty, thirty, or forty minutes for all of their moves.

t_755ef1e82948.overview: Wally Walrus has captured Tiki the kiwi and all his friends, but Tiki is the only one who manages to escape. In each level one of his friends is locked in a cage, and the goal is to navigate the maze-like stage to that friend. Tiki starts with a bow and an infinite supply of arrows, and the bow can be recovered by collecting a red arrow power-up. Unable to fly, Tiki rides balloons that rise while the A button is held, and vehicles can be hijacked from enemies. Spikes, pockets of water and mazes fill the large levels, and an air meter dwindles while Tiki swims underwater. The journey spans five worlds of four levels each, and most worlds end in a boss battle; in the first, Tiki is swallowed and must defeat the boss from the inside.

t_75689b3838e1.overview: Small four-wheel-drive machines resembling Mini 4WD cars face off in a top-down vehicular combat game, and the machines even carry the names of Tamiya's Mini 4WD models. Each stage is a limited arena with obstacles in the middle, and the goal is to clear out the enemy cars by ramming them, steering them into obstacles, or turning around to meet a pursuer head-on. Power-ups appear only occasionally; one of them makes every car on the screen explode at once. The mechanics vary from stage to stage. It is a single-player game.

t_759fb4c0dbc4.overview: A murder at a party in the Kansai region drives this command-selection adventure. Comedian Bunchin Katsura is found dead in the vault room at the villa of the Yoshimoto Kogyo president, and the player, as assistant to self-proclaimed detective Sanma Akashiya, questions witnesses and investigates to track down the culprit among a cast of real 1980s Yoshimoto comedians who speak in a Kansai dialect. Commands are chosen from icons, objects on screen are examined with a crab-shaped cursor, and a map screen moves the pair between locations. Action sections break up the investigation, such as a boat race that calls for rapid button pressing, plus chase and shooting games, including the optional Crabaxian, a parody of Galaxian. Besides the normal ending, three bad endings await if the wrong culprit is accused, the pair is stranded, or the culprit escapes.

t_75a0043263b3.overview: Based on a Japanese television quiz show whose contestants cross America, the cartridge holds 2,000 questions and supports password continues. The one-player mode follows the contest from a domed stadium and an airport through an in-flight quiz and on to more than a dozen checkpoints, mixing quiz rounds with role-playing touches such as gathering information in towns, moving between locations and local minigames. A tournament mode lets up to eight players face off in one-on-one buzzer quizzes: a correct answer scores a point, a wrong answer to a true-or-false question hands the opponent a point, a wrong answer to a three-choice question costs a point, and the first to ten points wins. After the championship is won, the story moves into a role-playing chapter about a statue and a medal, pitting the hero against a quiz cult in battles fought with quiz questions.

t_75d1c5ee0f87.overview: Slopes are built into the courses of this golf simulation from Namco, so techniques such as hitting uphill or downhill to use differences in elevation are required. Nineteen types of clubs are available and handicaps are used. Round Play is meant for practice or group games, offering stroke play for one to four players or two-player match play over a fixed 18 holes, while Tournament pits a single player against eleven computer-controlled pros across a tour of 30 events, competing for prize money; the top two money earners advance to the final Namco Classic event. Shots use a three-press swing indicator for power and ball height, and a caddie can be called up for advice. As the ball nears the green, the view zooms in through four stages.

t_75da5bcf5c40.overview: Built on the same rules as the first game, this side-scrolling sequel sends Takahashi Meijin across eight islands held by monster minions to rescue his kidnapped girlfriend Tina. The main addition is an inventory: before each stage the player chooses which rescued animal friends to bring and whether to carry one of the stockpiled stone hammers. Four dinosaurs can be ridden, summoned by playing card suits found in eggs: a blue camptosaurus that strikes with its tail and walks on ice without sliding, a fire-breathing red camptosaurus, a pteranodon that flies over obstacles and drops stones, and an elasmosaurus for underwater stages. Checkpoints are gone, so losing a life means restarting the now shorter stage, and underwater and vertical-scrolling stages appear. Keys from hidden eggs open bonus zones, item rooms or shortcuts.

t_7617caa40faa.overview:
Stopping a constantly mutating virus that has invaded the defense computer protecting the entire planet serves as the central mission in Kabuki - Quantum Fighter. Set on Earth in the future, the narrative follows Colonel Scott O'Connor, who is converted to raw data by the untested Image Transfer System and sent into the computer's circuits. Inside the system, his digital form takes on the appearance of his kabuki actor ancestor while battling enemies that keep mutating.

Players guide O'Connor across generally side-scrolling platforming environments spread over six levels. To defeat hostile threats throughout the computer system, the character attacks using his long hair alongside memory chips fired as weapons. Finishing a stage adds a new weapon, such as a Fusion Gun, Quantum Bombs, Dynamite, or a Remote Control Bolo. Each level concludes with a boss encounter, during which memory chips can be traded for energy.

t_762a33c1c5e6.overview: Running on the Street Fighter II engine, the one-on-one fighting game pits eight female fighters against each other. Chun-Li is taken directly from Street Fighter II, while Jean, Sugico, Ramma, Marry, Janifer, Vivian and Niny are mostly based on characters from Ranma 1/2 and Sailor Moon. Every fighter except Chun-Li has a fireball attack, and each also has two further special moves performed with directional commands. Music, stages, lifebars and other resources are reused from Kart Fighter and the bootleg Street Fighter IV. When the difficulty is set to 3 or above, winning a round rewards the player with an adult image.

t_764345138c13.overview: Based on the Yu Yu Hakusho manga and anime, this versus fighting game runs on the Datach, a Famicom peripheral that plugs into the cartridge slot and has a built-in barcode reader on its top, with each game supplied on its own mini cassette. Two modes are offered: a Dark Tournament mode in which the selectable characters are limited, and a versus mode in which any character appearing in the game can be chosen freely for a match. Some characters cannot be used at all until their barcode has been scanned through the reader.

t_764f10254fe3.overview: Dozing off during class one day, Tom Sawyer dreams his way into an adventure in which he must save Becky from Injun Joe. The dream plays out as a six-stage action game: a vertically scrolling river stage that ends against a giant alligator, a forest, a haunted house guarded by a giant stone statue, a sky stage whose boss fight against an airship becomes a side-scrolling shooting sequence, a pirate ship ruled by a giant octopus, and a cave. Defeated enemies leave panels behind: 20 Tom panels earn an extra life, a skull panel takes ten of them away, a slingshot panel temporarily changes the weapon, and a heart-marked panel grants brief invincibility. Injun Joe is the final boss, after which Tom wakes up in his Missouri classroom. A second player controls Huck.

t_76821e516604.overview: Loosely based on the Little Red Riding Hood tale, this overhead-view action game sends its heroine through a forest filled with wicked goblins, snakes, scorpions, bears and the Wolf. She fights them off with kicks on her way to Grandma, collecting fruit, candy and magic potions along the route. Each stage is cleared by searching staircases, which hide either power-ups or a key; once the key turns up, a white staircase appears at random as the exit to the next level. A dog hiding under rocks can also run loose and eat the enemies, giving the heroine an ally in the woods.

t_768774079449.overview: Based on the manga and anime The Three-Eyed One, this side-scrolling platformer puts the player in control of Hosuke Sharaku, the last of the Three-Eyed One. Prince Godaru, riding the ancient tank Gomorrah, destroys part of the city and kidnaps Sharaku's friend Wato Chiyoko. Sharaku moves, jumps and fires bullets from his third eye, and he can summon the Red Condor, a spear that deals double damage to enemies or serves as a platform when jumped onto. Defeated enemies drop coins for Chiyoko's shop, which sells bullets with different speed or damage. Each of the five levels ends with a boss, running from a city and stockyard through a jungle and cave, an ancient pyramid and an abandoned ship to the Sodom, where Gomorrah and Prince Godaru wait.

t_7687c5d2d81b.overview: Capcom's sequel to Destiny of an Emperor again draws on Hiroshi Motomiya's manga Tenchi wo Kurau. The story opens with Liu Bei taking refuge with Cao Cao during an attack by Lu Bu; after Cao Cao defeats Lu Bu, Yuan Shu declares himself emperor and Liu Bei is sent to defeat him. Up to seven characters form the party, five of whom fight while one acts as tactician, determining which tactics can be used from a pool of tactics points shared by the whole party. Characters now join as the story progresses rather than being captured, and each one's soldier count serves as hit points, rising with the party's level to a maximum of 9999. Rations are no longer needed, rivers restrict travel until the story allows crossing by ship, and new battle formation tactics grant stat bonuses. Every member specializes in one of five weapon groups: sword, saber, bow, ax or spear.

t_76f4c6f8e00c.overview: Vertically scrolling shooting action puts the player in command of a fast and powerful helicopter that must fight through waves of enemy aircraft and destroy their commander. Survival hinges on an 'Exx' counter that starts at 66 and serves as both health and fuel: it drains constantly during flight and drops sharply when enemy fire hits. Destroyed enemy vehicles leave power-ups, some of which refill the counter. Once it reaches zero, the helicopter can still fly but dies instantly if hit. Each of the three levels ends with a boss fight, and after the last one the game loops back to the first stage. One player or two players cooperatively can take part.

t_76fb9509a853.overview: Played as a one-on-one sport with similarities to basketball and soccer, this Famicom port pits two craft called rotofoils against each other on a flat checkerboard field, each side shown from a first-person view on its own half of the screen. Either rotofoil can be run by a human or by a computer droid with ten difficulty levels, allowing human versus human, human versus droid and droid versus droid matches. A player gains the floating ball by running into it, can knock it away from an opponent with the fire button, and scores by carrying or firing it between goalposts that slide from side to side and narrow as goals are scored. Pushing the ball through earns one point, a close-range shot two and a long-range shot three. Combined scores are capped at ten, so extra points come off the opponent's total in a tug of war, and a match ends at ten points or when time runs out, with sudden death breaking ties.

t_771adb8166ce.overview: Grand Dizzy is feeling down, so Dizzy and Daisy decide to bake him a cherry pie, only to find the cupboard empty and Pogie's pawprint inside. Chasing Pogie into the enchanted forest, the pair get lost and come upon a castle that seems deserted. There Daisy catches herself on a mystic spinning wheel and falls into an enchanted sleep, and before Dizzy can wake her, Rockwart the troll locks him in an underground prison. Dizzy must escape, wake Daisy, defeat Rockwart and find the cherries along the way. An enhanced version of Prince of the Yolkfolk, this adventure and platform game uses an interface and mechanics resembling Magicland Dizzy, with progress built on collecting objects and using them in the right places.

t_7720f5a6947c.overview: Modeled closely on Taito's Operation Wolf, Strike Wolf is a light gun shooting game that TXC published in 1992 for its Micro Genius line of Famicom products. Each stage scrolls slowly while enemy soldiers fire at the player, and every stage has its own boss. The game can be played either with a standard joypad or with a light gun, so a gun accessory is optional rather than required.

t_7724d45e8400.overview: Taken away to a laboratory, King Kong breaks out to rescue Lady Kong, his female companion, who was captured as well and is being held in captivity. The entire game takes place from an overhead view, with the action moving one screen at a time through nine maze-like worlds. Kong destroys enemies and landscapes by punching, stomping and throwing giant rocks as projectiles; when his supply of rocks runs out, more must be picked up. Doorways are the only means of reaching other worlds, and some lead to rooms with hidden power-ups or a world's boss. Defeating the bosses of the first eight worlds yields a key each, and with all eight keys the large door in world 9 opens to the final boss and Lady Kong.

t_7733eb7eb2cb.overview: Up to six players can take part at once in this field-day sports collection for the Family Trainer mat, which uses the 12-key B side with the left half assigned to the white team and the right half to the red team. The events are an obstacle race, offered as a long run combining courses A and B, either course alone, or a relay; a skateboard race; tug-of-war; and a centipede race, and the controls change greatly from event to event. Modes include one-player play against the computer, two-player head-to-head contests, a two-team mode in which teams of three compete for the highest combined score across all events, and a team tournament.

t_77650cb56f31.overview: Set entirely in a small frontier town of the American Old West, this Famicom version of the graphic adventure from Accolade puts the player in the role of the town's sheriff, who must survive a single day on the job until sunset. Each encounter begins with a character walking onto the street, and every line of dialogue is answered by choosing one of four responses. Conversations can turn into gunfights in which the sheriff must draw and shoot his opponent with a crosshair before being shot himself; the doctor may heal wounds but refuses if the sheriff is too trigger-happy. The port adds a time limit to each encounter, attackers who pop out from cover even mid-conversation, and a score tally after every encounter.

t_777d765ff2b3.overview: Agent Kenny Smith of the special forces unit Dead Fox is sent to deal with a huge drug syndicate operating across South America in this side-scrolling action shooter. After the agents sent to the syndicate's hideouts stop responding, commander Jones orders him to destroy the organization and rescue the hostages. Doors along each stage can hold power-ups, offer cover from enemies, or conceal captured hostages. The available firearms are a standard pistol and a fully automatic machine gun, and shots can be fired while jumping, with direction changes possible in midair. To exit each hideout, a captured commando must be rescued, since he supplies the grenades needed to destroy the blocked exit. Eight stages and three difficulty settings are offered for a single player.

t_77a3ebacd4b2.overview: A boy wearing a helmet heads into an amusement park to save his girlfriend from an unknown force lurking inside. Played as a platformer, the action has the hero kicking balls at enemies to defeat them. An unusual rule ties his strength to the punishment he absorbs: the more damage he takes, the more damage he does to enemies. This build is an English localization of Doki! Doki! Yuuenchi: Crazy Land Daisakusen, with a restyled title logo, a partly redrawn skyline and added licensing text, while the player character matches the Japanese version and the level layouts stay closer to the Japanese original than to the later European release.

t_77b91a922bf8.overview:
Directing a transforming protagonist called the Guardian, the player battles alien forces to trigger the self-destruction of an encroaching world known as Naju. The mission requires activating ten safety devices inside Naju. Exploration occurs on the surface, termed the Labyrinth, from an overhead perspective in humanoid form. Using a coordinate map, the Guardian navigates interconnected screens and uses keys to open new parts of the Labyrinth, which holds items, weapons, shops and information. Enemy attacks deplete a life meter, ending the game if fully drained.

Interior corridors shift gameplay to shooting sequences in fighter form. Flying through these corridors culminates in boss fights that can activate part of the safety system or yield keys. The Guardian wields a rapid-fire primary shot and secondary arms that consume Power Chips. Blue and Red Lander items raise maximum energy and the Power Chip maximum, while a friendly blue creature in certain rooms provides passwords to save progress.

t_77b93d74971b.overview:
The player controls miniature versions of either the Vampire or the Monster, jumping and attacking through six environmental stages to defeat Warlock and hostile minions. Movement includes walking, crouching, jumping, and executing a higher secondary leap at the apex of a jump. In combat, characters can strike directly or lift and throw everyday objects, such as keys and bolts, at oncoming adversaries.

Progress spans locations including a house interior, a kitchen, sewers, construction girders, an oriental garden, and Monster Mountain, each concluding with an encounter against an enemy leader. Characters possess an energy gauge and multiple lives, losing a life when health depletes. Defeated foes yield points, which grant extra lives at score thresholds. A second player can participate, and if one character runs out of lives, that player may take a remaining life from the surviving partner.

t_77d057b890f8.overview: Namco's vertically scrolling shooter appears here in its Family Computer form as part of a modern compilation. The flying attack craft Solvalou battles the Xevious forces plotting to take over Earth, using a zapper against flying enemies and a blaster for bombing ground installations and vehicles, aimed with a reticle in front of the ship. The game spans 16 connected areas that loop back to the first, and its challenge adapts: once the player does well against an enemy type, a more advanced type replaces it. The Andor Genesis mothership appears at certain points, launching endless projectiles and black spheres called Zakatos until its blaster receptacles or core are destroyed. Hidden Sol Citadels can be found by bombing specific parts of an area.

t_78db83410a88.overview: Rather than offering games against the computer, this shogi title is a library of annotated professional games for study. It gathers 95 games in five categories: title matches, notable official games, women's and ranking-league games, and classical and handicap games, mostly drawn from the 1991 season. Any game can be chosen from the start and replayed in one of two ways. A viewing mode steps through the moves manually or automatically, while a commentary mode pauses at key positions and offers four candidate moves, grading each choice at 100, 80, 50 or 30 points before returning to the moves actually played; the scores are not totaled. The basic design follows the previous year's edition, with the menu now marking which side moves first. There is no mode for playing a game against the computer or another person.

t_795c6197d2d2.overview: Super-deformed robots from many robot anime series fill a card-driven board game of territorial conquest that mixes card play with a board laid out like sugoroku. Three kinds of cards exist: battle cards for the robots that fight, item cards that strengthen allies or weaken foes for a single battle, and event cards that trigger favorable events on the map. Pieces advance space by space toward the enemy base, spending national strength to move and to produce new pieces at the capital, with up to six on the board. Contact with an enemy piece starts a dice battle in which speed decides who strikes first and attack dice minus defense set the damage; doubles produce a stronger attack, and special moves use particular item cards. A campaign mode tells of a rebellion against an invading empire, and a versus mode adds cities to capture and card drawing.

t_798914454d26.overview:
The Miracle Piano Teaching System functions as an educational program designed to instruct users in playing the piano. Using a dedicated electronic keyboard connected to the console along with a standard controller, the software presents a curriculum divided into thirty-six instructional sections. Users begin on a setup screen where they select their age category, which adjusts reading text between child and adult formats, and choose a section to start their study. Chalkboard screens introduce tasks, provide performance commentary, and explain musical concepts.

Instruction encompasses note reading, rhythm, finger positions, and two-handed technique. The program analyzes input to detect errors and supplies targeted exercises. Training tools include visual pointers that advance only upon receiving correct pitches, a rhythm practice option that sounds accurate tones regardless of keys struck, and a metronome. Learners also utilize minigames such as Roboman and a duck-themed Shooting Gallery, alongside a dedicated Practice Room that supports separate hand drills and orchestral accompaniment.

t_79d1e352cc85.overview: A dragon has kidnapped Celia, second princess of Lorence, and the swordsman Clovis sets out with a single sword to save her and his homeland. In this Famicom adaptation of the arcade action game, each of the 12 rounds begins on a map where branching routes lead through dungeons of varying difficulty to Dragon Mountain, where a dragon must be defeated one-on-one. The maps are more than three times the size of the arcade original and add forests and doors that require specific items. About 20 items fall into automatic, magic and utility groups; magic items such as the scroll, rod and lamp unleash fireballs, thunderbolts and pillars of fire. Vitality starts at 128 and its maximum grows with experience. After round 12, a much harder mode continues from round 13.

t_7a67232b78c0.overview: The year is 198X, and the Federation forces send a lone soldier, Rad Spencer, into Imperial territory. The legendary Super Joe has vanished while infiltrating the enemy, the Imperial leader Wiseman has seized secret documents on the Albatross plan, and Hitler himself has been revived. Rad cannot jump; instead he fires an extendable wire arm to swing across gaps and climb, and the wire can be fired again while airborne. A map screen links a large number of stages. In neutral areas he can talk with people to obtain information and items, but firing a shot there brings enemy soldiers running. Multiple weapons and items can be carried and switched for each stage, and each area requires finding communications rooms before reaching its computer room.

t_7b188c4b1078.overview: Business simulation set in the personal computer industry, ported from a PC-8801 original. Each player takes charge of one of five computer manufacturers and aims for the top of the industry; outright victory requires a share of 50 percent or more in all three hardware categories, supercomputers, desktops and notebook computers, while going bankrupt twice ends the game. Play follows a yearly cycle: an opening turn at the start of each year sets the broad framework for the year, and every month then has two turns, at its start and end, in which any number of commands may be issued. Sales battles erupt only in summer and at year-end, and occasional bidding events award a contract to the company offering the lowest price. Up to four players can compete.

t_7b5aec9ba6c7.overview: Keroppi, the frog character from Sanrio, stars in this children's puzzle game in which he must rescue his girlfriend Keroleen, who is locked up in a castle. To reach her, he solves action-based puzzles across seven differently themed worlds. The stages come in four different types: moving across the surface of a maze, flying a plane, playing a Reversi-like level, and making it through a field of lava. All the items in the game are pre-determined, so the pattern for each stage has to be memorized to make steady progress through a playthrough.

t_7b8807bb1237.overview: Rather than following one hero from start to finish, the adventure is broken into five distinct chapters. The first four introduce the future companions of the Hero one at a time: the soldier Ragnar, the tomboyish Princess Alena, the merchant Torneko, and two sisters seeking revenge for their father's murder by his former student, Balzack. The fifth chapter follows the Hero, bringing the cast together on a journey to save the world from Psaro, who plans to become the next Ruler of Evil. Battles use an artificial intelligence system called Tactics, letting companions act on their own by prioritizing damage, healing or MP conservation while the Hero remains under full control. The journey also features day and night cycles, travel by ship and hot air balloon, and a wagon for choosing battle party members.

t_7b8ca025b57c.overview:
Players control a young boy named Nemo as he journeys through two-dimensional, side-scrolling levels set within his surreal dreams. Moving across environments from left to right as well as vertically, the player searches for keys scattered across each area. These keys unlock the door at the exit, allowing Nemo to progress toward rescuing the good King of Slumberland from the wicked King of Nightmares.

While exploring, Nemo can feed candy to specific animals like frogs, gorillas, or moles to ride them and gain their special skills. Certain animal abilities are required to clear stages and bypass obstacles amidst constantly appearing enemies. Additionally, several creatures feature lifebars that differ from Nemo's, occasionally granting extra health to help endure hazards.

t_7ba6420364cd.overview: Bugs replace spaceships in this Galaxian-inspired shooter from Sachen. The player aims bug spray with the D-Pad and fires with the A button, clearing each stage by destroying every flying insect. A bug that enters in flashing colors drops a power-up if shot before it flies into place, granting an extra hit point, a double shot, laser projectiles that pierce several bugs, or an extra life, while a skull item powers the player back down. Later stages add small enemies that move sideways and block shots. Each of the five worlds holds six normal stages followed by a boss stage, where a much larger insect spawns smaller bugs and fires large projectiles, for 35 levels in all.

t_7bbafab6e940.overview:
Faxanadu combines side-scrolling platforming with action role-playing gameplay. The hero sets out from the Elf town of Eolis at the base of the World Tree, where meteorites are raining down, crazed monsters run amuck, and the wells are drying up. His mission is to penetrate the giant World Tree and overthrow the Evil One, who lives in the fortress of Zenis in the Evil Place. The journey passes through towns on the tree's trunk and branches, and reaching the fortress requires solving a number of mysteries.

The character walks, jumps, climbs ladders, strikes foes with bladed weapons, and casts offensive magic. Some defeated adversaries leave behind money or food that partially restores energy. Experience raises the hero's rank through Gurus, who also provide password mantras to resume play. Players speak with villagers for information, spend collected gold in shops on usable gear or armor, and monitor status meters for health, magic power, items, and experience.

t_7bdf5c77078d.overview:
American football action unfolds on vertically scrolling fields displayed from a top-down perspective, with the offense always moving up the screen. A 1 Player Game sets the player against the computer, and a 2 Player Game sets two players against each other.

On offense, the ball carrier can run, throw a side pass to the left or right lateral receiver, or throw a forward pass to the forward receiver. Kicks are aimed with an arrow, and a field goal can be attempted when the goal post is in view at the snap. Gaining ten yards in four downs earns a new set of downs. When defending, the player chooses which of two defenders to control and can make flying tackles. Play starts at the high school level and moves up through college, pro, and playoff levels to the Super Bowl level; the 1 Player Game also allows any of these five levels to be chosen.

t_7c672d45a8e9.overview: Modeled on the board game Monopoly, this Sachen release follows similar rules but replaces the street names on the board with countries such as Spain, Turkey and Switzerland, with Taiwan as the most expensive place a player can own. After buying places, players can build houses or hotels on them. Up to four players take turns, each starting with 7,500 dollars, and anyone left without money to pay the bills leaves the board; the last player standing wins. Programmed by L.C. Tchacvosky, the game displays an anti-drug message at the end of a game.

t_7cb3493b2584.overview:
Double Dragon is an action fighting game where players battle through the slums, factories and wooded outskirts of a city. Controlling martial artist Billy Lee, the player seeks to rescue his kidnapped girlfriend Marian from the Black Warriors gang and its mysterious Shadow Boss. Combat relies on punches, kicks, and advanced martial arts maneuvers, with the ability to level up to gain additional fighting techniques. Players can also pick up weapons, which include bats, whips, knives, and dynamite, or throw objects such as rocks, boxes, and oil drums.

Progressing through four side-scrolling stages requires clearing waves of thugs, navigating hazards like pits, and defeating bosses such as Abobo before time runs out. In the two-player mode, players challenge each other head to head rather than fighting through the stages together.

t_7cb72b286cee.overview: In the year 2010, the cyborg police officer Kevin Straker of the Galaxy Police hunts the "Parasites", interplanetary super-criminals whose powers come from armored parasitic insects implanted in their bodies. Each stage of this side-scrolling action game names a target enemy that must be destroyed to gather the energy needed to open a transdimensional portal; once the portal opens, only a limited time remains to enter it before a life is lost. One button fires energy projectiles and the other jumps. Kevin can shoot horizontally or upward, launch stronger curved power shots, climb walls and poles, hang from ledges and perform a backward flip jump. Power-up capsules hidden in item containers extend the range and strength of his shots, while damage lowers the power level. Before the final battle, the scientist Dr. Jose reveals the truth about the hero's own origins.

t_7cfe60a7f15c.overview: Planned as the release for the English market of Bio Senshi Dan: Increaser to no Tatakai, this cancelled side-scrolling action game survives as a 1989 prototype. In the year 2081, Earth has been taken over by a group of hostile monsters, and a warrior travels in his time machine back to 1999 to stop the invasion before it can devastate humanity. Exploration is emphasized, and there is no linear order to how a stage progresses. Defeating enemies earns energy points that are spent on power-ups; the hero starts out with a basic sword, and other weapons can be found or bought. Each of the five levels holds deadly traps and ends in a boss battle, and since the bosses grow larger over time, moving through a level quickly means facing a weaker boss.

t_7d0c9b2eb3d5.overview: Built as a tie-in to the 1990 film Zipang, this side-scrolling action platformer stars Bobby Yano, a fifteen-year-old who transforms into his samurai ancestor, Jigoku Gokurakumaru, to purge viruses from a space station's supercomputer. The near-future adventure takes place inside the computer system. Each level is generally side-scrolling and ends in a single room where a boss waits. The hero attacks enemies with his long hair and with chip-based weapons, and the game is for a single player. Releases outside Japan kept the same action but removed the references to the film.

t_7d18c3bfa73d.overview: Viewed from behind the aircraft in pseudo-3D, Taito's rail shooter puts the player at the controls of a Japanese World War II naval monoplane armed with machine guns and torpedoes, both with unlimited ammunition. The ultimate goal is to slip past enemy fighter squadrons and bomb an enemy fortress. Each stage moves through the times of day, with the sky changing from afternoon to evening to night and back to daylight. F6F Hellcats are the common enemy fighters, a B-24 bomber must have all four of its engines shot out before it flies away, and destroyers and submarines fire from the sea while aircraft carriers on the horizon can be sunk with torpedoes. A mobile shore battery on an island must be destroyed to clear the stage, followed by a bonus stage. A hit downs the plane and costs a life.

t_7db469e578f2.overview: An unreleased home port of the 1985 arcade game, developed by Tose and preserved as a prototype. The arcade original sends the witch Ptolemy through a series of single-screen stages, where the objective is to defeat all of the enemies on each screen. Her projectile magic temporarily transforms foes into large cakes, which can then be destroyed with further magic or by dropping them off a platform. Opponents include wizards that can make her shrink and disappear, clerics that multiply themselves, fire-breathing salamanders, and a flying devil named Horned that is invulnerable to her magic.

t_7dbaa03dea05.overview: Sachen followed its first Pang port with this unofficial Famicom and NES version of the arcade game Super Pang. Each player moves left and right, climbs ladders with the D-Pad and shoots upward with the A button to pop bouncing balloons; bigger balloons split into smaller ones, and the tiniest disappear when hit. New to the sequel are blocks in the playfield that can stop shots, along with ladders to climb up and down. Touching any balloon costs a life and restarts the current stage, which is cleared once every balloon is popped. Twenty stages lead to the staff credits, and two players can take part by alternating turns.

t_7ded2b037ef1.overview: Sachen made this simple slot machine simulator in 1989, and the English-language edition has only been found in its "adult" form. Credits come from inserting coins, and winning fifty coins brings up a reward screen showing a female model in two stages of undress. The original Chinese release, titled 777 幸運輪盤, exists in two revisions: a "clean" one in which pressing SELECT after inserting a coin shows the total winnings beside a picture of the male player whose expression improves as winnings grow, and the "adult" one shared by this English version. Hummer Cheng developed the game while working at Sachen.

t_7e01c5e2d6c3.overview: Two rival secret agents, a white spy and a black spy, race each other across an island at sea in search of a newly developed missile hidden there. After choosing one of the spies and one of several stages, the player must find the target item before the opponent and carry it to a designated spot to win. The screen is split, with the white spy shown on top and the black spy below, and both share a single time limit. Along the way the spies sabotage each other with traps: a shovel digs a pitfall, a rope hangs the rival upside down for a while, a coconut knocks a spy out, and a buried mine explodes when stepped on. A stick extends fighting reach, while a knife adds more attack power. One or two players can compete.

t_7e243f0fe543.overview: Railway buying drives dB-SOFT's Famicom board game, played on a map of cities in Britain, France, the Netherlands, Belgium, Luxembourg, West Germany and Switzerland. Players spin a roulette to advance toward destinations, receive money on arrival and compete to build the strongest assets. As in Monopoly, railways a player passes over can be purchased, but rivals are under no obligation to travel across them and can simply detour, so a purchased line often loses money. Turn order matters, since earlier players get first pick when rail lines and stations go up for sale and in some minigames. A property exchange event can swap a player's assets, sometimes all of them, with those of another player chosen at random or by choice. All city names on the board are written in hiragana.

t_7e754af26f21.overview: The series formula is rebuilt here as a strategic-scale simulation in which bases are captured one after another on the way to conquering the Earth sphere. As supreme commander of an army, the player directs four fleets, and each fleet can be assigned a commander, pilots, battleships and mobile suits. Ships are divided into flagships and battleships, and mobile suits into prototype and mass-production types. Machines from Mobile Suit Gundam 0083: Stardust Memory join the lineup, while the Sengoku and Gaiden characters of earlier entries do not appear because of the major system changes. Up to four players can take part.

t_7f588b71fa15.overview: In this baseball simulation created by Hiroyuki Sonobe, the player takes the role of a manager and battles through a pennant race in pursuit of the league championship. During games the manager sends in pinch hitters and relief pitchers and gives signs such as steal orders and defensive shifts, and the computer can also be left in charge of every team. Player names and ratings, graded in six levels from S down to E, can be edited freely, so real clubs can be recreated or original teams built. Player names are parodies of real players' names, extra innings run up to the 12th, and a starting rotation is part of the design, with pitcher stamina dropping by the number of pitches thrown. Data can be kept on the Turbo File external storage device.

t_7f5c9bd82cb0.overview: Sachen's Gaiapolis brings the arcade game of the same name to the Famicom, cut down from 18 stages to five. The first four stages come from the arcade version, the fifth is likely original to this port, and each stage ends with a boss. A character select screen offers Elaine Shee, Galahad and Gerard Himerce from the arcade game, renamed Amy, Lin and Ken. A second player can join at any time, and each player starts with 99 credits, spending one to continue after running out of HP. Players press A to attack and B to defend. Clearing a screen of enemies makes chests appear with random items such as jewelry and books that add EXP and food that restores HP, while an orb powers up a spell that strikes every enemy on screen.

t_7f5cfab5ec0e.overview: Fictional teams meet in matches shown from a vertical viewpoint of the field, drawn in a cartoon-like style rather than a realistic one. As play moves from midfield toward either goal, the display switches to a new area of the pitch, and when the ball nears a net the view zooms in and angles the camera closer to the ground, making it easier to line up a scoring shot. The soccer game was released only for the Japanese market and supports both single-player and multiplayer play.

t_80091e0cdc8c.overview: Built around the three legs of a triathlon, swimming, cycling and a marathon run, this single-player sports game has the player choose one of six athletes representing different nations and race rivals through each stage. In the water, the direction pad steers while rapid presses of the B button drive the swimmer forward and the A button takes a breath to restore stamina; jellyfish and whirlpools sap speed or stamina. On the bicycle, B accelerates and A brakes, and too much speed makes corners hard to take. The marathon uses A to jump and mashing B to run, with hedges and holes slowing the runner and draining stamina, while a skateboard can triple the pace. Running out of stamina ends the game. A harder special mode adds dangers such as a shark chase in the swimming leg.

t_8036bf0b8b1c.overview: Rather than chasing a pennant, this baseball game drops the season mode and asks the player to win single exhibition games as perfectly as possible. After every game, play is graded across thirteen categories on a scale up to 100, with bonus points for jumping and diving catches pushing the score higher; scoring 100 points at level 5 leads to the ending. A new edit mode, the first in the series, lets players create their own player names and data, and a watch mode shows computer teams playing each other. Three ballparks are available, current players appear alongside retired stars, and fielding and baserunning are shown from a view behind center field. There is no password feature, so play cannot be resumed later.

t_805711b6d076.overview:
Three modes structure this boxing title: the Ranking Game, the VS Game, and the Tournament Game. Standard matches consist of five 60-second rounds, while Ranking Game sparring lasts three. Fights conclude through a ten-second knockout, a technical knockout after three knockdowns in a round, or a decision on points. In the Ranking Game, boxers challenge the top five contenders across four weight classes to dethrone each division champion.

Controlling a fighter involves movement, attack inputs, and defenses like blocking or swaying. Before each round, players distribute power points among straight punches, uppercuts, body blows, and hooks. The stamina gauge decreases from landed blows and time, while a spirit gauge fills with attacks and dodges to enable knockdown strikes. Passwords store improved boxer attributes from training and victories for use across two-player head-to-head bouts or tournaments accommodating up to eight participants.

t_806e77e363a4.overview: Set in an amusement park, this side-scrolling action game, with a few vertically scrolling stretches, follows the boy Ponpon as he storms Crazy Land to rescue his girlfriend Liru and defeat the great demon king Otaking, who holds her captive. Ponpon attacks by kicking a ball: it flies straight ahead on the ground, angles upward when Up is held, and goes straight up when kicked in midair. Taking damage actually strengthens the ball, upgrading it from a small ball to a two-way shot, then a soccer ball and finally a two-way soccer ball, while a hit at the strongest level or a fall into a pit or water costs a life. Several stages are ridden on a mine cart that can be sped up for long jumps. Defeated enemies drop coins, hearts, clocks that freeze foes, and a bird that dives at enemies; passwords and limited continues are provided.

t_80713e1b286e.overview: A take on Balda, a Russian word game similar to Scrabble, the cartridge features a small green monster wearing a party hat and red shoes. Two modes are available: Balda itself and the 15 Puzzle. When Balda is played against the computer, the message "Quiet! The computer is thinking" appears while it works out its move, and entering a word the game does not know brings the reply "It isn't good to deceive the computer." The aim of play is to make as many words as possible from the letters on the playing field.

t_80750c40fb2c.overview:
Five distinct areas make up the amusement park setting, with each section featuring a different protagonist. Plucky Duck steers a bumper car, Hamton runs along a moving train, Babs Bunny travels along a rollercoaster, and Furrball evades enemy attacks aboard a log ride. Opponents such as Arnold the Pit Bull, the train's engineer, stand in the way, while various television series characters appear in cameo roles.

Every attraction requires an admission fee paid in tickets. Players collect points across the rides to buy additional tickets, and clearing each of the four main rides awards a gold ticket. Four gold tickets grant admission to the final Fun House Maze stage. Inside this final area, Buster Bunny must avoid multiple hazards before confronting Montana Max, who orchestrated the invitations disguised as a secret admirer.

t_80e14c32fa46.overview: Rival cavemen have carried off the women of the village, and the prehistoric heroes Joe and Mac set out to rescue them. This early build of the NES version still carries the arcade's Caveman Ninja title, but its content follows the drastically scaled-back home port rather than the arcade game. The side-scrolling action spans five stages, each split into two sub-areas that end with a boss, and the levels are based on the arcade's but longer and different. The first stage is a long, straight plain whose mini-boss is a small dinosaur, while the main boss is a giant T-Rex. Most of the arcade power-ups are missing, and unlike the arcade original the NES version has no two-player mode.

t_80ef8ab7198e.overview: Prince Fan Freddy, traveling far from his own land, arrives by chance in the Kingdom of Romancia, whose princess, Selina, has been carried off and is held prisoner in the Kingdom of Azorba. Also known as Dragon Slayer Jr., the third entry in Nihon Falcom's Dragon Slayer series is a side-view action-adventure built around puzzle solving, and a weapon called the Dragon Slayer sword can be found along the way. The Famicom version, published by Tokyo Shoseki and developed by Compile, differs considerably from the 1986 computer original. It places more weight on action, begins in a forest of adventure, and adds stages and items that the original lacked, while its scenario and systems were rearranged so that the puzzles and story are easier to follow.

t_80ff853dd3c9.overview: Lucia, a magic-wielding warrior of the Rameru clan, must retrieve a statue and stop Darutos in this side-scrolling action-platform game with role-playing elements. Across 16 stages she can jump, climb ladders, crouch, attack with her sword and use magic, and the main objective of each stage is to locate and defeat a boss. Items found along the way include boots that augment her overall speed and jumping abilities, and six types of magical attacks are available, ranging from flame swords to flash magic. Later stages become increasingly maze-like, making it easy to overlook items needed to progress.

t_810fa862a772.overview: Cast as the Beast, the player works through a side-scrolling platform adventure that reenacts a couple of scenes from the movie alongside original levels of its own, with very little presence from Belle herself. The action runs against a deadline drawn from the story: the levels have to be beaten before the enchanted rose loses all of its petals, at which point the Beast's curse can no longer be undone. The slowly fading rose therefore serves as the clock for the whole adventure, and finishing every stage in time is the only way to save the Beast from remaining cursed.

t_811dac4ba28f.overview: Adapted from the anime, this 1989 Famicom action game stars Kenichi on a mission to rescue Yukie from a dragon simply named Dra Gon. Control rotates among four heroes from stage to stage, with Hidou, Rocky and Shiranui also playable in some levels. The maps have a maze-like structure built from a chain of warps beginning in the first stage, and enemies keep appearing endlessly from every direction. The final showdown with Dra Gon abandons the action format and switches to a command-style battle screen in the manner of a role-playing game.

t_81ba4b487f0a.overview: An apprentice Dream Master training under the great Mugen Roushi sets out on a rescue mission in this adventure role-playing game. The evil Black Master, a top-tier dream master who hates beautiful things, has dragged the princess of the kingdom of Altaria into a nightmare world called the Black Dream. Enemies appear as visible symbols on the map rather than as random encounters, and some monster special attacks and spells can be evaded depending on the command chosen in battle. The hero's progress is measured by a Class rating that works like a level. Some dungeons are drawn in a 2D view and start out almost entirely covered by a dark haze. Play resumes through passwords called Dreamwords, which combine the hero's name, the princess's name and a short word of up to four characters. The game is for a single player.

t_81f9b22b0ac8.overview: Beach volleyball comes to the Famicom in this conversion of the arcade game about a pair of self-described beach bums who make their living playing beach volleyball against locals. The characters perform several moves, including power spiking, back spiking, jump-serving, blocking and diving. Rather than splitting play into separate courses, the Famicom version features a single tournament mode. It opens with five American Circuit matches in Daytona Beach, New York City, Chicago, Las Vegas and Los Angeles, continues with three World Cup matches in Hawaii against teams of random nationalities, and closes with two additional matches against the U.S. Navy and a Soviet Union team, in that order. The game was later localized under a different title with a restructured tournament.

t_821e96897d4e.overview: Built on Shisen-sho, a mahjong solitaire game, this tile-matching puzzle from Computer & Entertainment sets the player the task of conquering back the districts of Mainland China. The campaign consists of 21 boards split across 7 levels. To clear a board, every pair of tiles must be joined with fewer than three turns in the connecting path before the time runs out. Each successful pairing refills the time bar by two dots, worth about six seconds, so steady matching keeps the clock alive. After every three completed boards, a cutscene shows a warrior entering a fortress and replacing the flags of the conquered district, marking progress across the map of China.

t_824a481b404b.overview: A mischievous boy named Tarosuke, banished to jigoku for causing trouble in the world of the living, must journey through its monster-infested regions to reach Yama, the judge of the dead. Armed with a spiritual power granted by the gods, he fights through five levels of side-scrolling action, and the first four end in a boss fight against an oni guarding the entrance to the next stage. This Famicom version uses different level design and adds a pious meter representing Tarosuke's good heart: it rises through events and shops and falls after continuing or misbehaving along the road. Money collected and enemies defeated in the final level help determine which ending is reached, and the Famicom release adds a new best ending above the original five. The helper Monmontaro can be summoned anywhere by spending an ofuda item.

t_826d119da02b.overview: Based on the Taiwanese gambling game Xiao Ma Li, this Famicom betting game was developed by Nei-Hu Electronics and distributed by Idea-Tek before TXC Corporation re-released it as Bingo with slight changes. Each round the player bets credits on fruit images, up to 9 credits on an individual fruit, and wins by having bet on the image that lights up when the round ends. Compared with the similar Dian Shi Ma Li, the controls were adapted for a single controller. The game also uses an unusually dark color palette.

t_827872ce9dc2.overview: This unreleased Famicom build of the horror action game later sold in the US as Monster Party tells of a boy named Hiroshi who, on his way home from a baseball game, is approached by a winged, griffin-like alien named Value seeking help to rid his realm, Dark World, of evil monsters. Value fuses with Hiroshi, whose baseball bat is his weapon for attacking and deflecting projectiles; rebounding shots back at bosses is often necessary.
