Pills dropped by enemies briefly turn the boy into the alien, who can fly and shoot beams. Each level requires defeating particular bosses, reached through doorways, to earn a key. The prototype reflects a darker, more graphically complex original concept, with different bosses and parodies, and the green slime of the US title screen was originally blood.

t_8285fe19f9ff.overview: A one-player adult mahjong game, AV Jiu Ji Ma Jiang II sets the player against a single computer opponent, the GAL. The aim is to complete a winning hand or score more points than the opponent, and a game ends when one of the two runs out of points. Each time the GAL loses, the player is rewarded with ecchi content. The on-screen text is in Japanese rather than English or Chinese. Hummer Team developed the game as a backport of Dial Q o Mawase, an unlicensed Sega Mega Drive title, and title-screen codes unlock an ending slideshow or 900 extra points.

t_828e8b0f3bb4.overview: Association football gets the Moero!! treatment in this 1988 Famicom release developed by Tose, later released on the NES as Goal!. The object is the same as in the real sport: one team must score more goals than the other to win. Up to two players are supported, and in the longer competitions two players can either play on the same team or against each other. Its selection of modes includes World Cup, Tournament, League and Shoot Competition play alongside a dedicated Vs. Mode, covering everything from a shooting contest to extended tournament runs.

t_82a3b6fcf020.overview: The mysterious Mr. X hosts the First Annual Robot Tournament, then secretly reprograms eight of its top competitors: Blizzard Man, Centaur Man, Flame Man, Knight Man, Plant Man, Tomahawk Man, Wind Man and Yamato Man. Mega Man sets out to defeat them and eventually learns that Mr. X is Dr. Wily in disguise. Rush can now merge with the hero in two forms: Jet Mega Man allows short flights but no charged shots, while Power Mega Man throws a short-range punch that breaks blocks. Four of the eight stages have two routes to the boss, and only one of them holds a circuit board for the helper bird Beat. The Energy Balancer refills whichever weapon has the least energy whenever a weapon energy pellet is collected.

t_82cc0bbddb47.overview: Gameplay recalls Tetris and the later Puzzle Bobble in this adult-oriented puzzle game. Clusters of bubbles rise up the screen, and the player steers each one so that it connects with bubbles of a matching color gathered along the top. When enough similar bubbles touch, they are cleared, and all free neighboring bubbles float further upward, which makes combos possible. If the accumulated bubbles reach the bottom of the playing area, the game is over. Completing a level rewards the player with erotic imagery. Developed by C&E, the game was localized for Japan by Hacker International with its adult content left intact, while a separately licensed version, Mermaids of Atlantis, removed or obscured those elements.

t_82f55c0b8c3d.overview: Four games share this multicart released in Australia by HES, three of them Sachen titles. Math Quiz, a retitled Magical Mathematics, tests mathematical skills; Jackpot lets players try the pokies, or poker machines, from their own lounge room; Arctic Adventure, the HES name for The Penguin & Seal, sends Mr. Penguin north into 50 levels of puzzling adventure; and Galactic Crusader is a vertically scrolling shooter in which the player uses missiles and lasers against oncoming enemies and confronts a boss at the end of each level. Jackpot is the only game in the set not released by Sachen. The cartridge is a single-player PAL release.

t_82f88328181d.overview: Retelling the story from its earliest chapters up to the 23rd Tenkaichi Budokai, this card-based RPG follows Son Goku as he grows from a boy into a young man. On the map, the party advances by the number of stars on a chosen card, and special squares lead to items, training or battles, while story events unfold in an adventure mode of talking and investigating. In battle, a card's stars set attack power, its kanji numeral sets defense, and the central kanji chooses the attack type, such as punch, kick, weapon or special move. Krillin and Yamcha join certain battles. Victories grant training points that bring level-ups, each adding five bonus points to Speed, Power, Technique and Toughness. Foes include the Red Ribbon Army and Piccolo Daimao, and progress is resumed with passwords. Single player.

t_830e3f81e0f9.overview: Up to three players can fly together in this shoot 'em up: the first two pilot TwinBee and WinBee with the standard controllers, while a third can join as the green ship GwinBee using a controller in the expansion port. Seven stages mix vertical and horizontal scrolling, with stages 1, 3 and 7 moving sideways; in those side-scrolling sections the A button shoots hearts over the ship instead of dropping bombs to the ground. Six types of bells provide power-ups, such as a white bell for a twin cannon and a pink bell for a laser beam cannon, and some upgrades cannot be combined. Moon and star items add three-way and five-way shots, and two players can line up their ships to form a ripple laser.

t_83155d6699ae.overview: Famous professional Go games form the core of Igo Shinan '92, a study cartridge that can replay each record automatically or let the player work through it by hand, alongside a playing-strength assessment. This edition reorganizes the collection: the classical and early modern categories are gone, replaced by dedicated sets of games from three historical professional players, with 20 records for each. The rest of the library consists of 37 modern games and 25 handicap games, for 122 records in all.

t_83237dbfcb40.overview:
Rising psychokinetic energy threatens New York City, prompting the player to establish and operate a paranormal extermination franchise. Starting with a loaned cash balance, the player visits a shop to purchase ghost-catching gear, including beams and capture traps, before monitoring an overhead street map for signs of supernatural disturbance. The player drives toward active locations along city streets, collecting fuel and vacuuming stray roaming spirits along the way.

Upon arriving at an infested building, two operatives must maneuver into position to lure ghosts into an active trap for cash rewards. When prompted, the player enters the Temple of Zuul, where the team climbs twenty-two floors of stairs while avoiding lethal ghosts. On the top floor, operatives launch a beam to destroy Gozer before the Marshmallow Man finishes scaling the building.

t_832fe5720690.overview: Adapted from the $1,000,000 Kid manga by Yuki Ishigaki, this SOFEL casino game is the Japanese original of the release known in North America as Casino Kid. Set in Las Vegas, it tasks the player with earning a fortune and defeating the evil King of the Casino. The casino offers blackjack, five-card draw poker, slot machines and roulette, and waitresses in bunny costumes give hints. Several features are unique to this version: travel to other casinos such as New York City and Japan for a substantial airfare, the option of entering the player's own name, and a free mode for experimenting with gambling strategies. The introduction shows a kid imagining himself as the casino champion, and the Golden Nugget appears under its real name.

t_833ae2290f86.overview: Kenshiro returns in a second action game that now scrolls to the right, with many enemies drawn from the Tentei arc of the story. Defeated foes leave the word "hidebu," and collecting power raises Kenshiro through seven levels that bring an aura attack of up to seven shots and a full recovery of health. Items include gold and silver Yuria necklaces, one granting temporary invincibility and the other adding aura shots, and the Hokuto Banner, which restores health. New elements such as pitfalls and staircase-style progression appear across eight stages, and the route to the eighth opens only to players who clear the seventh without continuing. Finishing a boss with a special technique, or ougi, earns bonus points. Bosses include Falco and the final foe, Shura.

t_838533330cef.overview: Built on the rules of a strategy table game in the vein of Othello, this board game uses the round Spot character as the moving pieces on a square grid. On each turn a player selects one of his pieces and an empty position one or two squares away: moving one square copies the piece, while moving two squares relocates it without copying. Any opposing pieces next to the landing square change to the mover's color. Play ends when only one player remains on the board or when the board is entirely full, in which case the player with the most pieces wins. Up to four players can take part, sharing controllers, and the number of computer-controlled players and their strength can be set. Boards can also include blank spots where pieces cannot go.

t_8394cf06920c.overview: Continuing the series as a role-playing game, this sequel leads Ultraman and his fellow Ultra brothers through five stages in order: Earth, the Moon, Dokkun Star, the Monster Graveyard and the Land of Ultra. Brothers such as Ultraseven and New Ultraman join the party on the Moon. Battles are shown from the side in the style of Final Fantasy. There is no money or equipment, so characters cannot be strengthened by buying weapons or armor in towns; instead they grow by steadily earning experience points, up to a maximum level of 28. Capsule monsters provide support, and Ultraseven can carry more of them than any other brother. Continues use passwords, which are given out at Ultra bases and other locations.

t_83a7b87e315d.overview: Built to forecast the user's fortunes for the coming year of 1989, this Famicom program applies nine-star astrology to personal details rather than offering a game to play. After an opening prologue, which can be skipped by pressing the start button twice on the title screen, the user enters a birth date between 1900 and 1999 and a sex. Topics are then picked from a menu with the control pad and confirmed with a button, and another button returns to the previous screen. On the screen that explains the daily fortune, pressing left or right steps through the readings for the dates before and after.

t_83be98bcc817.overview: Instead of a single quest, this 1993 Famicom role-playing game gathers three short, independent stories from the world of Momotarō. In the first, the God of Poverty resolves to punish a greedy merchant through righteous theft; in battle, attacks steal the opponent's money, and a foe is beaten once its funds hit zero. The second follows the daughter of the king of hell as she sets out to defeat an invading king, choosing two or three companions to explore dungeons with her. The third sends Urashima Tarō on a journey, at the request of a hermit of the heavens, to punish a raccoon-dog king, while a raccoon dog who hinders him early on later becomes an ally.

t_83ff2f925864.overview: A mysterious army of monsters invades Earth, and Ultraman is sent to rescue the Ultra Brothers who have fallen into its hands. As in the original television series, the Color Timer imposes a strict time limit: failing to reach the boss within three minutes ends the game. Starting on Earth, the action game moves through a machine planet, an ice planet, a plant planet, a flame planet and the Monster Graveyard, where Ultraman sets out in turn to rescue Seven, New Ultraman, Ace, Taro and Leo. Bosses include Zetton and King Joe, and horizontal-scrolling shooting segments follow the first, third and fifth stages. Behind the invasion is Emperor Alien, the final boss and the mastermind who revived and controls the monster army.

t_840b1587d5b7.overview: Popularity becomes a player attribute in this Famicom baseball entry from Namco, and popular players are greeted with special cheers, a fanfare and cherry blossoms. Batting and fielding practice modes are added, with the manager commenting on the results, and benches grow to five players, allowing pinch-runners and defensive replacements as well as pinch-hitters. Play options include an All-Star mode with randomly assigned rosters, fictional versions of the Central and Pacific Leagues, and a combined-team mode that merges clubs into an original team chosen by position and popularity. Guest teams include squads modeled on the V9-era Yomiuri Giants and the 1985 Hanshin Tigers, the Major Leaguers and the Namco Stars, managed by Pac-Man. Home runs set off fireworks, and two new stadiums join returning parks. One or two players can compete.

t_84a575490daf.overview:
Set during the historical conflict of the Vietnam War, military aviators launch combat sorties from the aircraft carrier USS Constellation. A single player flies both an A-6 Intruder strike bomber and an F-4 Phantom interceptor against hostile forces in North Vietnam, with each waypoint determining which aircraft is used. The primary objective centers on executing twelve military assignments while confronting enemy fighter jets, anti-aircraft artillery, and defensive missile installations.

Assignments are divided into predefined waypoints, ranging from bombing runs to air-to-air combat against MiG jets, and some waypoints can be skipped from the map screen. In flight, the pilot monitors cockpit instruments, radar screens, and targeting mechanisms to engage targets using guns, missiles, rockets, or bombs. Missions begin with a catapult launch and conclude by deploying gear and catching an arrestor wire back on the carrier deck.

t_84b9e4da0593.overview:
Chef Peter Pepper must construct giant hamburgers across mazes composed of platforms and ladders while evading hostile food items. To prepare each sandwich, Peter walks across various oversized ingredients, including buns, meat patties, tomatoes, lettuce, and cheese. Walking across these items forces them to drop down onto lower levels and eventually assemble on waiting plates below. A stage concludes successfully once every hamburger on the board has been assembled, and the six screens grow progressively tougher.

The Food Foes, Mr. Hot Dog, Mr. Pickle and Mr. Egg, continuously hunt Peter throughout the maze and speed up if a stage takes too long. Contact with an active adversary costs a life. To defend himself, Peter can shake a limited supply of pepper at nearby foes to briefly immobilize them. Enemies may also be crushed under falling ingredients or carried downward atop dropping burger components. Bonus food items grant extra points alongside additional pepper shots. One or two players can play.

t_84d8e163d00b.overview: Mickey is working part-time selling balloons to buy a present for Minnie when Pluto brings news that she cannot wake up. Visiting her, he finds she has been trapped in a nightmare, and he must journey into Minnie's mind to free her from it. The platforming revolves around the balloons Mickey carries, which let him attack, jump higher or float; a balloon dropped on the ground also serves as a spring up to high platforms. Seven themed levels lead through the dream, with boss fights along the way. Treasure chests sometimes hold question-mark items with random effects, one of which briefly reverses the movement controls, and extra lives and extra energy can be collected in the bonus stage. This prototype is an English localization of the Japanese Mickey Mouse III: Yume Fuusen.

t_84eda53c9b26.overview: The second chapter of the Golgo 13 games opens when the US military satellite SK2 crashes. Soon afterward a group calling itself the Mafat Revolutionary Army sends threats to both superpowers, demanding military weapons and technology. Suspecting that the kidnapped scientist Dr. Barrows and his satellite-jacking system lie behind the crash, the CIA hires Golgo to rescue the doctor, eliminate the Mafat leader and destroy the system. Play moves between several screen types: side-scrolling action, timed stationary fights, a 3D driving section, 3D mazes where an infrared scope can be found, and sniping in which wind speed and direction must be considered. Instead of the steady life drain of the first chapter, a time limit applies. Six acts run from Paris through Venezia and the Orient Express to Afghanistan.

t_85680191825c.overview: Future Media, an alias of Cony Soft, made this 1995 Famicom port, in Chinese, of the Super Famicom game Crayon Shin-Chan 2: Dai Maō no Gyakushū. Play is very simple: the hero mainly jumps over the enemies, and B jumps instead of A. There are four stages, each with a boss. A stage select allows the first three to be tackled in any order, and the fourth becomes available once they are beaten, after which the credits roll and the game returns to the title screen. Compared with the original, the intro and all cutscenes are removed, the second stage becomes another beat-'em-up level instead of a platform stage, several layouts differ, and the Super Hero power-up cannot be used while throwing things.

t_85729884b1aa.overview: Built on formula car racing such as F1, this top-down racer for one player puts as much weight on the garage as on the track. In the setting mode, a car is created from one of six base bodies, painted and tuned, after which a machine code appears; entering that code later recalls the custom car at any time. Cars can then be taken on free runs across 40 courses, entered in sprint races split into four categories with eight cars including the player's, or driven in endurance races decided either by distance or by running for a set time. A spectator mode shows races from a fixed viewpoint or by following a chosen driver. Notably, there is no contact between cars on track.

t_858b38978852.overview:
Magic Darts simulates traditional dart games for up to four participants. Competitors select from a roster of characters, input three initials, and choose light, medium, or heavy dart weights. Executing a shot requires adjusting the starting position, stopping an indicator to choose the dart curve, and timing moving gauges to set the aiming angle and throwing power. Upon release, throws display through both two-dimensional and three-dimensional views.

Six game modes are available. The 301, 501, and 701 modes challenge players to reduce their starting total to zero without busting, using customizable rules that dictate whether matches require standard or double-ring hits to open and close. Count Up awards victory to the highest score across eight sets of darts, Round the Clock requires hitting numbers one through ten in consecutive sequence, and Half It penalizes failures on assigned board targets by halving point totals.

t_8594fbe2d5f8.overview: Ten-pin bowling against computer-controlled rivals is the focus of this unreleased US localization of the Famicom game Perfect Bowling. Each opponent has a distinct name, appearance and style of play. During character creation, players select which hand they favor and the weight of the ball. Throws rely on several precision options: the ball can be rotated to put spin on it, the power is selected, and a power gauge has to be stopped just right. The setting appears futuristic, with lanes restocking pins with lasers and certain characters dressed in strange, futuristic fashions.

t_867157e702c0.overview: Dr. Wily claims to have reformed and begins work with Dr. Light on a peace-keeping robot named Gamma, but eight Robot Masters go berserk and make off with Gamma's eight power crystals. Mega Man must recover them by defeating Top Man, Shadow Man, Spark Man, Magnet Man, Hard Man, Snake Man, Gemini Man and Needle Man. New moves and helpers broaden the action: Mega Man can now slide, and a canine companion named Rush transforms into Rush Coil for jumping higher and Rush Jet for flying around the screen. After all eight Robot Masters fall, the Doc Robots must be fought, and a mysterious rival named Break Man is eventually revealed to be Mega Man's older brother, Proto Man. A password system lets the player return with most of the stages completed.

t_869e97d43142.overview:
Multiple gameplay modes structure the adventure, beginning with Robin Hood escaping an Arab prison alongside Azeem and Peter Dubois. Upon returning to England, Robin discovers his father was killed and that the Sheriff of Nottingham governs unjustly. Robin seeks out outlaw allies hiding in Sherwood Forest, establishing a home base where he continually receives and completes missions, culminating in a final confrontation to remove the Sheriff.

Standard exploration occurs from an overhead perspective, directing Robin through environments while fighting hostile soldiers. Other sequences shift mechanics: side-view duels allow Robin to jump, flip, and strike single opponents; high-angle overhead views manage large clashes between rival armies; and horseback sequences have Robin leaping over obstacles during high-speed rides. An equipment system lets players place items in either of Robin's hands, with each hand tied to its own action button.

t_86aafb257abe.overview: Asuka and Maya, twin siblings descended from the ancient civilizations of Mu, are typical high-school students living in Tokyo until the seven monsters that sank the land of Atlantis threaten the world. Awakened to their true destiny, the pair become mankind's only hope, piloting fighter ships in this vertically scrolling shooter. The central feature is the craft's ability to transform into one of three configurations, each changing its attack method, and each mode has a normal power-up carried by blue orbs and a special power-up carried by red orbs. Taking damage lowers the power-up level by one with each hit until the ship is destroyed. Two players can fight cooperatively, and four different ships are available to choose from.

t_86c90078a5a4.overview: Three customized minigames based on Super Mario Bros., Rad Racer and Tetris are played back to back on one competition cartridge, under a total time limit of 6 minutes and 21 seconds on default settings. The run starts in Super Mario Bros., where the task is to gain 50 coins as fast as possible. Rad Racer follows, with a track to complete as quickly as possible. Whatever time remains goes to Tetris, where the aim is to score as high as possible before the clock expires. The final competition score adds the Super Mario Bros. score, the Rad Racer score multiplied by 10 and the Tetris score multiplied by 25. A bank of DIP switches on the cartridge can set a different time limit.

t_8708307f9d24.overview: Based on the anime Moero! Top Striker, this soccer game follows Hikaru, a boy who has come to Genoa, Italy, to study soccer and aims to become a top striker. The main story mode spans three chapters that follow the anime's tournaments, with three matches per chapter and nine in all, and progress is kept with passwords. Matches are viewed from overhead; the player controls only the captain while the other ten players move on their own, with buttons for shooting, passing and a limited-use special shot. Losing a match opens a board-game section in which dice rolls lead to training for experience, money for new shoes, scouting of new players and extra special shots. A training mode and a two-player versus mode let any of the twelve teams in the game be used.

t_877a26247401.overview: Played on the Family Trainer mat instead of a controller, this fitness game has the player run, jump and crouch in place to move a runner through an outdoor obstacle course, using only the eight-key side A of the double-sided mat. The five stages begin on a grassland full of fences, with moles popping up as surprises, then a mountain trail of wild boars charging from both directions, a narrow ruin-like fortress passage with repeated dashes up slopes, a bridge of rotating logs crossed by hopping on one leg, and a river where jumps and ducks on a small raft avoid wooden gates. Training mode allows any stage to be practiced, beginner mode runs all five in order, and expert mode adds surprise animal attacks. The entered age and sex set the time limit for clearing the course.

t_877d13c3909f.overview: In 199X a giant meteorite falls south of Tokyo Bay, and a typhoon that follows washes a giant bird's egg ashore. Researchers identify it as the egg of an ancient bird-beast and decide to carry it away to hatch, but the giant monster Deburas rises from the sea and comes ashore after it. As a member of the Earth Defense Force, a single player fights a turn-based war simulation on a grid against the computer, commanding ground, air and naval units such as tanks, attack helicopters, fighters and cruisers. A dice-like roulette decides how many squares the unarmed egg transport can move. Deburas attacks every adjacent unit with fire and electric blasts from its horn, regenerates quickly and slows when damaged. Each map has an objective, and the game ends if the monster lands on the egg.

t_87f127c71353.overview: Played with the Datach barcode reader, this one-on-one fighting action game is based on the Dragon Ball manga and its anime adaptation Dragon Ball Z. Barcode cards come in two main types, character cards and item cards. At the start, a character card is scanned to choose the fighter. Fighters can punch, kick, jump, high-jump and fly, and pressing A and B together unleashes special moves such as energy waves, though each use lowers an attack-related parameter. A countdown timer runs during a bout; when it reaches zero, an interval begins in which item cards can be scanned to restore health or strengthen various parameters. The match ends as soon as one fighter's health is reduced to zero.

t_87f1720d9666.overview: The original Japanese release of Castlevania III: Dracula's Curse is set in 1476, when Count Dracula begins ravaging Europe with an army of monsters, and the Belmont family of vampire hunters, once exiled from Wallachia, is called into action. Trevor Belmont can be joined by the young sorceress Sypha Belnades, who has weak physical attacks but strong magic; the wall-climbing pirate Grant Danasty; and Alucard, the son of Dracula, who shoots fireballs and turns into a bat. Only one companion travels with Trevor at a time, and taking on a new partner means leaving the current one behind. The route branches at several points, and multiple endings depend on the choices made. This version uses a VRC6 chip with extra sound channels, Grant throws daggers instead of stabbing, and some enemies deal less damage than in the North American release.

t_885188aa925c.overview: Konami's vertically scrolling shooter for up to two players pits TwinBee and WinBee against the forces of Poko Poko. One button fires at airborne enemies and the other drops bombs on ground targets, while shooting floating clouds reveals bells whose color changes as they are hit, granting points, speed, a double shot, a piercing laser, ship copies or a barrier. Ground items include a milk bottle for an extra ship and candy for a three-way shot. Flying side by side produces a Wide Shot of four star-shaped beams, and lining up vertically creates a Super Barrier. A destroyed ship leaves a ghost behind; picking it up after respawning recovers all of its lost power-ups. The options menu sets the difficulty, the number of ships and the order of the first four stages, which include Air Island, Castle Land and a coal mine Dungeon.

t_88591cb0d5d6.overview: Hect, a developer that specialized in adapting board games to video games, released this Go title for the Famicom. Its focus is on teaching the player to play Go like the professionals, and the meikan of the title, a directory, refers here to a list of techniques and tactics. As in every version of Go, the goal is to surround the opposing player's pieces, thereby capturing them and removing them from the board.

t_886815234cf9.overview:
Controlling the hero Mega Man, the player runs, slides, and fires a blaster to defeat hostile creatures across several stages. The protagonist must retrieve energy crystals from the mining worlds by vanquishing eight berserk Robot Masters. Stages can be tackled in any order chosen by the player. Defeating a boss yields a specialized weapon that can be selected at will, allowing players to target the specific vulnerabilities of other bosses. Pickups found throughout each level replenish health, weapon energy, and extra lives, while stored tanks restore life energy completely.

Sliding allows players to slip under barriers and enemy fire. Mega Man is also assisted by Rush, a canine companion who transforms into a springboard, jet, or submarine to aid traversal. Periodic duels against the mini-boss Break Man open passageways. After defeating the initial Robot Masters, the player revisits four sites to battle Doc Robots before infiltrating a final fortress.

t_887f3e17958c.overview: Puzzle play in Flipull centers on a stack of blocks bearing different marks. The hero moves up and down beside the stack and throws the block he holds, which flies sideways and drops when it strikes a wall, the ceiling or a pipe. Hitting a block with the same mark clears it, and matching blocks lined up in a row vanish together for a higher score. Striking a different mark swaps the two, and the returning block leaves the hero shaking and unable to move for about two seconds. A throw with no valid target uses up a special block, which can hit any mark. Stages are cleared by whittling the remaining blocks down under a time limit. The Famicom version has 50 stages and adds an ADVANCE mode of 50 fixed puzzle layouts with limited moves and no time limit.

t_88b9d85c5608.overview: In the year 2302, an invading alien armada plans to destroy mankind after obliterating the Andromeda galaxy, and the player takes control of the Recca415 space fighter craft to stop it. The ship can be equipped with five distinct main weapons, each with its own advantages and disadvantages, and collecting five sub-weapons adds two satellite-like options that fire in multiple directions. When the main weapon is not fired for a brief time, an energy shield charges in front of the ship, absorbing enemy shots and destroying nearby enemies when released. Normal Game runs through four stages, followed by a harder rearranged second loop; Score Attack asks for the highest score within two minutes; Time Attack challenges the player to clear two stages within five minutes. A hidden fourth mode, Zanki Attack, is reached via cheat code.

t_89580bbb7b13.overview: Developed by Nichibutsu, this professional wrestling game draws its roster from wrestlers well-known in the All Japan Pro Wrestling and New Japan Pro Wrestling promotions, among them Antonio Inoki and Giant Baba. Single and Tag modes are both offered, each for one or two players. Two-player singles bouts are decided in a best two out of three setting with a 15-minute time limit, while in the one-player tag tournament every team faces each other twice under a 10-minute limit. Before matches, the player selects charge moves, each assigned to a direction on the D-pad, and finishing moves are performed by pressing A and B simultaneously.

t_895a6a715a29.overview: Made by the team behind Tobidase Daisakusen and issued on cartridge instead of disk, JJ keeps its predecessor's formula: the player character dashes into the depth of the screen, dodging enemies and leaping over gaps. Fast scrolling starts from the very first stage, the difficulty is higher, and the comical look gives way to a more realistic, biological and mechanical style. Items behave as before under new names, such as the Psycho Buster, which allows shots fired into the screen, and the Life Saver, which refills the timer. Each of the eight bosses is a Cyberness Dragon, created from the most vicious criminals held on the planet Tokidarea and rebuilt in dragon form. A stereoscopic mode works with the separately sold Famicom 3D System.

t_895b0a6fc9a5.overview:
Defeating reigning world champion Disaster Don serves as the ultimate goal for competitors navigating powerboat races. In single-player mode, played at Easy, Normal or Expert difficulty, the driver goes head-to-head against rivals such as Seasick Sidney, Aquarious Rex, Vicious Vickey, Surfer Bob, Weird Willey, Mangler Mike and Veronica Alabaster before finally facing Disaster Don. Losing two races ends the run, and a two-player mode pits two drivers against each other.

Controlling a powerboat, the player steers primarily from an overhead bird's-eye perspective featuring multidirectional scrolling, though buoy sections shift to a third-person tracking view. Winnings accumulate from legs won, beating course best times, sinking the rival boat, and gathering cash bonuses. These funds pay for repairs and boat component upgrades or cover two-thousand-dollar fines assessed for false starts. Collisions with animals, stationary obstacles, or rival watercraft inflict craft damage.

t_8980c40257f0.overview: American football seen from above, adapted from an SNK arcade game, with the field scrolling vertically and in any of eight directions on a horizontal screen. The player chooses one of 12 teams, and two players can compete head to head. Teams come from cities that had professional franchises at the time, but without the league's nicknames or colors. On offense the human side picks among five basic plays: a long pass, a short pass, a quarterback sneak, a hand-off to the backs, or a punt or field goal, and field goals can be tried only from inside the 15-yard line. Most of the official rules are in effect, and after a touchdown a two-point conversion may be attempted.

t_8990f8c8d671.overview: Ghost-hunting action in which two members of the team work together. The player picks from Peter Venkman, Ray Stantz, Egon Spengler or Winston Zeddemore, and this version adds their accountant, Louis Tully, as a fifth playable character. The first character chosen is controlled directly and holds ghosts with the Proton Beam, while the second follows as a sidekick, moved by the computer, imprisoning zapped foes in a trap. The objective is to trap all the ghosts in an area until an arrow appears showing where to travel next, and a boss appears at the end of each stage. The route starts in the Courthouse and continues to Peter Venkman's apartment and the old N.Y. subway system before the Art Gallery, where Vigo awaits. A second player can join with a second controller and press B to release the trap.

t_89b37ffd449c.overview: Time travel drives this vertically scrolling shoot 'em up adventure from Tecmo, in which a pilot flies the Neo Final Star time-traveling starship against the evil planet Gordess. The story opens in DA (Dimension Almanac) 2010, and a non-linear structure lets the ship travel back in time nearly at will; time is stockpiled by battling enemy craft, and each of the eight stages is assigned its own era. Landing turns the action into on-foot dungeon exploration with shooting elements, where the seven time stones hidden in each level's dungeon must be collected. Shops sell goods at prices that differ from shop to shop, and items are used from a pause sub-screen. Play is for a single player.

t_89b50a5c7748.overview: Sherlock Holmes and Watson walk the streets of London in this murder mystery adventure, the follow-up to Towa Chiki's earlier Sherlock Holmes game. The player directs Holmes around the city, finding clues and interrogating witnesses and suspects in the style of menu-driven text adventure whodunits. Scenes are handled through commands such as moving, looking and examining, and examining means steering a magnifying glass over the picture and selecting the spot to inspect. Some actions cost money: shillings can be collected and spent on things like a coach fare, which allows faster travel around London. Much of the story was written specifically for the game.

t_8a02616dd38a.overview: Set in the North African theatre of World War II, this strategy simulation puts the player in command of the Afrika Korps as Erwin Rommel against a computer-controlled British army. The player's force consists of nine different types of units and one headquarters unit; tanks are the strongest ground units but are weak against bombers. Units cannot be produced, but they can be replenished, and terrain plays an important role in battle. Victory comes from occupying the enemy headquarters or destroying all opposing forces. Five scenarios grow steadily more difficult, and a two-player versus mode is also included.

t_8a0ef338128f.overview: Written in Russian by A. Chudov for the Dendy, this word-guessing game is styled after television game shows such as Wheel of Fortune. As a sequel to Pole Chudes, it brings new graphics and new features. Mario, drawn with a sprite taken from Family BASIC, appears as the co-host who turns the letters. Like the rest of the developer's Dendy games, all of its text is in Russian, and the game identifies its author with an Ulyanovsk contact string.

t_8a2aa24aff31.overview: The former king of Almamoon conquered the whole continent with a band of knights and the power of a mysterious egg, but he dies the day after unification and the subject nations rise in revolt. His young heir is left with only Almamoon Castle and a handful of loyal retainers, and does not yet know how to use the egg. The first entry in the comedic Square real-time strategy series has generals sent out from the home castle to take enemy castles, while a monthly command screen handles hiring soldiers, buying trump cards from a merchant and dismissing generals when the treasury runs dry. There is no single final boss; several rival powers must be beaten to unite the continent. Its three episodes differ only in their maps and number of enemy nations, up to 11.

t_8a3de3552ae8.overview: A vertically scrolling shoot-'em-up that first circulated as an unlicensed Famicom cartridge and was later reissued for modern platforms alongside its 16-bit counterpart. The player pilots a fighter plane through stages crowded with enemy craft, with the goal of destroying everything in the way and defeating the boss waiting at the end of each stage. Collected items and power-ups enhance the health bar, raise the ship's speed, and upgrade existing weapons or add new ones. Three weapon types are available, together with secondary missiles and orbiting ships that act as shields; taking a hit lowers the current weapon level and is not fatal while the shields hold. Controls are simple, with the directional pad for movement and a single fire button, and unlimited continues are offered.

t_8a603d5344f0.overview: Thirteen teams take the field in this Taito baseball game: twelve modeled on real Japanese professional clubs, plus Idol, a team made up entirely of female players. Batting is viewed from behind the hitter. In pennant mode, players can be strengthened between games in attributes such as hitting ability and speed; batters' builds change as they develop, and pitchers who grow learn magic pitches, a burning ball and a splitting ball. A zoom mode lets fielders make fine plays on balls that look uncatchable and also zooms in on close plays. Alternately pressing the A and B buttons twenty times after a hit-by-pitch starts a brawl, drunk fans can invade the field under certain conditions, and a highlight replay of a pivotal moment runs after the game ends.

t_8ab6015adedc.overview: Adapted from a reader-participation game serialized in a magazine, this role-playing game unfolds in a fantasy world with two moons in its sky. The hero, a young man created for the game, sets out after a demonic sorcerer kidnaps his twin sister. He can be a warrior who specializes in melee combat, a holy warrior able to use healing magic, or a magic warrior skilled in attack spells. Journeying across the land, he recruits characters from the original series and must defeat the sorcerer's five evil followers and finally the sorcerer himself. Class roles are sharply divided: non-warriors do little physical damage, and parties without a magic user struggle against heavily armored foes, so balance matters. Each class has special actions that trigger at random from the fight, cast or defend commands, and attacks can aim at weak points, with a head blow able to cause a concussion and a hand strike able to stop an attack.

t_8ae271a1cac2.overview: Monsters have stolen the light of Indora, the origin of a god's power, from a fictional planet whose people once lived peacefully under that god, and the world is now overrun by beasts. The hero, a resident of one of the planet's countries who is named by the player, sets out to recover the light, gathering companions along the way. Progress in this role-playing game is kept with a battery-backed save rather than a long password, enemies appear as symbols on the field instead of attacking at random, and each country in the game world speaks its own language.

t_8b36cf193deb.overview: Based on the 1988 animated film, the Famicom Akira is an adventure developed by TOSE and published by Taito. The player takes the role of Kaneda, who begins the game when his motorcycle gang is taken into police custody after the abduction of their friend Tetsuo by the military. Progress is made by selecting actions from a list, and the current location is shown as a static image, often redrawn from the film. Progress can be recorded with the help of passwords.

t_8b520c62f8b7.overview: Bubby and Bobby return in human form for a platform adventure in which parasols take the place of bubbles and rainbows. A parasol can block as a shield, stun enemies, capture droplets or hurl enemies, and weaker foes can be stunned, juggled and tossed across the screen at other enemies. Catching five droplets forms a large drop whose attack depends on its element: water floods downward through the stage, fire ignites flames along the ground, lightning sends a bolt across the screen and star releases a spiral of stars. The journey crosses eight themed planets, each made up of six stages and a boss battle, on the way to Chaostikhan, the villain responsible for stealing color from the worlds. The NES conversion by Ocean leaves out the extra world found in the computer versions.

t_8b70f614ba0f.overview: Rex Soft developed this Famicom fighting game based on SNK's Samurai Shodown; the label calls it Samurai Spirits, and it was also released as Samurai Shodown III. Two versions differ mainly in the size of the cast. The first offers only four characters, Nakoruru, Ukyo, Haohmaru and Charlotte, while the second expands the roster to eight by adding Jubei, Kyoshiro, Galford and Wan-Fu. In the Samurai Shodown III version, two players can pick the same character from the original four, and its select screen shows the roster cloned twice. The sound uses the NTDEC/Asder engine, and the packaging closely mimics the Super Famicom release, with the cartridge and box both carrying the line "Rex Reprogrammed".

t_8b9d96964380.overview: Four-player Japanese mahjong arrives on the Famicom here, following an earlier mahjong cartridge whose technical limits had reduced the game to just two participants. Matches use a half-game format in which everyone starts with 27,000 points against a 30,000-point return, and the top finisher collects a bonus at the end. Left and right on the controller pick the tile to discard, while up and down choose actions such as pon, chi, kan, riichi, ron and tsumo. A pre-game setting decides whether open tanyao is allowed, and pressing Select during play toggles an open mode that reveals the other hands. Illegal declarations, such as winning without a scoring hand or on a furiten wait, are simply refused instead of being penalized. Limit hands can combine, so double and triple yakuman are possible.

t_8ba9ecca760c.overview: Waves of Galaga aliens fly into formation from the top and sides of the screen, and the fighter at the bottom must destroy them all to clear each stage. Aliens break away to dive at the ship while firing, and colliding with either a projectile or an alien costs a life; later stages bring more shots and faster dives. The Boss Galaga at the top of the formation take two hits to destroy and can capture the fighter with a tractor beam. Shooting the captor as it dives rescues the ship, which joins the active one as a dual fighter with more firepower but a larger target. Destroying the captor after it has returned to formation turns the captured ship against the player instead. The third stage and every fourth stage after it are bonus stages in which aliens fly preset patterns without firing.

t_8bb302e40abe.overview: A chef named Kokkun must make his way through his own restaurant after a rival chef, Hors d'Oeuvre, places a curse on it. Armed with kitchen utensil weapons, Kokkun battles evil food monsters such as sausages, onions and hamburgers across six levels, each set in a separate part of the restaurant like the kitchen, freezer and basement, with a boss waiting at the end of each. Defeated enemies leave coins, which are spent on a slot machine after a level to play for more lives and a bigger health bar. Everything leads to a final battle against the rival chef. In this original Japanese version the chef's head serves as the default weapon, unlike the overseas Panic Restaurant release.

t_8bc6d69c6940.overview: Designed around the Barcode Battler II, this cartridge treats the handheld as a barcode reader connected by cable, and both modes require characters to be created first by scanning barcodes into it. The scenario mode, Silent Empire, is set in a peaceful space paradise that has fallen to an invading empire, and follows a band of rebels fighting back across 20 worlds. Battles take place at enemy-guarded star systems, and each victory opens the way to the next. At a space station, new allies can be registered with the reader and items created; up to eight allies can be registered, though only three join the party at once, and items can be used or a retreat made during battle. Defeating the emperor who serves as the boss of world 20 reveals a hidden mastermind. A versus mode for one or two players turns the reader's free battle rules into an on-screen contest.

t_8bd18c2f81d9.overview:
Rescuing captured comrades and destroying an enemy vessel, the Toad Magma Tanker, serves as the primary objective across the Aniverse. The player starts by directing Bucky O'Hare, captain of the spaceship Righteous Indignation, who journeys across four distinct planets to free his imprisoned crew. These opening worlds can be tackled in any order, spanning environments filled with hazards such as waterfalls, active volcanoes, slick ice, and laser cannons. Stages contain multiple scenes that scroll both horizontally and vertically, and each stage ends with a boss encounter.

Freed crew members become playable, allowing the player to switch between characters at any time. Each hero utilizes different weapons and special skills, including short flights, wall clinging, high jumps, and a steerable crystal ball. Holding and then releasing the attack button triggers these special abilities, which grow stronger with collectible power-up icons. Extra lives and health can also be collected while battling toad forces.

t_8c23e0ff3e81.overview: An unlicensed demake of Donkey Kong Country, this platformer was ported to the NES by Hummer Team, with visuals hand drawn at lower quality and music reproduced by ear. It follows the gorilla Donkey Kong and his nephew Diddy Kong as they set out to recover their stolen banana hoard from King K. Rool and the Kremlings. The adventure spans five stages, each containing several levels and ending with a boss fight taken from the original game. Players can swap between the two Kongs at any time; Diddy has a faster base speed on land, and barrels fire a Kong out in a direction set by where it entered. Running is the fastest way to move through the levels.

t_8c5a466fbcf9.overview: Playing cards drop onto the board in Hect's puzzle game, and the player steers them to form poker hands of three or more cards in vertical, horizontal or diagonal lines; completed hands score points and disappear. The next three cards are shown in a window, the falling card can be swapped with one of them, and a button freezes it for a limited thinking time. A round lasts 53 cards including a joker: leftover cards cost points, and a card resting on the sixth row ends the game. In the one-player game, an ante must be paid to advance through nine stages to a final stage that counts as cleared only when every card is removed. Two players can compete in a card mode or a suit-only mark mode, where big hands send face-down blind cards to the opponent.

t_8c878ffd7796.overview: Instead of simply simulating a single machine, the game casts the player as a salaryman inside a pachinko parlor with long rows of machines. Play starts with 10,000 yen, which must be exchanged for pachinko balls before a machine is chosen. The other players seated in the parlor can change from visit to visit, a touch added to make the setting look more real. Winning a certain number of balls rewards the player with adult content. Developed by C&E and published by Hacker International in 1991, the game is titled simply Pachinko on its title screen.

t_8ca0a47b9340.overview: Bowling, batting and fielding are all under the player's control in this cricket simulation developed by Beam Software. A team is chosen from an international line-up covering all the major Test cricket–playing nations, and play can be a single match or a series of matches, with practice in the nets available before going straight into the game. Batting uses two buttons, one for hitting the ball and the other for slogging it around. Without official team or player licensing, many player names, particularly on the Australian team, are parodies of real cricketers, such as A. Boulder standing in for Allan Border. The presentation style is shared with Aussie Rules Footy, and up to two players can take part.

t_8cdd58f65821.overview: A home conversion of Tecmo's 1985 arcade soccer game Tehkan World Cup, built around a World Cup tournament. The conversion stays mostly faithful to the original, keeping its music and nearly identical play, but squeezes it onto the smaller hardware with some concessions. Control is digital only, which calls for different tactics than the arcade's analog control, and players can now start slide tackles. A choice of national teams is also new: the Team Select menu offers sixteen sides, among them Brazil, West Germany, Italy, Argentina, England, France and Japan. Both single-player and multiplayer play are supported.

t_8ce19c4345b6.overview: Following the plot of the 1939 movie of The Wizard of Oz, this platformer by Waixing, with its text in Chinese, has the player guide characters from the film, each with abilities of their own. Dorothy is the only playable character at the start. In the first level much of the ground can be crossed on a skateboard before a stretch of jumping leads to the Scarecrow, and the Tin Man and Cowardly Lion are found in later levels. Each character gets only one life and there are no continues. Many enemies, graphics and sound effects are borrowed from other games such as Chip 'n Dale Rescue Rangers and Contra, while the music is original.

t_8cf0b6343cde.overview: A game-original story puts the hitman Golgo 13 on the trail of a conspiracy. A CIA helicopter transporting the bacterial weapon Cassandra G is destroyed in a mysterious blast over the Statue of Liberty, and Golgo sets out to uncover the truth behind it, a path that leads to a battle against neo-Nazis. The basic play is side-view action, but the mission also folds in adventure elements, 3D gun shooting, sniping scenes, 3D maze dungeons and horizontally scrolling shooting stages. Life ticks down every few seconds, while defeating enemies restores both health and bullets, and the mission begins with Golgo's trusted gun out of ammunition. The acts travel through locations such as East Berlin, Athens and Rio de Janeiro.

t_8d131d9d3b8b.overview: Dr. Jekyll is on his way to his wedding to Miss Millicent, walking to the church with his cane in hand while townspeople, animals and other obstacles obstruct his path. Taking damage lowers his Life Meter and raises his Anger Meter; if the Life Meter is fully depleted the game is over, but if the Anger Meter fills, he transforms into Mr. Hyde. Play then moves to a demonic world where Hyde fires a psycho wave at monsters, and as he kills them his anger abates until he turns back into Jekyll. Gameplay alternates between the two characters across six levels, and the ending depends on which of them, Jekyll or Hyde, reaches the church first. The levels of this Japanese release differ from those of the North American version.

t_8d3b55fb2cb7.overview: Released in Korea in 1993, this side-scrolling platformer came out on the Famicom at the same time as Toto World 3. Its design is closer to Super Mario World: Koko and his sidekick can slide down slopes by pressing down and destroy blocks with a spinning jump, which is also the only way to hurt enemies. The stages are less linear than a simple run to the goal, because the heroes have to find a number of keys in each one before they can open the door to the next level. Power-ups expand Koko's jumping abilities, first adding a double jump and then, with the second upgrade, the ability to fly a short distance. Many of the graphics are borrowed from Super Mario Bros. and Sonic the Hedgehog.

t_8ddaf7bda25c.overview: Snowman twins Nick and Tom fight their way through stage after stage in this platform action game. Each player throws snow at enemies until they are completely covered and turn into snowballs; partially covered enemies cannot move until they shake the snow off. A finished snowball can then be rolled or thrown, eliminating any other enemies it rolls into. Colored potions grant power-ups, with the color showing which effect each one gives, such as the red potion that increases speed. A boss waits at every tenth stage and must be beaten before progress continues, and two players can take part together. The home version also opens with a new story sequence giving the brothers a unique origin.

t_8e1f4b08154a.overview: Super Game's unlicensed 8-bit recreation of Boogerman: A Pick and Flick Adventure brings the side-scrolling platformer to the Famicom, though it is considerably less faithful than the separate Boogerman II pirate adaptation. The level order is shuffled and the hero's abilities are restricted, with unlimited ammunition offered in compensation. Like other Super Game bootlegs, the cartridge has no real ending: once the third boss is defeated, the game simply resets.

t_8e6519d498e8.overview: Set in a retro-futuristic 1988, this side-scrolling action platformer follows the ninja Ryu Hayabusa, who travels to America after finding a letter from his father, Ken, who was seemingly killed in a duel. There Ryu learns that a man called the Jaquio plans to use the Light and Shadow demon statues to awaken the demon Jashin and destroy the world. Six Acts made up of 20 levels each end with a boss from the Malice Four. Ryu fights with the Dragon Sword and with secondary weapons powered by spiritual strength, among them throwing stars, windmill throwing stars, the art of the fire wheel and the jump & slash. He can cling to walls and spring off them to climb, and the story is told through anime-like cinematic cutscenes.

t_8e94afd7274a.overview: Endorsed by professional player Kouji Tanigawa, this shogi program goes beyond simple play against the computer by adding problem modes for building strength. In the match mode the player works toward the meijin title, facing a series of computer opponents who talk during play, change expression and favor different strategies; defeating four of them leads to games against a character modeled on Tanigawa. A tsume-shogi mode offers 40 mating problems played against the computer, which punishes wrong moves and announces when mate is no longer possible. A next-move mode has the player pick moves in succession, scoring each choice by how close it is to the best move and finishing with an assessment of playing strength. An elapsed-time display and automatic saving that lets an interrupted game resume are also included.

t_8ebcb47236bc.overview: Rather than a straight port, the Famicom conversion of the Capcom arcade shooter 1943 is an arrangement with many original elements. The vertically scrolling campaign spans 24 stages of air and sea battles, and a large fuel meter takes the place of extra lives. Unlike the arcade game, the plane can be improved permanently, with points spent on offensive and defensive power, maximum fuel, and special weapons and their durations; few weapons are available at first. A charged shot fires a laser, passwords allow starting partway through, and two-player cooperative play was removed. To move away from the real wartime setting, warships and battlefields were given fictional names, aircraft on both sides were redesigned so their nationality is hard to tell, and Valhalla replaced Midway in the subtitle on the packaging.

t_8ec8f9acb98a.overview: Anpanman, Shokupanman and Currypanman race across a board-game map in this party game for up to three players, each aiming to finish with the most points. A roulette spin moves a character up to five spaces, earning points for every space advanced, while a Dokin-chan result brings either a rock-paper-scissors contest or the chance to steal a bonus smiley marker that makes subgames easier and adds 1,000 points at the end. Certain spaces start subgames: a maze, a card-matching memory game, a card-recall test, bingo and spot-the-difference. Baikinman always joins in as a spoiler, collecting the points players lose by failing subgames and taking 100 points when he lands on them. The game ends as soon as anyone reaches the goal. Six maps are available, and the subgames can also be played on their own.

t_8ef5998ecfff.overview: Sachen developed and released this slot machine simulator in 1990. The international edition uses a title screen that reads "75 Bingo" in the Latin alphabet, while the original Chinese release is titled Bingo 75. Betting builds up a credit total, and gaining enough credits rewards the player with adult content: there are four pictures in all, each showing a girl gradually losing more clothes. Hummer Cheng developed the game for Sachen after the company had incorporated Joy Van.

t_8efa051a91c3.overview: Grand Shocker has revived the arch-enemies of the various Kamen Riders, who now rule different regions of Japan, and the Rider corps sets out to liberate each region before heading for the hideout of Grand Shocker. Blending a board game with role-playing elements, the game replaces hand-to-hand combat with motorcycle races. Nine riders are divided into three teams suited to road, off-road or balanced riding, while Rider Man tunes bikes at the base to improve engine, durability and fuel tank. Riders move around sugoroku-style regional maps by spinning a roulette, meeting events such as flat tires. Random battles are turn-based sprint races on bike lanes with blocking, items and missiles, and each regional hideout holds a circuit race against a rival that combines roulette movement with card-based actions. Money buys fuel, repairs and items.

t_8f2bd160ee7b.overview: Ported from Bullet-Proof Software's Japanese home computer versions, this Famicom Tetris organizes play as a series of stages rather than an endless game. Six rounds each hold ten stages, and clearing 25 lines advances to the next stage, after which the screen is cleared. Gravity increases from stage to stage, while each new round raises the height of the garbage already in the well. The player has three lives, so two top-outs are allowed before the game ends. Pieces fall into a 10 by 20 playfield with one next piece shown and no hold. The controls carry over the computer keyboard scheme: pressing down rotates a piece and the A button performs a hard drop, the reverse of most later versions. Clearing the final stage of the last round shows an ending, after which play loops.

t_8f9d5a67f4f4.overview: Corporate strategy drives this text adventure, which revolves around making decisions and negotiating deals. Messages arrive in a data-feed style to give the proceedings a business feel, and play runs through a command menu offering look, think, talk, drink, telephone, analyze, opinion, negotiate and move. Along the way the player must deal with loan sharks in the Caribbean, ruthless corporate executives from rival companies and arbitration sessions, and at times the game plays more like a strategy title. A wrong decision at the wrong moment ends the game in a loss, much like losing a life in an action game. There are no items to use, and the only real movement is walking a character around a virtual office building.

t_8fea850b9462.overview:
Directing cue shots around a pool table, the player aims to sink balls and accumulate points. Scoring relies on successfully sinking targets and clearing them in sequential numerical order. Hitting targets into pockets marked by flashing stars grants special bonuses, which provide additional points or an extra ball. Cue actions support distinct techniques, allowing the player to apply various spins and execute masse shots.

Play progresses through a series of classes while operating under a limited supply of cue balls. Missing two shots or scratching costs a ball, and maintaining a sufficient score is required to proceed. After all balls are pocketed, a trick shot must also be performed to advance. Other modes include lesson and practice training, a two-player Pocket Game over five sets, and two-player 9 Ball.

t_907d84fc6f57.overview: Far away in the Q Galaxy, the animals of a glittering planet live peacefully thanks to the Rainbow-Flower until Dr. Mouse steals it, builds a base and tries to rule the world. Q-Boy sets out to defeat him and win the flower back. In this side-scrolling platformer the hero fires puffs of air that knock enemies into walls, other enemies or the screen edge, and holding the button charges a stronger puff. He can also jump in mid-air, and both moves drain a Power Meter that refills while he stands on the ground. The adventure spans five worlds, including slippery ice stages and an auto-scrolling cloud ride, with bosses beaten by deflecting their attacks and a whack-a-mole bonus game that awards extra lives.

t_9112d3bdbe3d.overview: In the Special edition of the baseball management series created by Hiroyuki Sonobe, both leagues can now progress at the same time. The player still acts as a manager guiding a club through the pennant race, calling for pinch hitters, relief changes, steals and defensive shifts, with player names and ratings open to editing. A Japan Series can now be played without a Turbo File, and domed stadiums are added as home parks. Background music now plays on the individual statistics and team data screens, which were silent in earlier entries, while the back-screen graphic changes from bright blue to monochrome. A bug that failed to swap players' statistics when the players were exchanged on the team data screen was fixed in a later production run.

t_911d2ede79b7.overview: Billy and Jimmy Lee set out to avenge the death of Billy's girlfriend Marian, killed in an attack by an unnamed gang, in this beat-'em-up for one or two players. Combat keeps the directional-based system of the arcade version, and each of the nine stages opens with still imagery and text that sets the scene. Two modes of play differ only in whether the two players can hurt each other with their attacks, and three difficulty levels are offered, with the entire game playable on any setting. The ultimate antagonist is a nameless martial artist who wields supernatural abilities. As a pre-release build, this version may differ in places from the finished game.

t_91fdddc4aa96.overview: Adapted from a manga by Oki Hajime about police officers working in a SWAT team, this role-playing game sends a squad of special anti-terrorist agents into a building where a hostage situation is taking place. Their goal is to take out the villains and free the hostages. Outside of combat, the building is viewed from a traditional 3D dungeon perspective: the team moves through hallways, chooses which rooms to investigate and which traps to disarm, and must reach the end within a given time limit. Battles with gunmen play out in turn-based RPG style, with commands entered for each surviving team member, including which weapon to attack with and which target to attack. Captured terrorists can be wounded and interrogated for more information.

t_921937175c73.overview: Modeled on Konami's Beatmania, this Famicom rhythm game asks the player to hit beats in time with the music. Five songs are included, one of them a version of A-ha's "Take On Me", and each remix is built from only a few notes on a loop. A health bar along the bottom of the screen drains whenever a beat is missed and refills when one is hit; if it runs out, play ends and the results screen appears. Four difficulty settings are available, Easy, Normal, Hard and Very Hard, and a practice mode makes the beats move more slowly. The title screen styles the name as Beat ⓝ Box and credits a company called YNC, dating the game to 2000.

t_923d2c0c00ad.overview: Baseball for one or two players that borrows only its name from a long-running baseball board game toy, sharing no game system with it. The main pennant mode has the player choose six of twelve teams to form a league and play a 30-, 60- or 130-game season. Players grow stronger as games accumulate, and earnings after each game pay for special training or for items that power up the roster. Winning the pennant leads to a championship series against one team chosen at random from the six not selected, and four wins bring the ending. An exhibition mode offers a single game with a starting budget of ten million yen for buying items beforehand. Three stadium types are available, and the items cover batting, baserunning and fielding.

t_9246fd31a39d.overview: A young American boy named Ninten is at the center of this role-playing adventure set in a slightly offbeat version of late 20th-century America. After his house is attacked by a poltergeist, Ninten learns that his great grandfather studied psychic powers and sets out to investigate crises occurring across America. In the land of Magicant, Queen Mary asks him to collect the eight melodies of a song that appears in her dreams, a quest that ultimately leads to a confrontation with an alien named Giegue. Ninten is joined by Lloyd, Ana and Teddy, and the whole party is visible as it explores the overworld from a top-down perspective. Combat uses random encounters, and items serve purposes such as healing, clearing obstacles and unlocking doors.
t_9246fd31a39d.official: See how the EarthBound saga began in this previously unreleased translation of the Japanese role-playing classic, also known as Mother. Devised and scripted by Japanese writer Shigesato Itoi, EarthBound Beginnings is an offbeat and irreverent twist on the RPG genre. In its modern day setting, young heroes arm themselves not with swords and magic, but with household items and psychic powers.

t_924ee0d1f661.overview: Built around character switching, Gardman is a single-player 2D platformer developed by Nice Code Software and published by Shenzhen Nanjing Technology. Getting past the obstacles along the way requires swapping between five different characters, each with its own unique ability; the five forms are dashing, climbing, flying, swimming and hitting. Story cutscenes shown in the game contain its only Chinese text.

t_92a41d19129c.overview: Loosely inspired by the legendary swordsman Miyamoto Musashi, this role-playing game in the vein of Dragon Quest stars his son, also named Musashi, who wants to live up to his father's name and become the greatest swordsman in Japan. The land of Yamato is being terrorized by an army of demons led by Gajiro the Fiend, who resides on Ganryu Island, so the young hero sets out across the country to aid the people plagued by the minions of Gajiro while collecting scrolls from the Book of the Five Rings. Only Musashi is controlled, though a tanuki he rescues joins him, occasionally helps in battle and can sniff out hidden key items. Random encounters, simple maze dungeons, poison marshes and shrine gates fill the journey, and the episodic story keeps a humorous, light-hearted tone.

t_92df38ead017.overview: This set pairs the baseball game with the OB All-Star child cassette, one of only two roster cartridges actually released for it. The small cassette plugs into a slot on the back of the main cartridge and supplies its own player data in place of the built-in rosters. Underneath is a conventional baseball game with sixteen teams: twelve modeled on the professional clubs of the day and four original teams. One or two players can face off in versus mode with any team, the pennant race runs for 30, 60, 90 or 130 games, and further options include a team editor, a winning-streak tournament, a home run contest and a watch mode. Inserting or removing the child cassette clears the save data.

t_92f308d6bf36.overview: The second Famicom entry in the baseball management series created by Hiroyuki Sonobe keeps the established formula: the player manages a club through a pennant race, calling for pinch hitters, relief changes, steals and defensive shifts, with player names and ratings open to editing. Team and player names are still not real ones. Standings, individual statistics and parameters now appear in kanji, making them far easier to read. Computer-run managers can be given selectable thinking routines, and ballparks can use artificial turf, which tires fielders over a long pennant race, or natural turf, which produces more errors. A new skip mode fast-forwards computer-versus-computer games and greatly speeds up a season. The top S rating now applies to every parameter, pitchers gain a stamina parameter, and Pacific League team cheering songs join the in-game music.

t_9301a5b66110.overview: Kyonshi have returned to town and stolen grandpa's sacred ritual implement, and evil spirits have carried off the souls of three of four orphan boys. Playing as one of the four boys, each differing in appearance and in attack and defense ratings, the player explores the town in an overhead view styled like an RPG; days are mostly safe, but kyonshi appear at night. Fights unfold as side-scrolling action. Collecting the fire, earth, water and wind talismans opens the spirit gate, revealing entrances to the towers at the town's four corners. Reaching and defeating the final boss completes the single-player adventure.

t_936529e7c2b6.overview: Mr. Penguin, a pioneer of the icy far north, collects diamonds scattered across each round and must stash every one of them safely in his igloo. Seals with tusks as sharp as blades roam the playfield, and the penguin can either crush them with a block of ice or dive out of their way. The block-pushing puzzle action continues over 50 rounds, and the cartridge also includes a construction feature for designing a custom round.

t_9385595d4f47.overview: Goku stars in this European release, translated into French, of the Famicom game Dragon Ball: Shenlong no Nazo, which very roughly follows the first two volumes of the Dragon Ball manga. Most of the action takes place in 2D overhead areas where Goku must fight many enemies, while boss fights switch to side-scrolling sequences. His Power drains over time and from enemy attacks, so he has to keep eating food to avoid running out. Items come from Hoipoi Capsules, including the Nyoibo staff, which turns his punch into a stronger, longer-reaching attack, and Kame Marks that unlock the Kamehameha. Unlike the North American Dragon Power, this version retains the Dragon Ball license and characters, although it carries the same censorship as the American release. A single player takes part.

t_93d813e8087d.overview: Set in the year 199X, this side-scrolling action game begins when an undersea volcanic eruption awakens the demon emperor Garus after 5,000 years. He revives fallen yokai and sends them against the human world, beginning with Tokyo. Akira, a boy with psychic powers whose ancestors once sealed Garus away, sets out to defeat the revived yokai leader and save the human world from chaos. Stages scroll either vertically or horizontally. Instead of a stock of lives, the hero has a life bar, so running out of life ends the game at once, and falling into a pit restarts the stage. Filling a separate experience meter upgrades his projectile attacks, and running out of time summons an enemy that kills him instantly. The adventure spans six stages for a single player, and early stages provide passwords when cleared.

t_942a1ccde3d5.overview: Based on Fujiko F. Fujio's Perman manga, this side-scrolling action game begins when Birdman, visiting to see how things are on Earth, has his flying saucer stolen by Dr. Mad, and Perman sets out to win it back. Along the way he fights with punches, a cell-transforming gun that turns enemies into animals, and stomping jumps. Boss encounters switch to a sugoroku board game: player and boss take turns rolling a die, and the first to reach the goal or drain the other's HP wins, though the final showdown with Dr. Mad is fought as action. Badges collected in each stage call allies for help during boss games. In stages 3 and 5 the player may pick Booby, who jumps higher, and each stage holds a minigame that awards a special item.

t_9462701d8caa.overview: Giga Zombie, whose plan for world conquest was once foiled by Doraemon and his friends, revives villains Doraemon had beaten in the past and tries again. When the group heads for his era by time machine, he hits them with a space-time storm that separates all five and scatters Doraemon's secret gadgets. Doraemon lands at the home of the player's own character, who joins him to search for the missing friends and gadgets. Four scenarios, each a follow-up to one of the feature-length adventures, rescue the friends one at a time. Gadgets take the place of magic and cost dorayaki to use, and dorayaki also buy goods at exchange shops; equipment is never sold and must be found in chests or received from people. Battles are turn-based against up to three enemies, and a helper called in towns restores health and saves progress.

t_9487cd31553b.overview: Science-fiction role-playing set during Star date 0991, STED follows a band of companions who track down a distress signal sent from a distant planet just as monster activity is on the rise. Battles are viewed from the first person and draw on weapons, items, armor and ESP, the game's form of magic. Rather than tracking a single pool of health, combat deals damage to individual body parts of each character, so wounds can call for treatment before the group is ready to press on. Alpha Denshi developed the game, and K. Amusement Leasing published it for the Famicom.

t_94c8e9543ca3.overview: Rather than racing horses directly, the player feeds race data into a horse racing simulation that focuses mostly on correctly predicting the outcome of races, with the idea of using that knowledge when gambling on the real thing. Races do take place, but the player has no active role in how they turn out; all interaction happens through menus and set-up screens. Manga artist Hiroshi Kurogane, famous for his love of betting on horse races, provides the endorsement.

t_94dd19ec23e4.overview: Packed in with Sharp's C1 Famicom TV rather than sold in stores, this cartridge pairs simplified versions of two Nintendo titles. The first is a cut-down Donkey Kong Jr. that keeps only the first and fourth stages and drops difficulty selection; Donkey Kong Jr. runs, jumps and climbs vines and chains while dodging enemies, working to free his father, Donkey Kong, from the cage where Mario holds him. The second, labeled Jr. Lesson on the cartridge, carries over only the +−×÷ Exercise from Donkey Kong Jr. Math, in which fixed arithmetic problems are solved by climbing chains to reach the correct numbers and symbols.

t_9566794c1cf5.overview:
Rescuing the kidnapped Dr. Light and freeing the city from Protoman's robots serves as the primary objective. The player controls Mega Man across stages where running, jumping, and shooting are needed to overcome enemy machines. Mega Man attacks using an arm cannon with unlimited ammunition, which can also be charged to unleash wider blasts that cancel if damage is taken during charging. Defeated foes and stage pickups restore lost health, while Energy Tanks, Mega Tanks, and extra lives provide additional support.

Advancement involves conquering eight initial stages and defeating their Robot Masters. Overcoming each boss yields a special weapon powered by finite ammunition. Specific levels include distinct features such as reversed gravity or operating a water craft. Completing certain areas unlocks traversal abilities via Rush, while collecting eight hidden letters that spell MEGAMANV grants access to Beat, a robotic bird that attacks enemies.

t_9595c5c388c1.overview: Set in a near future already wracked with disaster, Pax Softnica's role-playing game follows a spiritual wanderer trying to avert the end of days predicted by Nostradamus. The apocalypse begins when a meteorite slams into the young man's hometown, and along the way he unravels a mystery about his own origins. To stop the catastrophe he must invoke the powers of various religions and belief systems, including Hindu, Buddhist and Christian faiths. The quest involves finding eight pieces of a trigram, seven chakra statues and seven amulets of the star lords in seven mystic cities while fighting a cast of bizarre demons and gods. Vap published the game, whose Japanese title means "way" or "road."

t_959f5ba435d3.overview: Konami's NES conversion of its Turtles arcade beat-'em-up reached Europe under the Hero Turtles name. After Shredder kidnaps the Turtles' friend April O'Neil and their mentor Splinter, the four heroes give chase to rescue them and defeat Shredder. Leonardo is well-rounded, Donatello has slower attacks with longer range, and Michelangelo and Raphael strike faster at shorter range; color-coded Foot Soldiers make up most of the opposition. Compared with the arcade original, most stages are extended and two new levels are added, including a snowy Central Park, along with two new bosses: Tora, a polar bear-like blizzard beast, and Shogun, a robotic samurai. The parking garage stage now ends with a battle against the mutated fly form of Baxter Stockman.

t_95bb608bca74.overview: Digging through underground terrain, the hero Hottaman must find the four keys hidden in each stage, usually in treasure chests or buried in dirt, to make the exit appear. Monsters spawn from the earth, some breathing fire, and Hottaman fights back with a flamethrower; a hit from an enemy or its fire breath, exploding dynamite, or lava without a fireproof coat costs a life. Power-ups come from eggs and chests and are stored in a meter, picked with the Select button and used with B; they include a shovel that boosts speed and bombs that break blocks the drill cannot. Pits connect to other pits across the terrain, and different kinds of ground score different points when dug. The 15 stages repeat after the last one is finished.
