t_95c64a36dcc1.overview: Charged with saving the Kingdom of Alefgard, a lone hero sets out from the king's chamber after the Dragonlord has stolen the Ball of Light and captured the princess. Towns hold shops that sell better weapons and armor, along with inns where the hero recovers health and magic, and menu commands let him talk to people, check his status and search beneath his feet. Battles are turn-based and seen from a first-person view, with the hero facing one opponent at a time. Victories bring experience points and gold, and rising levels increase his strength, agility and speed. Each spell costs MP. If his HP reaches zero, he is returned to the king and loses half his gold. In this original Japanese release, a quest is continued with a password.

t_95d3c61da181.overview: A one-on-one fighting game in which the four turtles stage a contest among themselves to decide who is fit to take on Shredder's challenge. In the story mode the chosen turtle faces the other turtles, then Casey Jones, then Hothead, and finally Shredder. Matches run up to three rounds, with two round wins needed for victory. During a fight, a flying monitor bearing Splinter's face sometimes appears and drops a red ball power-up in the middle of the stage; either fighter can grab it and unleash it with the right command. Versus modes pit a player against the computer or a second player, a tournament mode supports four players, and options adjust difficulty, continues and speed.

t_961a0e8e2054.overview:
Piloting the Tiger-Heli attack helicopter, the player navigates vertically scrolling battlefields to destroy enemy forces. Opposing targets include ground and air units such as tanks, aircraft, gunboats, and artillery, alongside installations like fuel depots and buildings. The craft defends itself with short-range missiles capable of striking air and ground targets, as well as bombs that damage everything across a wide area.

Shooting color-changing crosses produces items that replenish bomb stocks or recruit up to two support helicopters that provide supplemental forward or sideways firepower. A hidden continue option allows players to resume play after a game over.

t_962ce813ce0e.overview: A text-based adventure with a comedic science-fiction premise, released only in Japan. Bunroku, a fourth-year student in the Department of Chrono-Travel Studies, comes from a family of merchants and dreams of opening a great general store, and he builds his own time machine to pursue it. After traveling back to Venice in 1275, he encounters his idol Marco Polo and joins the expedition bound for Japan, described as the Country of Gold. Play uses the menu-driven command style of Japanese adventure games, and a Zapping System lets the player switch characters in the middle of a scene. The trip starts out along the route of the real expedition but soon turns chaotic and surreal, as a plot to assassinate Kublai Khan and eliminate Marco's crew unfolds.

t_96368c23d312.overview: After the Emperor declares a ban on opium and appoints Lin Zexu as imperial commissioner, a young martial arts student named Longyin Yu pledges to help him uphold the ban and becomes Lin Zexu's apprentice. Fuzhou Waixing built the game as an action role-playing adventure in which the player takes the role of Longyin Yu. Progress comes through carrying out various tasks and going on different missions on Lin Zexu's behalf in support of the prohibition.

t_96fb03081c8a.overview: Donald, the McDonald's mascot known elsewhere as Ronald McDonald, sets out to restore peace after the demon army of the Gumon clan casts a spell over Donald Land, sealing away its people and turning its animals violent. Nearly all of his companions have been carried off, and some, brainwashed, occasionally attack him. The platforming adventure spans twelve worlds, from his hometown through a lakeside, forests, a sky castle, caves, a harbor and the ocean floor to the magic castle where Gumon lives. Donald throws apple bombs in an arc and can even ride on them, while touching an enemy starts a scuffle that damages the foe but costs a point of life. Hamburger coins collected in stages are spent after each stage on power-ups, a longer life bar or extra lives, or on McDonald's products that unlock mini-games.

t_97095b95875d.overview: Tuned cars, rather than purpose-built racers, are the focus of this Famicom racing game. The player starts out as a road racer driving a MINI, later switching to a Ferrari 512BB. Finishing a race within the time limit earns prize money that depends on the finishing time, and the winnings go toward buying parts that modify the car from its stock equipment and improve its performance. Victory in the Taito Grand Prix itself grants an F1 license and entry into F1 racing, where earning enough points across sixteen races leads to the ending. During races, the background music can be chosen from four options, engine sound included.

t_976a0ff14ec6.overview: Wagyan II, the son of the original hero, takes the lead in the sequel. Side-scrolling action stages again lead to boss encounters that are settled through mini-games with a strong battle-of-wits element rather than combat. Along the way, sonic attacks stun enemies, and the only difference from his father is that he cannot fire sonic blasts while invincible. Additions include special stages that cross clouds and lakes and the introduction of power-up items. Alongside the shiritori word chain and memory matching, the boss mini-games gain three new contests: Number Search, Sound Memory Match and Panel Rock-Paper-Scissors. Two players can take part, alternating after each miss, with no simultaneous or cooperative play.

t_9793a6dca938.overview: An enhanced Famicom version of Route-16, a 1981 arcade maze game by Sun Electronics, puts the player behind the wheel of a car in a top-down maze divided into sixteen rooms. The goal is to collect all the money bags while avoiding enemy cars and keeping fuel from running out, and once the car starts moving it can never stop. Leaving a room brings up a radar map showing the positions of cars, money and room entrances, though a room's internal layout stays hidden until the car enters it. Flags reverse the roles, letting the player crash into enemy cars to halt them briefly for bonus points. The story sends the hero into a criminal organization's secret base to recover money stolen from countries around the world. This release adds EASY, NORMAL and DIFFICULT settings, improved graphics and numbered rooms on the radar map.

t_97953fba0aa9.overview:
Players control a magical fighter who runs, jumps, ducks, and attacks using a sword to avenge the fallen land of Baljing. Holding the attack button unleashes a charged bomb. Vanquishing monsters fills a metamorphosis meter, which allows the warrior to transform into a flying dragon during a jump once the meter is half full. In dragon form, the character hovers and shoots forward across an auto-scrolling screen. This state slowly empties the gauge, and the player can also shift back manually.

Power-up items labeled G, B, and R alter the protagonist's outfit color, dictating the projectile attacks of both forms. Additional items provide healing, accelerate meter filling, or eliminate all on-screen foes. Across six stages, each culminating in a guardian battle, players receive a staff that extends maximum health and fully refills it. The fighter has three lives, and up to three continues are available.

t_97abbdc16924.overview: Long ago the God of Heaven captured the Evils of Hell and sealed them in four towers with four magic balls, but over thousands of years the balls have worked loose. The Abbot of Sou-Lin Temple sends Pan-zo and Pan-lo to recapture the Evils. Viewed from overhead, each stage is cleared by pushing every magic ball onto a podium of the same color, which locks it in place. Players can stun enemies with a projectile, kick a ball so that it rolls faster and flattens enemies in its path, or swap places with it. Candles mark the time limit, and when it runs out the enemies become invincible ghosts. Thirty levels span five worlds with passwords between them, and Pan-lo joins in two-player mode.

t_97d827268bf2.overview:
Set during the Warring States Period of feudal Japan, the game tasks players with unifying the country under one rule, either the 17 fiefs of central Japan or all 50 fiefs. Taking control of Oda Nobunaga or other regional daimyos, the participant manages land, builds an economy, and commands armies across the nation. Up to eight players are supported in this strategic contest.

Play unfolds in alternating turns, where strategic map turns represent seasons and tactical battlefield phases represent single days. Leaders allocate critical resources to sustain civil productivity, retain peasant loyalty, and expand military power. Decisions include levying taxes, improving flood defenses, trading through merchants, recruiting troops or ninjas, training forces, arranging political marriages, and spying on rivals. In warfare, victory comes from outlasting an invading force for a month, wiping out an enemy command division, forcing an opposing army to retreat, or starving foes of their supplies.

t_97e8389a62b6.overview: Super Game produced this Famicom recreation of Boogerman: A Pick and Flick Adventure, the platformer originally released for the Sega Mega Drive/Genesis and Super Nintendo. The port follows the original loosely, with a mixed-up level order and severely limited abilities for the hero, which it offsets by giving infinite ammo. Its music appears to be original, though some tracks vaguely recall the Genesis soundtrack, and the introductory story text is laid out in paragraphs. There is no true ending: after the final boss is defeated, the game returns to the story screen and restarts.

t_98115fc0c64d.overview: Instead of a character, the player steers a mysterious block, a cube that rolls around each location of this single-player shooter. Along the way the block collects tasty fruit and all sorts of other goodies while shooting the garden pests that roam the stage, among them mosquitoes, worms and snails, along with other nasty creatures. Thin Chen Enterprise developed the game, and Sachen published it in Asia in 1990.

t_9830a6aed7ef.overview: Drawing on the folktale of Urashima Taro but set in a near-future Japan, this action game stars Ken Urashima, a descendant of Urashima Taro. The Kijuu Empire, ruled by the emperor Goruza, has taken Otohime XVIII, princess of the Ryugu Kingdom, and a turtle who survived the kingdom's fall gives Ken the battle suit Brigandine. Across eleven areas, Ken defeats the boss in each island's machine castle to rescue the princess held there. Odd-numbered stages are side-scrolling action on the islands, while even-numbered stages switch to side-scrolling shooting as Ken pilots a Cyborg Beast to the next island. He can equip varied attack items and special items, obtained from a dog hermit or bought at item shops with E-balls, and has a life gauge and a stock of lives.

t_9848205d8fdd.overview: A modified version of the NES Contra for the PAL region, Probotector redesigns the human protagonists and some of the enemy characters with a robotic appearance. Up to two players fight simultaneously through eight stages that recompose the seven stages of the arcade original, and the two base stages no longer have the arcade's mazelike structure or time limit. Weapons come from pill box sensors and flying item capsules: a machine gun that fires rapidly while the button is held, a laser gun that shoots a powerful beam, a fireball gun with a corkscrew pattern and a shotgun that spreads five bullets, along with a rapid-bullets upgrade and a barrier that grants temporary invulnerability. The mission ends in an alien lair, where the regular enemy soldiers give way to otherworldly creatures.

t_984f817b0ccf.overview: Kunio-kun's cast moves into a period-drama setting in this action RPG from Technos Japan, whose map spans the country from Ezo to Hizen. The gang boss Bunzo has fallen ill, and the wanderer Kunimasa, who owes him a debt, comes to visit with his underling Tsurumatsu. There they meet Bunzo's daughter Okoto and Asajiro, a man claiming to be her fiance, before Okoto is kidnapped and Kunimasa sets out to track down the mastermind. Like Downtown Nekketsu Monogatari, it is a brawling action RPG, but the map forms a network instead of a line, characters have more status parameters, and the hero gains more actions and special moves. Money is counted in mon, shops sell items and techniques, and battery backup saves progress. One or two players can play simultaneously.

t_987de0c4d5c3.overview: Long after the world's destruction, the survivors have abandoned science and advanced technology to study the ways of magic, and they built a floating Tower to prevent any future cataclysms. The protagonist awakens with no memory and must combine the four elemental Swords of Wind, Fire, Water, and Thunder into the legendary sword Crystalis. Viewed from above, the action role-playing adventure allows movement in eight directions, with one button swinging the sword and the other using magic or an item. Each sword has its own strengths and also opens paths, such as freezing narrow sections of river, and the swords can launch powered-up elemental projectiles. Some enemies are immune to certain elements, defeating monsters earns experience points, and some bosses and enemies can only be damaged once the hero reaches a minimum level.

t_98870c4ae362.overview: Set in a parallel universe called Artelius, this science-fiction role-playing adventure follows a cyborg built by a scientist named Dr. Rado to defeat the diabolical king Sarbelor, whose machine has split the universe into spaces filled with asteroid belts. The journey moves among three planets and two asteroid belts. Players begin by customizing their character's traits, then use warp points to travel across the universe. On the map, red dots mark enemies, while blue dots mark space colonies where the hero can rest and stock up on supplies. Random battles are fought from a first-person perspective and earn experience points for leveling up. Strength governs attack, the shield sets defense, and high agility makes escaping easier. The laser beam can eventually be upgraded into a hyper magnum gun stronger than a fully powered-up missile or bazooka.

t_9892b00c7583.overview: Based on the anime known abroad as Samurai Pizza Cats, this side-scrolling action game is spread over 11 stages. Before each stage one of the three main cats, Yattarou, Pururun or Sukashii, is chosen, and projectile attacks drain the Ninpo meter, with stronger attacks using more of it. Four support members can be swapped in at any time from the pause menu, each with a single power: smashing obstacles, digging through soil, swimming underwater or flying. Using these powers drains a separate HELP bar. Stages 2 to 4 can be cleared in any order, and every stage has its own boss. There are no bottomless pits, and a password system with infinite continues keeps the challenge low.

t_98b918bec57e.overview: Set in a city, this Namco follow-up to the arcade game Tank Battalion puts the player in a tank that must wipe out enemy tanks while guarding headquarters. Enemies roll in from the top of the screen to attack both the tank and the base, marked by a phoenix symbol; one shell striking the base ends the game. Destroying 20 enemy tanks clears a stage; there are 35 stages, followed by a tougher second loop on the same maps. Foes range from fast armored cars to heavy tanks that take four hits, and flashing tanks drop random items such as a star that upgrades the tank, a grenade that clears the screen and a shovel that fortifies the base. Brick walls crumble, steel walls resist, forests hide tanks, ice makes them slide and rivers block them. Two players can fight side by side, and a construction mode lets players design stages.

t_98d369815f6f.overview: Turn-based strategy follows Genghis Khan or one of his rivals in a bid to conquer the Old World. One scenario, for a single player, starts in 1175 with Temujin uniting the land; the other, beginning in 1206, supports one to four players choosing among Genghis Khan, Alexios III, Richard of England and Yoritomo of Japan, and its goal is to conquer every opposing country. Each season a ruler can issue three commands at the home base, spending ability points on actions such as training troops, drafting soldiers, trading with merchants, sending treaties or going to war. Rather than using development commands, the ruler allots the population to towns, castles, food and specialty goods. Battles take place on hex maps where mountains, forests, deserts and seas matter, and fathering children supplies heirs and blood-related generals who never betray.

t_9904ff6638af.overview: Side-scrolling action and role-playing elements combine in this adventure starring Poco, an old wooden figure and hero who has lived in harmony with humans for many years. His journey is to find the fairy who teaches people to get back to being friendly with wooden dolls, and along the way he fights strange creatures and bothersome old men with his fists. One hand can hold a weapon and the other a passive tool, such as a lamp for dark areas. Gear can be bought, and the hero can sleep at hotels, gamble, steal and bribe other characters; stealing changes his appearance to that of a thief, and hotels and pawn shops then refuse him. Eating prevents hunger and governs health recovery, while an in-game clock runs day and night cycles through four seasons.

t_9953ca31390e.overview: Bob returns in this Famicom sequel, which trades the single-screen format of the first game for side-scrolling platforming. During his wedding, the prince of Merry Land is turned into a frog by an unknown force, and Bob must gather the ingredients for an antidote, scattered across five worlds, to restore him to human form. His hammer remains the main tool: it bonks enemies so they can be chucked away, since he cannot defeat foes by jumping on them, and it also plays a part in solving puzzles. New power-ups for the hammer include a staff that throws fire. Collectible medals add extra hit points, continues restart play at the last checkpoint, and there is no save or password system, so the adventure must be finished in one sitting.

t_9972fb301e78.overview: Gameinis, a Hong Kong maker of famiclone systems, paired two motion-controlled sports games on this cartridge, which came bundled with a wireless leg strap accessory for its Virtual Station console. Both games use the leg strap as their controller, and the cartridge has a motion sensor molded into the top of its plastic. TV Soccer offers three modes. In Shoot Mode the player alternates between kicking and goalkeeping; Technique Mode asks the player to kick a ball into the air as many times as possible without letting it hit the ground; Match Mode completes the set. Boxing is a first-person fight in which the player is shown only as a pair of levitating boxing gloves facing the opponent.

t_997c51e305b4.overview: Instead of a game, the cartridge holds a programming environment that lets the Family Computer run a dialect of BASIC enhanced for game development; this is a later revision of the original Family BASIC release. Programs are typed on a keyboard that connects to the console's expansion connector, with a programming textbook included in the set. Commands handle sprites, animation, backgrounds, musical sequences and gamepads, and predefined characters can be freely combined into sprite characters and background screens, while the interpreter only supports integers. A menu leads to BASIC or to the BG GRAPHIC editor for building backgrounds. Finished programs can be kept temporarily in the cartridge or saved to cassette tape with a recorder such as the Famicom Data Recorder.

t_99a953017d3c.overview: Ice hockey between national sides takes the place of professional clubs here, since no league license was involved. The eight teams are based on hockey-playing countries: the USA, Canada, Japan, the USSR, England, France, Norway and Czechoslovakia. Before each game, players designate a single-player match against the computer or a two-player game in which two people compete simultaneously against each other, and in single-player the skill level of the CPU opponents can be set. The length of the periods is adjustable as well, and the teams for the match are chosen on the same setup screen. Micronics, working as a developer for hire, produced the game for publisher K Amusement.

t_99ac231c97ff.overview: Drawn from the anime Magical Princess Minky Momo, the story follows Momo as she sets out to recover ten stolen Dream Pearls. Each case opens with a questioning segment in which information is gathered, and the problem is then solved in a mini-game built on what was learned. Momo uses her magical powers to transform into various occupations, such as a detective, a nurse or a police officer, and puts these forms to work solving problems through a series of different mini-games. Five mini-games appear in all, and the adventure unfolds case by case as the pearls are tracked down one after another.

t_9a29bf3f8e3b.overview: Kunio heads to America for a street basketball tournament in this sports game. After winning the quiz show Downtown Quiz and earning a trip to America as his prize, he forms the Nekketsu Dunk Heroes to take on the competition. Games are two-on-two, played in two halves of three minutes each, with no health gauges, and players can punch, kick and even use weapons. Scoring departs from real basketball: a shot into the high hoop is worth 4 points, while the middle and low hoops are worth 3, and a ring can be taken by the opponent and attached to their own board. Rival teams have distinctive home courts, such as an aircraft carrier for a team of marines or a court with slot machines that change point values. One or two players can compete.

t_9a2f844edaca.overview: Enix's murder-mystery adventure puts the player in the role of an unseen detective, simply referred to as Boss, who investigates the death of a successful bank's president in a locked room. The case unfolds in real Japanese locations, mainly Kobe, with a few sequences in Kyoto and Sumoto. An assistant named Yasuhiko Mano, called Yasu, speaks and carries out most commands. The Famicom version uses a menu of fourteen set commands selected with the gamepad, and one option lets the player move a cursor with the D-pad to search for clues, using the pointer as a magnifying glass or, during questioning, as a fist or hammer. A phone can dial any number, collected items serve as evidence, and an underground maze section plays like a role-playing game. Only one suspect is the true culprit; the others are red herrings.

t_9a44684d7e37.overview: Science fiction replaces fantasy in this role-playing adventure, set in the year 2300 after the human race has created an Earth federation government and begun colonizing nearby planets. When an alien species from the far reaches of outer space attacks, a young soldier stationed with the Rayieza unit on Mars retreats toward Earth with Blue, the only other surviving member of the force and an expert user of ESP who can sense dead souls. Rimi, a girl discovered in cold sleep inside a capsule, joins them, while Mio is the computer program that manages the unit's operations. Ported from an Enix computer game, the Family Computer version adds a side-scrolling screen when landing on a planet's surface and lets Rimi use psychic powers. New enemy special attacks can lower the maximum hit points of allied characters.

t_9a7031a23e5e.overview: Following the long-running television drama, the retired lord Mito Mitsukuni sets out with his retainers Suke-san and Kaku-san to travel the provinces, solving a crime in each of seven stages. The player controls Kaku-san in odd-numbered stages and Suke-san in even-numbered ones, questioning townspeople and gathering evidence; some villains must first be beaten until they cry before they will talk. Helpers such as Yashichi and Ogin can be summoned with special items to sneak into attics and uncover plots. Each piece of evidence raises a clue gauge, and once it is full the culprit is judged at the lord's inn. Every investigation must be finished within seven in-game hours, though lanterns extend the limit, and leaving any case unsolved leads to a bad ending. Shops sell useful items, and soba restaurants restore strength.

t_9b28e506fe5a.overview: Ten wrestlers, each with a nickname, a birthplace and signature moves, meet in the ring in this professional wrestling game. With no dedicated grapple button, holds and slams begin when wrestlers walk into each other and are chosen with joypad and button combinations, giving each fighter more than 20 moves. Certain signature moves on a weakened opponent trigger a close-up replay. Matches end by pinfall, submission or count-out. In single-player play, the chosen wrestler must beat every other competitor before facing a non-playable final boss, training between matches with button-mashing squats, sit-ups or push-ups to build strength. Two players can face off, with a momentum meter deciding who wins grappling exchanges. A password feature saves progress, and an announcer named Yasushi Geki calls the action.

t_9b832576113c.overview: This early build of Sunsoft's unreleased NES superhero game still stars Superman, before the project was reworked around a generic hero and renamed Sunman. At this stage the engine was mostly finished but only the first level had been programmed. Play matches the later game: the hero runs, jumps, punches and ducks, and can fly simply by pressing up. The build has no title screen and starts straight in the action, features two music tracks found only in this version, and lets a paused game skip ahead with Select. Its first boss, a giant helicopter, is fought from a lying-down position here. It is a separate game from the Kemco Superman released on the NES.

t_9c366d92401b.overview: Based on the television anime, this action role-playing game tells an original side story. Wataru and his companions are thrown into another world and separated, and Wataru is taken prisoner; his mecha Ryujinmaru asks a passing young traveler for help, and the boy becomes its temporary partner. Exploring towns, fields and dungeons on an overhead map, the hero searches for Wataru while meeting his scattered allies and borrowing their machines. Battles switch to side-view action, with one button to jump, one to attack, and the select and start buttons for magic and items. Strength depends on the hero's level, the mecha he rides and the sword and shield equipped, and spell books found along the way teach magic, some of it required to progress. Defeating the final boss starts a harder mode.

t_9c73ad65109c.overview: Block breaking gets a twist here: unlike the original Breakout, enemies appear on screen and can be hit to gain power-ups. A level is cleared by either destroying all the bricks or defeating the enemies, and the game spans four zones of eleven levels each, called Cubic Zone, Mirror Zone, Tube Zone and Final Zone. One to three enemies are typically on screen at once, emerging from trapdoors in the top corners or entering through the side walls. Power-ups include a parachute that slows the ball, multiple balls and projectiles, while Konami Man serves as a level warp, flying from the top to the bottom of the play area. Every few levels brings a boss, ranging from a small dragon to a centipede. Each level also hides a letter, and together the letters form a password that must be entered at the end to see the ending.

t_9c8b52d44545.overview: Namco's vertically scrolling shooter reached the Famicom in 1984, and Bandai released that version internationally, including this PAL edition. The player pilots the Solvalou attack craft against the Xevious forces plotting to take over Earth. Two weapons are always at hand: a zapper that fires at flying enemies and a blaster for bombing ground installations and vehicles, with a reticle in front of the ship showing where bombs will land. The scrolling areas are geographically distinct, with forests, roads, rivers and mechanical structures below. At certain points the Andor Genesis mothership attacks with an endless stream of projectiles, and it can be defeated by destroying all four blaster receptacles or the core in the center. Bombing specific parts of an area uncovers hidden towers called Sol Citadels.

t_9c9b605bb1e9.overview: Singles, doubles and mixed doubles matches are all available in this tennis game, which accommodates up to four simultaneous players when a multiplayer accessory such as the NES Satellite or NES Four Score is connected. In single-player mode, the goal is to compete in the four Grand Slams, but entry to them first requires winning the qualifying tournament, the Asmik Open. The game was released in other regions as Top Players' Tennis.

t_9cb37d9eee8e.overview: Princess Kurumi has been kidnapped, and the young ninja Yanchamaru sets out alone to rescue her from the villain Zoringen, whose gang has seized Furin Castle. The journey unfolds as a side-scrolling action game made up of seven rounds, each ending with a boss battle, before a direct showdown with Zoringen at the castle. Yanchamaru fights with his trusted sword, having mastered the secret rotating sword technique, and bells collected along the way grant temporary power-ups: the golden bell makes every sword spin fire a projectile, while the silver bell surrounds him with a spinning force field. Early in the story, the princess's pigeon Mamemaru arrives wounded, carrying a scroll that pleads for help.

t_9cc96ab29d13.overview: Fighting and role-playing mix in this martial arts adventure. After choosing one of three characters, the player starts in a village with shops, places to save and heal, and people to talk to; attacking is impossible in town. Enemies roam the land outside, and approaching one switches to a side-view battle that plays like a one-on-one fighting game in the style of Yie Ar Kung-Fu, with a punch, a kick, ducking and jumping. Victories build experience as the fighter trains for tournaments held in large buildings in the villages, where a series of opponents must be beaten one after another before a boss. Health is not restored after a fight, so regular trips to healers are needed, and the hero is finished the first time his life meter runs out.

t_9cd4ba00909c.overview: A nameless martial artist sets out to beat a collection of enemy fighters and be crowned grand master in this one-on-one fighting game. Bouts play out on a non-scrolling screen viewed from the side, where the fighter moves around to avoid the opponent's attacks and then strikes back with combinations of the attack buttons and directional controls. Special moves are triggered by specific combinations of directional inputs and unleash unique attacks, but each one depletes the stamina bar, which can leave the fighter defenseless against enemy attacks. The game is for a single player.

t_9d31d2c89591.overview: Planned for a US release by Innovation, this prototype localizes the Korean one-on-one fighting game The General's Son, developed by Gartist Team and published by Daou Infosys. Like most 8-bit fighters, it takes strong inspiration from Street Fighter II, but the moveset was deliberately simplified: the controls are very simple, and a special move comes from holding the A and B buttons together for about a second. The prototype is mostly identical to the Korean version. Only the title screen, the ending screen and the characters' names on the versus screen were adapted, with the names now shown as acronyms, while the end credits remain in Hangul. The prototype also grants infinite lives, presumably for testing and review.

t_9d75966babbf.overview: SD Nation, a peaceful land of SD warriors, is the setting for this action shooting game. A mysterious UFO suddenly attacks and carries off the Gachapon machine, mother of the SD warriors, along with its engineer Emmy. Behind it is the evil emperor Dark Brain, who means to multiply evil SD units with the machine. The playable heroes form four groups, Kamen Rider, Ultra, Gundam and Metal Hero, each with three characters that switch in turn as power-up items are collected. Eight planet stages can be cleared in any order, and once all are open the final ninth stage appears. Every character has 16 health, and with no lives, an empty gauge or a fall into a pit ends the game at once and returns the player to stage select. One player takes part.

t_9d83ce341647.overview:
Drivers maneuver off-road trucks around top-view stadium tracks, competing against other racers or computer-controlled vehicles. Up to four participants can compete simultaneously with specific multi-controller adapters. Across a season of Qualification races followed by a Tournament, competitors run eight tracks in both directions, and the first truck to complete four laps wins each race.

Participants begin with three lives and can gain a life by winning or lose one by finishing in fourth place. Players can continue after losing all lives during the initial fourteen qualification races, though accumulated cash resets to zero. Points are awarded based on winnings, while earned prize money allows players to purchase vehicle upgrades such as shocks, tires, top speed, acceleration, or extra nitro boosts.

t_9db5e33b6a4a.overview: Team building drives this baseball game from SNK. Eight teams come with the game and six more can be created, for a total of 14; when making a team, the player chooses its main strength, which favors that attribute when the computer randomly generates the players. Each new club starts with about $30,000 and 18 players: five pitchers, eight batters and five pinch hitters. Winning games earns money that buys upgrades to the abilities of players on the roster or signs free agents priced from $5,000 to $2,980,000. A mini-league of up to six teams, each playing up to 25 games against every other team, is kept with battery backup, and a simple one-off versus mode is also included. Among the default teams is an all-women's squad.

t_9e0ae43289d9.overview: Modeled on Sega's Space Harrier, Cosmos Cop is a pseudo-3D shoot 'em up in which the action moves into the screen rather than scrolling sideways. Enemies close in from the distance, and the player must shoot them down while avoiding the projectiles they fire back. The in-game text describes the mission as defeating a terror from the Alienation space invaded galaxy. The game pushes the NES hard, and its first-person scaling produces a lot of image breakup on screen. NTDEC first issued it as a stand-alone cartridge in Famicom format, and the same game also appeared on the Caltron 6 in 1 multicart.

t_9e2dfd794d7b.overview: Valiant, the exiled prince of Thule from the newspaper comic strip, sets out to earn his knighthood in a side-scrolling action adventure. The quest begins in treacherous marshland in search of the legendary Viking Ring of Peace, continues through a forest inhabited by cutthroats and thieves, and descends into underground caverns and a deadly maze where the ring rests. From there the prince must cross a stormy sea and battle a hostile Viking armada to reach Camelot, then find Arthur's Hall beyond a labyrinth of corridors and passageways. Armed with a crossbow, Valiant can walk, jump and throw things at opponents, while pit traps, water hazards and archers embedded in the background stand in the way.

t_9e3fea197001.overview: Drawn from the Chinese historical novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms, NTDEC's side-scrolling beat 'em up is an 8-bit version of Capcom's arcade game Warriors of Fate. The player controls one of three generals on a mission to stop the evil Cao Cao and his army, battling through enemy troops, and two players can team up for cooperative play. The arcade original, released in Japan as Tenchi wo Kurau II, follows Liu Bei's struggle against Cao Cao's forces, with one or more of Wei's generals waiting as bosses at the end of each stage.

t_9e4d7fce0f7a.overview: Developed by TOSE for Jaleco, this golf game offers stroke, course, challenge and training modes, plus a two-player mode in which each player takes a turn to stroke. Before each shot the player picks a club and a stance, then presses the A button at an exact moment to set the force with which the club meets the ball. A caddy menu on the B button gives hints for the current hole, allows a mulligan and even consoles the player after many missed strokes. Grass, sand and other terrain are simulated, along with wind, whose speed and direction are shown before each stroke. Progressing through the challenge mode earns money for buying new clubs and hiring new caddies.

t_9e944eb14e44.overview: Ported by Compile from a Nihon Falcom computer adventure, this command-selection adventure is set among the ancient Maya ruins of Chichén Itzá in Mexico. In the Famicom version, Professor Shiratori dies under mysterious circumstances, and the 17-year-old protagonist travels to Mexico with the professor's daughter Sayuri, his childhood friend, to uncover the truth and search for the Temple of the Sun and the Key of the Sun hidden in the ruins. Adventure scenes are played with command icons such as push, wait and wash along with collected items, while a field mode of 64 switching screens links the ruins. Companions explain puzzles, mechanisms and items, time is tracked by the sun's position, RPG elements add evil spirits that require leveling up, and progress is kept with passwords.

t_9ea269762941.overview:
Rescuing captured comrades and eliminating alien invaders before time runs out serves as the central mission. Controlling either Ricky or Mary, players navigate alien-infested ships across scrolling environments. A time limit applies to every stage, demanding swift action to locate and liberate the hostages.

Each of the seven ships holds 12 captives, and freeing all of them opens the exit door to the alien leader's room. Defeating the boss and its henchmen allows players to advance to the next ship. The game accommodates up to two players as they battle hostile creatures across the infested vessels.

t_9ecafc8aebb2.overview: Players roll a single die to move around a board in the first entry of the Itadaki Street series, buying unowned property they land on and earning money whenever opponents stop on their property. Stocks can be bought at the bank and on certain squares, and collecting a set of four suits before passing the starting position levels a player up and brings in extra gold. Assets count stocks, property value and gold on hand, and victory goes to the first player to make it back to the bank holding at least the board's required amount. One to four players compete, with computer characters filling any empty seats. Five maps and seven characters are included, among them a single map built for three players.

t_9f20096c59b3.overview: Tecmo's arcade platformer is reworked here into an action role-playing adventure. Armed with the Diskarmor, a razor-edged shield on a long chain that works like a yo-yo, a legendary warrior sets out to defeat Ligar, who has overrun the world with revived monsters. Side-scrolling areas branch off a central hub seen from overhead, much of the map is open from the start, and items such as the grappling hook, crossbow and pulley open new routes. Defeating enemies builds two kinds of experience: Tone raises attack strength and Lasting raises health, which grows from three points to as many as twelve. Stars dropped by enemies fuel three spells, Power-Up, Attack & Assail and Recover, and characters in safe rooms offer advice. There is no password or battery save, but continues are unlimited.

t_9f41cbf37791.overview: Modeled on Ishikawa Goemon, the noble thief of Japanese folklore, Goemon travels through a series of top-down action-adventure stages similar to The Legend of Zelda. In each stage he must find three passes to advance, uncovering them in boxes or hidden passages or buying them outright. Collected or purchased items power Goemon up, but these upgrades can be lost after a few hits. Clearing every stage brings him to a new Japanese province, eight in all; the levels stay the same while the ending changes. This first entry plays straighter than its sequels, without the comic situations and strange characters that came to define the series. It is a single-player game.

t_9f7cdd397e10.overview: Ported by Data East from its arcade vehicular combat game Burnin' Rubber, this Famicom release sends a car down each course toward the finish while knocking enemy vehicles off the road. Cars can be bumped into obstacles or destroyed by jumping on them, but trucks can only be destroyed by landing on them and sometimes drop debris that must be avoided. Once the car reaches at least 100 mph it can jump, which is needed to clear large obstacles such as bodies of water; a flashing exclamation point warns of them. A car is lost by wrecking into either side of the road, plunging into water or hitting an obstacle, and play continues until no cars remain. A change of seasons marks each new level.

t_9f7d19133ffc.overview: Booky Man, a beetle who likes everything clean, has promised a rat to help clean the streets of their community, but two lizards are always chasing him. Booky goes through tunnels to avoid the lizards' attacks or uses the sweeping brush to chase them home, and a bug that dirties the streets must also be killed. The game is NTDEC's hack of Brush Roller, itself a clone of the arcade maze game Make Trax, known in Japan as Crush Roller. The hack replaced the title screen, some of the graphics and the sound. In Spain the cartridge was published by Gluk Video, carrying the catalog code CN-08.

t_9fabdcbc1ed2.overview: This unreleased localization of the Famicom pinball game Super Pinball swaps the original's mahjong framing for sushi. A new opening shows the Statue of Liberty making sushi, followed by a text crawl on the history of sushi and Japanese sushi terminology, and the ending adds an explanation of how to use chopsticks. Underneath, the pinball follows the original design of six interconnected tables to explore for high scores, with early tables built around a car race and a pit stop and later routes leading to robot foes, a UFO screen and a Breakout level with a movable paddle. Up to four players can take part by taking turns.

t_9fe102fd6383.overview: Built around Tamiya's Mini 4WD toy cars, this Konami release combines a board game with automatic races. Turns are taken on a board-style grid where cash and parts are collected, and money can also be spent on new parts, which are then used to tune the car. Races run automatically, with performance decided by the parts equipped on the car, so success comes from build choices, including how the car handles each event's terrain. Strong finishes earn points, and accumulating enough points opens entry to the Japan Cup, where the goal is to take first place. Both single-player and multiplayer play are supported.

t_9ffa8db76e74.overview: Hanafuda, the traditional Japanese playing card game, is the basis of this adult-oriented matching game from Hacker International, sold under the full title Hayama Reiko, Katsuragi Mayako no AV Hanafuda Club. Matches are played against an opponent, and success is rewarded with increasingly lascivious and revealing artwork of that opponent. The presentation of these reward images is similar to that of other Hacker International releases such as AV Poker, Hot Slots and Soap Panic.

t_a01334415dbf.overview: Capcom's follow-up to the arcade game Higemaru began as a port and grew into an original action-adventure. Momotaru sails the seas in search of treasure hidden by the legendary pirate Captain Beard, boarding pirate ships to battle their captains, whose defeat yields the key to an island. Each island is a multi-screen scrolling area where progress depends on beating bosses and solving puzzles, among them Cook Island, Mermaid Island and Skull Island. Momotaru attacks by throwing barrels, rocks and similar objects, with an iron ball serving as a stronger reusable projectile, and the Higemaru pirates are the common enemies. Points double as life, so reaching zero ends the game, and a password allows resuming. The final boss is a Red Arremer from Ghosts 'n Goblins, and the number of jewels collected changes the ending.

t_a015ab887459.overview: Falling-block puzzling with an ancient Egyptian theme drives this Japanese edition of Pyramid, published in Japan by Hacker International. Pieces built from isosceles right triangles are rotated and dropped into a well, and each stone must be turned, twisted and carefully fit together as it falls. Filling a row makes it vanish so everything above drops down, while shapes lump into the general structure when they touch something below. Bombs and hidden surprises add to a game that calls for both planning and quick reflexes, and the one rule is not to let the pit fill up with stones. The Hacker version contains nudity.

t_a01a60e3fed3.overview: Monsters fall into four columns in this falling block puzzle game, and Mario, stationed below the playing field, swaps adjacent stacks so that each falling monster lands on a matching block and both are removed, such as a Goomba dropping onto a Goomba block. A stack can hold up to eight objects, and the game ends when any stack crosses the line at the top. Halves of a Yoshi eggshell also fall; joining a top half to a bottom half hatches a Yoshi for bonus points, and any monsters stacked between the halves are encased and eliminated, with larger Yoshi characters for more monsters. A-Type play continues indefinitely, B-Type requires clearing the field level by level, and in multiplayer a second player controls Luigi.

t_a04ef7f7ea8b.overview: Gathering the legendary ten braves is the goal of this field-map role-playing game. The player takes the role of Sanada Yukimura, acting on orders from his father, the lord of his home castle, and travels around Japan to bring together the ten braves scattered across the country and defeat the clan's sworn enemy. There are no experience points: the Sanada army grows stronger by persuading enemy soldiers met in random encounters to join it. When troops appear, they deliver an opening speech, and the player chooses to fight, persuade or retreat. Loyalty must be maintained by regularly paying rations as a stipend, since troops whose loyalty falls to zero rebel and force a battle. Each brave leads a type of troop and has a weapon and a special skill, such as procuring supplies, blowing up barriers or picking locks.

t_a05bb77fc273.overview: Unable to jump, Ladd of the FF Battalion relies on a mechanical arm with a grappling gun to pull himself forward, swing from ceilings, cross chasms and pick up items. His mission is to rescue Super Joe and stop the Albatros project. On an overworld map, Ladd's helicopter moves between connected Areas, and if an enemy vehicle intercepts it, an overhead shooting stage follows. Descending into a combat Area starts with an equipment choice and leads into side-scrolling platforming, where Ladd must find Communications Rooms and then destroy the computer core in the Computer Room, guarded by a boss. Weapons, protective gear and communications devices turn up along the way, while in neutral areas firing a weapon sounds an alarm and turns every soldier hostile.

t_a1548b03835c.overview: Six games share this multicart, all previously sold separately by NTDEC. Cosmos Cop is a pseudo-3D into-the-screen shooter similar to Space Harrier, while Magic Carpet 1001 is a horizontally scrolling shooter. Balloon Monster clones the arcade game Pang, and Adam & Eve is a single-screen platform game similar to Balloon Fight. Porter is a puzzle game in the style of Sokoban, and Bookyman reworks a clone of the arcade game Crush Roller. The selection menu also has two different songs that can be switched with the Select button.

t_a188a637a2bb.overview: Created in Russia by A. Chudov for the Dendy system, this puzzle game follows the Sokoban formula. The player moves a warehouse keeper around each stage, pushing boxes to sort them out and put them into their slots; a round is complete once the boxes are in place. Besides the built-in stages, the game lets the player build custom levels. Its title translates as Warehouse No. 18, matching the storeroom setting of the box-pushing puzzles.

t_a1a558e5c097.overview: Based on SNK's 1985 arcade game TNK III, this overhead tank shooter is set in World War II, with Nazi Germany as the enemy. Learning that a giant brain called THINK TANK is being built in Berlin, Allied commander Eisenhower summons the veteran Ralf Jones and orders him to land ahead of the invasion force at Normandy. After removing the Big Cannon that blocks the landing team, Ralf pushes on alone. The directional buttons drive the tank while its turret points in eight directions, with separate buttons for the machine gun and the main gun. Items give the main gun rapid-fire, piercing, explosive or long-range shells, restore energy or add reserve energy, and a radio receiver relays information. Different paths lead to the final level, and the level bosses include giant tanks, railway artillery, fortresses and grounded aircraft. One or two players take turns.

t_a23096909f18.overview: The final entry in the Kaiketsu Yanchamaru series is a single-player side-scrolling action game in which Yanchamaru once again appears with a changed look. Where the earlier games centered on close combat with a spinning sword, this installment focuses on fighting with staff techniques, which gives the action greater variety. The adventure is divided into seven stages.

t_a230bf734168.overview: Built on Shisen-sho, the mahjong solitaire puzzle, Idol Shisen Mahjong is Hacker International's adult reworking of a C&E tile-matching game known elsewhere as Tiles of Fate. A board is cleared by joining all matching pairs of tiles before the time bar runs out, and a pair can only be joined in fewer than three turns; every successful pair refills part of the timer. Instead of reconquering the districts of China as in the original, the player plays against a girl who undresses gradually, and after five or six rounds a partial nude picture is shown. Four different girls appear. The tile mechanics and tile graphics are unchanged from the original release, while all of the music was replaced.

t_a2598d1f62ed.overview: Starring Japanese Formula One driver Satoru Nakajima, this racer takes a simulation-style approach instead of arcade driving, recreating the full sixteen-race schedule of the Formula One World Championship. Circuits mix sharp and wide turns that force the driver to slow to the right speed for each corner, three of the four cars require gear shifting, and tire wear builds over a race so that at least one pit stop is needed to stay competitive. Rival cars behave like ghosts and can be driven straight through. Grand Prix mode spans nine levels of competition, each with more rounds and higher difficulty, and every race weekend opens with a five-lap qualifying session in which the player must post a lap fast enough to bump into the four-car starting grid. Passwords allow progress to be saved.

t_a2621db960fb.overview: Archaeologist and explorer Indy Borgnine is searching for the fabled Hanging Gardens of Babylon, and lost scriptures reveal that the only way to see them is to climb to the very top of the 64-story Tower of Babel. Each of the 64 levels is a puzzle in which he must avoid enemies while lifting and rearranging loose L-shaped blocks into staircases and using vines to reach the exit. Some exits are covered by a mask that disappears once every crystal ball on the level has been collected. A power count limits block handling, since each lift lowers it by one. Items such as pots, crowns, jewels, lamps and stars award points, restore power, grant invincibility, let him pass through blocks or increase his speed.

t_a2893fab2bd7.overview: A man's body turns up at Harumi Wharf in Tokyo Bay, opening this command-selection detective adventure. The victim is Masuda Bunkichi, and the unnamed protagonist, a police inspector, takes up the case with his subordinate Kuroki. The trail leads north to Hokkaido, where the inspector teams up with Shunsuke Saruwatari, a detective from the Kushiro police station known as Shun. The investigation moves through real locations such as Lake Mashu, Lake Kussharo, Abashiri Prison and the Yubari coal mine. Instead of typing words, the player picks actions from a fixed command list that is always on screen, with entries such as moving to another location or questioning the person present, so no effort is wasted guessing which words the game recognizes.

t_a2b8215ca9ee.overview: Di Guo Feng Bao, also titled Napoleon's War, blends real-time and turn-based strategy. Waixing made it in 1998 on the engine of its earlier Chu Han Zheng Ba: War Between Chu and Han, so it plays the same way but with completely new maps, fewer missions and new graphics and sound. A global map with a minimap gives an overview of the player's holdings, such as captured cities, and is where the army is managed. Battles are fought in a separate turn-based mode, in which the player directs divisions to destroy the enemy's armies and capture the fort. Progress can be saved at any time in one of two save slots.

t_a2bf12237cf9.overview: Modeled on Mitchell's arcade game Pang, known in North America as Buster Bros., Balloon Monster is a bubble-popping action game created by Mega Soft. Play centers on hitting bubbles, and the game's own short description advises striking them at their highest point. The challenge stretches across 50 levels. NTDEC also issued the game as a stand-alone cartridge in Famicom format, and it is one of the six titles gathered on the unlicensed Caltron 6 in 1 multicart.

t_a31e7f2cf187.overview: Based on the 1988 Fuji Television anime adaptation of Frances Hodgson Burnett's novel Little Lord Fauntleroy, this adventure follows Cedric Errol, known as Ceddie, an American boy who learns he is the sole heir to a British earldom and leaves New York for his ancestral castle. His grandfather, the Earl of Dorincourt, means to make an aristocrat of him. Play resembles a regular Famicom adventure game, with walking around, talking to people and finding items that are used to solve puzzles, but instead of choosing destinations from a menu, Ceddie is moved manually through each locale from a top-down perspective. Action sequences require dodging pedestrians when leaving the estate; colliding with someone or entering the wrong door brings a scolding from his tutor and a round of trivia questions.

t_a32b635170ae.overview: Loosely built around the Twelve Labors of Hercules, this role-playing game from Data East casts the player as a young Hercules who seeks to rescue Venus from captivity in Hades, with bosses that match the content of each labor. Combat is turn-based against land-based, air-based and sea-based enemies: swords, axes and hammers deal extra damage to land foes, bows suit airborne ones and spears work best at sea. Some weapons need one hand and others both; two-handed weapons hit harder but rule out a shield and increase the damage Hercules takes. Every weapon and piece of armor has an endurance value that wears down with use until the item breaks, and the blacksmith Hephaestus can restore it and, once hired for 5000G, travels along to repair equipment after each battle.

t_a32d3f0e2531.overview: Despite the '97 on its title screen, Rex Soft's 1997 Famicom fighter is a port of The King of Fighters '95. Nine fighters are playable: Kyo, Mai, Ralf, Clark, Choi, Chin, Andy, Robert and Eiji. Rather than the original fixed trios, they are unusually set up in several different teams of three, and about half of the original roster is missing. Terry, Joe, Ryo, Takuma and Iori appear in the intro even though none of them can be played. A "TM" mark sits beside the logo, and the intro announces the 1997 tournament. In the original release, defeating all of the regular opponents leads to a final boss and an ending; cartridges converted to other hardware forget which opponents have been beaten and never reach the final boss.

t_a32d8aacb1ab.overview: Licensed from the North American film of the same name, this baseball game uses the movie's title and its distinctive mohawk baseball mascot but otherwise borrows few elements from the film. Player, team and stadium names are all fictional. Ten teams contest a league: six modeled on the Japanese Central League clubs of 1989 and four modeled on MLB clubs. The team modeled on the Indians mixes players based on the film's characters with players modeled on the real Indians roster at the end of the 1988 season, although the film characters do not carry their real names. Modes include head-to-head play for two people, a single-player game against the computer, a Watch mode in which two CPU teams play each other, and a Batting mode for getting used to the timing of the swing.

t_a33f9e3b3156.overview: With Pachio-kun called away on urgent business to a neighboring planet, his only son Maru, prince of the pachinko planet, is left in charge just as a mysterious alien calling himself a Fuyuu Seijin sends a challenge: he will wreck the pachinko parlors of Earth. Maru sets off to protect them and spends 11 days on Earth. Each day he must empty at least 10 machines before going home to sleep and advance the date; as days pass, new machines arrive at shops advertised by flyers, the alien's minions hide around the parlors waiting to be caught, and messages from his mother Ginko turn up. The series' first exchange system converts winnings into coins at 150 balls per coin, while balls cost a coin per 100 and travel between stations costs fares. Three battery-saved diaries hold progress, and an optional pachinko controller is supported.

t_a3799ec5ac76.overview: Sold with a microphone, this Korean karaoke cartridge from Hicom offers a selection of 156 songs, most of them children's songs. Up to eight characters can be selected, among them Magpie, Frankenstein and Robocop, and each chosen character picks three songs, so a playlist can hold as many as 24 songs. Once the choices are made, the selected character comes out onto the stage and performs a variety of dance moves while the player sings to the music. During a song the controller changes the background, which also restarts the song, as well as the microphone volume, song pitch and song speed. When the song is over, the performance receives a score from 0 to 99.

t_a39ee3e3a1df.overview: Viewed from a top-down perspective, Go! Dizzy Go! is an action-puzzle game in which Dizzy must navigate a series of single-screen mazes. The story sends him out to rescue his friends. On many levels the goal is to collect all the items on the screen, usually fruit, while avoiding enemies, and Dizzy can fend those enemies off by pushing blocks around. Extra points are awarded for collecting the items in the order in which they start flashing. Other levels restrict his movement, so he has to be bounced off blocks and walls. Time limits are generous. The game developed out of the earlier Kwik Snax and, unlike that game, includes a two-player mode.

t_a3b21b3613aa.overview:
Venturing into the fantasy world of McDonaldland, two children named Mack and Mick embark on a quest to recover Ronald McDonald's magical bag after the Hamburglar steals it. Players select either Mick or Mack, who share identical abilities, to navigate through six lands. Supporting an alternating two-player mode, the characters can walk, duck, jump, and collect blocks to throw at enemies encountered throughout their adventure.

Advancing through each world involves visiting local characters and gathering required puzzle cards rather than simply reaching stage exits. Stages incorporate items such as Golden Arches, which open a bonus level when enough are collected, and extra-life icons. Traversing the levels involves riding or carrying a boat, unzipping pathways to warp across the stage, and activating a spin device that inverts gravity to flip the character upside down.

t_a3d124b9bd03.overview: Drawn from Yudetamago's manga and anime series, Muscle Tag Match stages tag-team wrestling bouts between eight playable characters, each with his own special move. Standing in the team's own corner and pressing the A button tags in the partner, though another tag is not possible for a while afterward. The A button jumps and B punches, and the move set includes drop kicks, shoves into the ropes, flying body attacks, lariats and back drops. During a match a trainer occasionally appears at the edge of the ring and throws in an energy ball; grabbing it makes the character flash, restoring health, raising speed and enabling the special move. Beating an opponent in two of three rounds clears the stage. One mode pits the player against a computer opponent, and a versus mode lets two players fight each other.

t_a45208d38a44.overview: Continuing the card system of Dragon Ball: Daimaou Fukkatsu, this RPG adapts the Saiyan saga together with the first Dragon Ball Z theatrical film. Five years after the 23rd Tenkaichi Budokai, Raditz kidnaps Gohan; later, stronger Saiyans approach Earth while Garlic Jr. and his demons pursue the Dragon Balls. Goku is unavailable at first and joins after training with King Kai, while Piccolo, Gohan, Krillin, Yamcha, Tien and Chiaotzu are playable. Cards drive both movement, by their stars, and combat, where stars set attack and kanji numbers set defense; matching a card's school to a fighter's raises attack, and special-move cards spend battle energy. Battles and training earn Battle Power, which raises levels. Progress is saved to flash ROM. Single player.

t_a484099c9d04.overview: Dooly the Little Dinosaur, a popular Korean animation mascot, stars in this 2D platformer developed by Daou Infosys and released exclusively in Korea in 1992. Daou Infosys had already brought the character to the MSX and the Sega Master System, and this cartridge was the studio's original game for Nintendo's 8-bit hardware. Stages mix platform traps with standard enemies. In the "Bravo Train" stage, Dooly works through a series of those traps and foes before doing battle with an obvious stand-in for Son Goku, who flies on Kinto'un. Another stage, "Heaven," includes an uncredited appearance by Nintendo's own Mario.

t_a4b4ada983c1.overview: Jinguji Saburo's second case moves the hard-boiled detective series from Tokyo to Yokohama and turns it into a pure command-selection adventure, dropping the earlier entry's field screens, time limits and game overs for wrong choices. Jinguji and his assistant Yoko are asked to find Eva Christina, a young woman working at the Yokohama consulate of the Republic of Baraka who has gone missing while engaged to a cargo-ship officer named Hinode. On the same day, another woman from the consulate was found drowned, and a police detective suspects she was tied to a smuggling ring. Commands cover going to locations, asking questions, examining people and objects, showing evidence, calling contacts and smoking a cigarette, which sometimes sparks an idea. Background music changes as the investigation advances, and passwords are used to continue.

t_a4cc280185bd.overview:
Skateboarders ride across five distinct competitive events, aiming to accumulate points or defeat opponents. The lineup features two downhill courses: a standard race and the downhill jam, which navigates town alleyways. Half-pipe challenges include freestyle, where players perform stunts to gather points, and the high jump, which focuses on attaining maximum vertical height.

Participants can also engage in the joust, an event in a drained swimming pool where the skater holding a stick tries to whack the defending opponent, with the two trading roles as they ride. Contests can be tackled alone or head-to-head against another participant, with support for up to eight players taking turns sequentially across the roster of events.

t_a4e4e5e9baf9.overview: Two kids, Mick and Mack, are hanging out at McDonald's reading a comic book when Ronald McDonald appears and sends them inside it. Whichever kid is chosen, the play is the same: an action platformer through enemy-crammed stages, armed with a water gun that fires an arc of orange goo. Each level is a large map to scour for miniature golden arches, and once at least thirty have been found, Ronald appears at the other end of the map to close out the stage. The journey begins in a slime world scattered with the bones of dead creatures, and the game carries a strong environmentalist message in which pollution is bad and recycling is good. This unreleased NES build has somewhat fewer enemies than other versions, with foes taking more hits to defeat, and uses a bright orange background throughout.

t_a4f5ed666e9e.overview:
Chef Peter Pepper must construct giant hamburgers across mazes composed of platforms and ladders while evading hostile food items. To prepare each sandwich, Peter walks across various oversized ingredients, including buns, meat patties, tomatoes, lettuce, and cheese. Walking across these items forces them to drop down onto lower levels and eventually assemble on waiting plates below. A stage concludes successfully once every hamburger on the board has been assembled, and the six screens grow progressively tougher.

The Food Foes, Mr. Hot Dog, Mr. Pickle and Mr. Egg, continuously hunt Peter throughout the maze and speed up if a stage takes too long. Contact with an active adversary costs a life. To defend himself, Peter can shake a limited supply of pepper at nearby foes to briefly immobilize them. Enemies may also be crushed under falling ingredients or carried downward atop dropping burger components. Bonus food items grant extra points alongside additional pepper shots. One or two players can play.

t_a536db4d8d9e.overview: Played from a top-down view of each hole, Data East's golf game asks for the ball to be holed in as few strokes as possible. For every shot the player sets the direction, chooses a club, and stops a rising and falling power meter; moving the clubface while the meter runs adds a hook or a slice, useful for curving shots around trees. Four caddies on the course offer advice. A ball hit out of bounds or into a water hazard costs a penalty stroke, while the rough and bunkers carry no penalty but shorten the distance a club can reach. Three modes are available: a stroke game over 18 holes, a tournament game, and a match game in which two players compete hole by hole. The stroke and tournament games can be played by one or two players.

t_a57957bd3e67.overview: The Famicom baseball series from Namco continues with this edition for one or two players. Fourteen teams are available: twelve modeled on Japanese professional clubs, plus the Major Leaguers and the Namco Stars, an all-star squad of Namco characters, and the four stadiums of the previous entry return unchanged. A new player edit feature creates eight batters and four pitchers to replace existing players, with no cap on total ability, and password continues come back. The league is renamed the Famista League. Beating the other thirteen teams unlocks two computer-only teams: the Pro Stars, made of former Japanese professionals under pseudonyms, and the Old Dreams, whose players carry names suggesting baseball manga characters and whose starting pitcher throws a vanishing pitch.

t_a59281b632e8.overview: International teams compete for the World Cup in this side-view soccer game. Before kickoff, players select one of eight national sides: Japan, Germany, Brazil, France, South Korea, England, Argentina, or the USA. During matches the field scrolls horizontally across the screen to follow the action, and the chosen team must keep winning to take the trophy. A single player can take on computer-controlled opponents, while two players can compete head to head. Although the cartridge was sold only in Japan, most of its menu options are written in English.

t_a5c926c80c9a.overview: Combat flying takes center stage, with the famous test pilot Chuck Yeager lending his name and voice to the action. Pilots choose between two training options and two gameplay options, one of them a two-player game in which the first player flies the jet while the second is in charge of the artillery. Four weapons are available, among them remote missiles that the player steers to seek out long-range targets, and the enemy forces include planes, helicopters and tanks. The view relies on pseudo-3D effects, and digitized voice clips of Yeager play during missions, with his disembodied head appearing on screen each time he delivers another one-liner.

t_a666471a028f.overview: An action-adventure from Sunsoft, it sends Bop-Louie through an interconnected world in the vein of Metroid to find his friends Freeon-Leon, Shades and Gil, who fell into a crater and suffer from amnesia. Each friend is first fought as a boss and then becomes playable, bringing a unique skill for reaching previously inaccessible areas: swimming and walking on slippery ice, jumping high, or diving underwater. Once all four are together, the group must collect three keys by defeating guardians to open a gate and face Unyohn. Defeated enemies turn into balloons called Popoons that can be thrown at other foes, health grows through life containers, and a password system preserves items and characters. This build is a prototype from the planned North American release, which was cancelled before the game reached stores there.

t_a6a5bf5060cf.overview: Played on the 12-key B side of the Family Trainer mat, Meiro Daisakusen is a maze exploration game for one player. A boy in a blue cap, walking across a grassland, hears a legend from a fortune-teller: a blue-crowned hero will bring back an ancient treasure that has slept for 3,000 years in a vast underground labyrinth. The boy has no way to attack, so progress depends on dodging monsters and avoiding traps such as pitfalls while exploring 28 stages spread over five floors. Once every area has been explored, a password entered at a stone monument leads to the ending. A separate five-minute maze mode asks the player to escape a randomly selected maze before time runs out.

t_a6f5a67fa06a.overview:
Six acts containing twenty side-scrolling levels structure the adventure. Players direct the ninja Ryu Hayabusa on a journey to America to avenge his murdered father and stop an antagonist calling himself Jaquio from taking over the world. Ryu can run, crouch, jump, climb ladders, and spring off walls to ascend vertical spaces, though he cannot attack while on ladders. Animated cinematic cutscenes present the narrative between areas.

Ryu primarily strikes foes using his Dragon Sword katana. Found inside street lights, lamps and other holders along the way, collectible items provide bonus points, health restoration, extra lives, five-second enemy freezes, temporary invincibility, or spiritual strength. Gathering spiritual strength fuels secondary weapons such as throwing stars, returning windmill stars, the fire wheel technique, and mid-air jump slashes. Ryu loses a life if his physical health depletes or the timer expires. Each act concludes with a boss battle.

t_a7069b85a50d.overview: Four games fill the first volume of the Super Cartridge series from Thin Chen Enterprise, released under the Sachen name. Bingo 75, credited on its title screen as 75 Bingo, and Lucky Bingo, credited as Lucky 777, are both slot-machine simulators, and Bingo 75 contains nudity. Honey Peach is a strip rock-paper-scissors contest: two hands rapidly open and close on screen, and a button press stops the player's hand on rock, paper or scissors. Each win removes a layer of an opponent's outfit, and a password earned after a match lets play start again at a chosen opponent. Chess Academy completes the set.

t_a715d24f87e4.overview: Taking its name from a holy book of Taoism, this role-playing game from Tamtex unfolds in a setting of Eastern mysticism populated by monks and creatures from Chinese and Japanese folklore. A monk and his partner, Raichi, set out to restore the hearts of three kings that have been tainted by a great evil, a villain who seeks four swords that would let him take over the world. Play follows the traditional Japanese role-playing pattern, with turn-based combat and equipment management in a composition very similar to early Dragon Quest titles. The adventure is divided into four chapters, and the party changes from chapter to chapter as various members join or leave over the course of the story. Irem published the game.

t_a752c91f44fd.overview: Hummer Team's Famicom version of SNK's The King of Fighters '96, released by Ka Sheng in 1998, trims the roster to seven characters. Built on the base of Street Fighter Zero 2 '97, it keeps the team mode of the King of Fighters series and adds a difficulty setting, but has no POW bar, so fights play more like Street Fighter II. Stages cycle in a preset order, and the last opponent is Goenitz, whose defeat leads to an English ending scene. The intro is copied accurately from the original game apart from a couple of typos, while much of the music bears little resemblance to the original soundtrack, drawing instead on covers of Jim Croce songs and tracks from The King of Fighters '98.

t_a7872bd5f30c.overview: Real team and player names from Nippon Professional Baseball appear in this Famista entry from Namco, licensed and based on data from the 1992 season. Along with the real names comes the designated hitter rule, used when a Pacific League team bats second. The Major Leaguers are replaced by All America, a team of foreign players active on Japanese clubs, and the All-Star mode uses ready-made Central and Pacific all-star teams drawn from the 1992 All-Star Game. Game results are reported in a sports newspaper. Two extra modes sit outside the main game: a baseball quiz that asks players to identify someone from his uniform number and statistics, and a baseball card viewer with illustrations and player data. New stadiums are based on Meiji Jingu Stadium, Koshien Stadium and Izumo Dome. One or two players can play.

t_a7d822981c38.overview: An alien force called the Ginga Gundan, led by General Shubaban, captures the capital Yokan, and Jack and Ryu set out on a journey to protect the peace of their world in this action role-playing game. Fights unfold in side-scrolling battles whose style borrows from the Kunio-kun series: characters cannot face up or down and can only attack to the left and right. A fighter can seize an enemy's weapon and use it against its owner, ninjutsu is available, and enemy encounters come frequently. Jack is the main character, and Ryu joins in simultaneous two-player play. Culture Brain developed and published the game as the third entry in the Super Chinese series.

t_a85e1542ce88.overview: A chess-like board strategy game mixed with magic battle confrontations, played with an army of fantasy creatures on a small chess board. The goal is to topple the opposing king. Each side commands a small army with units such as an orcman, a karate man and a warrior. When two pieces meet on the same square, the clash moves to a special battle screen built around a playing-card roulette, and the cards each unit receives determine the damage it does to its opponent. Units differ in health points and in their cards; some have a greater propensity than others for drawing the joker, which kills instantly.

t_a860fb4a6531.overview: After a nuclear war, the world lies under the rule of an evil army led by the Sword King, Achilles, and the hero Ryu, a master of every martial art, sets out to bring back peace. In Capcom's side-scrolling action game, one button swings a sword and the other holds a shield that blocks thrown knives and arrows. Blocking a magic ball knocks both away, leaving Ryu to fight barehanded with punches and kicks until they can be recovered; winged hearts restore health. Unlike the arcade original, the Famicom version ends after six stages with no second loop, and it adds hidden rooms, extra power-ups, new enemies and a new boss, King Shriek, armed with an iron ball on a long chain. A versus mode pits two players against each other in a first-to-three-rounds match, the second player controlling the boss Trojan.

t_a8a878f6e544.overview: Four games share this 4-in-1 cartridge, sold in Australia by Home Entertainment Suppliers as the Fun Blaster Pak: Pipemania, Twin Eagle, Joyvan Kid and Little Red Hood, all originally Taiwanese releases by Joy Van and Sachen. Pipemania is Sachen's Pipe V, a puzzle game largely inspired by Pipe Dream. Twin Eagle is a horizontal shooter in which the player's plane attacks a terrorist organization stationed in the south Pacific. Joyvan Kid, also known as Metal Fighter, is a horizontal shoot-em-up with slight platforming elements. In Little Red Hood, loosely based on the Little Red Riding Hood tale, Red Hood clears levels by going down staircases to find keys and eating fruit to make the exit appear.

t_a8c77311dc43.overview:
Seven levels structure this beat 'em up crossover, which sends the heroes to the giant spaceship Colossus to thwart an alliance between the Dark Queen and the Shadow Boss. Players choose from five characters, consisting of martial artists Billy and Jimmy Lee alongside humanoid amphibians Zitz, Pimple, and Rash. Progression shifts across environments, beginning on the exterior of the spacecraft, moving through interior corridors and the bowels of the ship, and transitioning to a space craft shooting sequence and a race along a missile headed for Earth before concluding with boss confrontations.

Two buttons control attacks and jumping. Combat maneuvers include specialized strikes, slams, throws, attacks from hanging ropes or ledges, and moves executed while riding speeder bikes. Play options provide single-player action along with two-player setups, offering settings with or without friendly fire. Each hero has a limited number of lives, and bonus pods can hold extra lives, energy, or weapons.

t_a90a11440c29.overview:
Rescuing a required number of creatures within a time limit is the primary goal across each stage. The creatures enter from overhead trapdoors and march continuously forward, turning around only when blocked or falling from ledges. Hazardous terrain threatens their path, including steep drops, blocking walls, and assorted traps. To shepherd the group safely to the exit, the player assigns specialized roles to select individuals.

Eight skills alter creature behavior or reshape the environment. Builders construct staircases, while Bashers, Miners, and Diggers tunnel through terrain at different angles. Climbers scale walls, Floaters descend safely from great heights, and Blockers halt the line of walkers. Bombers detonate after a countdown from five, carving away surroundings. The player can accelerate the entrance rate, pause the action, or trigger an explosion that eliminates all remaining creatures.

t_a90c026cc4f5.overview: NTDEC's vertical shooter has no plot at all: a single space ship faces a stream of incoming alien-shaped foes trying to take it down. Enemies and projectiles can spawn from any edge of the screen, the bottom included, and enemy shots are small and slow, flying in straight trajectories.
