Scrolling runs at a fixed speed, and play is punishing. The ending credits list the program by Kriss, graphics by Nelson and music by Martino.

t_a91956eaa2f5.overview: Based on the manga and anime about Musashi, the son of two kendo champions who strives to become as great at kendo as his parents, this action game offers two modes. In the single-player mode Musashi is in the middle of his training, running through obstacle courses and collecting swords and other items while his pet Akita runs the course behind him; he must not fall too far behind the dog. After three courses he enters a kendo tournament and must defeat five competitors, and enough collected swords give access to special strikes. Winning restarts the game at a higher difficulty, and a second championship ends it. In the two-player mode each player secretly selects five competitors from a roster, then the pairs square off in kendo matches, with three or more victories deciding the winner.

t_a96b0df96285.overview:
Piloting advanced rescue craft, the player flies continuously forward while adjusting speed and shooting through hostile forces to foil the global scheme of an alien mastermind named Hood. Missions are selected from a world map marked by Doctor Brain, where Hood prepares a power source over a sixty-day deadline. A ship damaged in an attack can take three days to repair, reducing the available campaign time. An onscreen information bar tracks the craft's life points as well as the orbital device configurations in use and available.

Destroying enemy targets produces collectible energy items. These pick-ups include life points, energy points that double or triple primary firepower, and orbital devices that deploy auxiliary firing units alongside the craft. Five firing configurations exist for these orbital units: forward, backward, sideways, diagonally forward, or in a circle around the ship. Two are available from the start, and the other three must be captured. Progress can be resumed using passwords provided during play.

t_a988505bf9b6.overview:
Double Dragon is an action fighting game where players battle through the slums, factories and wooded outskirts of a city. Controlling martial artist Billy Lee, the player seeks to rescue his kidnapped girlfriend Marian from the Black Warriors gang and its mysterious Shadow Boss. Combat relies on punches, kicks, and advanced martial arts maneuvers, with the ability to level up to gain additional fighting techniques. Players can also pick up weapons, which include bats, whips, knives, and dynamite, or throw objects such as rocks, boxes, and oil drums.

Progressing through four side-scrolling stages requires clearing waves of thugs, navigating hazards like pits, and defeating bosses such as Abobo before time runs out. In the two-player mode, players challenge each other head to head rather than fighting through the stages together.

t_a9a20f3edf91.overview: Adapted from Mark Twain's novel, this role-playing game is set in 1855 in the town of St. Petersburg, Missouri, on the Mississippi River. Tom Sawyer dreams that a pirate treasure lies buried in a southern location, and after Aunt Polly wakes him the next morning he sets out to find it. Companions such as Huck, his best friend, and Jim, a servant of his household, can join him, while a ruthless outlaw hunts for the same treasure. A party of up to four characters can be formed, and battles show the party from behind with enemies in the background. No experience points or levels exist; health, power and speed improve gradually through battles. Characters can fight barehanded, many collectible items can be found, and key cards and black magic also appear. One enemy even triggers a reset that returns play to the title screen.

t_a9b87cfd67cf.overview: Snowboarding down three mountains is the challenge in this single-player sports game, released in Europe under a new name but known elsewhere as Heavy Shreddin'. Each mountain has three degrees of difficulty, and the terrain grows harder to navigate on the way down. Five events make up 18 levels in total: downhill runs where the rider must avoid objects and falls, slalom courses that require passing through the flags, a points-driven half-pipe, mogul runs that demand tricks to jump over the bumps, and a final backwoods event mixing speed, tricks and survival. On the half-pipe the rider can jump or pull off one of four tricks mapped to the d-pad. The player starts with four lives, loses one when falling or running out of time, and earns a bonus life for each completed trail.

t_aa1c99ee2f3a.overview: A rising young jazz cat in New York City must save his girlfriend after a local crime boss kidnaps her in this action game, released outside Japan as Rockin' Kats. The hero is armed with a punch gun that he can launch at the various thugs or hook onto objects and swing from, and mastering it is critical to getting through. The levels are presented as channels on a television set. The first four stages can be played in any order, and the fifth and final channel becomes available only after the other four have been beaten.

t_aa21f080682a.overview: Hummer Team's first game, published by Supertone Electronics in 1992, is a Chinese-language role-playing game about Jing Ke, the historical figure who attempted to assassinate Qin Shi Huang. Play begins as Crown Prince Dan of the State of Yan, a hostage held by Qin Shi Huang, who must obtain a placenta and learn to imitate a rooster's crow to escape the closed town. Control then passes to Minister Ju Wu, Tian Guang and finally Jing Ke, whose preparations include finding Huan Yi, a poison-tipped dagger and Qin Wuyang. Menus work much like the Dragon Quest games, and martial arts replace magic in turn-based battles. Only one party member and one random foe act each round, and only attacking or fleeing uses up a turn. Qin Shi Huang is the only boss, and unlike history, the assassination can succeed.

t_abd97c746540.overview:
Ending the match with the majority of the board displaying their chosen color is the primary goal for players. Based on the strategy board game, matches take place on an eight-by-eight grid using double-sided chips that feature black on one face and white on the other. Participants select which color they wish to control, taking turns placing pieces onto the board. By trapping an opponent's discs between two pieces of their own color, players flip those sandwiched counters to match their own side.

Matches can be contested by a single participant competing against an artificial opponent, or by two human players facing each other. When challenging the computer, four skill levels are available. In addition, matches can incorporate time limits, giving each player a total of twenty, thirty, or forty minutes for all of their moves.

t_ac22b6d292f5.overview: Adapted from a manga about a high school cheering squad, this release plays as a stage-clear simulation RPG. Each turn, the player moves the squad's six members across a map, and moving a member onto one of the enemy characters placed there starts a one-on-one brawl. Commands in these fights are on a timer: an action has to be chosen before the approaching opponent's punch reaches the member's face portrait. If the whole squad is wiped out, play returns to the beginning of the stage, and continues are unlimited. In the original manga, a freshman raised in a household full of women joins his school's cheering squad to toughen himself up, only to find it led by a carefree crowd.

t_ac263aab0c3e.overview: Set one hundred years after the original Dragon Quest, the story opens with the wizard Hargon attacking Moonbrooke Castle in a bid to summon a demon. When a wounded soldier brings word of the assault to the king of Midenhall, the king sends his son, the Prince of Midenhall, to stop Hargon. The adventure begins with a single hero, and further companions join over the course of the journey, making it the first entry in the series in which the player controls several characters. Monsters appear at random during exploration, switching the game into a battle mode where groups of enemies are fought and orders are issued to each character. Defeating monsters raises experience levels, and growing stronger is necessary to progress.

t_ac41423b4f65.overview: Based on the 1987 arcade game of the same hero, this side-scrolling action game asks the player to reach the end of each action scene using sound wave attacks and jumping. Wagyan's sound waves cannot destroy enemies; instead they stun them temporarily, and the player can stand on top of a stunned foe. Collecting a Wagyanizer makes the sound effects bigger with each increment, so enemies stay stunned longer, and after four of them Wagyan becomes invincible for a limited period, gaining speed and defeating enemies on contact. There is no energy gauge: touching an enemy or falling into a trap costs a life. At the end of some stages, rather than fighting, the player is challenged to a battle-of-wits mini-game such as shiritori or a memory match and must outscore the opponent.

t_ac67a6bb6658.overview:
Prince of Persia presents platforming gameplay set in Persia. A single player guides an unnamed protagonist out of the Sultan's dungeons and through the palace to defeat the Grand Vizier Jaffar and reach an imprisoned princess before sixty minutes elapse. Progress requires stepping on pressure plates that raise gates, leaping over deep pits, and avoiding lethal spike traps and slicers. Two-story falls cause damage, and dying returns the protagonist to the start of the current level while the timer continues running.

Duels against enemy guards require a sword acquired during the escape. The protagonist advances, retreats, slashes, and parries attacks, and a guard is defeated by draining all of his health indicators. Three initial health units can be depleted by combat or hazards. Potions found throughout the areas heal injuries, raise maximum health capacity, slow the protagonist's falls, or inflict poison.
t_ac67a6bb6658.official: Relive this classic game that is often heralded as a pioneer of the platforming genre. This re-release is faithful to the original game, complete with the dashing acrobatics of the Prince that made the original famous. Traverse sprawling levels, dodge deadly traps like spikes and guillotines, clash swords with palace guards and face the evil Grand Vizier in your bid to rescue the princess. But be quick: you only have two hours!

t_ac79106dadc0.overview: Four Codemasters games share this cartridge, the edition for Europe of the compilation sold in North America as Quattro Adventure. In Linus Spacehead, an alien from the planet Linoleum has crash landed on Earth and must gather up all of his scattered radio parts in order to radio home for help. Super Robin Hood has Robin Hood fight his way through Nottingham Castle while avoiding a multitude of traps to rescue Maid Marian. In Boomerang Kid, the title hero must retrieve all of his boomerangs, which lie scattered throughout the outback. Treasure Island Dizzy leaves Dizzy stranded on an island, where he must figure out how to get home. All four are platform action games.

t_ac82d218d9e7.overview: A horizontal shoot-'em-up released by NTDEC in 1992, Go! Benny! puts the player in control of a bee. On the cover art the hero closely resembles Maya the Honey Bee, while in the game itself it looks like a plain bee. Enemies attack both in the air and on the ground, and pressing B fires a stinger straight ahead. Bonuses, including power-ups and extra lives, are hidden under pieces of wax floating in mid-air, and a boss waits at the end of each level.

t_ac9751237881.overview:
Bugs Bunny faces envious friends who try to stall his journey toward his 50th birthday party. Taking control of Bugs in this side-scrolling platformer, players advance through levels to reach the celebration. Bugs wields a hammer that can break blocks and eliminate the contraptions the other Looney Tune characters have unleashed, and striking one end of a seesaw launches him higher than a normal jump. Boulder wells lead to secret passageways. While traversing stages, he can pick up carrots and collect hearts left behind by Fireball contraptions to restore health.

Many levels culminate in encounters against familiar cartoon adversaries. Completing a level grants access to a Bonus Bingo round, where more collected carrots mean more chances to win additional lives.

t_acc2cde1b98c.overview: Jack the duck has one job in this puzzle-platformer from Bit Corporation: safeguard a giant egg on its way to the bottom of each stage. The egg is guided downward through 20 levels, and the duck clears or reshapes its path by moving or destroying blocks. Three lives are available, and one is lost whenever the egg touches an enemy or breaks after falling from too high, so every drop has to be planned. The concept is a clone of Sega's Doki Doki Penguin Land, a 1985 game for the SG-1000 and MSX. Originally released in Taiwan in 1987, the game was published in Australia by HES.

t_acd2e5976811.overview:
Players control a young boy named Nemo as he journeys through two-dimensional, side-scrolling levels set within his surreal dreams. Moving across environments from left to right as well as vertically, the player searches for keys scattered across each area. These keys unlock the door at the exit, allowing Nemo to progress toward rescuing the good King of Slumberland from the wicked King of Nightmares.

While exploring, Nemo can feed candy to specific animals like frogs, gorillas, or moles to ride them and gain their special skills. Certain animal abilities are required to clear stages and bypass obstacles amidst constantly appearing enemies. Additionally, several creatures feature lifebars that differ from Nemo's, occasionally granting extra health to help endure hazards.

t_ad02f09b49de.overview: Culture and technology are the central theme of this fourth entry in Koei's historical strategy series, which again spans all of Japan. Beyond developing domains and raising armies, a daimyo builds up a culture rating that affects income, and tea gatherings can be held once tea utensils have been purchased. Raising the technology rating unlocks gold mining, the manufacture of firearms and the construction of armored warships. Fighting is divided into field battles and castle sieges, with the daimyo under attack choosing the battlefield, and naval battles appear for the first time in the series. Scenarios begin in 1555 and 1571, while a hidden 1582 scenario appears only when certain conditions are met. Several players can compete in one game.

t_ad196e3c7023.overview: Designed for Famiclone-based educational computers, this Waixing cartridge collects three programs. Middle School English Computer Bank presents a series of English problems, such as filling in the blank word or phrase in a passage and selecting which word has a different pronunciation. Whiz Kid Magic Wand adapts matchstick puzzles: following an explanation at the top of the screen, the player must rearrange sticks into a certain position, represented by Pac-Man leaning on a tree and using his glove as the cursor while two squirrels dance to the music. Music Appreciation is a compilation of ten songs whose volume and tone can be adjusted, shown with a large graphic of a cat playing drums. The cartridge is the follow-up to Primary School Mathematics CAI.

t_ad34093bd024.overview: In the year 2081, Earth has been overrun by hostile monsters commanded by a mysterious entity called the Increaser. The warrior Dan takes his time machine back to 1999 to stop the invasion before it can devastate humanity. This action-adventure places its emphasis on exploration: the five levels have no fixed linear route, hold deadly traps and surprises, and end with boss battles. Defeating enemies earns energy points that can be spent on power-ups, and while Dan starts with a basic sword, other weapons can be found or bought. A strict time limit shapes each boss encounter, since clearing a level quickly means facing a weaker form of its boss, while taking longer brings a more powerful one.

t_ad7bf9159e48.overview: Adapted by Visco from the Rally Bike arcade game, this top-down motorcycle road racer pits the rider against computer-controlled rivals in races across locations in the United States. A race is won by crossing the finish line and passing a set number of rival racers. Obstacles are scattered along the road, and any accident causes a great reduction of fuel, so careful steering keeps the bike running. During races a helicopter drops items onto the road, ranging from turbo boosts to helper bikers that guard against crashing into rivals. After each completed race a shop offers new parts to improve the bike, a feature introduced for this home version, whose stages and backgrounds differ from the arcade original.

t_ada1fa7b4b07.overview: Developed by Dragon Co., Wait and See! is a platform game that casts the player as the Hare, who is being pursued by the Wolf; the Wolf himself shows up only in short scenes in between the levels. Along the way the Hare faces enemies such as spear mice, while the second stage adds hippos and alligators. Spinning is a key move, and the spin can be chained in mid-air to hover forward. There are no pickups anywhere, so damage has to be avoided without help from items. Bugs Bunny is featured on the title screen, even though there are no references to Looney Tunes in the rest of the game.

t_adacfd521379.overview: Waixing's Famicom adaptation of the strategy game Teitoku no Ketsudan, known overseas as P.T.O.: Pacific Theater of Operations, recasts the Pacific war as a conflict between two fictional forces. Rather than choosing Japan or the USA as in the original, the player commands either the La Meng army or the Na Sha army, and the generals' statistics are fixed instead of randomized. Only four of the original scenarios remain, all moved into the future: The Night Before the Sea Battle and The Battle of God of War in 2041, The Battle of the Pacific in 2042, and The Final Duel in 2045. All text is in Chinese, and the port has two different endings.

t_ae48f5b1c71f.overview: Based on the 1990/91 anime Karakuri Kengō Den Musashi Lord, this role-playing game is set in a medieval Japanese world where humans and human-like robots live together. Play takes the form of a bird's-eye-view action game in the Zelda style, combined with many role-playing elements and level-up progression. The adventure is divided into four chapters plus a bonus one, each with a different main character, and the player chooses at the beginning which one to play. These separate scenarios with different characters converge into a single story. In the anime, the robot hero Musashi sets out to become a top martial artist.

t_ae902385bf6a.overview: Drawn from the opening arcs of the SD Gundam Gaiden Carddass card saga, this fantasy role-playing game begins when the king of the Lacroa Kingdom, whose daughter Princess Fraw has been carried off by the Zeon tribe, summons Knight Gundam. The hero's foes include the demon king Satan Gundam, who changes into the Black Dragon for a rematch after his first defeat. Random encounters lead to command-based battles, and companions left at the training grounds sometimes rush in mid-battle and fight automatically. Spell names mostly come from weapons in the Gundam series. Cards bought from a white machine in shops can be collected, certain characters accept Carddass card battles, and monsters in combat use the same artwork as the cards. Life insurance keeps the party's money from being halved after a total wipeout, and saves use flash ROM.

t_af3986109935.overview: Two kinds of scenes alternate in this Z Gundam shooting game, in which the player pilots the Z Gundam against the forces of the Titans and Axis. In the first-person stages, seen from the cockpit, the player lines up the sights on enemy mobile suits moving across the screen and snipes them with the beam rifle. After enough time passes on the ground, or once particular prototype mobile suits appear or are destroyed, the Z Gundam leaves the atmosphere for a shooting stage set in space. Fortresses and battleships can appear there; a battleship must be hit several times to silence it before the Z Gundam storms inside. These side-view fortress stages lead through maze-like corridors, switching between mobile suit and waverider forms, to reach and destroy the core.

t_af43107d2fc7.overview: A death at a game developer sets off this command-selection mystery adventure. Young detective Akihito Kashihata receives a phone call from Inspector Nakamura: Masato Nishikawa, a programmer at the game software company Power Soft, has fallen to his death from a cliff at Jogasaki. The police first judge it a suicide, but Kashihata suspects murder, and the company president, Yutaka Tomino, asks him to investigate within three days as the case grows into a series of killings. The defining rule is a limit on actions: every command executed uses up three minutes of in-game time, each day's investigation ends at 18:00, and running past the three days or making a serious mistake ends the game. A single player takes part, and progress can be saved.

t_af645891fb21.overview: Drawn from the Choujin Sentai Jetman tokusatsu television series, this action game spans six stages, and the first five can be tackled in any order. Before each stage, the player chooses one of the team's five warriors to send in. A warrior who falls during a stage cannot be used again until that stage has been cleared, so each defeat narrows the remaining choices. Once all five opening stages are complete, the final stage begins, ending in a showdown with a monstrous beast; none of the enemy organization's executives appear.

t_af73b28c846e.overview: Covering the Frieza saga on Namek, this card-based RPG fields a party of Goku, Piccolo, Gohan, Krillin, Yamcha, Tien and Chiaotzu, while Vegeta appears only as a non-controllable character and Super Saiyan transformations do not appear. A card's stars decide how far the whole party moves, and on the overworld the group can walk, meeting fewer enemies but moving shorter distances, or fly, covering more ground with more encounters. In battle, stars set attack power and the kanji numeral sets defense, with attacks resolving in descending kanji order. Matching a card's school to a character's school enables combination and multi-target attacks, and special-move cards spend Battle Energy. Foes include Cui, Dodoria, Zarbon, the Ginyu Force and Frieza in four forms. Save points divide the adventure into 15 story segments. Single player.

t_af7c5c0c6a0a.overview:
Twin Cobra provides vertically scrolling shooter gameplay for a single player.

Taking control of an attack helicopter, the player navigates constantly moving environments to destroy military vehicles such as tanks, battleships, and artillery. Hostile forces fire projectiles, and being hit by enemy fire results in the loss of a life. The helicopter attacks using standard shots alongside destructive bombs. Destroying transportation helicopters, bombers, or barges sometimes releases colored saucers that switch between four distinct weapon types. Other items scattered throughout the areas provide extra bombs, firepower boosts, score stars, and extra lives.

t_afb9c3d2c0b9.overview: Developed by Mars Production and published by Waixing, this pirate role-playing game borrows its name from the Dragon Quest series and runs on an engine Waixing built for it, later reused for other pirate RPGs. Battles are heavily simplified: only one character fights, against a single enemy at a time, and the D-pad picks an action from attack, run, inventory or the option screen. The engine's most distinctive rule ties attack strength to health, so the lower a character's health falls, the less damage its attacks cause. This "less health, less damage" mechanic has been criticized for making fights far too difficult once health runs low.

t_b0113078e4a7.overview: Modeled on Donkey Kong Country, Panda Baby is a side-scrolling platformer whose panda hero can crawl, jump with the B button and roll into enemies with the A button. Unlike its model, he has no partner, cannot run and loses a life from a single hit. Bamboo takes the place of bananas and awards points. Three levels are playable: two jungle levels, the second of which requires climbing vines, and an underwater level in which the panda swims in whichever direction is held. Each jungle level has a boss to defeat before the exit, first a triceratops and then a man with a club, both beaten by stomping on them or rolling into them. The game is unfinished: the underwater level cannot be completed, and a cave level and a mine cart level exist in the data but cannot be reached normally.

t_b01a5782aac0.overview: Having driven the monsters out of the castle and recovered its treasure in the previous adventure, Ninja-kun follows the orders of his catfish master and storms the monsters' home base to defeat their leader, Ashura. This sequel moves beyond its predecessor's purely vertical stages: fields vary from stages with no tiers at all to stages with assorted terrain, stages with giant bosses and vertical-scrolling stages that open with strong enemies. New weapons are added as certain stages are cleared and switched by pressing up. Ninja-kun can now crouch to drop to lower levels, scale and wall-jump up walls, and roll to avoid dying after a long fall, and some walls block his way until he climbs them.

t_b0639f76b01c.overview: Raising a dragon sits at the heart of Samsara Naga, a role-playing game set in the fantasy-filled lands of India during the Vedic age. The young hero, who can be a boy or a girl, aspires to become a Dragoon and restore lost honor, and raises a newly hatched dragon along the way. The dragon grows and gains levels by eating monsters it has defeated in battle, while the protagonist never levels up at all: base statistics stay fixed, and the hero becomes stronger only through better equipment. Beyond the main journey, the world holds field map events, hidden landmarks, a few side quests and mini-games.

t_b0770cad762e.overview:
Hostile aliens have subdued Earth and placed humanity under the dominion of Babylon, a computer determined to eradicate the human race. To oppose these invaders, defenders construct the transformable machine MagMax and send a pilot into combat. MagMax travels through forests, deserts, seas, and automated cities across a horizontally scrolling field, using warp halls to shift between the surface and underground.

Navigating in eight directions, MagMax uses a beam gun to eliminate opposing machines and obstacles. Gathering additional body parts transforms the machine into a complete robot. Each attached part increases the number of projectiles MagMax can fire and absorbs damage from collisions, causing the added piece to separate and explode rather than ending the turn immediately. Missions culminate in confrontations with Babylon.

t_b0b0283c523e.overview: Rather than taking the role of a real driver, the player competes under their own identity against up to 12 rival drivers, and the choice of rivals changes the difficulty. Four machines are available, and their color schemes can be customized to a degree. A free run mode allows practice on any circuit, while the grand prix mode casts the player as a rookie driver aiming for the title across all 16 F1 races. Progress continues by password, and data can also be held in the console's memory as long as the power stays on. Racing is for a single player.

t_b0bf58e51bf7.overview:
Based on the film Rambo: First Blood Part II, the game begins at a prison where Colonel Trautman offers Rambo the opportunity to undertake a mission. Players must agree to this assignment to proceed through the camp, speaking with individuals until receiving full mission details from Trautman. Following these discussions, Rambo drops into a forest environment to start his objective.

While exploring the wilderness, the player contends with creatures such as spiders before confronting larger bosses, including giant arachnids and helicopters. Progressing further allows Rambo to gather an arsenal of weapons to combat hostile soldiers. The experience meter tracks advancement throughout the adventure, leading up to a finale back at the base where the player casts a massive kanji character at Murdock, transforming him into a frog.

t_b0df6788c5e8.overview: Mahjong here is a two-player variant: the human player competes against a single computer opponent in a series of one-on-one games instead of sitting at a four-player table. The title translates as Chinese Mahjong Story: East Wind. Play is set up as a tournament, and the player has to win several games in a row against the computer to be crowned the victor.

t_b0ec4db70ebb.overview: A motorcycle racer rides from Los Angeles to New York City across five stages that alternate between tarmac roads and unsealed dirt roads. Overtaking cars raises the rider's rank, while hitting cars, road edges, vegetation or rocks, or missing a bridge on a dirt stage, stops the bike and costs fuel. Fuel is the central resource: running out ends the game, and more can be picked up by running over gas can icons. Reaching each city awards bonus points and fuel based on the rank achieved, and wheelies and bridge jumps add to the score. After New York the run starts over from the first stage with the score kept, at a higher difficulty and on a faster motorcycle.

t_b0f3b2644c87.overview: Ported from the SNES fighting game of the same name, this unlicensed Famicom version was made by Hummer Team and runs on the Street Fighter II engine used by many pirated fighting games on the system. The story was completely removed, but Arcade, Versus and CPU vs CPU modes are present. Characters are fought in a random order and always on certain stages, many of which use multi-layered scrolling. Graphics and music are taken from the original game and simplified, with some characters sharing stages. Unlike most Hummer Team releases, all of the text is in Japanese, and the ending is taken from the original game without the credits.

t_b138cad681f3.overview: Super-deformed robot anime and tokusatsu characters meet in the sumo ring in this crossover sports game, the first entry in the Compati Hero series. Wrestlers belong to stables: the M78 stable of Ultra series heroes and monsters, the Rider stable of Kamen Rider heroes and villains, the MS stable of Gundam mobile suits, the Sentai stable of giant robots and villains, and an original stable. Each wrestler has a red gauge that drains when hit by techniques, sending the loser flying out of the ring once it is empty, and a blue gauge that enables the wrestler's specialty technique. Individual mode begins at the twelfth maegashira rank, with eight or more wins in a fifteen-day tournament earning promotion. Team mode allows two-player versus matches, and a continue code shown on screen replaces saving.

t_b1c5a0a325e1.overview: Adapted from a Japanese television quiz championship, the Family Computer release from Yonezawa pits contestants against one another in buzzer quiz rounds that build toward a final showdown with the reigning quiz king. The cartridge came bundled with a multiplayer adapter and six buzzer buttons, allowing up to six people to compete at the same time; the adapter was also sold separately. In single-player matches, computer opponents frequently buzz in and answer before the full question text has finished appearing, which makes solo play a demanding test of speed as well as knowledge.

t_b1d8ffc3ac26.overview: The sequel to Saint Seiya: Ougon Densetsu takes up the battle through the Sanctuary's twelve temples. Saori Kido, the goddess Athena, has been mortally wounded by a golden arrow, and the Bronze Saints must break through the temples guarded by the Gold Saints and then the Pope's chamber, thirteen stages in all. Unlike its predecessor, the action stages let the player control characters other than Seiya, including Shiryu, Hyoga and Shun, each with different abilities, while Ikki appears only in certain stages. Each character has Cosmo, Life and Seven Senses values, with Cosmo governing attack power and range. Seven Senses earned by defeating foot soldiers can be distributed to Cosmo and Life before each Gold Saint battle. Conversations during fights can bring recovery, weaken enemies or add powerful special techniques, and some stages can be cleared only with a particular character.

t_b1f04bd8d0ef.overview: Sixty years in the future, the world is virtually crime free thanks to the Clear System invented by Kane Nelson, until a secret organization called Romedrux sets out to prevent the system from ever existing by eliminating Kane or his ancestors. In Los Angeles in 1993, the student Dan Nelson comes under attack by Romedrux warriors, learns about his future son, and vows to protect his family past, present and future. The action spans five levels set at different points in time, including the Wild West of 1882 and a devastated 2052, and after the first level the stage order is randomized. Besides the default Laser, special weapons include the Digger for tunneling through ground, Earthquake and Flash attacks that wipe out regular enemies on screen, and a Stop Watch that freezes foes.

t_b208834551bf.overview: Set during the upheaval that ended the shogunate, this Famicom adventure with strategy elements has the player reshaping the political landscape of Japan. The first half is spent traveling between regions to recruit allies, negotiating with local leaders and samurai and sometimes fighting sword duels. In the second half the recruited forces march on Edo to confront the shogun, and play turns into turn-based tactical battles in the style of Nobunaga's Ambition. Dialogue choices, combat and historical decisions are combined, with real historical events built into the mechanics.

t_b28db4ae72e2.overview: Bullet-Proof Software rebuilt its computer role-playing game The Black Onyx for the Famicom as this expanded edition. Where the original limited combat to physical attacks with weapons, characters here can cast spells, and the game also adds more monsters and a larger dungeon to explore. The gameplay was completely redesigned around a new map, and the story and world differ greatly from the computer original. The graphics were enhanced beyond the computer versions, and the controls were simplified so the whole game can be played with a control pad. The adventure is for a single player.

t_b2ce598d6f29.overview:
David Crane's A Boy and His Blob - Trouble on Blobolonia offers puzzle-platform gameplay. Players guide a young protagonist partnering with an alien companion named Blobert to rescue Blobolonia from an evil emperor. The boy explores underground caverns beneath his city on Earth before journeying to Blobolonia. Progression requires avoiding falling rocks, stalagmites, stalactites, and indestructible Subway Serpents across interconnected screens. The boy can only walk left or right without jumping, and long falls or drowning cost a life.

Blobert follows the boy, altering forms when fed flavored jellybeans; shapes include a ladder, a bridge, and a trampoline, and each flavor's name hints at its shape. Whistling calls Blobert and turns him back into a blob. Subterranean regions contain diamonds and treasures that raise money to buy vitamins at a health food store. These vitamins fuel a VitaBlaster used on Blobolonia. Extra jellybeans and peppermints also rest across the terrain.

t_b2f66998bf85.overview: Based on the manga by Fujiko Fujio A, this side-scrolling action game sends the young ninja Kanzo Hattori running to the right across 16 areas, mainly through the woods, each to be finished within 180 seconds by reaching a goal marked with a torii gate. Besides throwing shuriken, Hattori can use ninja arts unlocked by collecting scrolls that appear when Mecha Ninja are defeated: running at double speed, jumping higher, crossing water, riding a cloud, freezing enemies and more, while Shinzo and Shishimaru can be called in to wipe out foes. Collecting 20 chikuwa turns Hattori golden for 30 seconds. His movement carries inertia and his jumps are low, and a difficulty level from 1 to 4 is chosen at the title screen; clearing area 16 starts the game over one level harder.

t_b31368ca9293.overview: Based on Hiroshi Motomiya's manga Tenchi wo Kurau, Capcom's role-playing game loosely follows the events of Romance of the Three Kingdoms. Liu Bei, Zhang Fei and Guan Yu form a small militia to defend their village from Yellow Turban rebels, followers of the sorcerer Zhang Jiao, and the campaign ends when China is united under the Shu Han banner. Most random battles are fought against generals roaming the land, and a defeated general may offer to join the party in exchange for a bribe of money or horses, giving 150 playable characters in all, with up to 70 in the party. Up to seven members are active: five fight, one stands by to replace fallen fighters, and one serves as tactician, providing magic-like effects. An "All-Out" option hands a battle over to the computer.

t_b34fdeee2e3d.overview: Ashtar, the evil lord of the Realm of Darkness who controlled the Jaquio, plans to rule Earth by opening the Gate of Darkness with the power of his Dark Sword of Chaos. Robert T. Sturgeon of a U.S. Army Special Intelligence unit recruits Ryu Hayabusa to stop him, and Irene Lew has already been captured. The side-scrolling Acts keep the earlier wall jumping and add the ability to climb up and down walls and to attack with Power Boosting Items while on walls and ladders. These items, such as windmill throwing stars, Fire Dragon Balls and the Invincible Fire Wheel, consume ninja power. The key new feature is the orange ninja symbol, which creates shadow clones that follow Ryu and copy every move, including attacks, and each Act ends with a boss fight.

t_b36dc1507dad.overview: Two prototype builds of this unreleased multicart survive, and their lineups are completely different. The later build opens with a title screen, an advertisement and a special thanks screen, then lists 30 entries over a three-page menu, among them F-15 City War, Tiles of Fate, Krazy Kreatures, Dudes with Attitude, Venice Beach Volleyball, Deathbots, Mermaids of Atlantis, Menace Beach, Poke Block, Captain Comic, Moon Ranger, Solitaire and Baby Boomer. Wally Bear and the NO! Gang appears as a prototype, and the Dudes II entry is only a placeholder that sends the player to Chiller. An earlier build also lists 30 entries, but many are split into two numbered parts of the same game, among them Magic Block, Balloon Monster and Baby Boomer, and some, such as Balloon Monster, seem unfinished.

t_b37485442856.overview: Conceived as a sequel to Capcom's Vulgus, this unreleased shoot-'em-up diverges significantly from its predecessor. Vulgus returns as the villain of a minimal plot, now taking a humanoid form. Twelve stages span six planets: the first level of each planet flies above land across a wider playing field, while the second takes place in space and generally squeezes the ship into tight corridors. Along the way the ship picks up speed-ups and power-ups such as a powerful laser and shots that bounce off walls, plus two pods that can be sent out horizontally to cover more space, similar to R-Type. The game loops, but only after twelve stages and a proper ending.

t_b386bb6606aa.overview:
Spanning 50 stages, this action-puzzle platformer presents multi-story brick environments filled with ladders, suspended hand-to-hand bars, and trapdoors. Players control a Galactic Commando tasked with collecting every piece of gold in each level and reaching the top of the screen to advance. While running through the stage, the commando must avoid enemy robots or guards that pursue the character and can also pick up gold bars. The character can drop from any height unharmed.

Defense relies on digging holes into brick surfaces to the character's sides, temporarily trapping pursuing guards and causing them to drop carried gold. Holes eventually refill, consuming trapped enemies and bringing new guards in at the top of the screen, but solid surfaces cannot be dug. A life is lost when an enemy catches the commando or the commando is trapped in a pit. Alongside the primary mode, an included edit mode allows players to create customized stages.

t_b3c0c7ed90eb.overview: Jaleco's 1988 baseball sequel, released overseas as Bases Loaded II: Second Season, brings back the same fictitious 12-team league with new players. Alongside single games there is a single-player pennant race, in which a strong regular-season record leads to a best-of-seven championship series. Every player has a biorhythm that can be monitored to ensure optimal performance, and the starting lineup and batting order of the user's team can be modified. Play moves faster than in the original, and once a ball is hit into play the view shifts to the first-base or third-base line depending on which team is batting. A nine-run rule can call a game early, and no game may last more than 12 innings.

t_b4070968fe78.overview: An office programmer who is secretly the agent Super Salary 008 must this time rescue his former girlfriend Marilyn, code number 777, who has been kidnapped by the boss of the nation of Succhaina. To reach her he infiltrates the dangerous pachinko parlors that Succhaina runs, once again given only 100 balls by his stingy boss. Four stages of three maps each are crossed by emptying machines, which makes three switches appear: the right one leads onward, while a wrong choice drops 008 into the basement, where ladders lead back up. Hidden switches and ladders are tied to Marilyn's memos, and solving their secrets is the fastest way through. Item counters sell a fixed shooting technique, reach patterns, spring control and goggles that flash the correct switch. A time set option makes machines explode if not emptied in time, and a 12-character password resumes play.

t_b4aca426ad4e.overview: Planets themed on vegetables have come under attack by evil forces in outer space, the setting of this side-scrolling platformer that Jaleco prepared for release in America as a localization of Ninja Jajamaru: Ginga Daisakusen but never shipped. The localization renames the main characters Maru and Cori, who have essentially identical abilities, and fills the dialogue with vegetable-based puns. Holding the B button makes the hero run in place, allowing a dash forward and higher jumps. Enemies can be defeated only by jumping on their heads, and a single hit costs a life. Power-ups are found by hitting blocks with the head or jumping on them, among them a star that bounces along the ground when thrown and an item that grants temporary invulnerability.

t_b4c74402cd8a.overview: Sachen gathered seven of its own games onto the fifth Super Cartridge compilation, each chosen from a menu. The lineup mixes puzzle, educational and table games: Penguin and Seal, a Pengo-like puzzle game; Dong Dong Nao II: Middle School English 1, which teaches Chinese speakers English; Pyramid, a Tetris clone built from triangular pieces; Magical Mathematics, which teaches various math formulas; Strategist, a competitive poker game with unique themes and gimmicks; a puzzle game featuring various logic puzzles; and Chinese Checkers. Previously released titles on the cartridge had their copyright years removed.

t_b4ee7887bbb5.overview: Rex Soft ported the Mega Drive version of Boogerman: A Pick and Flick Adventure to the Famicom with this side-scrolling platformer. Boogerman gains two powers absent from Super Game's port, Belch and Flame Gas, the latter working only when A, B and Select are pressed together, while garbage piles and the Milk Jug power-up are missing. The game also includes two bosses that the other port lacks, FlyBoy and Revolta. The story introduction is presented as a scrolling text crawl. Only two of the original four levels are included, kept as separate stages, and movement is slow.

t_b52eb7815891.overview: Set in the world of Alice in Wonderland, this side-view action game sends Mickey Mouse and Minnie Mouse to rescue Alice, a girl who wandered into Wonderland and was carried off by the queen of cards and her gang. The player controls Mickey, whose basic moves are walking, jumping and throwing erasers, across five worlds whose scrolling and clear conditions differ. Minnie always follows behind; enemies cannot hurt her, but a life is lost if she falls into a pit, and some enemies kidnap her, forcing Mickey to find an item and free her before the exit door will open. Villains from Disney cartoons and films appear as bosses. Mickey has a life meter, and there is no time limit.

t_b55926c5ae0f.overview:
The player controls miniature versions of either the Vampire or the Monster, jumping and attacking through six environmental stages to defeat Warlock and hostile minions. Movement includes walking, crouching, jumping, and executing a higher secondary leap at the apex of a jump. In combat, characters can strike directly or lift and throw everyday objects, such as keys and bolts, at oncoming adversaries.

Progress spans locations including a house interior, a kitchen, sewers, construction girders, an oriental garden, and Monster Mountain, each concluding with an encounter against an enemy leader. Characters possess an energy gauge and multiple lives, losing a life when health depletes. Defeated foes yield points, which grant extra lives at score thresholds. A second player can participate, and if one character runs out of lives, that player may take a remaining life from the surviving partner.

t_b599e1f6fc09.overview: Known in Chinese as Shaolin Warrior, Sachen's martial arts brawler for the NES appeared in Taiwan in 1989 and closely follows the template of the NES releases of Double Dragon, to the point of being described as a clone of that game. Its stages mix brawling with portions that place an emphasis on platforming, the kind of section that was more prominent in Double Dragon II. The game was later released in the West in 1990 under the title Challenge of the Dragon, a name it shares with an unrelated Color Dreams game.

t_b5b8371ecfc1.overview:
Destroying the Dark Sword of Chaos and stopping the evil lord Ashtar drives the player forward. Taking control of Ryu Hayabusa, the player navigates platforming stages called Acts to battle enemies and defeat bosses. Ryu can jump, climb up and down walls, and latch onto ladders. A life is lost if Ryu's strength meter empties, if he falls off the screen, or if the timer expires. Losing all lives ends the game, but continues are available from the current level.

Ryu strikes foes with his Dragon Sword or uses special items obtained from crystal balls. These techniques consume ninja power and include shurikens, boomerang-like stars, directional fireballs, and protective flames. Additional pickups restore strength, grant extra lives, expand ninja power, or summon shadow clones that follow Ryu and copy his moves.

t_b5c152a95ba7.overview: High-school nerd Chip McCallahan has met Melinda the Mental Marvel in the school science laboratory, and to gain membership in the Bit Busters Club he must find his way through her Clubhouse. The puzzle action unfolds across a long series of two-dimensional levels built from tiles. In each one, Chip has to collect enough computer chips to open the chip socket at the end of the level and then reach the exit, dealing with buttons, locked doors, water and lethal monsters along the way. This unfinished NES conversion contains a level unique to it.

t_b60168b41191.overview: Billy West, known as Bayou Billy, is a vigilante from the bayous of Louisiana who has long opposed the crime boss Godfather Gordon, and Gordon kidnaps Billy's girlfriend Annabelle Lane to lure him into one final battle. Most of the nine stages follow a side-scrolling beat-'em-up format, with Billy punching, kicking and jump-kicking and picking up melee weapons dropped by certain enemies. Two stages switch to a first-person rail shooting format in which as many gunmen as possible must be shot before the boss is destroyed, and two driving stages send Billy's jeep along the freeway from the grasslands before time runs out. In this Famicom version the jeep has a health gauge during the driving stages, the challenge is milder than overseas, and there are four possible endings.

t_b602551cd32a.overview: Set in crime-ridden New York in the year 199X, this side-scrolling action game follows Saizou, a New York police detective who is secretly a ninja. When a wave of child kidnappings hits the city, he learns that his own son Sasuke is among the missing and sets out to take down the criminal organization behind them. Across six stages he fights with shuriken, a sword for close attacks and ninja arts, rescuing captive children along the way, and each stage ends with a boss. Ninja arts are unlimited: holding the attack button charges a gauge, and releasing it unleashes the art assigned to the current direction input. More arts become available as stages are cleared, and one shooting section has Saizou flying on a kite. Touching certain enemies or freeing children starts conversations, most of them comically odd.

t_b62af9097d39.overview: Half-court street basketball is the focus of this sports game, played either one-on-one or two-on-two with a roster of eight playground players. Before tipping off, the player picks one of two courts and sets the rules, including whether winners' outs are in effect. Matches can be played against the computer or another player, or two players can team up against the computer. On the court, players can block shots, make steals, pass off or drive strong to the hoop, and dunk attempts are shown in slow-motion sequences that can still be blocked. An around-the-world mode lets players concentrate on making baskets without worrying about charging, pushing or traveling fouls.

t_b645ee94939d.overview: The famous artist Ichirō Mamiya hid several precious frescos in his huge mansion before he mysteriously disappeared, and a team of five documentary filmmakers sets out to recover the paintings from the abandoned, dilapidated building. The mansion is in danger of collapsing and is occupied by countless monsters. In this role-playing game, the five characters can venture solo or explore in teams of two or three, and the player can switch between characters and parties at any time. Each character has a unique item that is necessary to complete the adventure. A character who dies remains dead permanently for the rest of the game, and there are five different endings in total.

t_b66185f73835.overview: Players manage a high school girls' softball team with the goal of becoming the best in the world. Winning a regional tournament sends the team to the national championship, and the road then continues against stronger teams beyond the national stage, up to professional-level opponents. Batting, fielding and baserunning follow the style of a well-known baseball series, adjusted with touches such as slow pitches and weak throwing arms to suit high school players. Games run seven innings with unlimited extra innings, and a ten-run lead after six innings ends a game early. A password shown on the game-over screen lets play resume from the game just before the loss. Alongside the one-player mode, a two-player versus mode and an all-star mode are included.

t_b667143bfbbf.overview: Konami's Famicom adaptation of Rampart is a strategy game of castle defense in which play alternates between two time-limited phases: combat and building. The player's territory is a wall surrounding a set of castles and cannons. In the combat phase, the cannons are aimed at enemies trying to break the walls; in the building phase, shapes like those from Tetris are moved and rotated to repair the walls and enclose territory, and at least one castle must be enclosed when time runs out to avoid defeat. Single-player play offers four modes, PRACTICE, EASY, NORMAL and HARD, each with its own story and theme: a modern war against tanks and infantry, a fairy tale with wolves and rats, a mythological fantasy full of monsters, and a feudal warring-states setting. PRACTICE allows stage selection, while the other three modes use passwords. Two players can also battle each other in a versus mode.

t_b6876f91c4a3.overview: Viewed from overhead, this Famicom adaptation by Sunsoft of the film Gremlins 2: The New Batch puts Gizmo in charge of cleaning out a building overrun by Gremlins. Gizmo makes his way through a series of levels inside the building, picking up new weapons as he goes, from a genetically modified super tomato found in the laboratory to a bow that fires matchsticks in the later sections. The ultimate goal is to reach the Gremlin Control Center and wipe out every Gremlin gathered inside. The adventure is for a single player.

t_b6b6173d7dfd.overview: Tabo, Hangyodon, Pokopon, Keroppi and Kitty return from the first Sanrio Carnival, each carrying a hammer, for two kinds of puzzle. In the candy puzzle, candies fall from the top of the screen and are knocked sideways with the hammer to line up three or more of one color; cleared candies become petals that fly to the flowers above, and giving every flower its petals clears the stage. Black candies vanish only when ten are lined up, and the game ends if the screen fills or time runs out. The panel puzzle, following each candy stage, is a picture of Sanrio characters split into panels with one missing, to be put back in order within the time limit. A versus mode against a computer-controlled Keroppi, with bomb candies, goes to the first to three wins, and a challenge mode chases high scores without a time limit.

t_b6e80d5eaa2d.overview:
Taking control of the hero Orpheus, the player travels through ancient Greece across side-scrolling environments featuring light platforming and combat. The journey requires fighting through mythological creatures such as the Minotaur, cyclops, and Cerberus to reach Tartarus, defeat Hades in a two-stage encounter, and rescue his lover Helene. A top-down overview displays eight different locations, beginning in Arcadia, where players explore city-states and dungeons in a somewhat non-linear fashion.

Progression involves meeting Greek gods in their temples to receive important items. Beginning with a simple club, Orpheus gathers swords, shields, and other equipment, while ambrosia raises his maximum stamina. Available equipment includes the Staff of Fennel, which can emit the fire of Prometheus at distant enemies, and the Divine Sword, which shoots the power of Argus in a straight line. Players also acquire special items like the Sandals of Hermes and the Harp of Apollo, which lets Orpheus fly on Pegasus when played at the Monolith of the Sun.

t_b70f114449c2.overview: Hummer Team built this 1995 Famicom beat 'em up for J.Y. Company as a port of the SNES version of Mighty Morphin Power Rangers. Unlike that game, the player never advances through different areas of a stage: there are four stages in total, each about one and a half screens big, and the story has been removed entirely. The engine, modified from one of Hummer Team's fighting games, sends multiple enemies into each stage, but only one appears at a time. The player character has a health bar, while enemies and bosses do not. There is no two-player mode, and four difficulty levels are offered, although play is the same on each.

t_b73db0e64e6b.overview: Real team names and real player names appear for the first time in the series in this baseball game, which also brings back the pennant mode: seventy wins take the league title and send the team on to the Japan Series, and a season can be resumed with a password. During play, players earn or lose star-marked technical points; errors, strikeouts and runs allowed lower them, reducing a batter's chance of a hit or a pitcher's power, while fine plays and strikeouts raise them. Errors, fine plays and runs allowed are highlighted with animations. Instead of choosing a ballpark, games are played at the home stadium of the team batting last. Other options include two-player versus games, a watch mode and single exhibition games.

t_b75ece452b43.overview: In 2061, Halley's Comet has been approaching Mars, and the nations of Earth send a mission to investigate. Musou Hayao is stationed on the space lab J.E.S.U.S., where he grows close to Eline, a French mathematician and musician. Sent to investigate the first ship, he finds most of the crew missing and many dead or dying, victims of an alien that takes the knowledge and memories of each crew member it kills. The story proceeds as a linear adventure in which an action and its target are chosen from commands. Compared with the earlier computer versions, this Famicom adaptation removes game overs, minigames, puzzles and sexually explicit scenes, fixes Eline as the partner for the later part of the story, and turns the robot sidekick FOJY into a comic relief character.

t_b76052e55685.overview: Jaleco planned this role-playing game as the American version of its Famicom title Jajamaru: Ninpou Chou, but the localization was cancelled before its scheduled mid-1990 release. Unlike the earlier action games in the series, it is a traditional role-playing game: the party walks a world map, visits towns and dungeons, and meets random encounters fought on a separate turn-based combat screen. Much of the graphics and music had already been altered or redone, with art redrawn to look more realistic than the cartoonish original. The surviving prototype is playable but unfinished, with many enemies and animations missing, an entire chapter not implemented and the third quest barely started, while its early English script contains many translation errors.

t_b7639c4feb84.overview: A baby elephant by the name of Columbus Jumbo, or CJ, is captured in Africa to be put in a zoo, but when turbulence hits the plane carrying him to England his cage opens, and he leaps out with an umbrella somewhere over France. The platform adventure follows his journey back home on foot across four levels, France, Switzerland, Egypt and finally Africa, each ending in a boss fight. CJ can jump, fire an unlimited supply of peanuts and throw a limited number of bombs, and his umbrella slows his descent from heights. Two players can take part simultaneously in cooperation, but the screen scrolls only with player 1, and player 2 is lost whenever he leaves the screen. The NES version arrived as part of the Quattro Arcade compilation cartridge.

t_b7d1c3361c47.overview: Despite a title screen and cartridge art copied from Mega Man, Rocman X is an original action game created by Sachen, also known as Thunder Blast Man. An evil crime syndicate has kidnapped Miss Lucy and overrun the city with its many robotic enemies, and the hero must save the city. Thunder Blast Man starts with a super-weak boomerang and can upgrade to a triple shot of boomerangs or to batarangs, which are three times stronger than a normal boomerang and can travel through walls. When charged up, he can perform a horizontal air-dash or even dash upward. The stages, which have no official names, include ocean, city, sky, highway, building and cave levels, and some hold collectible coins. Two types of continues are available.

t_b7dd1acd11fa.overview: In the dark and cold Hades, Satan has seized the Devil Crystal Ball and used its evil power to throw the world into chaos. A Wise Old Man trains Lee Long, a young fighter armed with arrows and skilled in Chinese Kung-Fu, and sends him to destroy Satan and his devils. This Sachen action platformer has Lee Long jump with A and shoot with B; like Mario, he breaks tiles overhead by jumping into them, and pressing Down and B delivers a kick that smashes nearby tiles. His weapons are a fast Throwing Arrow and a slower, stronger Fireball. Orbs scattered through each level cycle through colors, and the power-up gained depends on the color when collected, from homing arrows to extra lives and orbiting shields.

t_b7fee1e2c481.overview:
Recovering the Lost Treasure of Babylon from the evil dragon Ryu serves as the goal for Karnov. The player directs the fire-breathing protagonist across nine stages filled with obstacles and bizarre enemies, such as the knife-throwing Lion Keeper, the swooping Chicken Bone, and the boulder-hurling Rock Man. Each environment demands careful navigation to overcome end-stage bosses and reach the final confrontation atop a mountain in the deep forest.

A solo player can run, jump, swim, and project fire against hostile creatures. Gathering special items enhances offensive abilities, allowing Karnov to release double or triple fireballs. Players can also collect and store utility items, including jumping boots, bombs, climbing ladders, and wings, to surmount terrain challenges and survive perilous encounters.

t_b8cdca57159c.overview: Jaleco's competitive action game revolves around manipulating a ball to meet a range of objectives. At the start, players choose among three Zones, each built around a different goal. In Arena of Death, the aim is to hit the other player with the ball. Building Breaker asks players to take down enemy-colored buildings by knocking the ball into them many times. Goal Shoot-out is a soccer-like three-on-three mode in which each side includes two computer-controlled teammates, and the object is to shoot the ball into the enemy goal. Up to two people can play.

t_b8fddff64690.overview: Four teams, Kunio's Nekketsu High squad, Hanazono, Reiho and an inter-school union, face off in a school athletic meet where punching, kicking and using weapons are all within the rules. Reiho's new student council president has organized the meet to crush every other school, stacking his own team with powerful fighters. Teams score by placing well, knocking opponents down and grabbing items, and lose points when knocked down. The events are a cross-country run through town, over rooftops and through sewers; a race through rooms full of obstacles; a contest to climb poles and punch open a ball hanging above; and a last-man-standing brawl in a ring where special moves come into play. Bombs, wooden swords, dumbbells, tires and brass knuckles can be swung or thrown. Up to four players can compete with a multiplayer adapter, and in single-player mode, falling out of first place after any event ends the game.

t_b90f751f5200.overview: Nintendo developed the falling-block puzzle game under the name Virus before releasing it as Dr. Mario, and this later prototype build was found installed in an otherwise-unremarkable PlayChoice-10 arcade cabinet. The core play matches the finished game: two-colored capsules fall into a bottle of red, yellow and blue viruses, four matching colors in a row disappear, and each level ends once every virus is gone. Several differences remain. The title screen and pre-game options menu are different, the music tracks are not yet named, and the speed setting is called the sick level. A bonus counts down with every pill dropped and pays out after the final virus of each level is cleared, a mechanic removed before release, and the viruses hang out in an oval rather than the magnifying glass of the retail version.

t_b95c292bf448.overview: When the Akudama Empire rises suddenly and attacks the Earth with an army of robots, a hired mercenary, Kagemaru, summons the only witch not under a seal, Doropie, since the machines are vulnerable to magic. The gameplay resembles Capcom's Mega Man series: Doropie wields a wand that fires different projectiles, and her outfit color shows the active power. Six powers are available, a normal shot, a phoenix ability, a freeze shot, a bouncing ball shot, a shield and a broom, and she can also shoot directly upward, crouch to dodge enemies and projectiles, and charge attacks. The invading army turns out to be led by the Machine God Emperor, whom she had previously sealed away. This original Japanese version includes a continue feature and story cutscenes.

t_b961b7b39832.overview:
Guiding Lieutenant Solid Snake, the player infiltrates hostile territory while avoiding detection by guards and surveillance equipment. Snake begins with a combat knife and handgun, using melee strikes, firearms, and planted explosives across locations such as a jungle, a battleship, a train, and a castle. Raising an alarm brings attacking soldiers, requiring the player to defeat the troops or escape them. Knocking out enemies with punches occasionally yields ammunition or rations. Rescuing hostages and interrogating enemy officers with truth gas increases Snake's rank, expanding his health and carrying limits.

Progression requires finding pass cards to unlock doors and using a transceiver to reach three contacts. Exploration shifts between top-down perspectives and side-scrolling sections where Snake walks, jumps, or crawls. In side-view areas, weapons are limited to a knife, handgun, and plastic explosives, with underwater paths requiring oxygen tanks.

t_b97ab5f8cf5a.overview: Hummer Team ported the Super Famicom fighting game Yuu Yuu Hakusho Final to the Famicom in Chinese and English versions, with translations apparently done from scratch. Story Mode offers four characters who all share the same cutscenes; cutscenes precede the first five fights, and after a loss the player can continue as a different character. A Contest mode supports two players. These modes have eight playable characters in the Chinese version and seven in the English one, and the single-player modes offer three difficulty levels. The graphics are taken from the original game and simplified, and the music mixes tracks from the original with tunes reused or remixed from other Hummer Team games. In the English version, the fighters' names in the HUD remain in Chinese for lack of space.

t_b99a7f03fb86.overview: Word guessing in the style of the Wheel of Fortune television show drives Fortuna, a Russian Dendy game by A. Chudov. It is the commercial version of his Field of Dreams 2, a sequel to Field of Dreams with new graphics and features: time limits, progression from level to level after scoring 1024 points, and Mario as the co-host who turns the letters. Fortuna adds a final screen with a unique code that could be presented in a store to claim real money, similar to Bonza.

t_b9a4ba5d7751.overview: Flying a jet fighter, the player shoots down enemy aircraft and attacks targets on the ground across a series of levels. The viewpoint alternates from level to level: odd-numbered stages scroll from an overhead perspective, while even-numbered stages switch to a third-person view from behind the jet. Opposition consists of ordinary-looking planes in the air along with tanks and missile batteries on the ground. Power-ups provide stronger weapons, smart bombs and extra lives, and weapon upgrades carry over between the two kinds of levels; losing a plane costs only one power level rather than the whole arsenal. No music accompanies the action. Alongside the single-player game, a 2-player competitive mode is included.

t_b9d249edc3ee.overview: Released in Japan before reaching North America as Uninvited, the Famicom version of the point-and-click horror adventure opens after a car crash: the unseen protagonist wakes, finds a sibling missing, and is drawn into a nearby old mansion. The house once belonged to a sorcerer whose most gifted apprentice turned against the others, leaving it haunted by undead residents and monsters that must be fought or evaded. The quest to find the sibling is a matter of gaining access to the locked parts of the estate. Spells are chosen by scrolling through the inventory rather than typed, the text is simplified and sometimes adds hints, and there is no time limit unless the player picks up a cursed ruby in one of the bedrooms.

t_ba84be8a8e82.overview: One Monday, Garfield notices that Odie is missing, carried off by the stray-cat Iron Claw gang, and sets out to find him. The side-scrolling action game spans nine areas, one for each day of the week, with Saturday and Sunday each split into morning and afternoon, and every area is cleared by reaching the goal door within a time limit. Garfield can run, crouch, jump and kick, and weapon items such as pie, bones and raisin cornflakes replace the kick with attacks that mostly use limited ammunition. Keys open doors, boots give a burst of speed, lasagna grants temporary invincibility, and milk and coffee restore health. Bosses wait at the end of the Thursday, Friday, Saturday morning and Sunday afternoon areas. It is a single-player game.

t_bad5ca6db6c6.overview: Under its Chinese title 777 幸運輪盤, this simple slot machine simulator was made by Sachen in 1989 and developed by Hummer Cheng. Credits are gained by inserting coins. The Chinese version exists in two revisions that share the same packaging and label: in the "clean" revision, pressing SELECT after inserting a coin shows the total winnings together with a picture of the male player, whose expression improves as the winnings grow; the "adult" revision drops that screen and instead shows a female model in two stages of undress after fifty coins are won. An English-language version, known as 777 Lucky Bingo, uses the adult reward pictures.

t_bb066d60731d.overview: As Charlie the circus clown, the player works through a series of circus acts against the clock: riding a lion through flaming rings, crossing a tightrope while jumping over monkeys, leaping from ball to ball, riding a horse over trampolines and walls, and swinging from one trapeze to the next. Points come from grabbing money bags, performing dangerous tricks, avoiding enemies and completing stages. Bonus points depend on the time remaining, but running out of time costs a life. Unlike the arcade original, the Famicom version leaves out the trampoline stage, and it adds a "B" mode in which all the levels are repeated with added difficulty.

t_bb0c90e00cb6.overview: Trading drives this role-playing game set along the Silk Road. The hero is an exiled prince of LittleLand who has only recently learned of his royal heritage. To reclaim the throne he must gather the seven shards of the Rainbow Mirror, scattered through Arabia, Persia, Mongolia, India, Cham, China and Japan, and then defeat the usurper, Zrool. Enemies drop neither money nor experience, so funds come from buying goods such as clayware in one town and selling them where they are valued more, while battles earn license points that let the prince sell more goods in different places. Combat is turn-based and seen in first person. Animals can be bought to carry more goods, soldiers can be hired to fight alongside the prince, and deserts drain a water supply that kills him if it runs dry.

t_bb604155e935.overview: Cast as supreme commander of a huge fleet, the player must win eight decisive battles in this full-scale naval warfare simulation. The Red and Blue armies take alternate turns, and each turn brings a budget set by production power, which rises with the number of strategic points held: capitals, naval ports, air bases and cities. In the armament phase units are built, postponed or scrapped; in the operations phase ships, aircraft and land forces move, attack, repair, resupply, bombard and occupy. Combat scenes are controlled directly by the player rather than left to the computer. Losing the home capital means defeat, and reaching turn 100 is a draw. Four short scenarios can be played as either side by one or two players, while the long scenarios must be cleared in order with the Red army. An optional search mode hides enemy ships until reconnaissance planes find them.

t_bb69da6b801a.overview: Adapted from Johji Manabe's science-fantasy manga, this action role-playing game picks up the story partway through the series. The hero, Tetsuya, has been imprisoned by the emperor, and after freeing himself he learns that Princess Kahm and all of his other friends are locked up as well. He sets out across a large world to fight enemies and free everyone from the emperor's grip. Cities are displayed from an overhead perspective, and battles use action combat. Items dropped by defeated enemies are picked up by standing on them and choosing a "take" command from the menu. Growth depends not only on experience points but also on pins awarded to Tetsuya for side quests and favors for other characters, and allies such as Battia can join the party.

t_bbbb82f56482.overview:
Taking down enemy aircraft that attempt to destroy the player's stealth fighter forms the primary objective in Stealth ATF. Piloting the Stealth Advanced Tactical Fighter, the player manages every phase of flight across missions set in theaters around the world, such as the Middle East, Alaska, and the Pacific. Two players can take turns, and a second player can also take control of an enemy plane for a dogfight.

Gameplay spans launching from a runway, aerial combat, and returning to touch down safely once the engagement concludes. Levels present distinct environments and runway styles, ranging from expansive land strips to compact aircraft carrier decks at sea. While engaging opposing bogeys with onboard cannons and missiles, the pilot must monitor current flight altitude to prevent fatal crashes, while also tracking craft damage levels and remaining munitions. Once per mission, a stealth mode hides the fighter from enemy radar to evade missile attacks.

t_bbfcbf72d9a8.overview: Released only in Japan as an entry in the Eggerland series, the puzzle game again sends Lolo through a series of rooms to rescue Princess Lala from King Egger. In each room, collecting every Heart Framer opens the treasure chest, and taking its contents clears the room. Pushable green blocks can stop enemy attacks or seal off paths, and a shot briefly encases an enemy in an egg. New elements include a stationary enemy that sucks Lolo in when its mouth lines up with him, and bridges that break; Lala can also be controlled. A hermit in a training hall teaches the basic rules, and after the early stages the puzzles turn consistently hard. Its completely different stages and new mechanics were later reused in the American Adventures of Lolo 3.

t_bc0a10fcfb3b.overview:
Rescuing captured comrades and destroying an enemy vessel, the Toad Magma Tanker, serves as the primary objective across the Aniverse. The player starts by directing Bucky O'Hare, captain of the spaceship Righteous Indignation, who journeys across four distinct planets to free his imprisoned crew. These opening worlds can be tackled in any order, spanning environments filled with hazards such as waterfalls, active volcanoes, slick ice, and laser cannons. Stages contain multiple scenes that scroll both horizontally and vertically, and each stage ends with a boss encounter.

Freed crew members become playable, allowing the player to switch between characters at any time. Each hero utilizes different weapons and special skills, including short flights, wall clinging, high jumps, and a steerable crystal ball. Holding and then releasing the attack button triggers these special abilities, which grow stronger with collectible power-up icons. Extra lives and health can also be collected while battling toad forces.

t_bc65f076641e.overview: Soccer matches pit eight of the world's top teams against one another, and play is either against the computer or head to head against a friend. The game was developed by Computer & Entertainment in 1991 and sold in several regions; this Japanese edition from Hacker International is an adult-targeted version that features nudity, while the releases elsewhere, such as Ultimate League Soccer and Futebol, are plain soccer games.

t_bc73985d1400.overview: Jajamaru and Princess Sakura head into outer space to defeat Don Destroyda, ruler of the universe, and restore peace across seven stages of this action game. Because the setting is space, enemies and items are all new to the series. The A button jumps, and coming down on enemies with a swinging weapon attacks them; the B button uses items, and holding it makes the character run in place, dash and spring into a long jump, then roll into a charging body attack, though holding it too long leaves the hero briefly out of breath. Items include the boomerang-like Cosmo Shuriken, the arcing Cosmo Shot bombs and a Cosmo Suit that absorbs one hit. Gathering three matching letter items summons a helper beast that assists during the boss battle, and pressing up at a stage's goal zone clears it.

t_bc745c4626a1.overview: Set in A.D. 20XX, this vertical shooter pits humanity against TASAC, a force of alien bionic mutants locked in fierce warfare with the human race. In the story printed on the packaging, Landsy and Dagrel, commanders of Earth Defense Arms, must destroy TASAC to rescue the Earth before humans are turned into slaves. That premise lives only on the box: in play, the game presents no story at all and is a straightforward vertically scrolling shooter. It also offers no closing scene that settles whether TASAC is ever defeated.

t_bca6c252a3ad.overview: Horizontal scrolling shooting action puts the player in control of a fighter ship that fires forward shots along with missiles angled downward. Holding B with the directional pad turns the ship around, unleashes a screen-clearing flash bomb, or warps several areas ahead. The ship's energy drains slowly over time and drops sharply whenever the bomb or warp is used, and both require a minimum energy level; running out of energy or touching enemies, their bullets or the terrain costs a life. Outdoor and cave areas alternate, cave layouts vary slightly each time, and destroying a set number of enemies opens the way to the next area. A launch pad near the cave entrance fires blue capsules that refill energy and yellow capsules that grant a temporary barrier, and koala items award extra lives. Across 512 areas the terrain narrows and attacks intensify until the boss Baltron appears in the final area, after which a second loop begins with recolored terrain.

t_bcd255242bb9.overview: A port of the arcade game Rally-X by Joy Van, Jovial Race puts the player behind the wheel of a car on a tortuous, maze-like map. The goal on each level is to collect the many flags scattered around the map while escaping faster enemy cars, aided by a radar that shows where the enemies and flags are. Pressing B drops trails behind the car, and enemies that crash into them get stuck for a few seconds, but fuel drains faster while trails are dropped; a flag marked with an L restores it. Some objects on the road award money, while running over a duck costs money and boulders cause a crash. Money is spent in a shop, opened with Start, on items such as Turbo, a rocket, a gun and extra lives, across 75 levels.

t_bcf4404feb9e.overview: Rather than putting the bat in the player's hands, this Asmik baseball title is a management game in which the player runs a team by controlling player training and various other aspects of the club. A new game begins with creating the manager and entering a name, after which a randomized number of attribute points is distributed across four categories. The player then picks one team to manage and five other teams to play against. Games are watched as they are played out, and the manager can step in during a match to make changes such as switching the pitcher, adjusting outfield player positions and changing the batting order.
