t_bcf8ab19f225.overview: Kyugo produced the Famicom Airwolf, a horizontally scrolling shooter based on the television series about an advanced prototype supersonic helicopter with stealth capabilities and a formidable arsenal. Its story has a mysterious organization challenging the pilot Stringfellow Hawke and his helicopter, Airwolf, to battle. The cartridge is a different game from the Airwolf released on the NES, which was developed separately by Beam Software as a mission-based design built around rescuing prisoners from enemy bases.

t_bd0fd85c9227.overview: Miniature golf comes to the Famicom with four courses: Traditional, Classic, Deluxe and Challenge. The Traditional course is a standard layout that calls for well-placed bank shots, the Classic offers animated bridges and other obstacles, and the Deluxe and Challenge courses have difficult hills and layouts. Across the courses, traps, ricochets and unusual gradations on the greens complicate each putt. A shot begins by moving a crosshair in the approximate direction and distance the ball should go; the level then rises in a power bar, and when the bar reaches the bottom it moves horizontally along an accuracy bar with a center line. Up to four players can either play a game or practice any hole on any course.

t_bd516efa3d09.overview: A three-dimensional falling-block puzzle, 3D Block is an unlicensed Famicom port of Blockout, itself a 3D version of Tetris. Shapes descend into a static well that is fixed at five by five by ten cubes, and the player must fit the various block designs into the container to clear space and manage the rising stack. The controls are unusual: the Start button speeds up the falling block, while the Select button pauses the game. The original 1989 version was made by Hwang Shinwei; this release carries a 1990 RCM Group credit and a slightly different title screen.

t_bd5e9d15f939.overview: Pogie, a pet fluffle who had always been cute, stars in this colorful side-on platform game built around racing through sugar-coated levels of arcade action. Collecting stars is the main objective, while enemies lie in wait along the way. Pogie gains a special power by swallowing a fizzola, a power-up that turns the normally cute character aggressive. The design draws clear inspiration from an obvious classic platformer.

t_bd7a3d4ba4f3.overview: Mangar, an evil sorcerer, has turned the prosperous town of Skara Brae into a world of winter where monsters lurk, and its brave survivors gather at the Adventurers' Guild to fight back. Published by FCI, the NES adaptation of the computer role-playing game begins with character creation from six professions: Warrior, Rogue, Hunter, Bard, Sorcerer and Wizard. Up to six characters form a party that explores the mazelike town and its dungeons in a three-dimensional view beside a scrolling map. The legendary wizard Kylearan, locked in a tower by Mangar, holds the key to the tower where Mangar lives. Battles are chosen from menus, the Bard sings songs with magical powers, and sorcerers and wizards cast illusionary and physical magic. The NES version is dramatically different from other versions and much smaller, with fewer dungeons; these entries are beta builds of it.

t_bdb8c4c6be3c.overview: In AD 2139 national borders have been abolished, yet crime keeps growing worldwide, and a squad of daredevil special detectives called VICE stands against the criminal organizations. The story opens as VICE detective Hart Brabham runs down a junkie whose hand has grown beastlike claws and who carries a tachyon particle gun, then asks fellow VICE member Chris to trace the fully synthetic drug the junkie was using. Developed by Aicom, the action is mostly fast side-scrolling platforming in the vein of Ninja Gaiden, broken up by car-chase stages and 3D gun-shooting stages that each appear twice. Hart can switch at any time between a light saber that strikes a wide area, including overhead and behind him, and a blaster and bombs with limited ammunition, and he can run while crouching to slip under shots. Close-up cinematic scenes tell the story across 11 stages for one player, and continues are unlimited.

t_bdbaae6671f6.overview: Adapted from the Disney animated film, Aladdin for the NES is a side-scrolling platformer developed by NMS Software and released only in Europe; its design follows the Game Boy version of the Sega game. Aladdin fights enemies at close range with a sword and can also throw apples at them, and plenty of power-ups are scattered through the stages. The route follows the film from the streets of Agrabah to a carpet ride through the Cave of Wonders, where the occasional rock must be dodged, and on to a final battle. The prototype included here is an NTSC build from 1994 that is very close to the finished game, with some sprites not shaded properly and other sprite glitches.

t_bddd12ec4552.overview: Track-and-field competition from the arcade comes home in a four-event cartridge built around rapid button pressing. The 100 m dash, long jump, javelin throw and 110 m hurdles are included, while the arcade's hammer throw and high jump are left out. Every event demands fast, repeated tapping, and an athlete moves on to the next event only when the result beats the required mark. Control uses just two buttons, one to run and one to jump, on a dedicated controller packed with the cartridge. A special edition replaced the player character with a television comedy character and added a round-select feature; it was made for a variety show and also sold to the public in limited quantities.

t_be245fd9a968.overview: Adapted from the 1989 film of the same name, this side-view action game puts a huge bounty on the heads of detectives Takayama and Oshita of the Yokohama port police, better known as Taka and Yuji. Fighting through wave after wave of hired assassins, the pair press on toward destroying the Ginseikai, the giant crime syndicate that rules the Yokohama underworld, only to find a terrible truth hidden behind the case. The player picks either detective or controls both at once, clearing each of the nine stages by reaching its goal or defeating the boss. A pistol with unlimited ammunition is backed up by a machine gun and grenades taken from panels dropped by enemies, while hearts restore life. Interludes include a shooting range, a top-down driving sequence against the clock and a sniping scene.

t_be4dea731a37.overview:
A single adventurer wanders the fantasy town of Hillsfar, undertaking quests and navigating mini-games. The player begins by generating a custom character or selecting a pre-made hero, choosing attributes like race, alignment, and class from cleric, fighter, magic-user, or thief. Attributes receive randomized values during creation.

Gameplay alternates between quest-based adventure and action challenges. The hero visits the guild of their class to find assignments. Outside of assigned missions, the player explores freely, traveling across landscapes and hunting for treasure. The story unfolds differently for each of the four classes, offering a distinct adventure with each one.

t_be745e76faa7.overview: The original Japanese release of the Predator action game casts the player as "Dutch" Schaefer, who must make it from the beginning to the end of each level. He starts unarmed and can pick up a machine gun, a laser gun and fragmentation grenades, but carries only one weapon at a time and loses it between levels; only the laser can damage the Predator. Some levels have two exits, one of which warps ahead several levels, and a Predator waits at the end of every few levels. Big Mode stages use larger sprites and an auto-scrolling screen, where Dutch shoots blue and red bubbles to collect weapon power-ups while avoiding touching them, ending in a Predator boss fight; these stages also act as checkpoints. Compared with the later USA release, the levels are redesigned or reordered, and play begins on a Big Mode stage.

t_bec97b6d9115.overview: Two cats named Pitter and Patter compete in this head-to-head fishing game for two players, each catching fish with its tail. The first player to fill a bucket with fish earns a shell, and whoever holds the most shells when the time limit runs out wins. Tin cans can be collected for power-ups, such as larger hooks. The game was created by GameTek employee David Wiebenson in his spare time and survives in more than one prototype build; the builds differ in small details, with one showing a blue sky even though the scene is set at night.

t_bed5103e5ed6.overview: Four card games share this compilation, which seats the player at a table against three computer-controlled opponents. The games available are Max 2, 99, Ghost-Buster and Change Around, each selected from the menu before play. When the menu options are set accordingly, a second human player can replace one of the three CPU opponents, so two people can play at the same table. Developed by Thin Chen and published by Sachen, the cartridge is the middle entry in the company's Poker series, which concluded with Poker III and its casino board game.

t_bed9935f360c.overview:
Riding a bicycle along a suburban street, the player throws newspapers to customer houses. Deliveries must reach a subscriber's paperbox or front porch while dodging hazards such as cars, tires, and skateboarders. Crashing into hazards costs a life, and the player must collect extra bundles along the way to refill a limited paper supply. Damaging non-subscriber houses and targeting select obstacles yields bonus score.

Subscribers cancel their subscriptions if they fail to receive an issue or if their property is damaged. Reaching the end of the neighborhood leads to a timed training course containing jump ramps and targets. A daily report then shows any canceled subscriptions, and a player who performs well continues to the next day's route, aiming to complete a full week. Losing every subscriber also ends the game.

t_bee8aadad75a.overview: Released in America as Metal Mech: Man & Machine, this action game puts the player in control of the driver of a vehicle that resembles the ED-209 from the RoboCop franchise. Levels filled with randomly generated enemies in an unnamed city have to be cleared to survive, and crates hide items that upgrade the vehicle's firepower and defense. The pilot spends as much time outside the armored unit as inside it, since the mech is a bigger, though tougher, target, and leaving it is also necessary to climb ladders that lead to needed items and advance the storyline. Radiation symbols scattered around the city must be collected.

t_bee8c9a59899.overview: Ported from the computer original, this tile-matching solitaire puzzle uses a full set of 144 mahjong tiles stacked on the board. The objective is to remove all the tiles from the board by matching pairs, but only tiles with at least one free vertical edge may be matched on a turn. Any two seasons can form a pair, as can any two flowers. Because the game ends when no legal moves can be made, the order in which pairs are removed matters. It is played by a single player.

t_bf589481706d.overview: Set in medieval Japan, Ikki follows a farming village's uprising against its feudal overlord, though the revolt consists only of Gonbe and, with a second player, Tago, facing an army of ninjas. Seen from above, the farmer moves in eight directions and attacks with a single button, throwing a sickle that automatically flies at the nearest enemy, so dodging matters more than aggression. A level ends when all eight gold koban coins are collected or a randomly appearing daikan is captured. Ghosts stop sickle throwing until a jizo or komainu statue is touched, and a handmaiden can pin the player in place. Items include a bamboo spear, a speed-boosting daikon, a scroll granting an extra life, a leaf that creates an invincible double, and smoke that opens a bonus round of catching onigiri thrown by a sennin. The Famicom version has four levels plus four alternate versions with relocated coins, looping endlessly.

t_bf5e891aec7f.overview: Earth has been seized by an unknown power and faces ruin, and a lone robot rises to fight back. Built as a 3D shooting game for one player, the cartridge supports the Famicom 3D System. The campaign runs across eight stages that move outward from Earth through near-Earth space, the planet Aquarius with its seas and orbit, and the planet Technos, then through open space to the battle satellite Aria. Every stage closes with a boss, among them the transport battleship Zugaihead, the bio-weapon Zeraim, the fortress Octatol, the gatekeeper robot Battle Gear and, at the very end, the reactor core of Aria itself.

t_bf6665a19b32.overview: Famed as an expert pachi-slot player, Sorotta-kun learns from the TV news that the Phantom Coin, said to guarantee wins at pachi-slot, has been stolen. At his regular parlor a suspicious man in black is winning nonstop; he names himself Kaijin 7 Mensou, boasts that he has the coin and vanishes, and Sorotta-kun resolves to catch him. Tips gathered from people in the parlor, whose floors open up as the game goes on, lead to a series of events, each cleared by reaching a set number of coins at the slot machines: the home of the coin's owner, a pachi-slot museum, a pachi-slot shrine and its grounds, and finally a suspicious mansion, with targets rising from 800 to 1,500 coins. Each event starts with 500 coins, the game ends when coins and credits run out, and a nine-character password saves progress.

t_bfca3fe454b6.overview: Picking up after the first game, the hero has become Matsumoto's apprentice and now faces a tougher assignment: grow four million yen into seven billion within two years and reach level 70, the expert class. He starts with a wife and a six-year-old child, whose names and birthdays are entered at the beginning. The market grows to 150 stocks, margin positions can be settled at any time, even on the same day, and cash calculations are instant, allowing several trades in a single day. Banks offer time deposits, dollar deposits and loans secured by property, brokers handle bond funds and investment trusts, and up to three homes can be bought. Each day ends with an automatic save, and resetting outside the proper procedure halves the player's cash.

t_c001df71e4a0.overview: Six adventurers try to discover the secret of the Inner Sanctum, a kind of holy grail quest, on the world of Varn, with its outdoor terrain, castles, caves, underground cities and an Astral Plane. The party is drawn from six classes, including knights, clerics, robbers, paladins, archers and the spellcasters this version calls wizards, and each character's race affects starting statistics and resistance to attacks. The world is shown in first person as a maze-like grid explored by moving forward or back or turning ninety degrees, and exploration, like combat, is turn-based. Hostile encounters can be fled, surrendered to, bribed or fought. Although the setting looks like medieval fantasy, science fiction elements are revealed later in the adventure.

t_c027a122e60a.overview: Rugby matches are viewed from a top-down perspective of the pitch, with the two sides oriented vertically on the screen. Before a match, the player can assign points to various stats to focus on certain areas of the team's playstyle. Three options are available: a one-off training exhibition match, a league game that pits the player against several CPU teams, and a versus mode in which two human players compete. Developed by ZAP and published by TSS, the cartridge has no connection to the later international rugby union competition that shares its name, which was formed years afterward.

t_c036adbe5506.overview: One night a wounded samurai reaches a ninja village with news that the castle has fallen and that the lord and Princess Sakura have been carried off, and the village elder sends JaJaMaru to gather eight spirit arts. Waiting at the summit of the golden castle is a monk from hell who plots to revive a legendary great demon beast. Played as an action role-playing game with top-down exploration, the journey crosses towns, dungeons and a world map divided into roughly five areas. Dungeons are made up of rooms full of enemies, and defeating the guardian demon at the deepest point or completing events earns spirit arts that raise the hero's health and spirit-art limits. Defeated enemies occasionally drop money for buying weapons and items or healing at an inn, and game data is saved at a sorcerer's house.

t_c084922e0fb6.overview: A great wizard named Warūmon has conquered Wai Wai World, kidnapped the Herb Princess and taken her to his base in outer space. To fight him, Dr. Cinnamon builds the robot Rickle, while Warūmon revives villains previously defeated by former Konami heroes. At the start the player chooses character groups made up of three different Konami characters, and Rickle can temporarily transform into one of them after collecting a special power-up. The roster includes Goemon, who throws his pipe like a boomerang, Simon Belmont with his whip, Getsu Fūma with a sword, Upa with a rattle and Bill Rizer with a spreader gun, while Vic Viper and Twinbee serve only in their shooter stages. Most levels are straightforward side-scrolling platforming, mixed with space shooter, driving and puzzle stages, and certain levels offer a choice of paths.

t_c0a899edf113.overview: Starring a super-deformed knight prince, this platform game was developed by KID and released by Takara. The hero, an island native, sets out to recover his island's stolen weapons and rescue a princess, crossing stages filled with dangerous fruit and vegetables such as human-sized bananas with bulging eyes. Stages do not scroll backward but often hold multiple paths and hidden goodies. The prince begins with a short sword; rings collected along the way buy projectile-firing weapons, and casinos offer a chance to gamble for more. A bag of seeds grows flowers he can climb, and flower tokens produce larger ones that lead to hidden platforms and doors. Companions join along the way, and certain treasure chests provide a protective sage. Between stages a board game serves as the frame for a quiz show whose rewards include health bonuses and warps to other levels.

t_c0bd15146ba0.overview: Adapted from the manga Be-Bop High School by Kazuhiro Kiuchi, a Famicom adventure from Data East stars the series' two rough-and-tumble high school friends, Hiroshi and Toru, who frequently cause trouble and start fights. Billed as a new kind of comical delinquent adventure, the story follows the pair as they search for the whereabouts of a student who has been carried off by an unknown party. Characters from the manga appear throughout, though some of them are renamed or restyled in the game version.

t_c0ea0c4b14b5.overview: An original story sets the Z Fighters against a new threat: Dende, the new god of Earth, detects a rise in Destron Gas, which destroys life cells. Goku, Gohan and Piccolo set out to wreck the gas devices and are later joined by Trunks and Vegeta, and King Kai reveals the mastermind to be Dr. Lychee, a Tuffle seeking revenge on the Saiyans for destroying his planet. Battles in this card battle RPG are dictated by randomly generated playing cards, each showing a star number, a character and a mark. There are no character levels; health and the number of usable cards grow through story events. Completing a specific card combination, an arrangement, triggers a special move, and pressing A or B just before an enemy special attack hits deflects or dodges it. Krillin, Yamcha, Tien and Chiaotzu appear as attack item cards. Single player.

t_c0f2657d3688.overview:
Superman casts the player as the titular hero attempting to protect Metropolis from Lex Luthor and exiled Kryptonian villains. Gameplay divides between a city map and side-scrolling action sequences. Players begin as Clark Kent, jumping and punching enemies, but entering a phone booth with enough power converts him into Superman. Transit options include superflight to landmarks on the city map or riding the subway with a free pass obtained from Jimmy Olsen.

Controlling Superman involves managing a power level that drops each time a super power is used; with too little power Clark cannot become Superman, and the game ends when it reaches zero. Powers include heat vision, super breath, super spin, super flight, and x-ray vision to detect hidden foes. Defeated enemies may leave power crystals that raise the power level, while red or green Kryptonite lowers it. Boss encounters include showdowns against Luthor and the Kryptonian villains.

t_c1183810b9fa.overview: Hwang Shinwei's follow-up to Magic Jewelry keeps the Columns formula of the original, in which falling blocks of three jewels are arranged into matching sets of three or more to remove them, and adds a number of new options. A menu screen lets the player start on any of the first nine stages and set certain jewel colors so that they give no points. A two-player mode is included, with an optional time limit called Flash. The music offers more tracks than the first game and can be switched off from the options.

t_c15150693ac7.overview: Set shortly after the first game, this Data East role-playing sequel hands the lead to a young boy living in an age when Hercules is already a legendary hero. Called by the queen to fight the Titans, the nameless hero leaves his aunt and village after learning that the last remaining offspring of the Titans has crowned himself king of darkness. Companions join along the way, including Centaurus, a young centaur searching for the god of courage, and a bronze goddess statue made by Hephaestus that travels with him to receive a soul, while the enigmatic Homeros supplies information about the world. A party system enters the series for the first time, joined by a day-and-night cycle, and the tragic, dramatic story draws on motifs from Greek mythology.

t_c1718c909bf7.overview: Chun, a small egg-shaped creature in a baseball cap, must clear each single-screen stage by trapping a band of pursuing aliens behind sliding doors. Stages are built from platforms linked by ladders. To set a trap, Chun approaches a door from its handle side, opens it by running across it, lures the aliens inside and shuts it before they escape; a trapped door cannot be opened again. The aliens follow fixed patterns: Namegon and Amechan take the most direct route, Invekun follows roundabout paths using ladders, and Otapyon shadows Chun's jumps. Touching an alien, a bomb or a nail is fatal, though Chun can jump over the aliens. Extra points come from trapping several aliens behind one door and from grabbing sweets that briefly appear, and some levels demand careful planning to avoid an unwinnable position.

t_c1783e75b9ff.overview:
Arranged as a side-scrolling, nonlinear cave maze, the environment requires players to navigate subterranean caverns set in the Andes Mountains. Controlling Pitfall Harry, the player seeks to locate the Raj diamond, rescue his niece Rhonda, free Quickclaw the Lion, and return to the entrance. Achieving this escape requires gathering items to restore Rhonda from stone, liberate Quickclaw, and secure a photograph of the Underground Kingdom that provides directions to the starting point.

Harry navigates hazards using three starting lives, which are lost upon touching adversaries or environmental dangers. The player moves, climbs, swims upward, jumps, and shoots enemies with a gun. Defeating hostiles and gathering items awards points, with extra lives earned at designated score thresholds. Hidden items, accessible only during certain jumps, include objects granting invulnerability, extra pistols, and crystal balls marked with playing card suits that unlock rock doors.

t_c17fe33bd4d7.overview:
Double Dragon is an action fighting game where players battle through the slums, factories and wooded outskirts of a city. Controlling martial artist Billy Lee, the player seeks to rescue his kidnapped girlfriend Marian from the Black Warriors gang and its mysterious Shadow Boss. Combat relies on punches, kicks, and advanced martial arts maneuvers, with the ability to level up to gain additional fighting techniques. Players can also pick up weapons, which include bats, whips, knives, and dynamite, or throw objects such as rocks, boxes, and oil drums.

Progressing through four side-scrolling stages requires clearing waves of thugs, navigating hazards like pits, and defeating bosses such as Abobo before time runs out. In the two-player mode, players challenge each other head to head rather than fighting through the stages together.

t_c1ed3d7517a4.overview: Pipemania puts the player in charge of a deep underground maze of pipes through which water is already flowing. The general idea is to keep the stream moving by adding the most appropriate piece of pipe ahead of it, choosing among cross pipes, straight pipes and points pipes, or connecting a storage tank along the way to slow things down. The pace gets hectic as the water picks up momentum, and as soon as one floor is done the next one begins, running a little faster. Originally titled Pipe V and credited as Pipe 5 on its title screen, the puzzle game was published for the Australian market by HES Interactive under the Pipemania name.

t_c2119fb41aaf.overview: Drawn from the folk tales of One Thousand and One Nights, this action role-playing adventure follows an amnesiac descendant of the magician Isfa who travels through time to rescue the princess Scheherazade from the evil wizard Sabaron and bring peace back to Arabia. The quest spans five chapters: four worlds, each with a palace where a demon must be defeated, then a final battle with Sabaron. At the outset the hero takes one of three classes, Fighter, Magician or Saint, each with different weapon strengths. On the overhead map enemies are fought in real time with swords, rods and spells, while moving between screens can trigger turn-based battles alongside up to two allies, with options to fight, escape or bribe. Time Gates link past, present and future, and towns hold shops, hotels, casinos, recruits and password saves at mosques.

t_c212b4845a3e.overview: Ten selections share the second volume of the Super Cartridge series from Thin Chen Enterprise, released under the Sachen name. Most are card games carried over from earlier releases: Omnibus Hearts, Fan Tan and Chinese Rummy come from The World of Card Games, while Max 2, Ghost Buster, 99 and Change Around come from Poker II. Hidden Chinese Chess, a 1989 Joy Van title, adds a board game to the lineup. Two versions of Fortune Telling, one in Chinese and one in English, complete the list and do not appear on either of the card collections.

t_c222cef4852e.overview: A 1993 ROM cartridge edition of the first Castlevania for the Japanese Family Computer, the game follows Simon Belmont, descendant of a legendary vampire hunter, into the castle of Count Dracula, who has suddenly reappeared 100 years after Simon's ancestor vanquished him. The castle is divided into six blocks of three stages each, 18 in all, and each block ends with a boss that must be beaten before time runs out. Simon fights with a whip, and backup weapons such as throwing knives, axes and holy water use hearts found by extinguishing candles or defeating enemies; only one backup weapon can be carried at a time. Compared with the original Famicom Disk version, this edition omits the name registration screen and saving and adds an easier difficulty mode.

t_c234d44d2cb5.overview: Shogi is presented as a tournament here, the title naming the Meijin Sen, a professional shogi tournament. The player takes part as one of its entrants against a diverse cast of participants, rising through the ranks by playing against each of them in turn. For anyone still learning, a separate training mode offers time to become familiar with the rules and tactics of shogi before facing the field. The matches themselves follow standard shogi rules, presented with characters and little animations.

t_c2a0d9f9403e.overview: A virtual pet-raising simulator, Chongwu Baobao hands the player the care of one of three dogs. An intro sequence frames the arrangement as an adoption, after which looking after the chosen dog becomes the ongoing task. The cartridge carries battery-backed RAM, so progress is saved and can be loaded again from the main menu. Nice Code Software developed the game and Shenzhen Nanjing Technology published it on Famicom cartridge; an English version titled Pet Dog functions identically but appears on plug-and-play systems, most of which cannot save progress.

t_c2bb0fcbaa17.overview: Gilgamesh must scale all 60 floors of a tower to rescue the maiden Ki from Druaga. On every floor he has to locate a key and use it to open the door leading onward, while monsters roam the maze. Each floor also hides a treasure that is revealed only after a specific task is completed, such as defeating certain enemies or entering a code with the controller. The mazes are randomized on each playthrough, so floor layouts change from one attempt to the next.

t_c2c51fb66a2d.overview: Two armies, led by Alm and Celica, come under the player's control in this tactical role-playing game set on the continent of Valentia, once divided between the Earth Mother Mila and the War Father Duma. Alm, a village boy, sets out to overthrow Desaix and drive Rudolf out of Zofia, while Celica, the exiled Princess Antheise of Zofia, embarks on a pilgrimage to discover Mila's whereabouts after the goddess vanishes. The overworld is freely navigable, with towns to visit and additional areas opening up as the story progresses. Units move across a grid-based battlefield, and battles are won by defeating all enemies on a map or killing a boss character. Characters can be promoted; Alm goes from fighter to hero, and Celica from priestess to princess.

t_c2f787aa37ff.overview:
Players control a young boy named Nemo as he journeys through two-dimensional, side-scrolling levels set within his surreal dreams. Moving across environments from left to right as well as vertically, the player searches for keys scattered across each area. These keys unlock the door at the exit, allowing Nemo to progress toward rescuing the good King of Slumberland from the wicked King of Nightmares.

While exploring, Nemo can feed candy to specific animals like frogs, gorillas, or moles to ride them and gain their special skills. Certain animal abilities are required to clear stages and bypass obstacles amidst constantly appearing enemies. Additionally, several creatures feature lifebars that differ from Nemo's, occasionally granting extra health to help endure hazards.

t_c2faf41ec7ec.overview: Bit Corporation's cartridge adaptation of the board game Othello is a contest of strategy and concentration built around one idea: outflanking the opponent. To outflank means to trap one or more of the opponent's discs in the middle of two of one's own, and trapped discs are flipped over to the capturing player's color. The object is to finish with a majority of the discs on the board showing that color. A single player can take on the computer at any of three skill levels, or two players can face each other using the controllers.

t_c327fdd5cd0c.overview: Rather than a straight conversion of the arcade hockey game, this unreleased NES version centers around a Quest Mode with role-playing elements. The player walks around an overworld map, exploring houses and stadiums and facing random encounters with rival hockey teams, and these matches provide experience and gold. Items include P Drinks, which provide a temporary speed and power boost, and hamburgers, which provide experience. Other items serve the adventure itself: apples can be given to an old man somewhere on the world map in exchange for an inner tube, which allows the player to cross bodies of water safely. The surviving prototype has a completable Quest Mode, although its role-playing elements are very low on content and game balance.

t_c37395508701.overview: Linus, an alien from the planet Linoleum, has crashed his spaceship at the bottom of an ocean on Earth, and the parts of his radio are scattered. To send an SOS signal back home and radio for help, he must gather up all of the missing radio parts. Play takes the form of a side-scrolling platformer in the mold of Mario Bros. The first stage is set underwater, where Linus has to ride rising bubbles to reach the surface, and after that the stages turn to more conventional platforming. The adventure later received a standalone sequel with a different story.

t_c37860593aa0.overview: Built around records of notable professional games, Igo Shinan is a Go study cartridge rather than a straightforward match against the computer. One mode replays a famous game automatically for viewing, while the other lets the player step through the moves by hand. The cartridge also offers a playing-strength assessment split into three levels: a beginner test covering ranks up to 2 kyu, an intermediate test spanning 4 kyu to 2 dan, and an advanced test for dan-level players. This first entry in the series carries 63 game records, divided evenly between classical games, modern games and handicap games.

t_c39974e5b32f.overview: Rising bubbles drive this puzzle game from C&E. Clusters of bubbles float upward, and the player steers them and places them so that they connect to matching-colored bubbles gathered along the top of the screen. When enough bubbles of the same color touch, they are cleared, and any free neighboring bubbles rise further, which allows for combos. The game ends when the accumulated bubbles reach the bottom area. Completing a level rewards the player with an erotic picture. The same design also appeared as Soap Panic and Bubble Bath Babes, and in a version with the adult content removed as Mermaids of Atlantis.

t_c39c634a554c.overview: Rally racing on tracks from around the world drives this Japanese edition of Championship Rally. The courses are set across numerous different terrains, along with a range of weather and track conditions. Many of the car's features can be customized, and those adjustments change how it behaves on each course. Steering follows a control scheme in the style of a radio-controlled car. Because the game is strictly single-player, only one car ever needs to be set up.

t_c3c034135936.overview: A reader of Weekly Shōnen Jump is pulled into a world where heroes from the magazine's manga live side by side, and that world is falling under the rule of a demon king. The adventure spans five areas, each with a present-day and a past version, and sixteen heroes such as Kenshiro, Son Goku and Tsubasa Oozora can be recruited by delivering requested items or defeating bosses; each hero can only fight within a set area. Encounters and boss battles play out as fighting, shooting, racing and sports minigames, and a hero who loses a decisive boss game dies. Once the area bosses fall, the recruited heroes face an alliance of thirteen villains in one-on-one, command-based duels in which the protagonist does not fight.

t_c3fe98857b69.overview: Adapted from the Jim Henson film, this top-down adventure has Sarah racing to free her infant brother Toby from Jareth the Goblin King before a thirteen-hour time limit expires. The limit appears as a clock in the top-right corner, and it doubles as Sarah's health, dropping rapidly whenever she takes damage, though some items replenish it; the Goblin King also turns up to drain time. Play mixes exploration, combat and puzzle-solving as Sarah navigates a series of mazes to find the pieces of a key. The creatures she befriends in the film, Hoggle, Ludo and Sir Didymus, can be called on by giving them heart items, after which they appear and help her defeat monsters for a while.

t_c406dd1c4887.overview: A boy and his shape-shifting alien friend Blobby set out to free the planet Blobania from an evil emperor who forces its residents to eat nothing but sweets. The adventure unfolds across connected single screens rather than scrolling levels, with the player controlling the boy, who can only move left and right; he cannot jump or swim, and long falls or hazards such as falling rocks and stalactites are fatal. His computer-controlled companion turns into useful tools when fed flavored candies, such as an apple candy that makes it a ladder, and a whistle returns it to its normal shape and calls it back. Treasures and diamonds pay for vitamins at a drugstore, which are used with a special Vitablaster on Blobania, and collecting enough coins grants extra lives. In this Jaleco release the jellybeans are candies, and the flavor names are puns meant to hint at their effects.

t_c4292188b94e.overview:
American football action unfolds on vertically scrolling fields displayed from a top-down perspective, with the offense always moving up the screen. A 1 Player Game sets the player against the computer, and a 2 Player Game sets two players against each other.

On offense, the ball carrier can run, throw a side pass to the left or right lateral receiver, or throw a forward pass to the forward receiver. Kicks are aimed with an arrow, and a field goal can be attempted when the goal post is in view at the snap. Gaining ten yards in four downs earns a new set of downs. When defending, the player chooses which of two defenders to control and can make flying tackles. Play starts at the high school level and moves up through college, pro, and playoff levels to the Super Bowl level; the 1 Player Game also allows any of these five levels to be chosen.

t_c44bf563e2f2.overview: Dan the Red is back for revenge, and Harry, the hammer-swinging carpenter, sets out once more after his girlfriend Donna is abducted. Originally released only in Japan as Daiku no Gen-san 2: Akage no Dan no Gyakushō, the game was later localized for the NES by Retro-Bit. Harry keeps the sprite, moveset and power-ups of the first game, but the adventure runs eight levels instead of five and places more emphasis on platforming than combat, with hazards such as lasers and spikes. Stages include a mall, a factory, a train in an underground tunnel and a secret base, and a pair of scrolling shoot-'em-up stages has Harry riding a rocket mallet. Bosses are typically Dan riding a giant robot shaped like an animal.

t_c4697bed888f.overview:
Destroying hostile industrial targets across island territories before an enemy empire can complete a devastating war machine forms the central goal of this shooter. Piloting a combat helicopter deployed from an aircraft carrier, the player targets six enemy factories located on islands across Bungeling Bay while shielding the carrier that serves as a home base.

Opposition mounts steadily from defensive gun turrets, guided missiles, fighter jets, and a battleship. Over time, surviving factories grow stronger and keep producing weapons, making swift demolition essential to prevent escalating counterattacks. One enemy island has a hidden area where the helicopter can land to steal bombs during operations.

t_c46a6e5de3d0.overview:
Three levels structure this single-player platformer, sending cat burglar Hawkins to steal two priceless Leonardo da Vinci works and the key component of an alchemy machine.

Controlling Hawk, the player runs, jumps, and crawls through tight passages while taking care to avoid electric eyes and pressure-sensitive floor panels that set off alarms. Enemies and enemy devices hinder progress across each area. To deal with hostile threats, the protagonist relies on his fists for close-range punches and can throw softballs to stun or knock foes off the screen. Softballs also trigger switches that momentarily disable electrical hazards, aiding Hawk as he searches for designated targets and navigates elevators, ropes, and platforms.

t_c49729dd020e.overview: An abridged Famicom adaptation of the DOS and Amiga adventure Dark Seed, made by Mars Production. The player controls Mike Dawson, who, after moving into a new house that is later found to be a gateway to a parallel universe, has an alien growing in his head and suffers a massive headache. He must go around figuring out what is going on. The storyline is drawn entirely from the original, though several screens are cut and the adventure is slightly shorter. Graphics taken from the Amiga version are compressed into a smaller bordered screen in mostly brown and green tones, while a single 15-second music loop plays throughout. The ending appears to be broken.

t_c4c289517ec2.overview: SASA walks on the ground or flies by using the recoil from the beam gun in its hands, so moving forward means shooting backward. The goal of each stage is to collect every energy pack while staying safe from enemy interference. Each shot uses a little energy, and enemy attacks or crashes into obstacles drain much more; when energy reaches zero, the game is over, as there are no extra lives. Every pack collected restores energy, but a pack hit by a shot is destroyed. Across 16 stages, gravity pulls in the early areas, buoyancy and currents act underwater, and the space stages bring near-weightlessness and finally a black hole. The Famicom version allows two players at once, with the second controlling NANA, and partners can transfer energy to each other.

t_c50e6add4fe7.overview: Viewed from overhead, this Famicom port of the Nichibutsu arcade game Kid's Horehore Daisakusen casts the player as one of the Booby Kids, who can instantly dig booby traps in front of where they stand. Hostile enemies roam the maze-like levels seeking out the kids, and the traps are used to bury them. Compared with the arcade original, the levels lean more on puzzle-solving. The 21 levels span different eras, from prehistory and feudal Japan to the World War II era, the modern era and the future, and each era has its own objects to collect: coconuts, ancient Japanese scrolls, radios, bags of money and computer monitors. Five bonus levels offer extra points.

t_c53f04b278c0.overview: Sailing in search of a legendary paradise called Dilmun, a party of adventurers is arrested on suspicion of spellcasting, because King Drake has declared all magic illegal, and is thrown into Purgatory stripped of everything. The ultimate goal of this fantasy role-playing game is to defeat Namtar, the villain manipulating the king, and restore light to the land. The party begins with four characters, either defaults or player-created, and its seven slots can be filled with recruited characters and summoned creatures. Leveling up grants points that must be assigned to attributes before a character grows stronger, and spells are learned by raising the matching magic skill. The Japanese console version keeps the original systems and world but uses entirely new music and sound effects and redesigned battle screens.

t_c551829a68ad.overview: Modeled on Sonic the Hedgehog, this Sachen platformer stars Chen, a pink dinosaur and the most intelligent member of his family, whose parents and brothers have fallen into the clutches of Dr. Crachi, the inventor of a time machine. Coins are scattered across every stage; a star is worth 50 coins, and 100 coins earn an extra life. When Chen is hit by an enemy, a projectile or spikes, he loses all his coins, up to two of which spin outward and can be picked up again, and a hit with no coins costs a life. Seven levels are spread across four worlds, most of them with multiple exits leading to different levels, and each level is cleared by running into a goal post.

t_c55b472b562c.overview: Googoo, a kid who appears to wear a karate uniform, is the hero of a Korean platformer that Zemina developed for the Famicom in 1992. He attacks by lifting rocks and throwing them at enemies or at pots that hold items: magic capsules, money (called "food"), and letters. Collecting all the letters to spell EXTRA earns an extra life. Pressing Select lets Googoo use special powers or turn temporarily into other characters, which consumes magic pills. Food is gathered in the levels or won in bonus minigames, and an item shop becomes available after quitting a minigame. The adventure spans seven worlds, each with a boss after a temple level, and a password gives direct access to each world.

t_c5b06c076d6d.overview: Virus was the working title of Nintendo's Dr. Mario, and these cartridges hold prototype builds from that stage of development; one of them carries EPROM labels dated 2-2-90 and sits in a Nintendo sample game pak labeled as a Tetris cartridge. The finished game is a falling-block puzzle: two-colored capsules drop into a medicine bottle populated by red, yellow and blue viruses, each capsule can be moved and rotated as it falls, and four matching colors in a row make capsule halves and viruses disappear. Several distinct prototypes are known, and their differences from the retail release are only partly documented; the first Virus build discovered, which turned up in Norway in 2008, has modified gameplay mechanics and a different cast of characters.

t_c5e83465904b.overview: Built on the Columns formula, Magic Cube drops blocks made of four pieces arranged in a 2x2 square rather than a column of three. Each piece carries one of four colors along with a symbol. When a falling block lands with part of it still hanging over a ledge, the loosened pieces can be steered elsewhere, and three identical pieces in a line are cleared for points. A combo of two or higher briefly summons a combo monster that can be squashed with a matching-color piece for extra points before it disappears. Beyond scoring, the main objective of each level is to clear a set number of specific line patterns, across 16 levels. Play is solo, against a second player, or against the computer.

t_c5f93341c78f.overview: Japanese comedian George Tokoro stars in this side-scrolling action game, heading home through a strange world where all kinds of things want to kill him, from flying fish skeletons to disembodied feet. The trip runs from a central city ward to his own mansion, and each ward or city forms a single stage whose position is marked with an arrow on an overall map before play begins. In the ward stages, a building at the far right end of the level holds a waiting boss; defeating it opens the goal doors, and each door warps to one of two fixed stages, so the route across the map can change from game to game. The main attack is a water pistol whose range shrinks as its gauge runs low, and he is also armed with his sunglasses.

t_c612551b4cca.overview: A lone soldier pushes through enemy territory with one ultimate goal: lobbing a hand grenade into the enemy's fort. The fight starts on foot against infantry, and at a certain point the soldier can take over a tank for a stretch of tank warfare. The light tank is nimble but easily destroyed, while the heavy tank is slower yet survives one hit from a light tank; a single shot from a heavy tank destroys either type. A tank struck by a fatal shot must be abandoned within a few seconds, or a life is lost. The fort, a brick-barricaded tank that fires mortars, can only be damaged on foot by tossing a grenade over the barricade, after which an enemy soldier waves a white flag in surrender. Each new round returns to the infantry battle with quicker, deadlier enemies.

t_c63d0b04df0b.overview: Like its predecessor, this role-playing game presents battles from the side in the style of Final Fantasy. The adventure runs from Earth to the planet Golgotha, on to another world, back to Golgotha and finally to the M78 Nebula. Experience points do not exist: levels rise when particular bosses are defeated, when companions join or leave the party, and at key story events. Capsule monsters are shared by the whole party, with up to three of each kind carried at once. When every ally's Color Timer has turned red, the party can unleash a combined special attack that instantly defeats all enemies, giving the familiar transformation time limit a tactical role in combat.

t_c6571bdad3a5.overview: Piloting a starship over the surface of a planet, the player fires at formations of bizarre alien amoeba, egg-throwing birds, pterosaur-like creatures and UFOs while avoiding their projectiles. A pseudo-3D scrolling background with parallax effects gives a sense of depth, and the ship handles with simulated inertia, carrying momentum as it is steered. Two guns are available: a slow double shot that can be fired without limit and a fast single shot with a limited supply. The cartridge brings the 1983 arcade shoot 'em up by Kawa Denshi Giken to the Family Computer.

t_c68d679ecdf7.overview: Planned by Namco as a role-playing follow-up to the cutesy Splatterhouse Wanpaku Graffiti platformer, this nearly finished project once again puts the player in Rick Taylor's shoes, in a story set in the present day. It plays as a traditional JRPG with many spells, and Rick must complete tasks in each town or area he reaches before eventually clearing an entire island, Thorn Island, of monsters. Jennifer joins the party from the moment the Pumpkin King is defeated, and other companions include Grady, a traveling guitarist searching for his mother, Melton, a human mutated by ooze, and Damiyan, a young boy with occult powers. Souls dropped by enemies can be equipped one per character and summoned through the Channeling command. The figure behind the zombie outbreak turns out to be Dr. West.

t_c6e99e697ce4.overview: Ocean's European NES conversion follows the arcade original more closely than the Japanese and North American NES releases, differing from them in level layouts and in two-player alternating play. Bubby and Bobby set out to defeat the Dark Shadow and rescue the Rainbow Islands, a chain of ten islands, each with a different theme. Instead of bubbles, the heroes release rainbows that act as weapons, makeshift platforms and item collectors. The goal in every level is to reach the top, and dawdling is dangerous because water starts to rise from the bottom of the stage. Collecting seven different-colored small diamonds on an island and finishing the round earns a big diamond.

t_c7577e59dbcf.overview: Billy and Jimmy Lee travel the world in search of three Sacred Stones in this beat 'em up for one or two simultaneous players, fighting from the United States through China, Japan and Italy to a final stage in Egypt. Two-player play offers an A mode in which the players cannot harm each other and a B mode with friendly fire. Punch and kick buttons are joined by a dash, a running jump kick and a midair somersault that throws enemies. Instead of lives, the party grows: Chin Seimei, a Chinese martial arts master, and Yagyu Ranzou, head of a ninja clan, join after being beaten as bosses, and the Select button switches between fighters, each with his own techniques, health and speed. In the Japanese release, the brothers seek the stones to become the world's strongest fighters, and the final boss is a resurrected Cleopatra.

t_c7a32a1439ef.overview: Made for Famiclone-based educational computers, the Bravesoft program offers a somewhat accurate recreation of the Windows 2000 experience on Famicom hardware. Most of the applications on its desktop do not function; opening one instead tells the user what that application does on the real Windows 2000. The applications that do work seem to come from other educational computer software or were created by Bravesoft itself. Several versions exist in Chinese or Russian, most of which change only the title screen, while the Russian-language SuborWin 2000 adds more applications such as Poker and Minesweeper. If the software stands idle for long enough, a screensaver featuring the Bravesoft logo appears until a key is pressed.

t_c7d5e1779137.overview: A pink dinosaur named Asmik-kun stars in this platform action adventure for a single player. His quest is to recover six fragments so that he can wake the dragon ruler of the world and turn Asmik Land into a paradise. Before each level, an overhead map guides him to the next stage, and the levels themselves follow a run-and-jump structure built around platforming. The same pink dinosaur is known by another name in the English release of a related handheld adventure.

t_c87a653d1067.overview: Time travel drives this side-scrolling platformer. On the way to see his girlfriend, Haruka, the young hero is ambushed, and the time-traveling villain Professor Time carries her off. The hero gives chase through the ages, running and jumping across eras that range from prehistoric times to the far future and battling dinosaurs, samurai and aliens along the way. His main weapon is a baseball cap: thrown forward, it returns like a boomerang, and jumping while it comes back makes it circle around him for a short time. Collecting enough chimes brings out a skateboard, which grants destructive power and invincibility.

t_c89bd74c1ff0.overview: A reworking of Namco's arcade games Rally-X and New Rally-X, this 1988 Famicom game by Hwang Shinwei was published by Chi Chi Toy Co. under titles including Mihun Che and Super Car. Driving through a giant maze, the player gathers flags while dodging enemy cars until every flag is collected. Dropped trails make pursuing cars spin out until the trail disappears, but fuel is limited and drains faster while trails are being laid. Diagonal movement makes flags easier to reach, yet the computer-controlled cars are much faster and more aggressive than in the arcade original, constantly homing in on the player's exact location. The type of trail changes from stage to stage, and the original's bonus stages are left out.

t_c8c2b84e6bf8.overview:
Circuits viewed from an overhead perspective frame the competitive action, with each race requiring drivers to complete five laps. Competitors guide Formula One-style vehicles across tracks that fit entirely on the screen without scrolling. The winner of a race earns advancement to the next course, while computer-controlled opponents contest the remaining positions. Up to two players can compete simultaneously.

Hazards populate the courses as participants progress, including tornadoes and puddles of oil that cause temporary loss of steering control. Drivers can also gather wrenches scattered along the road surface, trading a pair collected during a winning heat to increase top speed, boost acceleration, or improve tire traction.

t_c92d5d5b7eb2.overview: Rather than chasing a final villain, this role-playing adventure centers on the hero's moral self-improvement in Britannia, the realm ruled by Lord British. The quest is to understand and practice the Eight Virtues: Honesty, Compassion, Valor, Justice, Sacrifice, Honor, Spirituality and Humility. Actions raise or lower these virtues, and shrines scattered about Britannia grant enlightenment to those who meditate there and chant the proper mantra. Becoming an Avatar ultimately means descending into the Stygian Abyss to gain access to the Codex of Ultimate Wisdom. The cartridge version has completely redone graphics and music and fewer dialogue options. Spell-casting is simplified so spells no longer need to be mixed, combat adds an automated option, companions beyond the four in the party wait at a hostel at Castle Britannia, and the character Julia is replaced by Julius.

t_c95a2b3989b7.overview: An unfinished build of a planned NES edition of Super Kick Off, built on the codebase of the earlier NES Kick Off. The prototype's new work is concentrated in its presentation: a reworked intro with a new logo, different company graphics and credits, and an intro screen with a crowd sample and the box art. The menus largely follow the original game, though the language selection is missing, some areas are corrupted or absent, and choosing one of the cups leads to a blank screen. Matches play essentially like Kick Off, with no noticeable graphical changes; as in that game, the ball does not stick to a player's feet but is kicked ahead as he runs.

t_c95c7f7eff3e.overview: It is Bugs Bunny's 50th birthday anniversary, but his uninvited friends grow envious and decide to keep him from getting to his party. In this side-scrolling platform game, Bugs swings a mallet to defeat enemies, deflect certain projectiles and destroy bricks, and he can land on top of enemies without being hurt. Hearts restore health and carrots add bonus points. Most levels end with a mallet showdown against a Warner Brothers cartoon character such as Foghorn Leghorn, Sylvester or the Tasmanian Devil, while Daffy Duck can only be avoided on the way to a carrot that leads to the next level. A minigame after each level awards extra lives. This entry is a pre-release build of the game released as The Bugs Bunny Birthday Blowout.

t_c9614b2884d4.overview: Four sporting events make up this home adaptation of the arcade multi-event game: clay shooting, archery, triple jump and high jump, the last of which was missing from the earlier cartridge in the series. In clay shooting, targets appear on the left and right and must be hit with quick presses; archery asks the player to set the arrow's firing angle before releasing it; the triple jump combines a running approach with timing the takeoff. In the high jump, the bar stays at one height during a lap but rises with each new lap. Players compete for points and must beat a qualifying mark to advance, and clearing every event leads into a harder round. The dedicated controller from the earlier release is required to play.

t_c9854808c811.overview: Four games share this single cartridge: Pac-Man, Sidewinder, Duck Maze and Othello. Sidewinder is a vertically scrolling shooter for one player or two players cooperatively; destroyed enemy vehicles leave power-ups, and some of them refill an "Exx" counter that serves as both health and fuel. In Duck Maze the player controls a duck that guides an egg downward through 20 levels by moving or destroying blocks, losing one of three lives whenever the egg touches an enemy or breaks after falling too far. Pac-Man and Othello round out the collection.

t_c993f65ae3dd.overview: Sachen's arithmetic tutor is meant for children from 7 to 15 years old, who can work through its exercises step by step. Topics cover addition, subtraction, multiplication and division of integers and fractions, linear equations with one unknown, and compound exercises. Each question carries a two-minute limit, and answers are typed on an on-screen keyboard. A separate Mathematic Blocks game has the player remove blocks in combinations that match equations, with five minutes per level: each valid combination earns 100 points, while trying to remove blocks that cannot be removed or do not match costs 50 points. By the time the clock runs out, a good part of the blocks must already be gone.

t_c998118e3750.overview: Behind the wheel of one of two Formula One cars, the player races on a variety of tracks lined with landmark scenery, with a 3D look created from 2D sprites. Two laps of each course must be finished within the time limit to advance, and points are awarded for distance traveled. Cars use a two-speed manual transmission with low and high gears, and completing the first lap adds time. Three skill levels hold five tracks each, and on the fifth track of every level the race never ends while the time extensions shrink until the game is over. Hitting other cars or roadside objects destroys the car and costs several seconds, and taking bends too fast causes skids that can send it off the road.

t_c9d93965eff8.overview: Kunio's Nekketsu High School and three other Japanese teams, joined by Oklahoma High School from America, square off in five rule-free athletic events in this Kunio-kun sports game, with the most gold medals deciding the winner. The events are 400 m hurdles that can be jumped, slid under or smashed; hammer throw golf on an 820-yard course; a one-on-one swimming battle royale in which air runs low underwater; rooftop jumping between buildings by long jump, pole vault and unicycle on ropes; and Hachamecha Judo, where draining an opponent's spirit unlocks big moves. Medals also buy power-up items at shops. Normal mode plays all five events, Short mode three and Practice mode one, and up to four players can join without a four-player adapter, while Oklahoma High School stays computer-controlled.

t_c9f8a14ebf45.overview: Themed on the Paris-Dakar Rally, this racing game changes its content greatly from area to area, mixing in action and shooting. Before the rally begins, the driver must find a sponsor in Japan, buy a car and complete training. Early stages are city drives, one a free-roaming maze where oil dropped behind the car turns rival cars aside. Side-view stages follow, with shooting from the third through the sixth stage, and at times the driver gets out on foot to press a button that opens a blocked road. Later come a bridge with an underwater section, a desert full of camels, scorpions and tornadoes, a forced-scrolling wilderness under air attack, and a narrow coastal road. Crashes, running out of fuel or exceeding a stage's time limit end the game, with unlimited continues and passwords, and finishing first overall brings the ending.

t_ca108960e111.overview: Built to plug into the special slot on Family Noraebang, the Korean karaoke cartridge for the Famicom from Daou Infosys and Daewoo, this song pack adds new material to sing along with. The base cartridge holds an initial selection of 56 songs, and song packs like this one expand that library. Expansion data is identified by the main program through a header reading "OPEN FAMILY SONG". As the title states, the pack contributes 32 songs, played back through the base cartridge's own sound chip and selected and sung with its karaoke menu and microphone.

t_ca1d3b4aecfb.overview: Wario and his monsters have taken control of the Peaceful Woods, once a peaceful area for sprites and gentle creatures, and Toad sets out to defeat him. Toad moves across the playing field on top of the fallen objects; he can pick up individual objects or lift entire stacks and place them elsewhere, kick objects across the field and scurry up the sides of stacks. Levels are cleared by using bombs to destroy groups of enemies: three or more objects of the same color placed adjacent to one another form a match, with at least one being a bomb. A sprite drops the bombs from the top, and Thwomps can descend several rows. Clearing the field advances to the next round, and the game ends if the field fills up and traps Toad. A VS mode lets two players compete.

t_ca5335d3e8e2.overview: Sokoban-style block pushing meets mahjong tiles in this puzzle game, whose title means "Forbidden City." On a single screen full of oversized mahjong tiles, the player must reach the exit, pushing the blocking tiles out of the way. Pushing tiles of like designs into each other makes them vanish and clears a path to the exit. Certain tiles cannot be pushed at all, while the wind and dragon tiles turn any tile that touches them into their own design and render it immovable, so a careless push can seal off the route.

t_cab6597eba2c.overview: A nameless young man from an ancient village is sent to find the lair of a vicious monster that has been attacking his home and to defeat it. On his return he learns that imperial troops have abducted some of the villagers, and he sets out to uncover the Empire's true motives and solve a larger mystery. Much of the play follows the Dragon Quest pattern: the hero travels a large world map, visits towns and dungeons, faces bosses, and battles random monsters in turn-based fights viewed from a first-person perspective. The major addition is a layer of strategy battles, in which the hero must recruit knights and fight whole armies of enemies on a much larger scale.

t_cad0ca7dc40c.overview: Hummer Team's 1993 Famicom port of Street Fighter II: Champion Edition, published by Yoko Soft, plays like an upgraded version of the team's earlier Street Fighter II: The World Warrior port. Unlike other bootleg ports, it includes the whole roster of the original game, and each fighter is joined by a clone with a different name, portrait and palette, such as Animal for Blanka, Amy for Chun-Li and Big Gun for Zangief. Some characters use different special-move commands than in the original game, and the computer opponents seem easier than in the earlier port. Three difficulty settings can be selected on the title screen, though the ending is the same on each. Most fighter and stage graphics are taken from Super Fighter III, while the stage music comes from the earlier Street Fighter II port.

t_caf31dfcfc91.overview:
Dirk the Daring journeys through a castle to defeat Singe the Dragon and rescue Princess Daphne. Guiding the protagonist through two-dimensional, side-scrolling stages, the player can make Dirk walk, crawl, or jump forward while finding and utilizing diverse weapons to eliminate hostile creatures. Dirk maintains two resource meters, one permitting him to generate light and another tracking the damage he can sustain.

After the Drawbridge and the Entrance Hall, an Elevator Shaft hub leads to stages such as the Gold Mines, the Hall of the Grim Reaper, and Singe's Cavern, alongside the Treasury, where gold can be reclaimed from the Lizard King. Multiplayer allows participants to alternate turns controlling Dirk in a competitive pursuit of high scores, which are recorded on a top-scores screen.

t_cb177f442712.overview: A prince of Arabia sets out to rescue a kidnapped princess in a platform game made up of four stages. Each stage holds six jars, and collecting every one clears it; the jars bear letters that, in this home version, spell assorted words beyond the arcade original's ARABIAN. The prince wears a sword but fights hand to hand with kicks, defeating enemies in a single hit yet losing a life on any contact, and kicking three or more enemies at once makes him invincible for a short time. Three lives are given. The backgrounds are fully colored, there is no ending, and clearing the fourth stage, where touching the princess no longer ends the stage early, starts a second loop. Two-player play is supported.

t_cb3ed8bdd5f8.overview: Jack and Ryu, two hot-blooded kung fu boys, take on the demon clan that has seized Chinese Land in this action role-playing game, which adds RPG elements to the stage-clear action of the first game. The world is explored from a top-down view like traditional RPGs. Ordinary encounters switch to fixed-screen action fights, won by defeating the required number of enemies to earn experience points and money, while major bosses are fought in command-selection battles. Striking rocks and obstacles can release items or question-mark balls that aid the heroes. The final foe is the demon king of the demon army, based at Kunlun Mountain. In one-player mode Jack is the hero, and in two-player mode Ryu joins him, with both characters moving and fighting together.

t_cb3f4bf9c8b5.overview: In the Salad Kingdom, a peaceful land whose inhabitants are all anthropomorphic foods, the royal advisor Minister Pumpkin stages a coup and kidnaps Princess Tomato, and her father King Broccoli dies of grief. Before his passing, the king sends Sir Cucumber the knight to rescue her. Along the way he is aided by his sidekick Percy the baby persimmon and by a resistance force led by Prince Lettuce, the princess's younger brother, in the fight to stop Pumpkin and his Farmies. Play resembles a text adventure: the possible commands appear as fixed buttons lining both sides of the screen. The game consists mostly of still screens, broken up by rounds of "finger wars", and the only way to lose is by failing to beat Minister Pumpkin at finger wars.

t_cb65633a45ac.overview: After the history of humanity has ended, dominion over the planet has returned to the demons, until invading robots begin a war to seize the demon world for machine rule. In this post-apocalyptic role-playing game the player commands the demon side against the robot invaders. Turn-based battles are viewed from a third-person perspective, and both sides can use magic or physical attacks; some enemy spells poison creatures, and a creature left poisoned too long will eventually die. The player controls two groups of four monsters, one active during the day and the other at night, and an inactive group recovers no HP or MP until its next phase. The Famicom version lacks the monster encyclopedia found in the other versions.

t_cb662b7f2920.overview: Four lakes host a series of bass fishing tournaments, and the angler advances only by ending each day, which runs from sunrise to sunset, with a large number of bass at a high average weight. Pike, rainbow trout and brown trout can also be hooked but do not count toward the standings. Fishing is shown from an overhead perspective: a power meter sets the strength of each cast, the lure is worked in the water to entice a bite, and a hooked fish must be reeled in carefully so the line does not break. Lure types and colors vary in effectiveness with weather and time of day, and different parts of a lake pay off at different hours. Passwords awarded after each tournament record rank, the next event, total bass caught and average weight.

t_cb6ecfa50995.overview: Riding the flying cloud Kintoun, the hermit Michael Chen sets out on a training journey in this horizontally scrolling shooter, defeating enemies along the way. One button fires the main shot and the other unleashes magic. Specific enemies and formations drop items that strengthen the shot, raise speed, add rapid fire or grant extra lives. Defeating the two or three mid-bosses in each round opens a door, and entering it lets the player choose a magic spell to use; the Famicom version offers spells that differ from the arcade original. Touching enemies, taking hits or being squeezed off the left edge of the screen by terrain costs a life. The Famicom release spans six stages plus a hidden stage.

t_cb988cb03fa2.overview: Lord Maliss kidnaps the Prince and sends Snow White fleeing into the forest, where Blossom, one of the Seven Dwarfelles, endows her with special flower powers. Across four side-scrolling stages, the heroine fights enemies by twirling her magic cape with the B button, and she can take five hits before collapsing. A select screen lets the player activate powers with A: a moving petal platform ferries her across a lake, the powers of Marina shoot water jets out of holes in the land, and the powers of Muddy make a boulder disappear. The route runs from the Seven Pines past a cave with bouncing boulders, waterfall ledges and magma-spouting volcanoes to the maze of a castle, where Mother Nature advises her to enter the Looking Glass. Tied to an animated film sequel from Filmation Associates, the game was never released and survives as a prototype.

t_cb9fcb429ed3.overview: Martial arts stunt master Jackie Chan brawls against hordes of enemies on a quest to save his sister, fighting through five levels that each end with a boss. Frogs carry either power-ups or rice bowls and must be hit to release them; power-ups grant a special type of attack for a limited number of uses, while rice bowls restore health. Jackie can also charge a beam-like special attack usable up to five times. Most defeated enemies drop green orbs, and collecting 30 replenishes his life, but dying costs all orbs and power-ups. Only one life is given, with up to five continues at first. Bells in the levels lead to 30-second bonus stages of jumping on clouds or hitting statues, and the points earned can buy extra lives and special attacks.

t_cbb4e596024e.overview: Mappy, a police mouse, is tasked with recovering stolen items from a mansion that serves as a hideout for a gang of thieving cats. A round is cleared by collecting all 10 stolen items, which form five pairs, and taking both items of a pair consecutively multiplies the value of the second. Goro, large and red, leads the gang, and the smaller pink Meowky cats are his underlings. A trampoline breaks if Mappy bounces on it four consecutive times. Doors can be opened or closed by both Mappy and the cats, while only Mappy can open a microwave door. Bells hung above trampolines can be knocked loose to stun cats below, and bonus rounds challenge Mappy to pop as many balloons as possible in a short time.

t_cbbf58ada843.overview:
Three levels structure this single-player platformer, sending cat burglar Hawkins to steal two priceless Leonardo da Vinci works and the key component of an alchemy machine.

Controlling Hawk, the player runs, jumps, and crawls through tight passages while taking care to avoid electric eyes and pressure-sensitive floor panels that set off alarms. Enemies and enemy devices hinder progress across each area. To deal with hostile threats, the protagonist relies on his fists for close-range punches and can throw softballs to stun or knock foes off the screen. Softballs also trigger switches that momentarily disable electrical hazards, aiding Hawk as he searches for designated targets and navigates elevators, ropes, and platforms.

t_cbcb2c9898b6.overview: Rather than a game, this package turns the Family Computer into a programmable home computer running a dialect of BASIC enhanced for game development. The set pairs the cartridge with a keyboard that plugs into the console's expansion connector and a programming textbook. Commands cover sprites, animation, backgrounds, musical sequences and gamepads, and predefined characters can be combined to build sprite characters and background screens with little effort; the interpreter only supports integers. A start-up menu offers the GAME BASIC programming mode and a BG GRAPHIC editor for designing background screens. Programs can be kept temporarily in the cartridge and are saved to and loaded from cassette tape, using a recorder such as the Famicom Data Recorder.

t_cc0631696264.overview: An adventurous Arabian prince sets out to rescue the princess from her palace in this platform game, which plays out in the form of chapters of a book. Over the course of the journey the prince will sail seas, crawl through caves and fly magic carpets, and along the way he must find and take the letters that spell out ARABIAN. Although the hero is described as an Arabian boy, the adventure is set in Persia. Sunsoft developed and released this Famicom version of its arcade game only in Japan, and the game supports both single-player and multiplayer play.

t_cc1677a321e6.overview: Aimed at younger players and played on side A of the Family Trainer mat, this hopping game has the player guide a baby kyonshi, a hopping vampire child, back to its waiting parents. An amidakuji ladder lottery picks the route, and the player jumps from foothold to foothold on the chosen stage while holding the kyonshi stance. Not every path ends happily: some lead to bad endings in which the baby runs into a priest. Up to three people can play at the same time, and with each one taking a different course, every ending can be seen in a single session.

t_cc70e3de4e1c.overview: In this beat 'em up sequel, the hero Johnny Thomas is a former police officer turned private investigator who stands alone against the drug syndicates. His investigation into illegal drug routes leads him to an international criminal organization known as Hawk. Where the first game took place entirely inside a five-story pagoda, the action now spreads across six stages set on a train, in a warehouse, on a boat, on an airplane, in a mansion and finally at the Hawk drug plant, each ending with its own boss. Thomas keeps all of his moves from the original and gains an uppercut and an over-the-shoulder throw, performed after crouching for an extended period. Clearing a stage restores only part of his vitality, but Stamina X potions dropped by certain enemies refill more along the way.

t_cc88c2dc7c7e.overview: Horse racing is approached here as a pure simulation: there is no racing for the player to control and no gambling. Instead, the player adjusts the parameters of each race and of the horses competing in it, changing statistics such as fatigue, age and the weight of the jockey. With the settings in place, the player watches the race play out and observes which horse wins. The title draws on racing vocabulary, keiba being the Japanese word for horse racing and honmei a term for the favorite to win.

t_cc929a22861b.overview: After his schemes were exposed in the first game, the Mito domain elder Ando escapes and flees to America, and Mito Koumon sets out across the world after him with his retainers Sukesan and Kakusan. The six stages take place in America, Germany, Italy, India, China and Hawaii. At the start of each stage the player chooses whether to control Sukesan or Kakusan, then investigates the town, using the Select button to show evidence to people on the street or inside buildings. Each culprit is judged by presenting two or three pieces of evidence of wrongdoing or weapons that exploit a weakness; the correct item makes the villain prostrate himself and closes the case. A trader buys unneeded items, and casinos replace the earlier game's shooting gallery. Running out of time ends the game unless a travel diary allows continuing.

t_cce43eb18c38.overview:
Controlling the hero Mega Man, the player runs, slides, and fires a blaster to defeat hostile creatures across several stages. The protagonist must retrieve energy crystals from the mining worlds by vanquishing eight berserk Robot Masters. Stages can be tackled in any order chosen by the player. Defeating a boss yields a specialized weapon that can be selected at will, allowing players to target the specific vulnerabilities of other bosses. Pickups found throughout each level replenish health, weapon energy, and extra lives, while stored tanks restore life energy completely.

Sliding allows players to slip under barriers and enemy fire. Mega Man is also assisted by Rush, a canine companion who transforms into a springboard, jet, or submarine to aid traversal. Periodic duels against the mini-boss Break Man open passageways. After defeating the initial Robot Masters, the player revisits four sites to battle Doc Robots before infiltrating a final fortress.

t_cd13cf2bd642.overview: Based on the baseball manga by Yasuichi Oshima, this side-scrolling action game leaves the ballpark behind for a demon realm, where the heroes race against a mysterious dragon army. The player controls a baseball superhero named Batsu, who uses baseballs to defeat opponents that include machinery, humanoids and animals. Being hit once reverts him to his normal form, Terii, who swats at enemies with a baseball bat, and defeating foes in this form results in a larger energy bar. The cartridge also contains an unusually large number of hidden tricks and secret codes.

t_cd4b095a47dd.overview: Faces of Sanrio characters, among them Hello Kitty, Hangyodon and Pokopon, serve as the pieces in this falling-block, match-three puzzle game. Lining up identical blocks vertically or horizontally in rows of three or more clears them from the field. From the menu, a single player can choose among three play styles, each with a different goal, and can also change the music and the block theme. A two-player versus mode is included, as is a mode with a very small grid and very large faces suited to younger children.

t_cd554f9ebadd.overview: Drawing on the setting of Gradius, this turn-based space war strategy game begins after humanity founds its first star nation in the Procyon system and its planets come under attack from an unknown life form.
