Each scenario contains several star systems, each with its own square-grid battle map, and planets occupied there become sources of income. Funds pay for planetary investment, commanders, new units and supplies. Every unit is a group of ten craft drawn from sixteen types, and carrier-based fighters and humanoid battle machines need a space carrier in their fleet. Turns run through phases such as production and movement, and combat in a chosen system lasts three alternating turns. Victory means invading enemy star systems and capturing the enemy home planet. One player can face the computer, or two can play against each other as humanity and the Bacterians.

t_cd68857b70c8.overview:
Burai Fighter tasks the player with shooting robo-mutants, half robot and half living flesh, to stop the Burai's conquest of the universe across seven bases. Controlling an unnamed protagonist equipped with a proton pack, the player floats through two-dimensional space environments. In the side-view levels the screen scrolls in changing directions, requiring the character to avoid getting caught against the screen edges, and a boss waits at the end; in two top-view levels the goal is to destroy the bases. Holding the attack button locks the aiming angle so the player can fire independently of movement. Hidden rooms may contain power-ups.

Beginning with a basic weapon, the protagonist can acquire upgrades such as ring, laser, and missile armaments, and Cobalt Bombs clear the screen of ordinary enemies. Three difficulty settings are available: Eagle, Albatross, and Ace. Higher difficulties feature faster and more aggressive enemies, different adversaries, adjusted bonus multipliers, and alternate endings. Level progression can be resumed using passwords.

t_cd8d91ddb0ec.overview: A sorcerer named Dana sets out to retrieve Solomon's Key and restore the world to light after demons were accidentally released. His path runs through the rooms of Constellation Space, grouped by the twelve Zodiac constellations, and each room is passed by acquiring a key to the door that leads to the next. Dana can run, jump, create or destroy orange blocks adjacent to him, and cast fireballs to destroy demons, all while enemies keep spawning and a countdown timer runs. Reaching each key and door means building and breaking blocks in the right order. This version holds 64 levels in total, 15 of them secret plus a final level, and shows a deviation-value score on the game over screen.

t_cda5ad0a5cb0.overview: Xiangqi, the strategy board game commonly known in the West as Chinese chess, is adapted here for one or two players. The game represents a battle between two armies, and the primary object is to checkmate the enemy's general. Against the computer, three levels of difficulty range from easy to hard, and a two-player mode is also available. Play proceeds turn by turn: the player picks a piece and sets it on a valid target location. The usual distinctive rules apply, such as the cannon, which must jump to capture, and the river and palace areas that restrict the movement of some pieces. While the computer decides on its next move, the music briefly freezes. This common multicart version drops the Micro Genius credits splash screen in favor of a plainer title screen.

t_cdc623502c19.overview: A first-person dungeon crawl, this cartridge adapts the third original Wizardry scenario, Legacy of Llylgamyn, renumbered as the second entry for its Japanese console release. The City of Llylgamyn is threatened by the violent forces of nature, with earthquakes and volcanic rumblings endangering everyone, and only by seeking the dragon L'Kbreth can it be saved. The six-level dungeon is a volcano, so the party journeys upward rather than downward. Parties of up to six characters explore, and characters transferred from the first scenario are reborn as weaker descendants, though newly created characters can also play. Some floors bar entry by alignment, so a good party and an evil party must both be raised. This version also adds items and raises the experience earned from enemies.

t_ce170710e8d0.overview: Following up its 1988 predecessor, this historical simulation opens in the year 189 and, unlike the earlier game, lets the player freely choose a ruler from seven candidates. Commands still draw on order sheets, though a new appointment command needs none, and reconnaissance costs one sheet but allows unlimited viewing of castles at home and abroad. Generals now have levels, and formations can be changed at the start of each battle. A disaster prevention command spends funds to guard against floods and droughts, while a new strategy command can lure away other states' generals, sow discord between rulers or form alliances. Defeating an enemy ruler no longer hands over that ruler's entire domain. The game is for one player.

t_ce2f4153851f.overview: Despite the numeral in its catalog name, this prototype is a localized version of the shooter Exerion rather than a sequel. A starship fires at enemies on the screen while avoiding their projectiles, facing formations of bizarre alien amoeba, egg-throwing birds and pterosaur-like creatures, as well as UFOs. The ship has a sense of inertia, carrying momentum as it is steered, and a pseudo-3D scrolling background with parallax effects gives a sense of depth. Two weapons are available: a slow double shot with unlimited use and a fast single shot that is limited. Compared with the Japanese Famicom version, the build uses larger ROMs for better graphics and music, including new title screen music.

t_ce303a32704d.overview: A side-scrolling action game, Little Lancelot sends its hero on a long quest that ends in a dream of knighthood. The journey begins in treacherous marshland in search of the legendary Viking Ring of Peace, passes through a forest inhabited by cutthroats and thieves, and drops into underground caverns and a deadly maze. Crossing a stormy sea and battling a hostile Viking armada leads to Camelot, where Arthur's Hall lies beyond a labyrinth of corridors and passageways. Along the way the hero can walk, jump and throw things at opponents, facing pit traps, water hazards and archers embedded in the background. Combat and action platforming are mixed throughout, with many enemies to conquer.

t_ce7beb4e4a8d.overview: Defending a castle against waves of enemy tanks is the task in this Gamtec maze game, also known as Super City Tank, which is a direct clone of Battle City. The player or players control tanks and must destroy every enemy tank in a stage before losing all their lives or letting the castle be destroyed. Two enemy types appear: gray tanks that are easy to destroy, and yellow tanks that move faster, shoot more projectiles and are much harder to knock out. Most power-ups match those of Battle City, joined by two new ammunition items, a yellow missile and a blue missile, which both destroy every tank they collide with, although the blue one leaves tiles intact. Unlike the original, touching an enemy tank destroys both it and the player.

t_ce9c60ae1310.overview: Juubei, a silent swordsman who was found fifteen years earlier as a scarred infant inside a glowing capsule that fell from the sky, leads this role-playing adventure through a fantastical version of Sengoku-era Japan. Joined by his destined companions Ryuuhime, Wolf and Iwan, he sets out to crush the ambitions of the Makai-shu. Random encounters fill the field and dungeons, while some powerful foes appear as visible symbols, and turn order follows each character's speed so allies and enemies act interleaved. Psychic powers draw on their own energy pool, many attacks carry elemental properties, helpers can be summoned with a command, and Juubei learns up to seven sword techniques as he gains levels. The battle system largely follows the developer's earlier Kaijuu Monogatari.

t_cf1f446022f3.overview: A yellow armadillo in a red hat, Billy the Shell, stars in this platformer. Between levels he travels a map of small squares that are captured one at a time and can then be crossed freely; larger picture squares start action stages that must be cleared to pass, and a character roaming the map triggers a boss battle when met, with victory opening the next world. Billy can walk and jump, but enemies can be attacked only by rolling into a ball, which bounces higher when the jump button is held and can feel slippery to control. In the two-player mode, players in red and green hats take turns on the same map, and beating the boss moves both to the next world. A bonus life is awarded every 30,000 points.

t_cf35c945f035.overview: Out in the outback, the Boomerang Kid must retrieve all of his scattered boomerangs across a run of short platform stages. The boomerangs he collects are never thrown, and the B button has no use; running and jumping carry the whole game. Falling too far is fatal, and walking off a ledge starts a fall at once, while a jump first carries the Kid upward, so lower platforms are often reached by jumping. After most stages a choice of the left or right path decides the next stage, and well-hidden warps allow rapid progress. Stages include Shark City, Lord Grimdown's Castle, Nightmare Mansion and Stalactite City, with conveyors, breakaway platforms and a switch maze along the way. The Falcus brothers created it, and Codemasters also released it as part of the Quattro Adventure compilation.

t_cf607c63ccb6.overview: Set in an offbeat parody of the late 20th-century United States, this 1989 role-playing game follows a young American boy named Ninten as he works to resolve paranormal troubles across the country. Ninten, Lloyd and Ana, the main protagonists, are roughly 11 to 12 years of age, and in the land of Magicant its monarch, Queen Mary, asks Ninten to collect the eight melodies of a song from her dreams. The overworld is explored from a top-down perspective, and random encounters lead to battles with options to fight, guard, check enemy attributes, run away or use items. Rather than conventional weapons, the party wields baseball bats, toy guns, frying pans, knives and inherent psychic abilities. Hospitals heal for a fee, and progress is saved by using a phone to call Ninten's father.

t_cf628178e740.overview: Set on Coolmint Island, an island made of ice and home to the winter fairies, this puzzle game sends the apprentice wizard Dana to defend the island against flame monsters at the request of the fairy queen. Dana's most important ability is his ice magic: he can create and destroy blocks of ice, push them across the stage, and climb small ledges. Fires are put out by sliding an ice block into them or by dropping one on top of them from above. Later stages bring in pipes and jars, and burning jars block movement and destroy ice. The main game spans 10 worlds of 10 stages each, and a stage editor lets players design their own stages and puzzles and save them.

t_cf7ac4be6082.overview: Evil youkai have opened a series of realms called Makyō in a bid to conquer the human world, and Kitaro ventures in to stop them. Each of the 16 stages begins on a top-down map holding several Makyō, a hut belonging to Sunakake-baba and the Youkai Castle, where the boss waits. Clearing a stage requires recovering a crystal ball from one of the side-scrolling Makyō, whose tasks include collecting spirits, defeating enemies, riding Ittan Momen through the sky and lighting candles with Tsurube-bi. Kitaro fires hair needles without limit and can pick up special weapons such as finger guns, a floating cloak and a remote-controlled geta. A single hit costs a life, and an Ocarina summons allies like Nurikabe to help against bosses. After stage 16 the game loops. One player.

t_cfb61e293f6d.overview: Set in 50 BC, when Gaul is entirely occupied by the Romans except for one small village protected by a magic potion, this Infogrames platformer was released only in Europe. Obelix has vanished, captured by the Romans, and the short, mustached Gaul must rescue his friend before Caesar throws him to the lions. The journey spans four acts that pass through Gaul, Helvetia, Spain, Egypt and Rome, each made up of several levels, with Romans and various aggressive animals along the way. Asterix punches enemies and can punch big A blocks to get stars for points or other secrets, while a magic potion bottle gives brief invincibility. After each act comes a bonus round of breaking barrels thrown by a pirate or log rolling at sea, and the only boss is the last one, Briseradius.

t_cfb789f070a7.overview: Nintendo's edutainment spin-off of its Popeye arcade game uses a similar platform layout to teach English spelling. Players cannot lose a life; a mistake only counts as a wrong answer. Three modes are included. In Word Puzzle A, the player sees a Japanese word from a category such as animals or food and fills in the English spelling by moving Popeye to letters; each wrong guess makes Bluto punch the basket holding Swee'Pea, so the puzzle must be solved before the basket falls. Word Puzzle B works the same way but does not show the Japanese term first. Word Catcher is a two-player contest in which the players collect letters thrown by Olive Oyl, and the first to spell five words wins.

t_cfd438b8c4ee.overview: Side-scrolling shooting in the vein of Gradius and R-Type unfolds inside a monster. In the year 5012, the planet Abadox has been eaten by Parasitis, a giant alien organism that later devours the hospital ship carrying Princess Maria. Second Lieutenant Nazal, the only surviving fighter of the galactic fleet, enters the creature's body to rescue her. Most enemies resemble internal organs. Power-ups include speed boosters, increased firepower, homing missiles and shields, and the starting single shot can be upgraded to a 3-way gun, spread fire, a laser or a hoop-like weapon. A single enemy projectile destroys the ship, and death costs every upgrade and returns play to the last checkpoint. The second, fourth and sixth stages switch to a vertical view that scrolls downward, and the final stage is an escape before the alien implodes.

t_cffc82ad4a4d.overview: This set pairs the baseball game with the '91 Opening Day Edition child cassette, one of only two roster cartridges actually released for it. The small cassette plugs into a slot on the back of the main cartridge and supplies player data, so the game can use rosters newer than its built-in ones. Underneath is a conventional baseball game with sixteen teams: twelve modeled on the professional clubs of the day and four original teams. One or two players can face off in versus mode with any team, the pennant race runs for 30, 60, 90 or 130 games, and further options include a team editor, a winning-streak tournament, a home run contest and a watch mode. Inserting or removing the child cassette clears the save data.

t_d0093f463e60.overview: Set in a dystopian future during the year 2048, this unreleased Japanese build of Strider stars Hiryu, the youngest ever elite-class member of a secret organization of hi-tech ninja-like operatives known as the Striders. Sent to assassinate his friend Kain, who has been captured by hostile forces, Hiryu uncovers the development of a mind-control weapon codenamed Zain and sets about finding and destroying the Zain units. The game opens on the Blue Dragon, the Striders' base of operations. Hiryu fights with his Cypher, a plasma-generating blade, and must leap off walls with the Triangle Jump to reach some areas. Disks recovered along the way hold information pertinent to the plot, and passwords keep track of progress. The Famicom release was cancelled, leaving this prototype unfinished.

t_d00c63d586d9.overview: Written in Family BASIC by Shinkan Soft, this shoot-'em-up was published in 1990 as a type-in game in Micom BASIC magazine. The action is extremely smooth and fast paced, and three layers of background stars move at different speeds to add depth to the scenery. Opposition comes from at least three standard enemy types and from many bosses, which are smaller than usual but look more ship-like. The game is for a single player.

t_d01cb6d36f56.overview: Released by Bit Corporation in Taiwan in 1987 and sold there simply as Duck, the puzzle-platformer here is the one known in other markets as Duck Maze. The player controls a duck whose job is to safeguard a giant egg, guiding it downward through 20 levels by moving or destroying blocks. Care is needed on the way down: a life is lost if the egg touches an enemy or breaks after falling from too high, and three lives are provided. The design follows Sega's Doki Doki Penguin Land, which appeared in 1985 on the SG-1000 and MSX. Escorting the egg safely is the whole objective, so each level becomes a small puzzle of block placement.

t_d02023d49711.overview: Layla, a 17-year-old member of the special forces group CAT, must rescue her team partner Iris, who has been captured by the evil scientist Dr. Manitoka. The search covers eight asteroids built up as his bases, each divided into a surface section followed by an enemy base. The screen always scrolls from left to right, no backtracking is allowed, and destroyable and indestructible blocks are sometimes impossible to tell apart. A handgun is the starting weapon; stronger weapons and hand grenades appear when green containers along the way are destroyed, though their ammunition is limited. Bonus levels let Layla destroy enemy squadrons while invulnerable, and a password shown after a game over allows play to resume later.

t_d025955bc1fa.overview: Joy Van developed this horizontal shooter in 1989, and it was later released in North America as Double Strike with a redesigned player plane. Flying the titular plane, the player attacks a terrorist organization stationed in the South Pacific; flags in some boss stages hint that the enemy are Nazis. Three types of levels, sky, land and sea, loop three times at different times of day, and each level type has a boss fight against turrets. Weapon upgrades can be collected along with the ability to drop bombs on enemies below, though picking up the same power-up repeatedly does not keep upgrading the plane. Despite the shared name, the game has nothing to do with the Seta helicopter shooter Twin Eagle.

t_d054531e8aa5.overview: Years before the story begins, an evil usurper conquered the Kingdom of the Crystal Palace and crowned himself king; only the infant prince and a loyal dog escaped. Now a teenager, the prince sets out to retake the palace, choosing at the start one of three crystals: one raises his jump height, one increases his health, and one grants unlimited use of a fireball attack. The side-scrolling platform action leads through five realms filled with bizarre enemies. The prince fights mainly with a sword, scrolls add long-range attacks, and the dog can be summoned to damage foes. Power-ups dropped by defeated enemies or sold in a shop temporarily copy the crystals' effects. Compared with the later US release, this original version is harder and includes ghostly child-like enemies and stage elements that were changed abroad.

t_d0a4f224822c.overview: A vertically scrolling shooter set in a space war, adapted from the arcade game developed by NMK, puts the player in control of the fighter Wol-Arg. Air and ground targets call for separate attacks: odd-numbered stages arm the ship with a forward shot that fires three in a row and even-numbered ones with a ring-shaped three-way shot, while a single ground weapon fires at a sight ahead of the ship. Floating pipe-like terrain destroys the ship on contact. Each of the 18 stages ends at a flying fortress that falls only when its open core is hit, followed by a landing bonus on a runway. Rare blocks reveal B or P letters for a barrier or stronger shots, and a secret action at a ship-shaped shadow transforms the craft into an invincible robot that rams enemies for a limited time.

t_d0f1350c3a58.overview: A wicked fiend named Baramos threatens to destroy the world, and the legendary warrior Ortega has already fallen short in his attempt to stop him. His child, the Hero, sets out from the castle town of Aliahan to finish that quest and rid the world of the archfiend. Companions are recruited at a tavern, and each recruit's class greatly affects their statistics and the spells they can learn. Only four characters can travel in the party at a time, while the others wait behind. A day and night cycle also shapes the adventure, since certain items, characters and quests are only accessible at specific times of the day.

t_d0f9a0f40865.overview: Real professional team and player names appear throughout this officially licensed baseball game, which sets out to recreate a pennant race. The pennant race mode is a 130-game league season, and the league winner goes on to a seven-game Japan Series. An open league mode plays 36 games against the other teams, with the goals of earning 50,000 points for a created original player and winning the title. Other modes include watching the computer play itself in a three-game series, practice for batting, pitching and fielding, and a three-game series against the computer with a chosen team. One original player can be made with a chosen name, position and ability type, up to five trades are allowed, and three background music tracks can be chosen. League results are saved by battery backup, and a contest mode lets records be sent in by telephone for prize events.

t_d11c50602f5c.overview: Adapted from the first volume of the classic novel Nansou Satomi Hakkenden, this role-playing game opens with the Satomi clan's castle plagued by the evil spirit of Tamazusa and occupied by monsters and other supernatural phenomena. The hero, one of the eight Wild Dog Warriors of Satomi, must gather his brothers and go on an adventure to find the eight magical jewels. Towns are places to talk with residents, equip weapons and armor, and receive quests and directions before leaving to fight random encounters on an overworld map that links locations together. Combat is turn-based: the player chooses each character's actions and then watches the turn play out. Most of the enemies are based on classical Japanese monsters, usually youkai.

t_d1227b630f88.overview: Mahjong solitaire is the basis of this Joy Van game, distributed in Taiwan by Thin Chen Enterprise and later issued in Japan by Hacker International as Shisen Mahjong: Seifuku Hen. Players clear tile layouts by making connections between tiles, working through six difficulty levels with three stages in each, and completing a stage rewards them with an adult image. Time to finish each stage is short and the puzzles grow increasingly complex. The game includes voice clips and an autocomplete feature. A two-player mode passes control to the other player whenever a connection is not made in time. Two revisions circulated, the later one adding music and upgraded graphics.

t_d15c67cec783.overview: Four Sachen-developed games make up the eighth Super Cartridge, and three of them are unique to this multicart. Final Combat, the only previously released title, is a Battle City clone with an adjustable turret. Worm Visitor, a port of the Mega Duck and Game Boy game of the same name, is a Frogger derivative in which the player has to avoid moving objects. Frog Adventure is a more standard Frogger clone that reuses several assets from Worm Visitor, and Magical Tower is likewise a port of the Mega Duck and Game Boy game of the same name.

t_d15f93bcb9c5.overview:
An expedition into uncharted subterranean caverns sends an explorer in search of an underground pyramid and its hidden riches. Starting at the cave entrance at the top, the player aims to reach the treasure located at the bottom of the labyrinth. Navigation involves walking, jumping, climbing ropes and ladders, and operating vehicles such as elevators, boats, and mine cars.

Throughout the journey, the explorer must monitor a depleting energy gauge and recharge it with energy items. Falling off cliffs, into pits, or depleting energy results in losing a life. Hazards include bats, scalding steam vents, and haunting ghosts, which can be dispelled by firing a Phantom Blaster from solid ground. Along the route, the player gathers flares, dynamite to destroy boulders, color-coded keys to open doors, and treasures like jewels and sacks of money.

t_d1621d260957.overview: Igo Shinan '93 continues the series of Go study cartridges built on records of notable professional games, which can be watched as an automatic replay or stepped through manually, with a playing-strength assessment also included. The historical player sets and handicap games of the previous edition are removed. In their place come collections devoted to four other historical professional players, holding between 23 and 27 games each, while the modern category keeps 36 games, bringing the total to 135 records.

t_d2050d4cc26c.overview: Chosen by Buzz, a servant of the wind spirit Aerial, a warrior descends into an underground labyrinth to defeat Dolgo, the earth spirit who has stolen the Life Seeker from the city of Palma and plunged it into darkness. This side-scrolling action role-playing game spans six stages, one on the surface and five underground, each ending with a boss behind a door that needs a key dropped by certain enemies. The hero moves left and right, crouches, jumps and swings a sword. Encounters occur at fixed points, where up to four enemies must be defeated or driven off. Experience raises the hero's level from 0 to 31, increasing power, stats and jump height. Up to ten items can be carried, weapons other than the basic sword wear out with use, and eight types of armor are available. There is no save or continue.

t_d24098fd2398.overview: Twelve teams modeled on Japanese professional baseball, all under parody names, are available in this baseball game. After choosing one, the player battles the five other clubs of its league in a 30-game round-robin season; taking the pennant leads to the Japan Series against the other league's champion, and winning it brings the ending. Season records are saved with battery backup. A one-player exhibition mode offers games against a team of former professionals and a team of foreign players, both packed with strong hitters, and two players can face each other on a choice of three ballparks modeled on real stadiums. Visual touches include managers whose faces change during time-outs, bullpen and pinch-hitter scenes, hero interviews after a win, and a sports news show reporting results and standings after each game.

t_d250878920a4.overview: Takara's role-playing take on Jinsei Game, the Japanese version of The Game of Life, replaces the familiar spinner with free movement. Starting from home, the player explores a city full of stores, places of employment and places of learning, earning money and raising statistics to unlock better features. Random encounters occur as in Dragon Quest, and strangers met in town may offer advice or do something malevolent to the player character. As in the board game, the player chooses from careers such as musician, photographer and professional wrestler; most of the tasks are mundane, though one quest involves chasing down UFOs. Buildings crucial to the quest can be fully explored, while elsewhere the player simply talks to the resident. Fights resemble those of a standard role-playing game, but the character's stats are used in place of hit points and magic points. Single-player and multiplayer modes are available.

t_d25db7b047f0.overview: Rebuilt as a demastered 8-bit version that runs on real Famicom/Nintendo Entertainment System hardware, Pac-Man Championship Edition keeps the basic loop of the original Pac-Man: run through a maze, avoid the ghosts, and eat pellets, power pellets and bonus items while chasing a high score. Instead of a stage-clear structure, play becomes a never-ending run, as the left and right portions of the maze fill in with new pellet patterns after pellets and bonus items are eaten. Two modes are offered. Normal provides a five-minute run in which the speed starts modest and grows as the timer ticks down, while Extra sets a three-minute time limit.

t_d268885be9d8.overview:
Controlling Donkey Kong Jr., the player walks, jumps, and climbs to solve mathematical problems presented by Donkey Kong. Stages feature chains holding digits and islands holding arithmetic symbols for the player to collect. By gathering these items in the Calculate modes, the objective is to build equations that match a target figure displayed by Donkey Kong on a placard.

Three game modes are offered: Calculate A, Calculate B, and the single-player Exercise. Calculate A and B can be played solo or by two competitors simultaneously. During a two-player contest, participants race against each other to produce the target value first and earn five apples, even hindering an opponent by taking numbers and symbols before the rival can reach them. Exercise presents ten arithmetic problems per game, where the player climbs chains under a Nitpicker to select missing numbers.

t_d29600b1b9b8.overview: Two role-playing games share one cartridge here: the original Final Fantasy and Final Fantasy II, each launched by choosing its logo on the title screen and each with completely independent save data. In Final Fantasy, the player begins by choosing four characters to form a party, four youths called the Warriors of Light, in a world whose four crystals each govern one of the classical elements, and the quest ends with the defeat of Chaos. Final Fantasy II follows the warrior Firion and his allies as they join a rebellion against the expanding Palamecian Empire; instead of earning experience levels, characters develop depending on the actions they take in battle, and special keywords learned in conversation can be repeated to other characters. Both games are carried over almost unchanged.

t_d3146a456182.overview: Conector's Brazilian cartridge of Battletoads carries intro text translated into Portuguese and several rule changes. Professor T. Bird flies Rash and Zitz to a nearby planet called Ragnarok's World to rescue Pimple and Princess Angelica from the Dark Queen. Stages mix scrolling beat 'em up brawling with racing, climbing and vehicle-based obstacle courses, such as the Turbo Tunnel, where the toads ride a Speed Bike past stone walls. The toads punch, head-butt and throw enemies, finish them with powerful Smash Hit blows, and restore their six hit points by eating flies. Compared with the original release, play starts with an extra life and continues are unlimited, while the second level, Wookie Hole, which comes right before the Turbo Tunnel, is skipped entirely.

t_d3213ccce126.overview: Single-screen mazes form the playground for Chack'n, a yellow creature with extendable legs who can walk on floors or ceilings but not on walls. He throws hand grenades to his left or right, and after a short time each one explodes into a cloud of smoke; separate buttons make him roll in either direction. Solid walls slow his progress, so hearts must be freed from their cages with grenades to clear the way. Monstas hatch from eggs to obstruct him, and destroying all of them or none of them earns a bonus at the end of the level. Every screen is played against a time limit, marked by a Mighta pushing a boulder along the top of the screen. This Family Computer release is a home port of the platform game Taito first made for arcades in 1984.

t_d327154f9d5b.overview: Built by Enigma Variations, this NES conversion of the god game casts the player as a deity who shepherds people by direction, manipulation and divine intervention against an enemy force led by an opposing deity. The most basic power is raising and lowering land, giving followers room to build more houses, which in turn create more followers. Progressing to the next level requires increasing the number of followers. Stronger acts of intervention draw on divine power and include causing earthquakes and floods, creating swamps and volcanoes, and turning ordinary followers into more powerful knights. The conversion was fully completed for the publisher Imagineer, which chose not to release it.

t_d32b2a3e0dae.overview: Adapted from the Jaleco arcade game Momoko 120%, this Famicom version swaps the heroine Momoko for Lum and replaces the enemies with characters from the manga. Each stage takes place in a burning building: flames gradually creep upward from the bottom, and touching them counts as a miss, so the goal is to climb to the roof and grab the airship waiting there. Escalators are the basic way to move between floors, and warp doors can lead to a different floor or elsewhere on the same one. Enemies can be defeated, while contact with them also costs a miss. Compared with the arcade original, support characters appear to help out, and collecting three items grants temporary invincibility, making the game easier overall.

t_d3ce9fb3d976.overview: Again supervised by Yousuke Ide, the sequel keeps two-player mahjong with four-player-style scoring but drops the earlier free match mode. A league mode advances through seven stages of knockout competition, ending with a match against Ide. A study mode presents discard problems based on Ide's own real game records. The most distinctive addition is a role-playing mode in which the hero searches for a missing father and investigates a mysterious mahjong organization. Bosses are fought in mahjong matches where cheating techniques such as tile stacking, learned through leveling up, can be used, while minor enemies are fought only for money. Each boss defeated raises the hero's level, HP, MP and point limit. Progress is saved by password, and the bundled dedicated controller also works with the first game.

t_d3d029e66443.overview: Aimed at children, this simple board game sends the players traveling across a map to reach a certain landmark before the others, buying souvenirs at locations along the way. Besides earning Yen, players gain Happiness Points by buying souvenirs and sending them home to enjoy. Special cards can be received to affect the other players or oneself. Results are not saved or carried over to a new map, so each session ends when the current game is won.

t_d3e1e81aace3.overview: Prototype builds of a Robin Hood adventure show the game at an earlier stage of development, with more of a role-playing bent than its eventual form. Rather than opening with an escape from prison, the quest drops the hero in the middle of Sherwood Forest with orders to find three worthy companions. Deadly bears roam the land right next to friendly characters, and when talking to people the player can question them on specific topics or try to rob them. Alongside the usual status information, separate meters track food and water. A dueling mode and an archery mode can also be selected directly from the title screen, the duels playing out as one-on-one fights.

t_d41099d5c4de.overview: Side-scrolling action platforming drives this adaptation of Kamen no Ninja Akakage. The masked ninja Akakage fights enemy ninja, warlords and kaiju with a sword, shuriken, a boomerang, a variety of bombs and ninjutsu techniques. Not all of them are available at the start: they are acquired by finding red hearts throughout the stages in order to talk to old man Tomizou. Akakage can also call for help from his allies Aokage and Shirokage. The story is based on the anime of the same name, which in turn draws on an older live-action tokusatsu television series about a masked ninja who helps people.

t_d43101adeeb1.overview: Rather than relying only on units deployed on the map in advance, players produce weapon units near their own headquarters and advance them across the map, capturing cities along the way. Taking the enemy headquarters wins the battle, which is the basic rule, and unit production is the distinguishing feature of the series. Depending on the map, up to four nations can take part. Instead of true hexagons, the Famicom version builds its map from square cells arranged in a pseudo-hex layout that follows the hexagonal pattern.

t_d45090979898.overview:
Defeating Count Dracula and his army of monsters is the primary objective of this platforming adventure. Controlling the vampire hunter Trevor Belmont, the player fights through Terror Levels, each with a time limit and a boss; there are seventeen in all, though the route chosen determines which are played. Trevor combats threats using the Mystic Whip alongside various items. At several points the road forks, and the player chooses which path to take toward the castle. Different endings can be reached depending on the companion who travels with Trevor.

Trevor can also team up with a single spirit companion encountered along the way. Available allies include Sypha, the Mystic Warlord, who attacks with flames, frozen crystals, and lightning bolts; Grant DaNasty, a ghost pirate able to cling to walls and ceilings and jump high; and Alucard, Dracula's son, who fires a Ball of Destruction and transforms into a bat. Partnering with a new companion requires leaving the previous ally behind.

t_d4699c0e57d2.overview: Having finished his training in Kyoto, the fireworks craftsman Kantarou heads home toward Edo, where Momoko, the woman he loves, waits, but the crooked merchant Gozaemon and his gang attack him along the way to steal a secret gunpowder recipe. The side-scrolling action game follows the old Tokaido road through 21 stages modeled on its post towns, beginning at Sanjo Ohashi and ending in Asakusa. Kantarou throws firecrackers that fly in a limited arc, or crouches to set them down so they explode after a short delay. A single touch from an enemy, a projectile or a pit costs a life. Rice balls grant temporary invincibility, geta let him ride clouds, and collecting ten gold coins opens a hidden back road. One or two players take turns.

t_d4707acade95.overview: Roberto is staying in Las Vegas with his girlfriend Marian in a motel room when she is apparently kidnapped by a mysterious person under the employment of Akiko, and $800,000 in ransom money must be raised to learn where she is. The game mixes a mystery adventure with casino gambling: the player can go straight to blackjack, slot machines and roulette, or work at solving the mystery. In the adventure portion, informants give advice whenever Roberto makes a notable amount of money at blackjack; the first shows up once his bankroll reaches $5,000, and the last appears at $100,000. A female dealer runs the table games, and running out of money ends the game instantly.

t_d4bd9cc12066.overview: Monsters have broken into a castle to steal its treasure, and the red-clad Ninja-kun slips in alone to drive them out and win back what was taken. Each vertically scrolling stage is built from tiers of platforms, and all of its enemies must be defeated to clear it. Holding the jump button leaps up to the next tier, a short press makes a small hop, and jumping without a direction drops to the tier below. Shuriken fly only one at a time, so the safer tactic is to jump into an enemy to stun it and then finish it off. Foes such as Kuroko, Daruma, Kabuki and Yoroi each use a different weapon and react to Ninja-kun's position, and collecting three falling orbs opens a bonus stage.

t_d4be37db50de.overview:
A devil named Mandora and his monster forces have driven humanity into the ocean depths. Taking control of a fighter craft, the player flies into vertical combat to eliminate opposing aerial forces and ground targets in an effort to reclaim the Earth.

Destroying hangars releases numbered fighter parts that dock directly with the craft. Up to four attachments add weaponry such as double shots, backward shots and a rear barrier, while also shielding the vessel from incoming strikes. Pressing the A button separates the docked parts into a battle formation whose pattern depends on how many parts are attached, and an on-screen counter limits how often formations can be used. When fully assembled with every component, the craft temporarily changes into an invincible Fire Bird. A design mode lets players arrange their own formations by setting part positions and beam directions.

t_d5a34946748d.overview: Players create their own sumo wrestler, choosing his eyes, ears, mouth and nose to give him a unique appearance, with all characters drawn in a chibi style. The custom wrestler then fights other sumo wrestlers for the title of Yokozuna. Each competitor has two bars that are used to fend off and deliver attacks. A tutorial mode lets players practice their moves against a computer opponent that is less intelligent than the main game's AI.

t_d5b93bfb8316.overview: Mahjong matches against characters from a manga make up this Famicom adaptation of Gambler Jiko Chuushinha, the mahjong comic by Katayama Masayuki that began serialization in Young Magazine in 1982. The roster of opponents drawn from the manga numbers 24 in all, split between 12 members of the Tako squad and 12 members of the opposing Anti-Tako squad. Asmik published the cartridge in Japan, and a sequel followed on the same system in 1990.

t_d5e233034851.overview: Based on a manga about ancient China, this adventure covers the era between the Qin and Han dynasties, a period of intrigue and conflict a few decades before the Three Kingdoms era began. The original manga stars Liu Bang, the founding emperor of the Former Han, with Xiang Yu as a central figure, and spans the late Qin period to the end of the Chu-Han War. Play follows the traditional Famicom adventure format, in which the player controls a protagonist through a series of menus in order to solve a series of puzzles. It is a single-player game.

t_d5fadd07f32c.overview: Rather than adapting the manga, the second game tells an original story that picks up after it. The first part follows Tsubasa in Brazil, leading his Sao Paulo team toward victory and meeting Carlos Santana along the way, before the story cuts to his old Nankatsu side, now led by Misaki Taro, in a high school championship. Later, Tsubasa's club plays a match against Japan's national team, and the national squad goes on to a world youth championship. Matches use command-based play: each player spends guts to dribble, pass, shoot or attempt a one-two, and many characters have special shots shown in dramatic animations. A more useful mini-map now lets passes go anywhere on the field, shots can be faked in the penalty area, players level up through experience, and passwords save progress.

t_d606641198e9.overview: Produced in Brazil for the NES clone Turbo Game, the game takes its premise from the Persian Gulf, the paradise of black gold on whose oil many countries depend for their economic development. One ambitious politician, seeking to control the world, organizes an army. Unable to resist on their own, the nations of the world create an organization for the protection of peace and send the SUPER AH-64 helicopter to intervene on the enemy battlefield.

t_d60a9f167f9e.overview:
A single adventurer wanders the fantasy town of Hillsfar, undertaking quests and navigating mini-games. The player begins by generating a custom character or selecting a pre-made hero, choosing attributes like race, alignment, and class from cleric, fighter, magic-user, or thief. Attributes receive randomized values during creation.

Gameplay alternates between quest-based adventure and action challenges. The hero visits the guild of their class to find assignments. Outside of assigned missions, the player explores freely, traveling across landscapes and hunting for treasure. The story unfolds differently for each of the four classes, offering a distinct adventure with each one.

t_d62b62d38fb8.overview: On the desolate planet RS-121, ravaged by disasters that made life impossible, only one structure remains: a highway called the Black Line, said to be tied to an ancient legend. This vehicular combat racer puts a single player behind the wheel of a car resembling a 1982 DeLorean, firing missiles to knock enemy vehicles, which resemble dune buggies, off the road before they can do the same. Repair shops along the highway fix the car and resupply it with weapons. A meter in the lower-left corner of the screen shows how close the driver is to the goal, and continues are unlimited.

t_d6411e2c3682.overview: Modeled on the Taiwanese gambling game of the same name, Xiao Mali was developed by Nei-Hu Electronics and distributed by Idea-Tek, with a later release by Computer & Entertainment. The player places credits on the fruit and other images of a gambling board, up to 9 credits on an individual fruit, and wins by betting on the image that lights up when the round ends. Play is adapted to a single controller, unlike Dian Shi Ma Li, which is based on the same gambling game but requires two. The original release uses an unusually dark color palette, which the C&E release brightened. Despite the name, which literally means "Small Mario", Mario does not appear anywhere in the game. A cheat on the title screen starts play with 5000 credits.

t_d64deafec86b.overview: Leading a band of adventurers, the player searches the Realm for the seven pieces of the broken Destiny Wand. Forged by the Archmage Turin, the wand had kept the land at peace for 700 years before it was seized by the mage Lagoth Zanta and broken, its fragments hidden in dungeons throughout the kingdom. Recovering every piece, defeating Lagoth Zanta and reforging the wand are the party's goals. Like the series' other cartridge versions, this role-playing adventure published by Pony Canyon substantially rearranges the systems and maps of the original computer release rather than reproducing it directly.

t_d68974902da5.overview: When the Foot Clan under Shredder kidnaps April, presented here as Splinter's daughter, Leonardo, Raphael, Donatello and Michelangelo set out to rescue her. Across six areas the turtles also defuse bombs at a dam, rescue Splinter, destroy Big Mouser and hunt down the Technodrome. Missions begin on an overhead map, and entering sewers or buildings switches to side-scrolling action with jumping, crouching and attacking, plus alternate weapons such as shuriken, boomerangs and a scroll that releases a crescent beam. The player can switch turtles from the information screen, and each turtle's weapon differs in speed, power and reach. Pizza restores health, and from the third area a captured turtle can be rescued once per area. One player.

t_d6c31f6458dd.overview: Turn-based battles on grid-based maps drive this tactical role-playing game set on the fictional continent of Archanea. The story follows Marth, prince of the kingdom of Altea, in a conflict against the evil sorcerer Gharnef and his dark master Medeus, the titular Shadow Dragon, and part of the quest involves retrieving the sacred sword Falchion. A unit's class affects its range of movement and strength on the battlefield. A total of 52 characters can be recruited over the course of the adventure, but any character who falls in battle is lost to permanent death. Maps are unlocked and played in a linear fashion, as dictated by the storyline.

t_d6d3dbf8bd5e.overview: Wagyan leaves his home island when the Hisopiso, distant relatives of the Wagyan race, come asking for help after their planet is invaded by an unknown force. The setting moves to a space city where the Hisopiso live, and many stages use gravity as a gimmick, with abnormally high jumps or with up and down reversed. A Rocket Belt, received from the Hisopiso just before the space cactus stage, appears only in this entry. Wagyan stuns enemies with sound wave attacks shouted from his mouth, and each stage ends with a boss confronted in a battle-of-wits mini-game such as shiritori or memory matching. Hidden Hisopiso can sometimes be rescued for battery 1UP items. A versus mode, in which players face each other in the boss mini-games, makes its debut.

t_d6dd1c491b09.overview: Hebe, a penguin-like character, sets out to find his colleagues Ō-Chan, Sukezaemon and Jennifer, who fell into time and space during a large-scale war, so that they can fight an alien named Unyohn and return to their homeworlds. Exploration of an interconnected, free-roaming world is the focus, with items, power-ups and boss battles in the vein of Metroid. Three of the bosses are the missing friends, who join as playable characters once defeated: Ō-Chan can swim and walk on slippery ice, Sukezaemon jumps high and Jennifer dives underwater, opening previously unreachable areas. Characters can be switched at any time from a sub-menu. Enemies are attacked by jumping on them while holding down, and defeated foes turn into balloons called Popoons that can be thrown. A password system allows continuing.

t_d6dda33ed7ff.overview:
Missions send the player into the Pacific Ocean during World War II, ranging from torpedo and gun practice and historical convoy actions to full war patrols. Operating as a single-player submarine simulation, the experience centers on tracking down and attacking Japanese shipping targets while defending against hostile destroyers.

Controlling a United States submarine, the player chooses when and how to engage hostile vessels, such as surface attacks at night or submerged periscope attacks by day. Time moves quickly while patrolling between engagements, and the time scale can also be sped up during battles until the enemy detects the submarine or a weapon is fired. Operations demand managing navigation, firing weapons, and monitoring damage across separate battle stations.

t_d6f588240614.overview:
An expedition into uncharted subterranean caverns sends an explorer in search of an underground pyramid and its hidden riches. Starting at the cave entrance at the top, the player aims to reach the treasure located at the bottom of the labyrinth. Navigation involves walking, jumping, climbing ropes and ladders, and operating vehicles such as elevators, boats, and mine cars.

Throughout the journey, the explorer must monitor a depleting energy gauge and recharge it with energy items. Falling off cliffs, into pits, or depleting energy results in losing a life. Hazards include bats, scalding steam vents, and haunting ghosts, which can be dispelled by firing a Phantom Blaster from solid ground. Along the route, the player gathers flares, dynamite to destroy boulders, color-coded keys to open doors, and treasures like jewels and sacks of money.

t_d72061f75b72.overview: Sent out to investigate a series of unexplained attacks on local temples, Kujaku soon finds the Iwato Clan apparently trying to obtain real-world artifacts that will allow them to resurrect their Serpent God, though the case proves to involve more than it first seems. Progress comes through a menu of actions: talking to characters, examining locations and using items to solve puzzles. Random encounters are fought in a turn-based manner, always one-on-one, with spells cast through commands. There are no experience points or money; Kujaku levels up automatically at the end of each of the eight chapters, and health can be restored only at specific places in each chapter. Losing a battle sends him back to his mentor rather than ending the game, and progress is kept with passwords.

t_d7430227b8e2.overview: Adapted from an animal-ecology gag manga, this adventure stars a clumsy white-furred bear cub, an albino brown bear, who is chosen by a god as the hero to save the forest and sets out to defeat the forest's demon king. He travels in a party of three animals, joined by a wild boar piglet and another companion, and other main characters from the manga appear as well. Gags and scenes from the original are worked in, yet the game departs from it with humanoid original characters, a god, man-made objects, animals that clearly do not belong to the setting, and the power to revive a creature from the dung left after it was eaten.

t_d745e68693e2.overview: Life from kindergarten to old age unfolds as a board game for one to four players, with the computer filling the empty seats when fewer than four people play; controllers are passed between players, or a multitap can be used. Before play begins, each player assembles a face from separate parts in the manner of fukuwarai, the face-arranging party game. Spaces on the board hold events such as casinos and marriage. Characters develop three parameters, intelligence, stamina and luck, and pursue careers ranging from chef, teacher and police officer to lawyer, professional baseball player, singer, pilot and racer. Mini-games include a 100-meter dash, a slot machine, tests and entrance exams, singing contests, kart racing and a flight test.

t_d771c94b798f.overview: No story accompanies this vertical shooter, developed by NTDEC and released in Spain by Gluk Video. The player controls a space ship against incoming alien-shaped foes trying to take it down. Both enemies and projectiles can spawn from any edge of the screen, including the bottom, and enemies fire small, slow projectiles that travel in straight lines. The screen scrolls at a fixed speed, and the game closes with a credits screen.

t_d7b961a850e4.overview: Leon Franco, the young, ambitious son of a noble family fallen on hard times in Portugal, sets out to sea to restore his family's former glory and achieve his dreams. Only three nations are represented: Portugal, Spain and the Ottoman Empire. Many neutral ports around the world can be invested in, bringing them into the sphere of influence of Portugal. Investing, discovering ports and defeating other merchants and pirates in sea battles all increase Leon's fame. With greater fame he can complete tasks for the King of Portugal and earn higher titles of nobility, gradually rebuilding the standing of the family name.

t_d7caabef4c39.overview: Stock market simulation supervised by economic commentator Matsumoto Tooru. To be accepted as his apprentice, the player must turn one million yen into more than 100 million within two simulated years spanning 1988 and 1989. Trading runs in real time on weekdays from 8:30 to 16:00, with prices frozen over a lunch break, and covers 100 listed stocks chosen by Matsumoto, bought outright or on margin; real estate, funds, insurance and time deposits are other options. Information comes from newspapers, trade papers, friends, brokers and Matsumoto himself, while random events such as salary, marriage, illness, traffic accidents and theft shape daily life. Health and life points, a level that limits daily actions, and an automatic save each day round out the system.

t_d7fe9015ff30.overview: Painting every path of a maze while two fish give chase is the task in Brush Roller, an unlicensed clone of the 1981 arcade game Crush Roller, also known as Make Trax. In the arcade design, rollers on overpasses can be pushed along to crush the pursuing fish, which leave the maze for a few seconds, and another character leaves footprints that must be painted over. This version changes several rules: play starts with 9 lives instead of 3, a 200-second timer is added, no points are given for painting the road, and running over a fish awards one point more than the player's current points on that level. The graphics are mostly the same as the original, though the title screen is completely different and the footprint-leaving enemies look different. Hwang Shinwei programmed the game in 1990.

t_d809ed81bcb4.overview: Based on the manga version of Devilman, this action game progresses by switching between Akira Fudo and his Devilman form. At certain points a choice appears whether to save a human who is under attack; abandoning them lowers the HUMAN gauge, and the game is over if that gauge reaches zero. Besides Devilman himself, Miki and Dosu-Roku can also be controlled. The story branches into multiple endings, with several bad endings along the way, and defeating or losing to the final boss leads to two different conclusions. One ending runs opposite to the original manga, with Devilman saving humanity, defeating Satan and then confronting the gods.

t_d821433b1e33.overview:
Players control one of four selectable protagonists—Mario, Luigi, Toad, or Princess Toadstool—running, jumping, and climbing while lifting and throwing objects or foes to navigate the dream world of Subcon. Rather than eliminating adversaries by landing atop them, the characters stand on, pick up, and hurl opponents, mushroom blocks, or uprooted vegetables. Each hero provides distinct physical traits, such as Luigi's high jump, Toad's quick lifting and undiminished jumping and running while carrying items, Princess Toadstool's temporary floating ability, and Mario's balanced attributes.

Progress spans twenty levels distributed across seven themed worlds featuring vertical and horizontal scrolling. Stages contain rooms connected through doors, ladders, and jars, alongside hidden Sub-space areas opened with magic potions to obtain coins and health-increasing mushrooms. Items include screen-clearing POW blocks, stopwatches, cherries that yield stars, and extra lives. Overcoming stage hazards and boss encounters leads to a final confrontation against the tyrant Wart.

t_d839c80f7496.overview: A police officer protects the peace of Manhattan in New York in this side-scrolling action game, played by stepping on the 12-key B side of the Family Trainer mat. Each of the six stages opens by showing a wanted criminal who serves as the boss, and the officer must collect items marked on a map at the bottom of the screen within a time limit, defeat a set number of henchmen and then bring down the boss. Separate keys handle a ranged attack, throwing items or shooting, and a close-range strike with a baton, and dashing into an enemy from behind knocks it down. Later stages have larger maps and place the boss at random. The game is for one player and has no save function.

t_d841884ebe1c.overview: Picking up after the first Famicom game, the hammer-wielding carpenter Gen-san sets out again to chase Dan the Red, who plots revenge against him and has kidnapped Kanna together with Dr. Parallel. The adventure covers eight stages that are played through twice. Bonus games occur only on even-numbered stages, apart from the final stage. Dr. Parallel serves as the last boss, and clearing the second loop adds color to the closing still picture and reveals one more image.

t_d84386df7fbe.overview: Battles unfold in real time across a map of squares in this strategy game starring Napoleon. The French government orders him to wipe out the Italian army in northern Rome, which France had failed to defeat after nearly three years of fighting. Each unit advances one square at fixed intervals, so the player keeps changing its direction, stopping on neutral units and weapon squares to reinforce troops and on town squares to add infantry. Musketeers fire on enemy soldiers at regular intervals, while artillery can only be ordered to advance or halt, and its shells also hurt friendly units they land on. A single defeat is not final: clearing the comeback scenario, the Battle of Waterloo, returns the player to the lost scenario for a rematch. The game is for one player.

t_d8972d0d3ea0.overview: Stock trading is the subject of this simulation, in which the aim is to invest wisely in the stock market and develop a bountiful portfolio. The player is given regular money goals that must be reached before the next target falls due, and buys, sells and manages stocks to build as much wealth as possible along the way. Public domain classical music accompanies play, including an 8-bit rendition of Bach's Air on a G String on the title screen.

t_d8ac260891d2.overview: Starring the doll character Jenny, this side-scrolling action game mixes stage clearing with exploration. An important script is stolen by the evil BB cult, and Jenny resolves to get it back on her own. Play begins on a top-down town map that leads into the action stages, and which stage comes first is entirely random. Inside the stages she fights with kicks and punches and can also use a spray as a ranged weapon. Each action stage requires finding a key to clear it, while letters and numbers won by defeating specific enemies form the keyword needed to finish the game; they are not displayed, so the player must note them down. The ultimate aim is to open the doors of a musical theater and solve the lost word. Health and lives are both used, and a game over restarts everything from the beginning.

t_d8bb2443026c.overview: After population growth drove humanity to search for a new home by spaceship, the exploration ship Jarvas finally returns to Earth with only one crew member left: the astronaut hero. Radio calls go unanswered, and after an emergency landing in what seems to be the Americas, the hero finds the former civilization gone, with no big cities, no skyscrapers and not even hamburgers. The journey that follows seeks the old Earth and the cause of the great change, and leads to defeating a tyrant to become king of the new world. Much of the play revolves around hunting for items, gathering companions and earning money. Levels rise only by returning to a guild once enough experience is earned, casting magic costs experience points, and progress is kept by battery backup.

t_d92c2018791b.overview: Drawing on the second anime series, this adventure game sends Osomatsu on a time-machine journey through three different eras in pursuit of the mystery behind a certain character's famous buck teeth. Familiar characters from the anime appear along the way, joined by figures created just for the game. Progress comes through a command-driven adventure format, with options shown as icons such as an ear for listening to other characters, a shoe for moving between areas and a light bulb for reading the hero's inner thoughts about the current situation.

t_d959b04811eb.overview: Known outside Japan as Rad Racer, this racing game from Square puts the player behind a car in a Transamerica race from the West Coast to the East Coast. Either a 328 Twin Turbo or an F1 Machine can be chosen, though both perform the same. The objective is to complete eight stages through varied skylines and locations, including Los Angeles, San Francisco and Athens, reaching each checkpoint in time; when the clock runs out, the car coasts to a stop, leaving a few extra seconds to make it. Opponents grow faster as the stages progress, and striking obstacles or other cars can flip the vehicle into a crash. The driver can brake, steer and change the background music while racing, and pressing Select during play switches on a stereoscopic 3D mode compatible with the Famicom 3D shutter glasses.

t_d98b73728187.overview: Alien invaders from the far reaches of outer space have overrun Earth and seized Japan, driving its ninja warriors into exile, and two ninjas are sent back to destroy the evil in this side-scrolling action game for one player or two playing simultaneously. Four weapons can be picked up along the way: shuriken, kusarigama, bō and sword. Each has its own fighting style and a transformation. The shuriken turns the ninja into a tiger, the fastest form with the highest jump but the shortest range; the kusarigama grants a sea scorpion that swims well but moves slowly on land; the bō yields a falcon that flies above everything but cannot attack; and the rarely seen sword unlocks an invincible flying dragon that destroys everything in one hit, usable only once and for a limited time.

t_d9d3519f4e09.overview: Earth faces disaster in 1999 when the Moon leaves its orbit and drifts dangerously close, and the cause is traced to Battle Star, a mechanical planet that has appeared beyond Pluto. Earth's defense force hurriedly launches the newly completed spaceship Cosmo Carrier. The objective is to travel between planets and moons, collect six photon missile parts and fire the finished missile at Battle Star, all before 100 in-game days run out. Play alternates between two parts. In space, a cursor targets objects and carries out commands such as missiles, beams, shields, warping and communication. When landing on a planet, a Command Suit is steered across the surface with the D-pad to fight enemies. Warping, attacking and taking hits drain energy, and the game ends when it reaches zero. Progress can be saved with passwords.

t_da0ef9cf6b0e.overview: Activision's planned North America release of the Famicom game Atlantis no Nazo, rebranded as a sequel to Super Pitfall and submitted for manufacturing approval in 1989 but never released. An amateur adventurer named Wynn travels to Atlantis, a landmass that rose from the southern Atlantic Ocean, where his master disappeared more than half a year earlier. The side-scrolling platforming, which can scroll in both directions, spans 101 zones linked by hidden and visible entrances that do not follow numerical order, and some of them skip many zones at once. Wynn fights by throwing sticks of dynamite and can be killed by his own blasts. Compared with the Japanese release, this build has an overhauled title screen and corrected ending text.

t_da5f3e57cbb8.overview: Cookies of several types fill a rectangular grid in this tile-matching puzzle game, and each level is won by clearing every cookie from the playing field. A cursor rotates individual rows and columns in a manner similar to a Rubik's Cube, and any row or column made up of a single cookie type is removed. New cookies keep entering from the top and right sides, and the game ends when the grid overflows. A sixth cookie, shaped like Yoshi's head, occasionally appears and acts as a wild card that helps clear a line of any other type. The single-player Action Mode presents successive levels that grow more complex, while VS Mode lets two players compete on a split screen.

t_dab4a95e028e.overview: Rather than a simple compilation, the third and final installment of Sachen's Poker series wraps its card games in a board game called King of Casino. The story follows a guy named Jack, who is invited to Las Vegas by its mayor to become a millionaire. The player travels the board by rolling a die, which determines which game can be played or which of several characters is encountered. The games are King Poker, a standard poker game, Texas Hold 'Em, Blackjack and 13 Cards, and each can still be selected individually from the main menu. Every $200,000 milestone plays a short cinematic, and becoming a millionaire cuts straight to the ending.

t_dacfb031dfd1.overview: Based on the manga and anime Chibi Maruko-chan, this unlicensed Famicom release developed by Mars Production is entirely in Chinese and mostly text-based. The player controls Maruko, walking around her town and, for most of the adventure, in and around the school. There appears to be some sort of point system. At the school, Maruko can play mini-games such as running to a finish line, putting a puzzle together and playing music, and an in-game map helps with getting around. Some of the sprites are taken from the Mega Drive game Chibi Maruko Chan Waku Waku Shopping. The current ROM dump tends to crash a lot, which can interrupt play.

t_daee88bd3052.overview: A stock-trading business simulation and the sequel to The Money Game, Kabutochou no Kiseki follows a protagonist out to claim a six-hundred-billion-dollar inheritance from the wealthy Benedict family. To prove worth, the protagonist must grow $500,000 in seed money into $1,000,000 through investment. Success brings rewards such as weekend shopping trips and the chance to buy expensive items like a house, and spoiling a girlfriend is encouraged. Failing to raise the money needed for a key item, such as a boat or the house, gets the protagonist disowned by the family and ends the game. The storyline of this original release differs from that of its western adaptation, Wall Street Kid, but the office layout and overall scheme of the two versions are nearly the same.

t_db32dcb00723.overview: Firion and his allies join a rebellion against the expanding Palamecian Empire, whose ruler, the Emperor of Palamecia, is a powerful mage seeking to conquer the world. The rebels are headquartered at Fynn Castle. Instead of traditional level-ups, the game uses a usage-based growth system in which each character develops depending on the actions taken in battle; a character who takes heavy damage, for example, may earn an increase in maximum HP. A "Word Memory" system lets the player ask other characters about keywords that can later be repeated to others to move the story forward. Battle parties consist of up to four characters at a time.

t_db39fd076fba.overview: A year after the battle with the Red Falcon Organization, Bill and Lance are sent on another mission: alien forces have taken over an allied military base and possessed most of its troops. Graphics and gameplay follow the home port of the first Contra, and two players can fight simultaneously. The default gun can be replaced with one of four possible weapons, and the fire ball power-up launches a large projectile that spreads fire after hitting its target. In the overhead stages a hyper shell item destroys all on-screen enemies. Three vertically scrolling stages, a high-tech base, a mountain and an alien nest, are unique to this home version, which also reorders the later stages and bosses and adds a new final boss. The Famicom release keeps a stage select code removed from its NES counterparts.

t_db4c2e369c57.overview: An alien power has taken over Earth's military forces, and the player controls the only one left unaffected. This run-and-gun action game spans eight levels, among them a military base, a forest and an amusement park, with a boss at the end of every stage. Different weapons drop down from the sky throughout each level as enemies attack. The player begins with three lives and a health meter of three small shields; contact with an enemy or an enemy's projectile costs half a shield, and hearts that appear at random from defeated enemies restore health. Oddly, every enemy killed turns into a bat. Play is single-player.

t_db61aee11149.overview: Long ago, two kingdoms that divided the world lived in friendship, and their prince and princess had pledged their futures to each other, until a sorcerer declared he would rule the princess's kingdom with her as his wife. This strategy simulation from Data East follows the struggle to defeat the sorcerer and rescue the princess. Units move across the map in the simulation part, and some can cast magic as well as move. When units clash, the fight plays out as a one-on-one action battle viewed from the side. Besides the story mode against the computer, a versus mode lets players battle each other, and a battle mode offers the action fights with no time limit.

t_dbab77701344.overview: Four casino games make up this gambling simulation: keno, blackjack, roulette and slot machines. Play begins with a bankroll of $700 at the fictional Epic Palace hotel, which replaces the HAL Palace Hotel of the later overseas release, Vegas Dream. Two modes are offered. The Vegas Dream mode adds a storyline with random encounters between games, and such meetings can go either way; sometimes the unidentified man turns out to be a pickpocket. The One Spot mode drops the story entirely and concentrates purely on gaming. Victory comes from building the bankroll past $10 million. Both single-player and multiplayer play are supported.

t_dbb74aba17d0.overview: The dimensional fortress DOH has revived and nests inside the giant ship XORG, so the craft Vaus 2 is launched against it in this block-breaking sequel. The paddle-like ship deflects an energy ball to clear bricks, some of which regenerate after being destroyed or slide from side to side. Finishing a round or catching the break capsule opens two Warp Gates at the bottom of the playfield, and the gate chosen decides which version of the next round follows. Round 17 brings a mid-boss, and the final round pits the ship against DOH and then the brain behind it. Besides the arcade-based mode, the cartridge adds a versus mode and an edit mode for building rounds, and a renewed dedicated paddle controller came packaged with it; plugging in the first game's controller lets two players compete.

t_dc12be7f07b4.overview: Loosely based on the 1992 comic book miniseries of the same name, this cancelled NES game pits the cyborg police officer RoboCop against the machines of the future. Human soldiers of John Connor's resistance force are fighting a losing war against Skynet and its robot forces. After discovering that one of the foundation technologies for Skynet is the cybernetics used to create RoboCop, the resistance sends a soldier named Flo back in time to destroy him and stop Skynet from being built. Skynet learns of the attempt and sends Terminators to stop her. RoboCop soon meets up with Flo and must battle Terminators, the forces of OCP and several obstacles.

t_dc22213af242.overview: Set on the world of Minelvaton, in the area known as Southern Ofelia, this role-playing game begins with tragedy in the kingdom of Palmeccia, where both the King and Queen have been murdered by a servant of Ragon, son of the Zuhl. The player takes control of the Prince of Palmeccia on a quest for revenge and to kill the evil Ragon. Early on, wandering the land and visiting towns looks and plays much like Dragon Quest, but fighting works very differently: combat is action-based rather than turn-based. When a battle begins, the prince starts at the bottom of the screen facing the enemies lined up at the top, and the encounter plays out as an action sequence.

t_dc6affa41dd8.overview:
Aliens have captured a woman named Jeannie Jungle, and the bumbling hero Master Higgins sets out to rescue her. The action unfolds on a two-dimensional plane, where Higgins can jump, swim, run and throw weapons as he works through each stage. A timer doubles as his energy bar, and collecting fruit, milk or meat refills it before it runs out.

Eggs hold five dinosaur friends, each a different color-coded species with unique powers. The pteranodon grants the power of flight, while the elasmosaurus can swim fast. Taking a hit while riding a dinosaur makes the mount abandon Higgins, so protecting a ride is as important as finding one.

t_dc6fd0473017.overview: Upa, the baby prince of a magical kingdom, sets out after breaking an urn that held Zai, an evil goatish demon who drains the life force of the kingdom's adults and kidnaps its babies. A fairy trapped in the same urn gives Upa a magical rattle. In this Konami action game, a rattle strike inflates enemies so they float away; an inflated foe can serve as a temporary platform, though it explodes if Upa stays on top too long, or it can be pushed so it ricochets into other enemies. Milk bottles refill the health meter, and blocks bearing Upa's face hold items such as apples, hourglasses that freeze enemies and bells that grant temporary invincibility. This cartridge edition remixes the music and offers an Easy mode alongside Normal.

t_dc7a70422c07.overview:
Players engage in the sport of golf, taking into account environmental and physical factors such as the wind and the angle at which the ball is struck. Progress throughout the experience is maintained through the use of a password system.

Three distinct modes are available to select from. Participants can compete in a standard tournament mode, or they can practice their skills across two training modes. The game supports participation for up to four people.

t_dc99aac3cb5c.overview: Eurocom originally built this side-scrolling action platformer for Taxan under the code name John Smith, Special Agent. After Taxan decided it did not want the game, it was renamed James Bond Jr. with a few superficial cosmetic changes and published by THQ, so this beta preserves the earlier identity. The agent explores large complexes, tracking down objectives in each level and then finding the level exit, with tasks such as disarming missiles in the sewers, searching for safes and blowing up reactor objects. Disarming a missile requires a sliding puzzle to get colors into the right order, and some safes are traps. A pistol slowly recharges its ammunition, and a jet pack and scuba gear can be found along the way.

t_dcb3d238bf63.overview: Instead of porting the arcade action game, Namco reworked the Genpei Touma Den setting for the Family Computer as a virtual board game that blends board game rules with role-playing systems. Players compete against each other to conquer all of Japan, engaging in battles with enemies and purchasing items and equipment from stores as they advance around the board. Up to four players can take part. The original package came with a physical cloth game board, cards, and metallic player figures molded after Kagekiyo, the resurrected samurai hero of the arcade original, and this version marked the first in-game appearance of Yoritomo in his true form.

t_dceb5b0aa5c4.overview:
Athletic competition forms the focus as players guide an athlete through eight events, including the 100-meter dash, long jump, hurdles, javelin throw, skeet shooting, triple jump, archery, and high jump. Running speed in athletic contests is built strictly by repeatedly pressing the A button, while the Control Pad handles the timing and angle of jumps, the javelin release, and shot release in skill-based trials.

Advancement requires matching or beating designated qualifying times, distances, or scores during every event. Fouls count as attempts in the long jump, the hurdles allow only a single heat in which one missed hurdle spells failure, and failing to qualify in any contest immediately ends the game. Sessions can be played solo against the computer or between two players on alternating turns, with selectable novice and expert difficulty settings.

t_dd322b324d0d.overview: Bandai's first game adaptation of Masami Kurumada's Saint Seiya follows the story from its beginning up to the battles against the Gold Saints in the twelve temples. Pegasus Seiya travels through towns, caves and mountains, defeating foot soldiers with punches, kicks and shock waves on the way to each boss. Boss encounters switch to one-on-one battles fought by selecting commands turn by turn, with Seiya's damage and Cosmo acting as hit points and magic points. The other Bronze Saints first appear as enemies and become allies once defeated. Losing a boss fight does not end the game: Seiya is rescued and tries again with his values rolled back, but running out of Cosmo can leave him unable to beat a boss. Progress is kept by password. Because the anime had not yet revealed the mastermind, the final boss is an original character chosen through a reader contest in Weekly Shōnen Jump.

t_dd34c8cc1ae4.overview: Fighting for the Helic Republic, the player commands a Gojulas against the Zenebas Empire, whose forces occupy towns, forts and castles. Each occupied location is liberated by defeating every enemy unit stationed there. Exploration takes place on a tile-based overworld where enemies appear as visible symbols and can often be avoided, while hidden staircases and other secrets, some required for progress, must be found. Battles switch to a first-person shooting view with enemies surrounding the player on all sides; the player rotates the view, aims up and down, and dodges while firing, and choosing to run always escapes. Leveling up the Gojulas strengthens the whole team. Unusually, the Zoids themselves talk, and only a few key figures such as the Republic's president appear as humans.
