t_f1f900f3714f.overview: Built on the arcade platformer by Tecmo but expanded into an action role-playing adventure, the quest sends a legendary warrior armed with the Diskarmor, a razor-edged shield on a chain that swings like a yo-yo, against Ligar and his revived monsters. A central hub viewed from overhead links side-scrolling areas, much of the map is reachable from the outset, and finds such as the grappling hook, crossbow and pulley open further routes. Every defeated enemy adds Tone, which strengthens attacks, and Lasting, which raises health from three points up to twelve. Stars dropped by foes power three spells, Power-Up, Attack & Assail and Recover, while characters in safe rooms give advice. Progress cannot be saved or resumed by password, though continues are unlimited.

t_f21dc0eeef0c.overview: Elite Systems developed an NES conversion of its computer action game, but it was never released, and a working prototype surfaced in 2008. The player steers a group of constantly bouncing balls across each level, using left and right to alter their travel speed and the fire button to make them bounce higher. Ten balloons must be gathered on every level to move forward. Dangers include sharp rocks, venus flytraps, hedgehogs and flying birds, and each collision bursts a ball; if all four balls are burst, a life is lost. The original game takes place over 12 levels, while the NES version was going to feature different levels than the released computer version.

t_f27f5cf4d71f.overview: Boxing moves into outer space. In this build the playable fighter is Mike Tyson, cast as the undefeated heavyweight champion of the world. When an alien boxing promoter for the Intergalactic Boxing Federation answers the champion's boast, he is taken off Earth to compete against the best fighters in the universe and defend his earthly title. Each bout against a computer-controlled opponent lasts up to three rounds, and rounds are only one minute long. Fights are scored on punch percentages as well as knockdowns, and training sessions between opponents let the player improve the boxer's statistics before the next match.

t_f29425d6fac3.overview: Four separate games share this multicart. CJ's Elephant Antics is a side-scrolling platformer in which C.J. the elephant must make his way home to Africa, and he can drop bombs along the way. Stunt Buggies is an overhead maze driving game: the player drives around collecting bombs while enemy buggies try to stop the run. F-16 Renegade is a shoot-em-up whose levels alternate between overhead stages and third-person views from behind the plane. Go! Dizzy Go!, part of the Dizzy series, has the player push around columns of blocks. The collection was published by Camerica without a license by Nintendo.

t_f2a7e6756f34.overview: A board game in Chinese released by Waixing in 1996, built around Qin's wars of unification and the classical essay Thirty-Six Stratagems. At the start the player chooses one of three characters based on historical Chinese figures, Qin Shi Huang, Xi Shi and Nan Guo Xian Sheng, and the computer controls the two left over. To grow stronger, players buy food, soldiers, stratagem cards and items, and can also develop territory. Stratagem cards include tactics from the essay, such as the empty fort strategy and the beauty trap, alongside original ones like a pre-emptive strike. Collectible treasures include legendary swords and a qilin. Single-player and versus modes are available, and there are three different endings.

t_f2c6b1db3705.overview: Murder strikes aboard the luxury riverboat Delta Princess in this adventure game, the Japanese Famicom version of Murder on the Mississippi licensed by Jaleco. While heading to New Orleans from St. Louis, the detective Sir Charles and his companion Watson are caught up by chance in a murder case they must solve, beginning with the ship's owner Brown, found dead in Room 4. Investigating means moving between the ship's rooms, questioning passengers and crew, and keeping notes, though only a few of Watson's memos can be taken. Each suspect can be spoken to only once per piece of new information. Traps add danger: pitfalls in Room 1 and Room 14 and a flying knife in Room 16 cause instant death. There is no save feature, so every session starts from the beginning.

t_f2c82fd1196d.overview: Namco's Rally-X and New Rally-X are the models for this maze driving game, programmed for the Famicom by Hwang Shinwei in 1988 and first published by Chi Chi Toy Co. The player drives around a giant maze collecting flags while avoiding other cars, and can drop trails that make pursuers spin out when they crash into them. Fuel is limited and drains faster while trails are being laid. The computer-controlled cars are faster and more aggressive than in the arcade original, constantly targeting the player's location, while the player's car can move diagonally across the screen. The type of trail changes each stage, and the original's bonus stages are absent.

t_f2ca6e909b9a.overview: Developed by Home Data and published by Namco, Hayauchi Super Igo simulates the board game Go on either a full 19x19 board or a smaller 13x13 board. The computer replies quickly, and every move must be made within a time limit or the game is lost on time; matches also end when both sides pass or one resigns. Three modes are offered. The Honinbo battle, for standard players, starts at the lowest rank and climbs toward champion. The rank game, meant for beginners, starts in the middle of the ladder and moves up or down with results. The dojo mode sets up custom games, choosing board size, number of players, who moves first and any handicap stones, and supports two-player games and study features.

t_f3141571290d.overview: A mysterious Russian scientist, Dr. Cossack, unleashes an army of robots with the intention of world domination, and Mega Man sets out to stop him. Eight Robot Masters stand in the way: Toad Man, Bright Man, Pharaoh Man, Ring Man, Dust Man, Skull Man, Dive Man and Drill Man. The truth emerges that Dr. Wily had kidnapped Cossack's daughter Kalinka, forcing her father to build the robots, and Wily manages to escape in the end. Holding down the fire button now charges a more powerful shot. Rush returns with the ability to transform into Coil, Jet and Marine modes, and two additional support items, a wire and a balloon, help Mega Man reach difficult places.

t_f3ca7f973b08.overview: Chinese myth supplies the setting for this action platformer, whose title means Yellow Emperor: Battle of Zhuolu, after a legendary rebellion against Huang Di on the Zhuolu plains. An opening cutscene shows an old man on horseback watching winged demons above a burning village. Play follows a standard platformer pattern with secondary weapons, and progress is tracked on a map screen; dying sends the player back several levels to an earlier point on the map. Stages include a flaming village where headless warriors fling their heads, an underground cavern with branching pathways, a bamboo forest, a fungi jungle and a closing maze, with foes such as flying wasps, swordsmen, a seven-tailed blue fox and a mystical tiger.

t_f400625bc6ff.overview: Winning the presidency means getting through party primaries, the national convention and the general election in this strategy simulation set in America. The player picks one of three selectable candidates from either major party, and five contenders in all fight each state's primaries and caucuses. In every state the campaign decides which policies to push hard, checks opinion polls and runs speeches and television ads, drawing on 48 policy issues that span the environment, defense, the economy, education and morals, relations with Japan and foreign affairs. Some states are resolved automatically, and a day of many simultaneous primaries is handled by splitting the states into three regions. A nominee then picks a running mate from the four rivals. Falling below 15 percent of delegates in two states in a row, or exceeding the cap on campaign funds, forces a withdrawal and ends the run.

t_f45e83a9351b.overview: This menu-driven adventure opens as Michimune celebrates his friend Miu's 18th birthday with her grandfather, until a demonic face called Rosenkreuz appears and snatches Miu away. Michimune teams up with Kiyojo, a doctor aware of Rosenkreuz's history, and the two set out to rescue Miu and stop Rosenkreuz's plans. Investigation is handled through a command menu at the side of the screen, and Kiyojo can be asked for help when the situation calls for it. Some sections require navigating mazes. The adventure is divided into chapters that move from one area to the next in a linear order; earlier areas cannot be revisited, so backtracking is never needed. A password for the current position can be viewed at any time by pressing Select.

t_f463aac92bf1.overview: Originally released in Korea as Koko Adventure, a platformer by Daou Infosys, Buzz and Waldog was its planned unlicensed release in America, cancelled before it reached store shelves. One of the title characters makes his way through each stage by running left or right, jumping, spinning and sliding. The spin attack destroys enemies, which usually take one or two hits. Progress depends on keys: a certain number of them are scattered through each level and must be collected to advance to the next stage. The adventure spans five worlds, each made up of three levels and one unique boss battle, and a boss is damaged by spinning into specific damage zones on its body six times.

t_f48e6ff1d8a3.overview: Four years after the previous tournament, Ryuhi is training in the mountains when five Dragon Warriors are sent out to stop the revival of Daimajin, a demon lord sealed away long ago by the hero Ryuten Taisei. The Culture Brain sequel adds transformations and magic to its martial arts action, lets the five warriors appear together, and allows free scrolling in either direction, with levels marking progress and passwords available even without a game over. Play is split between an easier kids' mode and a harder Mania mode, in which some enemies can only be recognized when specific conditions are met and whose completion is required for the true ending. An Anime RPG mode replaces the real-time action with command selection, and a versus mode is also included.

t_f4ece3c6c2e1.overview: Sachen's unlicensed Famicom/NES port of the Mitchell Corporation game Pang places the player at the bottom of the screen, limited to left and right movement, firing a grappling hook with rope attached straight upward at bouncing balloons. Larger balloons split into smaller ones when hit, while the tiniest simply disappear, and contact with any balloon costs a life, with play resuming close to where it stopped. Items sometimes appear on the floor to pick up. Popping enough balloons fills a meter in the bottom-right corner of the screen, and a full meter clears the stage. Fifteen stages lead to a simple cutscene and staff credits, and two players can play by taking turns.

t_f4fa389865aa.overview: Jaleco's 1989 Famicom baseball simulation stands apart within its series for a diagonal play view, carried over from the previous entry's fielding and baserunning screens. Three ballparks are available, and between innings the back screens of the franchise stadiums are shown; close plays trigger a full-screen zoom-in. Player condition follows a biorhythm system with three values, Physical, Sensitivity and Intellectual: positive numbers lift a player above his usual skill, negative numbers keep him below his potential, and zero marks a critical point. Teams are identified by letters, split between the Western League and the Pacific League. In single-player play, a 130-game season in a two-league setup requires 75 wins for the pennant, and four wins in the Japan Series bring the national title.

t_f50c3516e49a.overview: Compile's follow-up to its MSX shooter Guardic splits play between overhead action exploration and vertically scrolling shooting. Naju, a huge capsule of unknown purpose, is on course to strike Earth because the vicious life forms that multiplied inside it are fighting over territory. The combat android System D.P., called Miria, is sent in to set off the ten safety devices that control Naju's self-destruct mechanism. On the surface, a field called the Labyrinth, she explores on foot in search of corridor entrances, some of which stay sealed until clues are gathered. Inside a corridor she transforms into a fighter for high-speed shooting that ends with a boss, and a key won there opens new parts of the Labyrinth. Special weapons consume chips, the in-game currency, and Landers hand out passwords. Life is measured by a gauge with no spare lives, so the game ends when it runs out.

t_f5356acef4e2.overview:
Participants guide athletic competitors across a series of cold-weather events centered on high-speed winter action. Five distinct disciplines are featured, consisting of downhill skiing, aerial ski maneuvers, halfpipe snowboarding, inflatable sled racing, and snowball battles. Players can tackle each of these events individually for practice or progress through them sequentially as a complete competition set to earn cumulative scores.

Up to six competitors can participate in the action by taking turns, with play alternating between participants. When a round ends, the next registered player activates either controller to take their turn on the slopes.

t_f53cd150f9bd.overview:
Bringing down Al Capone and ending his criminal regime forms the primary objective of the mission. Set within 1920s Chicago, the game spans seven distinct scenarios adapted from the film, putting the player in command of Eliot Ness and his squad of lawmen.

Play alternates across multiple formats throughout the investigation. Across various levels, the player ducks for cover while aiming gunsights down alleys, jumps across warehouse crates to retrieve dropped ledgers, and shoots contraband bottles along a border bridge. Later sequences require steering a baby carriage down steps while avoiding gunfire, stopping a hostage taker with a single precision shot to his hat, and pursuing hitman Frank Nitty during a rooftop shootout.

t_f5460d392f4f.overview: Motorcycle racing over rough ground is the subject of this motocross game published by Konami, in which riders must navigate difficult terrain while staying ahead of the other competitors. Although the jumps and wheelies give it a passing resemblance to Excitebike, it plays more like a traditional top-down racer in the style of Super Sprint or R.C. Pro-Am. The circuit is made up of eight tracks, full of twists, turns and tricky jumps that every racer must negotiate. Progress is strict: a rider must place in the top two and then win a race to advance to the next track. A practice mode lets the player try each track before racing it for real.

t_f573c0e1f5bf.overview: Two players can fly at once in this vertically scrolling shooter, with Player 1 taking control of the titular ship TwinBee while Player 2 controls WinBee. One button shoots enemies in the air and the other drops bombs on ground enemies. The main power-ups are bells, uncovered by shooting at the floating clouds where they are hidden; yellow bells give points, while other colors add a twin cannon, raise speed, create image copies of the ship or add a barrier. Ground enemies can also release a bell that grants a three-way gun, or a star that eliminates all on-screen enemies. A single enemy bullet costs a life, but a hit to the side only takes off one of the ship's arms, and an ambulance repairs them. Two players can align their ships vertically or horizontally to perform more powerful attacks.

t_f6009c790577.overview: In the year 2052, the third planet of Sophia lies devastated after an invasion by the Invem Dark Star Cluster, led by the fearsome Goez. The science academy on the satellite NORA builds the all-purpose combat vehicle Metal Attacker, and the 15-year-old genius Kane Gardner takes the controls. Across eight areas, the vehicle explores side-view stages, while small dungeon entrances can only be entered on foot; inside, the action switches to an overhead view in which the pilot fights with a gun and grenades. Some dungeons hide a boss at their deepest point, and defeating it earns new equipment for the vehicle. Those upgrades let the vehicle get past the traps of the side-view stages and advance to the next stage.

t_f60482042eb9.overview: Ported from Sega's 1985 arcade remake, the Famicom Choplifter puts the player in the role of a combat helicopter pilot who must rescue hostages held in barracks. Each rescue follows the same pattern: shoot one of the hostage buildings to release the prisoners, land to let them board, then fly them back to the starting point. Hostile tanks and other enemy combatants harass the helicopter throughout. While it is grounded, enemy tanks can attack it, and enemy jet fighters are deployed that strike at it in the air, so loading passengers and returning them safely is a constant balancing act.

t_f62313a08c8b.overview: Bored in his quiet town, Goemon is invited by Ebisumaru to the World Thief Tournament in Oedo Town, where a grand prize of 100 million ryo persuades him to enter. After qualifying, the pair must gather eight keys that open the way to the legendary Wish Orb hidden on Mangetsu Island, though breaking the seals sets off earthquakes that threaten the planet. The role-playing journey reaches a pyramid, Antarctica and the Moon, with travel by camel, boat, submarine and UFO. Turn-based battles use front and back rows, and a full four-member party can unleash a combined attack on all enemies at a cost in HP. Goemon now learns skills, while Koryuta, a boy who is secretly a dragon deity, can transform into a dragon. Simon Belmont joins as a guest.

t_f66bdc7b6446.overview: Bandai's side-scrolling action game opens with the scholar Hashimoto being turned into a dinosaur by Salamander, a villain calling himself the Emperor of Space-Time. Keeping his human mind, the transformed hero, Hashimoto Zaurus, pursues Salamander through the ages in the Time Capsule, a time machine he built himself. His main weapon is a boomerang, which can also be thrown upward, and collecting the Super Shield turns him into Super Zaurus, who throws boomerangs faster and three at a time. Stages include Dinosaur Island, Egypt, Future City, Enchanted Realm and Age of the Gods, with Dinosaur Island first and the order of several later stages random. Defeating each stage boss yields one of the Swords of the Ten Kings, the key items of the quest. Quiz questions award bonus points, and a message window offers hints.

t_f679f857e524.overview: Pulled into the world of a dream mirror, Kiteretsu and his friends try to find their way out in an action game adapted from the Kiteretsu Daihyakka series. The maps are assembled from psychedelic map pieces laid out in monotonous rows. Inventions are created by rapidly pressing buttons, and companions join the group along the way, yet they never attack; instead, every added companion enlarges the area that can take damage, so a bigger party becomes a burden rather than a help. Continuing after a game over requires taking on a debt through an invention built early in the adventure.

t_f6b0a20d19b2.overview: Rather than a straight conversion of the arcade shooter, this version reworks the music and stage structure into a largely original game with a gentler difficulty. Everything begins when four planets, including Gradius, reach an alignment that occurs once every 10,000 years, and the Bacterion Empire attacks again under Gofer, the giant head. Across seven stages, one of them made up entirely of boss confrontations, collected capsules advance a power-up gauge. Double and Laser can each be upgraded twice for a faster rate of fire, and a force field protects the whole ship. Selecting another option after four sends the options rotating around the ship for a time. Some power-up voices are reproduced through the DPCM sound channel, and two players take alternating turns.

t_f6b456fd1b95.overview: Dragon Co. followed its The Lion King III: Timon & Pumbaa with this reworked sequel on the same engine. Simba, Timon and Pumbaa again serve as the selectable heroes, but many sprites are redrawn, including enemies and Simba himself, the level order is completely reversed, and every music track is replaced with new pieces running on Sunsoft's sound engine. The title screen shows new animations of the three characters, while the credits screen shows portraits of the developers. Each hero has a separate game over screen, and these screens are notorious for depicting the selected character committing suicide. Unlike its predecessor, the sequel has no pause screen.

t_f6c1e470a83f.overview: Eight fighters gather on the Aotis continent, a land where swordplay and magic coexist, in this one-on-one fighting game from Sachen. The roster includes Rex, Malcolm, Roger, Big Whale, Daphne, Ned and Rock Tiger, with Dark Moon waiting as a boss who cannot be selected. Matches follow the pattern of Street Fighter II, and each fighter has special moves of their own. After the regular opponents are beaten, the player also faces Dark Moon and a recolored copy of the chosen character. Every fighter has an individual ending, and the difficulty setting does not change which one is shown. Voice samples are used for the fighters and for the match announcer, and two players can battle head to head.

t_f6c20b54b13d.overview: Endurance rather than sprinting is the focus of this jogging game for one player on the Family Trainer mat, which uses the eight-key side A and the same controls as the series' first game. One course is a lap of roughly five kilometers, run counterclockwise around the outer grounds of the imperial palace, the country's most famous jogging route. The other is an obstacle marathon over a fictional 42.195-kilometer course, though the full distance is not actually run. Obstacles such as oil cans litter the way; hitting one knocks the runner down and drains stamina, and running out of stamina means retiring. A skateboard item carries the runner forward without running on the mat, though jumps must still be made.

t_f6cf1cd96d16.overview: Kickle, a boy who can freeze enemies with his icy breath, sets out to defeat the demon king who has turned the land of dreams into a world of ice, and to rescue its king and his daughter. Play takes place on small ice islands surrounded by sea: frozen enemies become blocks of ice that can be kicked into the water to create new land, and collecting three treasure bags clears a stage. The adventure spans four lands themed on vegetables, fruit, sweets and toys, each ending in a boss battle in which items produced by the boss's attacks are kicked back at it. Running out of time, touching an enemy or being hit by sliding ice costs a life. Clearing everything opens 20 harder special stages, and stages within a land can be played in any order.

t_f7065f4828fb.overview: Konami's action role-playing game features two heroes who can be swapped at any time: Popolon, hero of the original Majou Densetsu, and Aphrodite, whom he rescued in that adventure. While Popolon was away, the grand bishop Galious invaded the Greek kingdom, turned its castle into a demon fortress and abducted Pampers, the child Popolon and Aphrodite were destined to have. The goal is to explore the castle, with its many hidden secrets, and five worlds, defeat five bosses, namely four great demons and Galious himself, collect five Great Keys and rescue the infant Pampers. Each demon must be summoned by chanting a spell entered with the controller, and the spells are learned in rooms hidden within the worlds. Password continues allow progress to be restored even after the power is switched off.

t_f72b5862cb0d.overview: A tournament-style fighting game in the Kunio-kun series, designed as a chaotic brawler for up to four players. Kunio receives a challenge letter announcing a fighting tournament to decide the strongest high school student. Story mode pairs characters into two-person tag teams that battle through eight pairs of tough rivals, and partners who lock together or stand on one another can begin a combination special move. Battle mode stages four-way battle royales with free choice of characters, opponents and stages. Items collected during a fight have various effects on the characters and the match. Players can also create an original fighter by entering personal data such as a name, birthday and blood type, and a password shown on the status screen restores that character later. More than two players requires a multitap.

t_f7352d463150.overview: Tag matches pit the RICKY FIGHTERS against the STRONG BADS in this Famicom version of Data East's arcade wrestling game The Big Pro Wrestling! A single player works through a total of 35 tag matches, competing in a series of tournaments for ever larger trophies, while a separate versus mode lets two players face each other. Every bout is a one-fall match with a time limit, decided by a three-count pinfall, a 20-count outside the ring, a submission or time running out. Wrestlers have a variety of moves, including dropkicks, but all are executed the same way: landing an A-button punch puts the opponent in a controlled state, from which a technique can be applied.

t_f764d369bb64.overview: Falling blocks become plumbing in this puzzle game, whose nominal goal is a pipeline from Moscow to Tokyo built to strengthen Japan–Soviet Union relations, with Mikhail Gorbachev pictured on the title screen and packaging. Two-square blocks printed with pipe segments drop into a vertical well and must be joined into working lines. Water enters at the bottom of the right wall and has to reach an outlet in the left wall. A completed pipeline disappears, and the blocks beneath it turn into blue water blocks that earn bonus points when cleared together. Items include a drill that carves through blocks and a water bottle. Blocking a pipe end usually forces a restart, and later stages offer fewer exits on the left wall.

t_f7b51f5f6fd6.overview: Folklore drives this 1987 role-playing game built around Momotarō. An old woman washing clothes at a river finds a large peach floating down from upstream, and the boy who emerges from it ultimately sets out to defeat the oni on their island. By offering kibi dango, he gains a dog, a monkey and a pheasant as companions, who join battles as computer-controlled allies acting on their own judgment. Familiar role-playing terms are recast in traditional style: level and experience become dan and kokoro, hit points and magic points become tai and waza, and magic becomes jutsu. The eight kinds of jutsu are learned from hermits rather than through leveling, and progress is recorded through passwords called the voice of heaven, obtained from shrine priests in villages and the capital.

t_f7d3de6002ed.overview: Robot building and one-on-one combat make up this tournament fighting game for Bandai's Datach Joint ROM System, which the cartridge needs in order to run. Each combat robot is put together in a factory that gives the machine a name and fits its head, body, shoulders and feet. A pre-game lobby is used to get ready before the robot combat begins. Every match is divided into rounds of 60 seconds, and each robot has separate gauges for energy and for damage. Alongside standard punches and kicks, the robots can fire off special moves. Play is single-player.

t_f7e68bd7e52b.overview: Ei-How Yang made this bootleg Famicom backport of the SNES game Contra III: The Alien Wars, also titled Super Contra 3. Like the original, it is split into six areas, but the order changes: the original's third and fourth stages come second and third, its second stage becomes the fourth and scrolls only upward without rotating, and the fifth area nearly repeats the second with a pink sky. The only collectable weapons are the laser and spread guns, smart bombs remain, and the player carries one gun instead of two. An options screen sets the number of starting lives and offers a sound test, but there are no continues. The ending shows the player holding on to a helicopter above the word "THEND".

t_f7fa5a2d5fb1.overview: Gen-san, a hammer-wielding carpenter, takes a stand against the Kuroki-gumi after the gang destroys his house. Adapted from the arcade game, the Famicom version differs so much in enemies and stages that it is almost a different work. Arcade one-hit deaths give way to a life meter of four points plus spare lives, and the power-up item appears here as a giant hammer itself. Items such as a recovery drink that restores one point of life are chosen with the Select button. The adventure spans five stages played through twice, with the ending already shown after the first loop. Up to the third stage, each cleared stage triggers a bonus game to rescue Kanna, who is kidnapped again every time.

t_f8a2e88817c0.overview: Waixing's unofficial 8-bit reverse port of Koei's strategy RPG Sangokushi Eiketsuden was not made by Koei, and it trims some of the original's content and contains several notable bugs. The player takes the role of Liu Bei, the noble general of the Shu kingdom, usually accompanied by his sworn brothers Guan Yu and Zhang Fei. Play alternates between strategic battles fought with multiple soldier units and an adventure mode in which Liu Bei visits towns, talks with townspeople, buys equipment and recruits for his army. Depending on the player's choices, the story may branch into different battles. In the original design, every playable officer except Liu Bei can change unit class by using special items.

t_f8bdab492a3f.overview: Based on the computer game Oil's Well, this Sachen release opens on an Earth flooded with litter, where the genius Dr. Po Po invents an auto-tracing garbage collector, Chi Chi Po, to save the planet. The player controls a snake-like collector attached to Dr. Po Po's vehicle that starts retracted at the top of the screen, extends with the D-Pad and snaps back with the A button. Collecting every trash pellet clears a stage. Enemies drift across the screen and most score points when eaten, but eating a mine, letting an enemy touch the body or running out of time costs a life. Items include food, a pinwheel that slows everything down, a gas canister for temporary invincibility, and the six letters of Sachen's logo for an extra life. Sixty stages span six worlds, with stage passwords and a short cartoon after every tenth stage.

t_f8c00ca3ce94.overview: Four real-life Japanese impressionists compete in a board game to be crowned king of impressions, with one to four players and the computer handling any unused performers. Each turn begins with a roll of two dice, and the mover may stop on any space within reach to trigger its event before rolling a special die for happenings such as fan changes, mini-games, lost turns, performance bans or a rigged championship. Spaces are either the homes of stars, where material is learned or skills improved, or venues where performing wins fans; performing at a rival's home can steal fans and block that rival's act. A recurring impressions championship and routines going stale affect popularity. Play ends when one player earns a perfect score from a stern critic or goes bankrupt, and rankings combine her evaluation, fans and championship points.

t_f95c2db94015.overview: Released in North America as Shingen the Ruler, this turn-based strategy game is set in Japan's Sengoku period, with the player as Takeda Shingen, based in the holding of Kai and Shinano. The goal is to conquer central Japan, roughly from Kyoto to Kamakura, with play starting in January 1545. Shingen must build and train an army, cultivate provinces, and make and break alliances with neighboring daimyo, while random disasters and predefined events, such as the death of his father, shape the campaign. His heir, Takeda Katsuyori, can also be trained. Combat unfolds in two stages, a skirmish in the field followed by a battle at the castle itself, and the layout of each holding's field and castle varies. An automatic battle system that calculates the damage done by each army is also available.

t_f95d95412e7a.overview:
Sky Kid provides horizontally scrolling shooter gameplay featuring up to two players. Participants operate biplanes piloted by Baron, in red, and Max, in blue, flying through levels filled with hostile air and ground units. Missions challenge pilots to locate and bomb specific targets, which include battleships, aircraft carriers, factories, and headquarters. Because the aircraft do not begin with explosives, players must collect a bomb along the flight path before reaching the objective, then land back at base.

Pilots use a machine gun to fire upon enemy forces and can execute a loop maneuver to evade hazards or reveal secrets. Reaching mission objectives requires flying through enemy defenses. Points are awarded for destroying opposing units and successfully bombing targets, with bonus points granted at the end of a mission for completely demolishing targets.

t_f960837e54e5.overview: On the planet Pan, outside Earth's galaxy, a mysterious alien force able to consume living things, machines and buildings overwhelms the army, and the population is told to evacuate. Army captain Max Maverick refuses to leave and takes on the invaders alone. Seen from an overhead oblique, isometric viewpoint, the shooter has Max collecting weapon upgrades for a firearm with two modes, including a wide shot for hitting enemies at angles, and releasing bombs while jumping to clear out nearby foes. Separate icons power up each weapon and the bombs, other pickups restore life or add a shield that lasts five hits, and pitfalls and land mines must be avoided. Stages include a hovercraft run over water and a fast motorcycle ride, bosses guard each level, and progress is kept by password.

t_f96d0f5af804.overview: Seen from inside a spaceship cockpit, this first-person space shooter casts the player as a lone pilot protecting a transport ship, the CosmoStation Noah, full of planetary refugees, from a fleet of intergalactic terrorists known as the Molok Wardrivers. Play moves between sub spaces of a larger world map laid out as a 10x10 grid that is randomized at the start of each game. Each enemy fleet has a mothership that endlessly deploys spacecraft as long as it remains operational. Fuel crystals drain over time and faster during warping or after damage, and shields can be raised to minimize harm. Space stations allow refueling and repairs, and up to eight planets can be visited in search of engine and weapon upgrades. The battle is won by defeating the enemy armada and returning safely to base.

t_f991aa62437e.overview:
Play progresses through a continuously looping sequence of three zones: a bike chase through an obstacle zone, a bike chase across a slippery zone, and a final battle with the Dinosaur Tank across the battery zone. The player steers the rescue bike Gilgitt Petras, throwing enemy Basrah bikes into walls and obstacles or destroying enemies with a laser beam.

While maneuvering through each area, the bike rescues stranded Petras for bonus points and collects Energy Packs that refill its energy; carrying too many Petras drains energy faster, and the bike stops working when its energy reaches zero. In the slippery zone, excessive movement can send the bike sliding into obstacles. Up to two players are supported.

t_f9d009803a03.overview: Square blocks marked with numerals, hearts or diamonds fall into a well in this puzzle game, and the player arranges them into horizontal, vertical or diagonal lines of three to five identical or consecutive numbers to score points and remove them. Every level sets a goal that must be met before moving on: completing a set number of lines, reaching a stated score, or eliminating a certain number of blocks at once through any combination of line directions. Treasure blocks act as wild cards, while death blocks can be removed only by combining them with other death blocks.

t_f9d16c538cc8.overview: Planned as an NES port of the Super Nintendo game of the same name and cancelled late into development, this educational rail sim has the player help Thomas the Tank Engine complete various tasks, such as taking children to the seaside, bringing medicine to the hospital and delivering the mail. Dead ends, level crossings, other trains and vehicles create obstacles to overcome along the way. The surviving NES build matches the Super Nintendo version in its content, but it has no voice acting and lower quality graphics.

t_f9e86f039108.overview:
Levels in this action game take place within an enclosed maze where the objective is to consume every pellet scattered along the corridors. Players guide the title character through the pathways while evading four pursuing colored ghosts, each driven by distinct behavioral patterns. Losing a life occurs whenever a ghost contacts the character, and exhausting all lives concludes the run.

Power pellets located near the maze corners temporarily turn the ghosts blue and vulnerable. Chomping these weakened pursuers yields bonus points, with consecutive captures awarding escalating values. Bonus fruit appears twice in each maze near the center of the area, and its value rises in later mazes. Warp tunnels on the sides let the title character cross directly to the opposite edge of the maze.

t_fa1d38cc18c6.overview: Speech synthesis gives this installment of the Famista baseball series from Namco a talking voice, and its music was overhauled. The league mode of the previous entry is dropped in favor of a knockout format with password continues, played against the computer or a second player. Players gain fielding and throwing-arm ratings, pitcher stamina now drains by batters faced rather than pitches thrown, and pitching forms include tornado and other distinctive deliveries. When setting a lineup, up to four players of equal ability can be acquired from other teams by trade. A separate home run contest has batters swinging at straight pitches, and beating each computer team's batters in turn leads to an ending. All four stadiums are new, including parks based on Wrigley Field and the cornfield diamond from Field of Dreams.

t_fa206b619ea0.overview: A mysterious entity has kidnapped Takahashi Meijin's five dinosaur companions, and he sets out to rescue them. Instead of separate stages, the adventure plays out across a complex scrolling map of connected areas. The hero moves forward and backward, jumps, climbs trees and enters doors, and gathers a wide variety of items: some, such as boomerangs and spears, serve as weapons, while others, like the water gun, solve puzzles and open the way forward, and a compass shows his location on a 3D map. Bosses guard the way, and defeating one frees a kidnapped dinosaur and opens paths to new areas. A life gauge lets him take more than one hit; collecting enough fruit restores part of it, and gathering two fragments of a heart container expands it.

t_fa95ca3ffcb1.overview: Sachen's 1990 Famicom card collection, also released as The World of Card Games, puts four playing-card games on a single cartridge: Omnibus Hearts, Fan Tan, Chinese Rummy and The Clock. Some of Sachen's back labels call the program simply Poker, and the company followed it with further card compilations, Poker II with four games and Poker III with five. The four games here were also later reissued on Sachen's Super Cartridge Version 2 multicart.

t_fa9900a45a33.overview: Rock, paper, scissors is the basis of this adult-themed Sachen release. The player challenges five different women in turn, and each must be beaten across three rounds; a round goes to whoever first collects two winning hands. Clothing serves as the stake, and every set the player secures is rewarded with a picture of the opponent missing the item that was bet. Losing a round shows nothing unless the player was betting underpants, and losing three rounds ends the game. Rather than picking a hand directly, the player watches the possible hands switch rapidly on screen and presses A to lock in the current one.

t_fafc0066b104.overview: In the star year 4622, a research fleet from a time-travel company sets out for ancient Earth, but nearly all of its ships are wrecked by a horde of strangely evolved biomechanical creatures, leaving the lone ship Noah to fight on. The Hudson Soft shooter alternates vertically scrolling stages with horizontally scrolling ones across six stages, set in places such as the Inca Empire, Atlantis, Egypt and Mu, each ending with a boss. The ship fires a light particle cannon at airborne enemies and cluster bombs at ground targets. A life gauge absorbs several hits, though walls, fire pillars and some enemies destroy the ship at once, and capsules released by bombing supply points restore energy. Clearing all six stages opens a hard mode with doubled enemy bullet speed, and two- and five-minute contest modes are included.

t_fc01726d8710.overview:
Across a sequence of distinct stages, players control the humanoid warrior toads Rash and Zitz on a mission to defeat the Dark Queen and rescue their captured companions, Pimple and Princess Angelica. Levels incorporate varied formats, including beat 'em up brawling, platforming, descents along suspended cables, obstacle courses, and vehicle rides on the Speed Bike, Jet Turbo and Space Board, as well as a unicycle. Players have a limited number of lives and an energy meter that is replenished by eating flies.

Progression requires defeating enemies and maneuvering through hazards. Standard offensive moves include punches, kicks and a running head-butt, and double-tapping the control pad with the B button gives access to powerful Smash Hits such as the Battletoad Butt and Big Bad Boot. Certain objects, such as the legs of defeated walker enemies, can also be picked up and wielded. Some moves suit particular hazards; the BT Bashing Ball, for example, uproots Saturn Toadtraps and short-circuits the wall-mounted Retro-Blasters.

t_fc5e0d1c6aba.overview: Tennis for the NES from Palcom Software, built around an athlete controlled on the court. Shots such as volleys and lobs are performed by pressing buttons with the correct timing in relation to the ball's movement. Alongside a tournament of several matches against more and more experienced opponents, there is a training mode and a free match in which the parameters, such as the court surface and the number of sets, can be set beforehand. One unusual touch is that the player can complain to the referee during a match.

t_fc6a45480b4f.overview: Despite the numbering, this 1993 NTDEC release shares little with Fighting Hero beyond its genre. It is a one-on-one fighting game in which the A button punches and the B button kicks, each with different animations when Back or Forward is held while attacking; a throw is performed with Back and A at close range, and holding Back blocks. The cast consists of ten original characters, among them a biker in street clothes, a Bruce Lee clone, a samurai-like kicker, a bulky professional wrestler, a Muay Thai kickboxer and a pirate with a hook hand and a peg leg, each with special moves entered as joystick motions. Every character has two duplicates with different names and colors; in single-player the computer always uses a duplicate. The difficulty cannot be changed, but nine continues are given.

t_fc6f82dcb757.overview: Built entirely within the Family BASIC programming add-on for the Famicom, Fisraduth: Castle of Tyramis is an action game from C.A.T. SOFT. Family BASIC limits programs to a small set of built-in sprites such as Mario, Pauline, Penguin and Fly, but Fisraduth combines them into much larger characters, from a shielded knight to a flame-spewing tektite and a gowned lady, each two to three times taller than normal sprites. Although such programs normally use a single background, darkness hides portions of the screen to create the feeling of multiple rooms, and there are hidden, secret rooms to find. The game is very difficult, and alternate Easy and Very Easy versions with modified difficulty also exist.

t_fc840c806b0c.overview: The Famicom version of Salamander reworks the arcade shooter rather than copying it directly. Its six stages alternate between horizontal and vertical scrolling, but the stage layout is rearranged, and the fourth and fifth stages are entirely original to this version; the fourth is a cell stage with a high-speed blood vessel section in the middle. In place of the arcade's instant pick-ups, capsules left behind by certain enemies feed a Gradius-style power bar. Two players can play together, flying ships that differ only in color, and the options trailing them are limited to three between both players. Larger bosses and extra features are made possible by a custom chip in the cartridge. A player may continue up to three times, and the ending picture changes with the number of continues used.

t_fc91c5830ecb.overview: In the kingdom of Fairyland, three magic jewels were enshrined in the palace to keep the peace, until the most vicious demon in the kingdom, Varalys, took control. Varalys has also cast a spell on Princess Ann, turning her into three fairies and hiding them somewhere in the land. The young knight Jim takes up the task of restoring peace in this action role-playing adventure, adapted for the cartridge from an earlier computer game. Combat is governed by a switch between an attack mode and a defense mode, and the hero's health slowly regenerates while he stands still. A later export release kept the content essentially unaltered apart from minor changes to the title screen and some prompts and messages.

t_fd3aa867e1ff.overview: Controlling the space fighter craft Michael, the player battles through a horizontally scrolling shooter to stop the Gamma organization from using the alien creature Kassandra to take over the Alpharos star system. The ship can fire forward or backward with the A or B buttons. Some enemies drop power-ups, including weapons and satellite pods; each of the three weapons is strengthened by collecting its letter three times, and the pods fire their own projectiles while blocking incoming enemy fire. Before starting, an Edit Mode lets the player spend up to five points on weapon modifications and set the pod formation. Six stages follow, each with its own environmental gimmick and boss. Getting hit costs a life and reduces firepower.

t_fd6e9316f0dd.overview:
Piloting the starship Caesar, the player shoots down waves of hostile forces threatening the galactic empire. This vertically scrolling journey spans sixteen stages set across a massive space station. The craft moves across the screen and fires upward to strike both grounded targets and airborne enemies arriving from above. At certain points, the ship can enter a trap zone, slipping beneath the station structure to evade incoming fire. Each stage ends with a confrontation against a supercomputer boss called Starbrain, while a Big Starbrain variant appears at the end of stages 4, 8, 12, and 16.

Destroying special markers releases power capsules that bolster the starship's capabilities. Collecting capsules enhances speed, strengthens weapon output, and alters firing patterns. Gathering multiple items enables the craft to transform, fire behind itself, and eventually shoot in five directions. A third capsule grants a shield absorbing up to five hits, while a fourth upgrade eliminates flying enemies.

t_fd781b500104.overview: Supervised by professional mahjong player Yousuke Ide, the cartridge pits one player against a single computer opponent while scoring hands as if four people were at the table. A dedicated controller modeled on an arcade mahjong control panel is bundled and handles every operation; the standard controller cannot play it. Three modes are offered. The free match mode allows detailed rule settings, local hand options and background music selection, plus features that swap the entire hand, flash the dora tiles, or show a girl cheering on each hand. The league mode starts in the lower league and climbs to the top league, where a final match against Ide himself leads to the ending. The practice mode poses discard, waiting-tile and hand-value problems.

t_ff2b71570b2d.overview: A lone soldier named Eric sets out to fight evil all over the world in side-view action that is somewhat reminiscent of the Contra series. Eric begins armed only with his fists and grenades, but soon obtains a sub-machine gun that can be upgraded to a spread shot and even to a rocket launcher, whose missiles are slower but very strong. Enemies attack from the foreground and the background simultaneously. Unlike most Contra games, Eric does not die in a single hit; he has a life bar that is partially replenished or extended every time he picks up a weapon upgrade or a medal. The missions range from the jungles of Vietnam to a shipyard and a train.

t_ff44700c55d6.overview:
Ten levels of action span locations such as Times Square, the SoHo Sewer System, and Snowy Central Park, each concluding with an encounter against a lethal boss. Players select either Leonardo, Raphael, Michaelangelo, or Donatello, each outfitted with their signature weapons such as katana blades, sai daggers, nunchakus, or a bo staff. The mission involves fighting through hordes of Foot Soldiers and assorted enemy machines to rescue April and confront Shredder in the Technodrome.

Turtles can walk in eight directions, jump, attack with their weapons, or combine movements to deliver jumping kicks. Wounds deplete a turtle's life meter, though consuming pizzas restores energy. Each turtle begins with three lives, with a bonus life earned for every two hundred opponents knocked out. The game supports single-player action or two-player cooperative play. If a player exhausts their supply of lives during two-player mode, an extra life can be borrowed from their partner. Up to three continues are available.

t_ff4961d1f49e.overview: Viewed from directly overhead, this top-scrolling racer begins with a choice of team from three, then sends detailed machines around detailed courses built to convey speed. Steering turns the car's wheel much as in a real car, and tires wear and lose grip depending on how the car is driven, so pit stops are needed and their timing becomes a tactical decision. Fuel does not have to be managed. When the number of wrecked cars passes a set limit, a red flag is shown and the race restarts. Hardware limits slowed this home version down overall.

t_ff9b0b39979c.overview: Top Hit 20 Vol. 2 is the second song cartridge made for Karaoke Studio, the Famicom karaoke system that comes with a microphone peripheral capable of detecting a human voice. Like the first volume, this smaller cassette plugs directly into the back of the Karaoke Studio subsystem and expands it with twenty new songs that the original unit does not contain. The songs are performed the same way as the built-in ones: the music plays while the lyrics appear on screen over a graphical depiction of each song's theme, the singer follows along in karaoke style, and the performance is scored on accuracy of singing. It requires the Karaoke Studio subsystem to be used.

t_ffb10ec91473.overview: An action role-playing game with side-scrolling battles, Kagerou Densetsu sends its hero out to defeat a demon lord and avenge his father. Two of the hero's friends follow him, and the player can switch between them when taking on random encounters. These encounters occur while traveling across the world map and move the action to a side-scrolling zone, where fast-moving ninja opponents and other monsters must be defeated through a combination of slashes and jumps. Magic is also available, but it takes time to cast and leaves the caster vulnerable.

t_ffbff6b040e5.overview: Two players can fly at the same time in this vertically scrolling shooter, battling insect-type enemies, skull-shaped foes and ground turrets on the way to the floating fortress Exed Exes. Collecting a white "Pow" item turns every enemy on screen into bonus fruit, and other power-ups strengthen the main shot. A crush attack, usable once for each star in stock, sweeps enemy bullets off the screen but does not damage regular enemies. Each round ends with a floating fortress boss that must be destroyed completely, and the final weapon of the Exes army appears in Round 16. When two players fly together, they draw on a shared stock of stars.

t_ffd50431e287.overview:
Ten areas form the structure of this single-player shooter, guiding secret agent Albatross through a rescue mission in the underground headquarters of a conspiratorial group. Operating as part of the Rolling Thunder secret police organization, the protagonist infiltrates enemy territory to rescue fellow agent Leila from a criminal organization named the Evil Society.

Controlling Albatross across multi-level floors and stairs, the player leaps over obstacles, takes cover behind crates, and enters doorways to hide from hostile forces. Albatross defends himself with a standard handgun and can acquire a continuous-firing machine gun, replenishing ammunition by accessing marked supply doors. Enemies include ninjas, creatures such as human-faced bats, color-coded Hooded Thugs, and the Evil Society leader Mabu at the final showdown.
